records.sourceEnglish:
Because they were aware of the Supreme Lord's sweetness, the cowherd people became the the
most wise philosophers (parama-jïäné). The demigod Brahmä, who had personally seen numberless
four-armed forms of the Lord, specifically took shelter of the form of Lord Kåñëa. Brahmä said in
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.14.1):


nauméòya te 'bhra-vapuñe taòid-ambaräya
  guïjävataàsa-paripiccha-lasan-mukhäya
vanya-sraje kavala-vetra-viñäëa-veëu-
  lakñmä-çriye mådu-pade paçupäìgajäya


   "My dear Lord, You are the only worshipful Supreme Lord, Personality of Godhead. Therefore I
am offering my humble obeisances and prayers just to please You. Your bodily features are of the
color of clouds filled with water. You are glittering with a silver electric aura emanating from Your
yellow garments.*
   "Let me offer my respectful repeated obeisances unto the son of Mahäräja Nanda who is standing
before me with conchshell, earrings, and peacock feather on His head. His face is beautiful. He is
wearing a helmet, garlanded with forest flowers, and He stands with a morsel of food in His hand.
He is decorated with cane and bugle, and He carries a buffalo horn and flute. He stands before me
with small lotus feet."*

   The spiritual love the cowherd people feel for Lord Kåñëa is the crest jewel of all kinds of love.
When opposing things suddenly appear, that love does not waver. On the contrary, that love
eclipses all opposition. When obstacles arise, that love increases. In this way spiritual love is like the
love hedonists feel for material sense objects. That love the hedonists feel for material senses
objects, love that the scriptures and direct perception both declare to be be full of faults, is indeed
very passionate and strong. In that sense spiritual love is similar to that material love. This is seen
in the following prayer spoken by Prahläda Mahäräja to Lord Nåsiàha in Viñëu Puräëa (1.20.19):


yä prétir avivekänäà

   viñayeñv anapäyiné
tväm anusmarataù sä me
   hådayän näpasrpatu


   "Fools fall in love with material sense objects. As they always love senses obejcts, may I always
love You. I always meditate on You. I pray that You will never leave my heart."

   The intensity of spiritual love is also seen in these words spoken by Nanda and Yaçodä to Lord
Balaräma in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.65.3):


ciraà naù pähi däçärha
   sänujo jagad-éçvaraù
ity äropyäìkam äliìgya
   netraiù siñicatur jalaiù


   " `O descendant of Däçärha, O Lord of the universe, may You and Your younger brother Kåñëa
ever protect us.' Saying this, they raised Çré Balaräma onto their laps, embraced Him, and moistened
Him with tears from their eyes."***

   Even though it was very clear the Lord Balaräma was Vasudeva's son, a kñatriya, and the
Supreme Personality of Godhead Himseelf, Nanda and Yaçodä still thought of Him as their own
son. This is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.65.1-2):


balabhadraù kusu-çreñöha
   bhagavän ratham ästhitaù
suhåd-didåkñur utkaëöhaù
   prayayau nanda-gokulam


  "O best of the Kurus, once Lord Balaräma, eager to visit His well-wishing friends, mounted His
chariot and traveled to Nanda Gokula.***


pariñvaktas cirotkaëöhair
   gopair gopébhir eva ca
rämo 'bhivädya pitaräv
   äçérbhir abhinanditaù


   "Having long suffered the anxiety of separation, the cowherd men and their wives ambraced
Lord Balaräma. The Lord then offered respects to His parents, and they joyfully greeted Him with
prayers."***

   When spiritual love (préti) becomes very prominent, it eclispses everything else. This occurs
even amongst the devotees who are naturally attracted to the Lord in His feature of power and
opulence. An example of this is seen in the following description of Çré Devahüti in Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (3.33.21):


vanaà pravrajite patyäv
   apatya-virahäturä
jïäta-tattväpy abhün nañöe
   vatse gaur iva vatsalä


   "Devahüti's husband had already left home and accepted the renounced order of life, and then
her only son, Kapila, left home. Although she knew all the truths of life and death, and although
her heart was cleansed of all dirt, she was very aggrieved at the loss of her son, just as a cow is
affected when her calf dies."*

   A similar situation, where spiritual love overcomes awareness of the Lor'd power and opulence, is
seen in these words spoken by Çré Devaké-devé in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.3.29):


samuvije bhavad-dhetoù
   kaàsäd aham adhéra-dhéù


  "O Madhusüdana, because of Your appearance, I am becoming more and more anxious in fear of
Kaàsa."*

  The same sentiment is seen in these words describing Mahäräja Yudhiñöhira in Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (1.10.32):


ajäta-çatruù påtanäà
   gopéthäya madhu-dvisah
parebhyaù çaìkitaù snehät
   präyuìkta catur-aìginém


   "Mahäräja Yudhiñöhira, although no one's enemy, engaged four divisions of defense [horse,
elephant, chariot and army] to accompany Lord Kåñëa, the enemy of the asuras [demons]. The
Mahäräja did this because of the enemy, and also out of affection for the Lord."*

   This same senitment of spieritual love eclipsing awareness of the Lord's power and opulence is
again seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (1.10.33):

atha dürägatän çaurih
   kauravän virahäturän
sannivartya dådhaà snigdhän
   präyät sva-nagaréà priyaiù


   "Out of profound affection for Lord Kåñëa, the Päëòavas, who were of the Kuru dynasty,
accompanied Him a considerable distance to see Him off. They were overwhelmed with the thought
of future separation. The Lord, however, persuaded them to return home, and He proceeded
towards Dvärakä with His dear companions."*

  How spiritual love overwhelmed even Lord Balaräma's awareness of Lord Kåñëa's power and
opulence is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.53.20-21):


çrutvaitad bhagavän rämo
   vipakñéya-nåpodyamam
kåñëaà caikaà gataà hartuà
   kanyäà kalaha-çaìkitaù

balena mahatä särdhaà
   bhrätå-sneha-pariplutaù
tvaritaù kuëòinaà prägäd
   gajäçva-ratha-pattibhiù


   "When Lord Balaräma heard about these preparations of the inimical kings and how Lord Kåñëa
had set off alone to steal the bride, He feared that a fight would ensue. Immersed in affection for
His brother, He hurried to Kuëòina with a mighty army consisting of infantry and soldiers riding
on elephants, horses, and chariots."***

  Here the word "bhagavän" means "all-knowing". Another example of devotees being
overwhelmed by love for Lord Kåñëa is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.11.49):


kåñëaà maha-baka-grastaà
   dåñövä rämädayo 'rbhakäù. . .


   "When Balaräma and the other boys saw that Kåñëa had been devoured by the gigantic duck,
they became almost unconscious, like senses without life."*

   The bliss the cowherd people attain by perceiving Lord Kåñëa's sweetness far surpasses the bliss
that comes from perceiving Brahman or perceiving the opulence and power of the Supreme
Personality of Godhead. Seeing the good fortune attained by the cowherd people, Çréla Çukadeva

Gosvämé became filled with wonder. He said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.12.11):


itthaà satäà brahma-sukhänubhütyä. . .


   "In this way, all the cowherd boys used to play with Kåñëa, who is the source of the Brahman
effulgence for j{.sy 241}änés desiring to merge into that effulgence, who is the Supreme Personality
of Godhead for devotees who have accepted eternal servitorship, and who for ordinary persons is
but another ordinary child. The cowherd boys, having accumulated the results of pious activities for
many lives, were able to associate in this way with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. How can
one explain their great fortune?"*

   He also said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.9.20):


nemaà viriïco na bhavaù. . .


   "Neither Lord Brahmä nor lord Çiva, nor even the goddess of fortune, who is always the better
half of the Supreme Lord, can obtain from the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the deliverer from
this material world, such mercy as was received by Mother Yaçodä."*

   He also said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.9.21):


näyaà sukhäpaù. . .


   "The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kåñëa, the son of mother Yaçodä, is accessible to
devotees engaged in spontaneous loving service, but He is not as easily accessible to mental
speculators, to those striving for self-realization by severe austerities and pen- ances, or to those
who consider the body the same as the self."*

   He also said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.60):

näyaà çriyo 'ìga. . .

   "When Lord Çré Kåñëa was danciong with the gopés in the räsa-lélä, the gopés were embraced by
the arms of the Lord. This transcendental favor was never bestowed upon the goddess of fortune or
other consorts in the spiritual world. Indeed, never was such a thing even imagined by the most
beautiful girls in the heavenly planets, whose bodily luster and aroma resemble the lotus flower.
Ansd what to speak of worldly women who are very beautiful according to material estimation?"*

  Sometimes the manifestation of the Lord's opulence increases the perception of His sweetness.
This occurs when the devotee has the idea "How can this by our son (or other relation) in this

wonderful situation?" An example of such a situation is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.28.18):


nandädayas tu taà dåñövä
   paramänanda-nivåtäù
kåñëaà ca tatra cchandobhiù
   stüyamänaà su-vismitäh


   "Nanda Mahäräja and the other cowherd men felt the greatest happiness when they saw that
transcendental abode. They were especially amazed to see Kåñëa Himself there, surrounded by the
personified Veòas, who were offering Him prayers."***

   Because of its great purity, the love the residents of Çré Gokula feel is very glorious. It is said in
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.14.35):


eñäà ghoña-niväsinäm uta bhavän. . .


   "My Lord, sometimes I am puzzled as to how Your Lordship will be able to repay, in gratitude, the
devotional service of these residents of Våndävana. Although I know that You are the supreme
source of all benediction, I am puzzled to know how You will be able to repay all the service that
You are receiving from these residents of Våndävana. I think of how You are so kind, so
magnanimous, that even Pütanä, who came to cheat You by dressing herself as a very affectionate
mother, was awarded liberation and the actual post of a mother. And other demons belonging to
the same family, such as Aghäsura and Bakäsura, were also favored with liberation. Under the
circumstances, I am puzzled. These residents of Våndävana have given You everything: Their
bodies, their minds, their love, their homes. Everything is being utilized for Your purpose. So how
will You be able to repay their debt? You have already given Yourself to Pütanä! I surmise that You
shall ever ever remain a debtor to the residents of Våndävana, bein unable to repay their loving
service.*

  It is seen that even the cows love Lord Kåñëa very deeply. When Lord Kåñëa dove into the
Käliya lake, the cows were overwhelmed. This is described in the following words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.16.11):


gävo våsä vatsataryaù
   krandamänäù su-duùkhitäù
krsne nyastekñaëä bhétä
   rudantya iva tasthire


   "The cows, bulls and female calves, in great distress, called out piteously to Kåñëa. Fixing their

eyes on Him, they stood still in fear, as if ready to cry but too shocked to shed tears."***

   When Lord Kåñëa finally emerged from the Käliya lake, the cows were overjoyed. This is
described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.17.16):


gävo våñä vatsataryo
   lebhire paramäà mudam


   "Lord Balaräma embraced His infallible brother and laughed, knowing well the extent of His
potency. Out of great feelings of love, He lifted Him up on His lap and repeatedly looked at Him.
The cows, bulls and young female calves also achieved the highest pleasure."***

   Even the unmoving living beings, like the trees and plants, became filled with joy. This is
described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.17.15):


kåñëam sametya labdhehä
   äsan çuñkä nagä api


  "Having regained their vital functions, Yaçodä, Rohiëé, Nanda and all the other cowherd women
and men went up to Kåñna. O descendant of Kuru, even the dried-up trees came back to life."***

  Even the plants of Gokula were filled with love for Lord Kåñëa. For this reason the demigod
Brahmä prayed in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.14.34):


tad bhüri-bhägyam iha janma kim apy aöavyäà
   yad gokule 'pi katamäìghri-rajo-'bhiñekam


   "I am most humbly praying at Your lotus feet for You to please give me any sort of birth within
this Våndävana forest so that I may be able to be favored by the dust of the feet of some of the
devotees of Våndävana. Even if I am given the chance to grow just as the humble grass in this land,
that will be a glorious birth for me. But if I am not so fortunate to take birth within the forest of
Våndävana, I beg to be allowed to take birth outside the immediate area of Våndävana so that when
the devotees go out they will walk over me. Even that would be a great fortune for me. I am just
aspiring for a birth in which I will be smeared by the dust of Your devotees' feet. I can see that
everyone here is simply full of Kåñëa consciousness. They do not know anything but Mukunda. All
the Vedas are indeed searching after the lotus feet of Kåñëa.*

   The devotees in Gokula aware of the Lord's sweetness are of two kinds: 1. the followers (anugata)
of the Lord, and 2. the friends and kinsmen (bändhava) of the Lord. Of these two kinds of dear
devotees of the Lord, the Lord's friends and kinsmen are more exalted, for they are more firmly

convinced that {.sy 168}the Lord is mine". Their exalted position is described in these words of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.14.32):


aho bhägyam aho bhägyam. . .


   "How greatly fortunate are Nanda Mahäräja, the cowherd men, and all the other inhabitants of
Vrajabhümi! There is no limit to their good fortune because the Absolute Truth, the source of
transcendental bliss, the eternal Supreme Brahman, has become their friend."*

    It is said that even the least important of the residents of Gokula consider Lord Kåñëa their
friend. In this way their friendship with Lord Kåñëa is glorified.
    The exalted position of Lord Kåñëa's friends (sakhä) is described in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.12.11):


itthaà satäà brahma-sukhänubhütyä
   däsyaà gatänäà para-daivatena
mäyäçritänäà nara-därakena
   säkaà vijahruù kåta-puëya-punjäh


   "In this way, all the cowherd boys used to play with Kåñëa, who is the source of the Brahman
effulgence for j{.sy 241}änés desiring to merge into that effulgence, who is the Supreme Personality
of Godhead for devotees who have accepted eternal servitorship, and who for ordinary persons is
but another ordinary child. The cowherd boys, having accumulated the results of pious activities for
many lives, were able to associate in this way with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. How can
one explain their great fortune?"*

   In this verse the word "satäm" means "the jnanis, before whom the Lord appears as the
impersonal Brahman". The devotees of the Lord are extremely rare. The words {.sy 168}däsyaà
gatänäm" mean "they who have attained service to the Lord." These persons are deascriobed in the
following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (6.14.5):


muktänäm api siddhänäà
   näräyaëa-paräyaëaù
sudurlabhaù praçäntätmä
   kotiñv api mahä-mune


   "O great sage, among many millions who are liberated and perfect in knowledge of liberation,
one may be a devotee of Lord Näräyaëa, or Kåñëa. Such devotees, who are fully peaceful, are
extremely rare."*

    Thus the devotees who worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead are extremely rare. In
Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.12.11 the word "mayasritanam" means "persons who have neither knowledge
of, devotion to, nor friendship for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and who thus do nto
understand Lord Kåñëa's spiritual form, do not understand that He is the Supreme Personality of
Godhead, and do not love Him, and who are thus not qualified to directly see the Supreme
Personality of Godhead standing before them. These persons think Lord Kåñëa is an ordinary
human boy. Lord Kåñëa describes these persons in the following words of Bhagavad-gétä (9.11):


avajänanti mäà müòhä
   mänuñéà tanum äsritam


   "Fools deride Me when I descend in the human form. They do nto know My transcendental
nature and My supreme dominion over all that be."*

  Lord Kåñëa alsop says in Bhagavad-gétä (7.25):


nähaà prakäçaù sarvasya
  yogamäyä-samävåtaù


   "I am never manifest to the foolish and unintelligent. For them I am covered by My creative
potency (yogamäyä), and so the deluded world knows Me not, who am unborn and infallible."*

    In these three quotes it is seen that the Supreme Lord very rarely makes Himself visible in this
world. Still, even though He very rarely appears in this worled, He personally enjoys pastimes
(vijahruù) with His dear friends who are filled with love for Him. This truth fills Çréla Çukadeva
Gosvämé with wonder. Or, these words may also be interpreted to mean: "He very mercifully
appears before even the ordinary persons who have taken shelter of mäy.ä (mayasritanam) and
before them He manifests His all-glorious spiritual form which seems to be the form of a human
being, and which is very rarely visible in this world." Still, ordinary persons cannot become the
friend or kinsman of the Lord in His rare, more rare, or most rare spiritual forms. With these
friends the Supreme Lord enjoys pastimes (vijahruù). Here the word "kåta-puëya-puïjäù" means
"they are the best among persons weho have performed many pious deeds to please the Supreme
Personality of Godhead. Thweir friendship with the lord is not like the fiendship of ordinary
persons. Their friendship for the Lord is glorious. How can the good fortune of these loving friends
of the Lord be described? Even the ordinary people of Vraja have great good fortune. Even the
persons who have only seen Lord Kåñëa have great good fortune. The good fortune they have
attained is attainable by the great sages. This truth is described in the following words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.12.12):


yat-päda-päàsur bahu janma-kåcchrataù. . .

   "Yogés may undergo severe austerities and penances for many births by practicing yama, niyama,
äsana and präëäyäma, none of which are easily performed. Yet in due course of time, when these
yogés attain the perfection of controlling the mind, they will still be unable to taste even a particle
of dust from the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. What then can we describe
about the great fortune of the inhabitants of Vrajabhümi, Våndävana, with whom the Supreme
Personality of Godhead personally lived and who saw the Lord face to face?"*

   These words affirm the truth that the friends of Lord Kåñëa were very fortunate. This truth was
also confirmed by Akrüra in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.38.15):

athävarüòhaù. . .
 . . .namasya äbhyäà ca sakhén vanaukasaù

    "Then I will at once alight from my chariot and bow down to the lotus feet of Kåñëa and
Balaräma, the Supreme Personalities of Godhead. Theirs are the same feet that great mystic yogés
striving for self-realization bear within their minds. I will also offer my obeisances to the Lords'
cowherd boyfriends and to all the other residents of Våndävana."***

  When Lord Brahmä kidnappeed Lord Kåñëa's friends and calves, Lord Kåñëa created new friends
and calves. Brahmä then returned the original friends and calves. Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.12.11
quoted in this anuccheda was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Debido a que eran conscientes de la dulzura del Señor Supremo, el pueblo de los pastores de vacas se convirtió en el
los filósofos más sabios (parama-jani). El semidiós Brahma, que había visto personalmente innumerables cuatro-
formas armadas del Señor, específicamente se refugiaron en la forma del Señor Krishna. Brahma dijo en
Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.14.1):
naumidya te 'bhra-vapuse tadid-ambaraya
gujavatamsa-paripiccha-lasan-mukhaya vanya-sraje kavala-vetra-visana-venu-
laksma-sriye mrdu-pade pasupangajaya
"Mi querido Señor, Tú eres el único Señor Supremo digno de adoración, Personalidad de Dios. Por lo tanto, yo
Te ofrezco mis humildes reverencias y oraciones solo para complacerte. Tus rasgos corporales son de la
color de nubes llenas de agua. Estás brillando con un aura eléctrica plateada que emana de
Tus prendas amarillas.
"Permítanme ofrecer mis respetuosas y reiteradas reverencias al hijo del Maharaja Nanda que está de pie
Ante mí con una caracola, pendientes y una pluma de pavo real en la cabeza. Su rostro es hermoso. Él
lleva un casco, adornado con flores del bosque, y está de pie con un bocado de comida en su mano.
mano. Está adornado con bastón y corneta, y lleva un cuerno de búfalo y una flauta. Está de pie.
Ante mí, con pequeños pies de loto."
El amor espiritual que el pueblo de los pastores siente por el Señor Krishna es la joya suprema de todo tipo.
amor. Cuando aparecen repentinamente cosas opuestas, ese amor no vacila. Al contrario, ese amor
eclipsa toda oposición. Cuando surgen obstáculos, ese amor aumenta. De esta manera, el amor espiritual es
como el amor que los hedonistas sienten por los objetos de los sentidos materiales. Ese amor que los hedonistas sienten por
objetos de los sentidos materiales, amor que las escrituras y la percepción directa declaran estar llenos
de defectos, es de hecho muy apasionado y fuerte. En ese sentido, el amor espiritual es similar a eso.
amor material. Esto se ve en la siguiente oración pronunciada por Prahlada Maharaja al Señor Nrsimha en
Visnu Purana (1.20.19):
ya pritir avivekanam
visayesv anapayini tvam anusmaratah sa me
hrdayan napasrpatu
"Los tontos se enamoran de los objetos materiales de los sentidos. Como siempre aman los objetos de los sentidos, ¿puedo yo...
Siempre te amaré. Siempre meditaré en ti. Ruego que nunca abandones mi corazón.
La intensidad del amor espiritual también se ve en estas palabras pronunciadas por Nanda y Yasoda a
El Señor Balarama en el Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.65.3):
ciram nah pahi dasarha
sanujo jagad-isvarah ity aropyankam alingya
netraih sisicatur jalaih
"Oh descendiente de Dasarha, oh Señor del universo, que Tú y tu hermano menor Krsna
«Protégenos siempre». Diciendo esto, alzaron a Sri Balarama sobre sus regazos, lo abrazaron y
Lo humedecieron con las lágrimas de sus ojos.
Aunque estaba muy claro que el Señor Balarama era hijo de Vasudeva, un kshatriya, y el
Nanda y Yasoda seguían pensando en la Suprema Personalidad de Dios misma como su propio hijo.
Esto se observa en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.65.1-2):
Balabhadrah Kusu-Srestha
bhagavan ratham asthitah suhrd-didrksur utkanthah
prayayau nanda-gokulam
"Oh, el mejor de los Kurus, una vez Señor Balarama, deseoso de visitar a sus amigos que le deseaban lo mejor, montó
En su carroza viajó a Nanda Gokula.
cirotkanthair de parisvaktas
gopair gopibhir eva ca ramo 'bhivadya pitarav
asirbhir abhinanditah
"Tras haber sufrido durante mucho tiempo la angustia de la separación, los pastores y sus esposas se abrazaron
Señor Balarama. El Señor ofreció entonces respetos a sus padres, y ellos lo saludaron con alegría.
rezo."
Cuando el amor espiritual (priti) se vuelve muy prominente, eclipsa todo lo demás. Esto ocurre
incluso entre los devotos que se sienten naturalmente atraídos por el Señor en Su aspecto de poder y
opulencia. Un ejemplo de esto se ve en la siguiente descripción de Sri Devahuti en Srimad-
Bhagavatam (3.33.21):
vanam pravrajite patyav
apatya-virahatura jata-tattvapy abhun naste
vatse gaur iva vatsala
"El marido de Devahuti ya había abandonado su hogar y aceptado la orden de vida de renuncia, y entonces
Su único hijo, Kapila, se fue de casa. Aunque ella conocía todas las verdades de la vida y la muerte, y aunque
Su corazón quedó limpio de toda suciedad, estaba muy afligida por la pérdida de su hijo, como una vaca.
se ve afectada cuando muere su ternero."
Una situación similar, donde el amor espiritual supera la conciencia del poder del Señor y
La opulencia se aprecia en estas palabras pronunciadas por Sri Devaki-devi en el Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.3.29):
samuvije bhavad-dhetoh
kamsad aham adhira-dhih
"Oh Madhusudana, debido a Tu aparición, me siento cada vez más ansioso por el temor a
Kamsa."
El mismo sentimiento se observa en estas palabras que describen al Maharaja Yudhisthira en el srimad-
Bhagavatam (1.10.32):
ajata-satruh prtanam
gopithaya madhu-dvisah parebhyah sankitah snehat
prayunkta catur-anginim
"El Maharajá Yudhisthira, aunque no era enemigo de nadie, empleó cuatro divisiones de defensa [caballos,
elefante, carro y ejército] para acompañar al Señor Krishna, el enemigo de los asuras [demonios]. El
El Maharajá hizo esto a causa del enemigo, y también por afecto al Señor."
Este mismo sentimiento de amor espiritual eclipsa la conciencia del poder y la opulencia del Señor.
Esto se ve nuevamente en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (1.10.33):
atha duragatan saurih
kauravan virahaturan sannivartya drdham snigdhan
prayat sva-nagarim priyaih
"Por profundo afecto al Señor Krishna, los Pandavas, que pertenecían a la dinastía Kuru,
Lo acompañaron una distancia considerable para despedirlo. Estaban abrumados por la idea de
futura separación. Sin embargo, el Señor los persuadió a regresar a casa y procedió hacia
Dvaraka con sus queridos compañeros."
Cómo el amor espiritual superó incluso la conciencia del Señor Balarama sobre el poder del Señor Krishna y
La opulencia se aprecia en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.53.20-21):
srutvaitad bhagavan ramo
vipaksiya-nrpodyamam krsnam caikam gatam hartum
kanyam kalaha-sankitah
balena mahata sardham
bhratr-sneha-pariplutah tvaritah kundinam pragad
gajasva - ratha-pattibhih
"Cuando el Señor Balarama se enteró de estos preparativos de los reyes enemigos y de cómo el Señor Krishna
Se había marchado solo para robar a la novia. Temía que se produjera una pelea. Inmerso en afecto.
Por su hermano, se apresuró a llegar a Kundina con un poderoso ejército compuesto de infantería y soldados.
montando en elefantes, caballos y carros."
Aquí la palabra "bhagavan" significa "el que todo lo sabe". Otro ejemplo de devotos abrumados.
El amor por el Señor Krishna se ve reflejado en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.11.49):
krsnam maha-baka-grastam
drstva ramadayo 'rbhakah. . .
"Cuando Balarama y los otros muchachos vieron que Krishna había sido devorado por el pato gigantesco,
Se volvieron casi inconscientes, como sentidos sin vida."
La dicha que alcanzan los pastores al percibir la dulzura del Señor Krishna supera con creces la
La dicha que proviene de percibir a Brahman o de percibir la opulencia y el poder del Supremo.
Personalidad de Dios. Al ver la buena fortuna alcanzada por el pueblo de los pastores, Srila Sukadeva
Gosvami se llenó de asombro. Dijo en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.12.11):
ittham satam brahma-sukhanubhutya. . .
"De esta manera, todos los pastores solían jugar con Krishna, quien es la fuente del Brahman
resplandor para los janis que desean fusionarse en ese resplandor, quien es la Suprema Personalidad de
Divinidad para los devotos que han aceptado el servicio eterno, y que para las personas comunes es solo
otro niño común. Los muchachos pastores, habiendo acumulado los resultados de actividades piadosas para
muchas vidas pudieron asociarse de esta manera con la Suprema Personalidad de Dios. ¿Cómo es posible?
¿Alguien puede explicar su gran fortuna?
También dijo en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.9.20):
nemam virico na bhavah. . .
"Ni el Señor Brahma ni el Señor Shiva, ni siquiera la diosa de la fortuna, que siempre es la mejor
la mitad del Señor Supremo, puede obtener de la Suprema Personalidad de Dios, el libertador de
este mundo material, tal misericordia como la que recibió la Madre Yasoda."
También dijo en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.9.21):
nayam sukhapah. . .
"La Suprema Personalidad de Dios, Krishna, el hijo de la madre Yasoda, es accesible a
devotos comprometidos en servicio amoroso espontáneo, pero Él no es tan fácilmente accesible a los devotos mentales
especuladores, a aquellos que se esfuerzan por la autorrealización mediante severas austeridades y penitencias, o a
aquellos que consideran que el cuerpo es lo mismo que el yo."
También dijo en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.47.60):
nayam sriyo 'nga. . .
"Cuando el Señor Sri Krishna estaba bailando con las gopis en el rasa-lila, las gopis fueron abrazadas por
los brazos del Señor. Este favor trascendental nunca fue otorgado a la diosa de la fortuna o
otros consortes en el mundo espiritual. De hecho, jamás se imaginó algo así por parte de los más
Hermosas muchachas en los planetas celestiales, cuyo brillo corporal y aroma se asemejan a la flor de loto.
¿Y qué decir de las mujeres mundanas que son muy bellas según los estándares materiales?
A veces, la manifestación de la opulencia del Señor aumenta la percepción de su dulzura.
Esto ocurre cuando el devoto tiene la idea "¿Cómo puede esto por nuestro hijo (u otro pariente) en este
¿Una situación maravillosa? Un ejemplo de tal situación se ve en estas palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam.
(10.28.18):
nandadayas tu tam drstva
paramananda-nivrtah krsnam ca tatra ccandobhih
stuyamanam su-vismitah
"Nanda Maharaja y los demás pastores sintieron la mayor felicidad cuando vieron que
morada trascendental. Se asombraron especialmente al ver allí al mismo Krishna, rodeado de la
personificaba los Vedas, que le ofrecían oraciones."
Debido a su gran pureza, el amor que sienten los residentes de Sri Gokula es muy glorioso.
Se dice en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.14.35):
esam ghosa-nivasinam uta bhavan. . .
"Mi Señor, a veces me desconcierta cómo Su Señoría podrá recompensar, en gratitud,
el servicio devocional de estos residentes de Vrindavana. Aunque sé que Tú eres el supremo
fuente de toda bendición, me desconcierta saber cómo podrás devolver todo el servicio que
Estás recibiendo de estos residentes de Vrindavana. Pienso en lo amable que eres, así que
magnánimo, que incluso Putana, que vino a engañarte vistiéndose como una muy cariñosa
madre, fue premiada con la liberación y el puesto real de madre. Y otros demonios pertenecientes a la
La misma familia, como Aghasura y Bakasura, también fueron favorecidas con la liberación. Bajo el
circunstancias, estoy perplejo. Estos residentes de Vrndavana te han dado todo: sus cuerpos,
sus mentes, su amor, sus hogares. Todo está siendo utilizado para Tu propósito. Entonces, ¿cómo será?
¿Podrás pagar su deuda? ¡Ya te has entregado a Putana! Supongo que tú
permanecerá siempre en deuda con los residentes de Vrindavana, al no poder devolverles su amor.
servicio.
Se ve que incluso las vacas aman profundamente al Señor Krishna. Cuando el Señor Krishna se sumergió en el
En el lago Kaliya, las vacas fueron abrumadas. Esto se describe en las siguientes palabras de Srimad:
Bhagavatam (10.16.11):
gavo vrsa vatsataryah
krandamanah su-duhkhitah krsne nyasteksana bhita
rudantya iva tasthire
"Las vacas, los toros y las terneras, muy angustiadas, clamaban lastimeramente a Krishna. Arreglando
Con la mirada fija en Él, se quedaron inmóviles por el miedo, como si estuvieran a punto de llorar pero demasiado conmocionados para derramar lágrimas.
Cuando el Señor Krishna finalmente emergió del lago Kaliya, las vacas se llenaron de alegría. Esto es
descrito en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.17.16):
gavo vrsa vatsataryo
lebhire paramam mudam
"El Señor Balarama abrazó a su infalible hermano y rió, conociendo bien el alcance de su
potencia. Por grandes sentimientos de amor, lo levantó y lo sentó en su regazo y lo miró repetidamente.
Las vacas, los toros y las terneras jóvenes también alcanzaron el máximo placer."
Incluso los seres vivos inmóviles, como los árboles y las plantas, se llenaron de alegría. Esto es
descrito en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.17.15):
krsnam sametya labdheha
asan suska naga api
"Habiendo recuperado sus funciones vitales, Yasoda, Rohini, Nanda y todas las demás mujeres pastoras de vacas
Y los hombres subieron hasta Krishna. ¡Oh descendiente de Kuru, incluso los árboles secos volvieron a la vida!
Incluso las plantas de Gokula estaban llenas de amor por el Señor Krishna. Por esta razón, el semidiós
Brahma oró en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.14.34):
tad bhuri-bhagyam iha janma kim apy atavyam
yad gokule 'pi katamanghri-rajo-'bhisekam
"Humildemente te ruego a tus pies de loto que me concedas cualquier tipo de nacimiento.
dentro de este bosque de Vrndavana para que pueda ser favorecido por el polvo de los pies de algunos
de los devotos de Vrindavana. Incluso si se me da la oportunidad de crecer como la humilde hierba en
Esta tierra será un nacimiento glorioso para mí. Pero si no tengo la fortuna de nacer
dentro del bosque de Vrndavana, ruego que se me permita nacer fuera del área inmediata de
Vrindavana para que cuando los devotos salgan caminen sobre mí. Incluso eso sería genial.
fortuna para mí. Solo aspiro a un nacimiento en el que seré manchado por el polvo de Tu
pies de devotos. Puedo ver que todos aquí están simplemente llenos de conciencia de Krishna. No
No conocen nada más que a Mukunda. Todos los Vedas, en efecto, buscan los pies de loto de Krishna.
Los devotos en Gokula conscientes de la dulzura del Señor son de dos tipos: 1. los seguidores
(anugata) del Señor, y 2. los amigos y parientes (bandhava) del Señor. De estos dos tipos
de los queridos devotos del Señor, los amigos y parientes del Señor son más exaltados, porque son más
firmemente convencido de que el Señor es mío". Su elevada posición se describe en estas palabras de
Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.14.32):
aho bhagyam aho bhagyam. . .
"Qué afortunados son Nanda Maharaja, los pastores de vacas y todos los demás habitantes de
¡Vrajabhumi! No hay límite para su buena fortuna porque la Verdad Absoluta, la fuente de
La dicha trascendental, el eterno Brahman Supremo, se ha convertido en su amigo."
Se dice que incluso los residentes menos importantes de Gokula consideran al Señor Krishna su
amigo. De esta manera se glorifica su amistad con el Señor Krishna.
La posición exaltada de los amigos del Señor Krishna (sakha) se describe en estas palabras del srimad-
Bhagavatam (10.12.11):
ittham satam brahma-sukhanubhutya
dasyam gatanam para-daivatena mayasritanam nara-darakena
sakam vijahruh krta-punya-punjah
"De esta manera, todos los pastores solían jugar con Krishna, quien es la fuente del Brahman
resplandor para los janis que desean fusionarse en ese resplandor, quien es la Suprema Personalidad de
Divinidad para los devotos que han aceptado el servicio eterno, y que para las personas comunes es solo
otro niño común. Los muchachos pastores, habiendo acumulado los resultados de actividades piadosas para
muchas vidas pudieron asociarse de esta manera con la Suprema Personalidad de Dios. ¿Cómo es posible?
¿Alguien puede explicar su gran fortuna?
En este versículo la palabra "satam" significa "los jnanis, ante quienes el Señor aparece como el
Brahman impersonal". Los devotos del Señor son extremadamente raros. Las palabras dasyam gatanam" significan
"aquellos que han alcanzado el servicio al Señor". Estas personas se describen en lo siguiente:
Palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (6.14.5):
muktanam api siddhanam
narayana-parayanah sudurlabhah prasantatma
kotisv api maha-mune
"Oh gran sabio, entre muchos millones que son liberados y perfectos en el conocimiento de la liberación,
Uno puede ser devoto del Señor Narayana o Krishna. Tales devotos, que son completamente pacíficos, son
extremadamente raro."
Por lo tanto, los devotos que adoran a la Suprema Personalidad de Dios son extremadamente raros.
srimad-Bhagavatam 10.12.11 la palabra "mayasritanam" significa "personas que no tienen conocimiento de,
devoción a, ni amistad por la Suprema Personalidad de Dios, y quienes así no entienden
La forma espiritual del Señor Krishna, no entiende que Él es la Suprema Personalidad de Dios, y
no lo aman, y por lo tanto no están capacitados para ver directamente a la Suprema Personalidad de Dios.
de pie frente a ellos. Estas personas piensan que el Señor Krishna es un niño humano común y corriente. Señor Krishna
Describe a estas personas con las siguientes palabras del Bhagavad-gita (9.11):
avajananti mam mudha
manusim tanum asritam
"Los necios se burlan de mí cuando desciendo en forma humana. No conocen mi naturaleza trascendental.
y mi dominio supremo sobre todo lo que existe."
El Señor Krishna también dice en el Bhagavad-gita (7.25):
naham prakasah sarvasya
yogamaya-samavrtah
"Nunca me manifiesto a los necios e ignorantes. Para ellos estoy cubierto por mi creación.
potencia (yogamaya), y así el mundo engañado no me conoce, a mí que soy innato e infalible."
En estas tres citas se ve que el Señor Supremo muy rara vez se hace visible en
este mundo. Aun así, aunque rara vez aparece en este mundo, disfruta personalmente
pasatiempos (vijahruh) con Sus queridos amigos que están llenos de amor por Él. Esta verdad llena
Srila Sukadeva Gosvami con asombro. O bien, estas palabras también pueden interpretarse como: "Él muy
aparece misericordiosamente incluso ante las personas comunes que se han refugiado en maya (mayasritanam).
y ante ellos Él manifiesta su gloriosa forma espiritual que parece ser la forma de un
ser humano, y que rara vez es visible en este mundo." Aun así, las personas comunes no pueden
Conviértete en amigo o pariente del Señor en Sus formas espirituales raras, más raras o sumamente raras.
Con estos amigos el Señor Supremo disfruta de pasatiempos (vijahruh). Aquí la palabra "krta-punya-pujah"
significa "son los mejores entre las personas que han realizado muchas obras piadosas para complacer al Supremo".
Personalidad de Dios. Su amistad con el Señor no es como la amistad de los demás.
personas. Su amistad por el Señor es gloriosa. ¿Cómo puede la buena fortuna de estos amorosos?
¿Cómo describir a los amigos del Señor? Incluso la gente común de Vraja tiene una gran fortuna. Incluso
Las personas que solo han visto al Señor Krishna tienen gran buena fortuna. La buena fortuna que tienen
alcanzado es alcanzable por los grandes sabios. Esta verdad se describe en las siguientes palabras de
Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.12.12):
yat-pada-pamsur bahu janma-krcchratah. . .
"Los yoguis pueden someterse a severas austeridades y penitencias durante muchos nacimientos practicando yama,
niyama, asana y pranayama, ninguno de los cuales se realiza fácilmente. Sin embargo, con el tiempo, cuando
Estos yoguis alcanzan la perfección del control de la mente, pero aún así no podrán saborear ni siquiera
una partícula de polvo de los pies de loto de la Suprema Personalidad de Dios. ¿Qué podemos entonces hacer?
describe la gran fortuna de los habitantes de Vrajabhumi, Vrndavana, con quienes el
¿Quién vivió personalmente a la Suprema Personalidad de Dios y vio al Señor cara a cara?
Estas palabras afirman la verdad de que los amigos del Señor Krishna fueron muy afortunados. Esta verdad
Akrura también lo confirmó en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.38.15):
athavarudhah. . . . . .namasya abhyam ca sakhin vanaukasah
"Entonces descenderé inmediatamente de mi carro y me postraré ante los pies de loto de Krishna y
Balarama, las Personalidades Supremas de Dios. Sus pies son los mismos que los de los grandes yoguis místicos.
el esfuerzo por la autorrealización está presente en sus mentes. También ofreceré mis reverencias a la
a los novios pastores de vacas de Lords y a todos los demás residentes de Vrndavana."
Cuando el Señor Brahma secuestró a los amigos y terneros del Señor Krishna, el Señor Krishna creó nuevos amigos.
y los terneros. Entonces Brahma devolvió a los amigos originales y a los terneros. Srimad-Bhagavatam 10.12.11
Lo citado en este anuccheda fue pronunciado por srila sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
Lord Kåñëa parents are even more fortunate than His friends. They are described in these words
of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.8.51):


tato bhaktir bhagavati
   putré-bhüte janärdane
dam-patyor nitaräm äséd
   gopa-gopéñu bhärata


   "Thereafter, O Mahäräja Parékñit, best of the Bharatas, when the Supreme Personality of
Godhead became the son of Nanda Mahäräja and Yaçodä, they maintained continuous, unswerving
devotional love in parental affection. And in their association, all the other inhabitants of
Våndävana, the gopas and gopés, developed the culture of Kåñëa-bhakti."*

  In this verse the word "bhaktiù" means {.sy 168}love", nitaräm" means "up to the levels of sneha
and räga", "gopäù" means "all the gopas", and {.sy 168}gopyaù" means "the gopés who were not Lord
Kåñëa's beloveds". This statement will be explained later in this book.

   Ofg all thes edevotees, the gopés of Vraja, who have the most glorious prema, praëaya, mäna, and
räga love for the Lord, and who have the great good fortune of having anuräga and maha-bhava
love for the Lord, and whose pure love brings Lord Kåñëa under their control, are very glorious and
fortunate. Their glory and good fortune have no equal or better. The gopés are thus very exalted.
Even Uddhava asked permission from them. This is seen in the following words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.47.64):


atha gopér anujïäpya
   yaçodäà nandam eva ca
gopän ämantrya däçärho
   yäsyann äruruhe ratham


  "Uddhava, the descendent of Daçärha, then took permission from the gopés and from Mother
Yaçodä and Nanda Mahäräja. He bade farewell to all the cowherd men and, about to depart,
mounted his chariot."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Los padres del Señor Krishna son incluso más afortunados que sus amigos. Se les describe en estos
Palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.8.51):
tato bhaktir bhagavati
putri-bhute janardane presa-patyor nitaram asid
gopa-gopisu bharata
"Después, oh Maharaja Pariksit, el mejor de los Bharatas, cuando la Suprema Personalidad de
La divinidad se convirtió en hijo de Nanda Maharaja y Yasoda, y mantuvieron una relación continua e inquebrantable.
amor devocional en el afecto paternal. Y en su asociación, todos los demás habitantes de
En Vrindavana, los gopas y las gopis desarrollaron la cultura de Krsna-bhakti."
En este verso la palabra "bhaktih" significa amor, "nitaram" significa "hasta los niveles de sneha y
raga", "gopah" significa "todos los gopas", y "gopyah" significa "las gopis que no eran del Señor Krishna"
"Amados". Esta afirmación se explicará más adelante en este libro.
De todos estos devotos, las gopis de Vraja, que tienen el prema, pranaya, mana y más gloriosos
amor raga por el Señor, y que tienen la gran fortuna de tener amor anuraga y maha-bhava.
para el Señor, y cuyo amor puro pone al Señor Krishna bajo su control, son muy gloriosos y
Afortunadas. Su gloria y buena fortuna no tienen igual ni mejor. Por lo tanto, las gopis son muy exaltadas.
Incluso Uddhava les pidió permiso. Esto se ve en las siguientes palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam.
(10.47.64):
atha gopir anujapya
yasodam nandam eva ca gopan amantrya dasarho
Yasyann Aruruhe Ratham
"Uddhava, descendiente de Dasarha, entonces pidió permiso a las gopis y a la Madre Yasoda.
y Nanda Maharaja. Se despidió de todos los pastores y, a punto de partir, montó su
carruaje."
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
The gopés are the most exalted of all the residents of Gokula. This truth is seen in the following
words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.87.57-58):


dåñövaivam-ädi gopénäà
   kåñëäveçätma-viklavam
uddhavaù parama-prétas
   tä namasyann idaà jagau


  "Thus seeing how the gopés were always disturbed because of their total absorption in Kåñëa,
Uddhava was supremely pleased. Desiring to offer themn all respect, he sang as follows.***


etäù paraà tanu-bhåto bhuvi gopa-vadhvo
   govinda eva nikhilätmani rüòha-bhäväù
väïchanti yad bhava-bhiyo munayo vayaà ca
   kià brahma-janmabhir ananta-kathä-rasasya


  "Among all persons on earth, these cowherd women alone have actually perfected their
embodied lives, for they have achieved the perfection of unalloyed love for Lord Govinda. Their

pure love is hankered after by those who fear material existence, by great sages, and by ourselves as
well. For one who has tasted the narrations of the infinite Lord, what is the use of taking birth as a
high-class brähmaëa, or even as Lord Barhmä himself?"***

    In the second of these towo verses the word "param" means "only", "etas tanu-bhrtah" means {.sy
168}whose birth in this world has borne its fruit", {.sy 168}akhilatmani" means "in the Supreme
Personality of Godhead who, although rarely seen in this world, is present as the Supersoul in all
living beings", "govinde" means {.sy 168}the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is directly
manifest in this world as the prince of Gokula", "evam" means {.sy 168}with sweetness like this", and
"rüòha-bhäväù" means "whose ecstatic mahä-bhäva love is manifest". The words "väïchanti yad
bhava-bhiyo munayaù" mean {.sy 168}If somehow the description of the sweetness of ecstatic love
reaching up to the level of mahä-bhäva enters their ears, then the sages who ordinary yearn for
liberation will renounce that desire and, understanding its glories, will yearn to attain ecstatic
love." The word "vayam" means "even great devotees like myself yearn to attain that love. That
means we have not yet attained it. We are not qualifiedto feel that very sweet ecstatic love." That is
the meaning. Then the speaker of this verse criticizes persons who do not yeran to attain that
ecstatic love. He says: "kià brahma-janmabhir ananta-kathä-rasasya", which means "What is the use
of taking birth as the demigod Brahmä numberless times if we cannto taste the nectar of the
hearing the topics of Lord Kåñëa, whose pastimes have no end?" This rhetorical question implies the
answer:"there is no use in taking birth as such a Lord Brahmä."


Anucchedas 103 and 104


   Here someone may protest: "Is it not true that the sages who yearn after liberation and who have
already attained liberation are glorified in all the scriptures? How can the devotees be superior to
them? Why would the sages desire anything but liberation?" To answer this protest, Uddhava speaks
these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.59):


kvemäù striyo vana-carér vyabhicära-duñöäù
  kåñëe kva caiña paramätmani rüòha-bhäväù
nanv éçvaro 'nubhajato 'viduño 'pi säkñäc
  chreyas tanoty agada-räja ivopayuktaù


   "How amazing it is that these simple women who wander about the forest, seemingly spoiled by
improper behavior, have achieved the perfection of unalloyed love for Kåñëa, teh Superme Soul!
Still, it is true that the Supreme Lord Himself awards His blessings even to an ignorant worshiper,
just as the best medicine works even when taken by a person ignorant of its ingredients."***

   In these verses, from beginning to end, Çrémän Uddhava's great devotion to the Lord is clearly
seen. Here someone may protest that the gopés' relationship with Lord Kåñëa was adulterous and
therefore immoral. This protest is answered by these words spoken at the conclusion of the

description of the räsa dance (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.33.35):


gopénäà tat-paténäà ca
   sarveñäm eva dehinäm
yo 'ntaç carati so 'dhyakñaù
   kréòaneneha deha-bhäk


    "He who lives as the overseeing witness within the gopés and their husbands, and indeed within
all embodied living beings, assumes forms in this world to enjoy transcendental pastimes."***

   The idea of wicked-hearted men that the gopés acted immorally in their relationship with Lord
Kåñëa is refuted by this verse, by the word "paramätmani" (the Supreme Personality of Godhead) in
Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.59, and also by these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.61):


ärya-pathaà ca hitvä. . .


    "The gopés of Våndävana have given up the association of their husbands, sons, and other family
members, who are very difficult to give up, andf they have forsaken the path of chastity to take
shelter of tyhe lotus feet of Mukunda, Kåñëa, which one should search for by Vedic knowledge. Oh,
let me be fortunate enough to be one of the bushes, creepers, or herbs in Våndävana, because the
gopés trample them and bless them with the dust of their feet."*

   Now is not the right time to refute the mistaken idea that the gopés acted immorally. Later in
this book we will proove that the gopés acted rightly. In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.58 and 59 the
words "kvemäù striyo vana-caréù" mean "what is the status of the women who enjoyed pastimes in
Våndävana forest and took shelter of Lord Kåñëa?" In these verse the words "kva vyabhicära-duñöäù
bhava-bhiyo vayam" mean {.sy 168}and what is the status of us, sages who have not attained exalted
spiritual love and who are not attached to Lord Kåñëa, are afraid of material existence?" The
meaning here is: {.sy 168}The difference bewteen us and the gopés is very great." Here the question
may be asked: "Why does such a great difference exist?" The answer is given here in the words {.sy
168}eña paramätmani rüòha-bhäväù", which mean "In the gopés is seen great ecstatic love (mahä-
bhäva) for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is worshiped by everyone and who is the
abode of all desires. That same ecstatic love is not seen n us." If this is so, then the following
question may be asked: If you do not directly see Lord Kåñëa's glorious qualities, qualities that made
the gopés fall in love with Him, then how will you attain that ecstatic love even if you yearn to
attain it? This quesyion is answered in this verse in the passage beginning with the word "nanu"
(the Supreme Lord Himself awards His blessings even to an ignorant worshiper, just as the best
medicine works even when taken by a person ignorant of its ingredients.) Here the word "aviduñaù"
means {.sy 168}the Lord Hismelf makes this love spontaneously manifest within me." That is the
example given here. Uddhava declares in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.27):

viraheëa mahä-bhäga
   mahän me 'nugrahah kåtaù


   "You have rightfully claimed the privilege of unalloyed love for the transcendental Lord, O most
glorious gopés. Indeed, by exhibiting your love for Kåñëa in separation from Him, you have shown
me great mercy7"***

   Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.59 may also be interpreted in a different way, in a way that sternly
rebukes ladies who, although very faithful to their husbands, are averse to the rasas of devotional
service. In the first interpretation of this verse the words "kvemah striah" referred to the gopés, who
enjoy pastimes in Våndävana forest. The second interpretation of this verse is based on the
asumption that an "a" was originally present before the word "vana-carih" and then elided by
sandhi. Thus the word was originally "avana-carih", which would mean "women who are not like
the gopés". Such materialistic women are described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (5.18.19):


striyo vratais tvä. . .



   "My dear Lord, You are certainly the fully independent master of all the senses. Therefore all
women who worship You by strictly observing vows because they wish to acquire a husband to
satisfy their senses are surely under illusion. They do not know that such a husband cannot actually
give protection to them or their children. Nor can he protect their wealth or duration of life, for he
himself is dependent on time, fruitive results and the modes of nature, which are all subordinate to
You."*

   These words were spoken by Çrématé Lakñmé--devé in the midst of Çrémad-Bhägavatam's
description of Kutmäla-varña. In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.59 the words "imäù striyo vyabhicära-
duñöäù kåñëe kva paramätmani" may then be interpreted to mean "What is the status of women who
are averse to Kåñëa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead?" The meaning then would be: "There is a
great difference between such women and the gopés." Then the word {.sy 168}rüòha-bhäväù" may be
interpreted to mean: "Not even the smallest fragment of the exalted spiritual love that is the crest
jewel of all goals of life is not seen in such women". That exalted spiritual love is present only in the
devotees, who are filled with love for the Lord. Only the devotees love the Lord. This is confirmed
by the passage beginning with the word "nanu" (Still, it is true that the Supreme Lord Himself
awards His blessings even to an ignorant worshiper, just as the best medicine works even when
taken by a person ignorant of its ingredients.) What moremay bhe said? The next verse of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.47.60) declares:


näyaà çriyo 'ìga u nitänta-rateù prasädaù
  svär-yoñitäà nalina-gandha-rucaà kuto 'nyäù

räsotasave 'sya bhuja-daëòa-gåhiöa-kaëöha-
   labdhäçiñaà ya udagäd vraja-sundaréëäm


   "When Lord Çré Kåñëa was danciong with the gopés in the räsa-lélä, the gopés were embraced by
the arms of the Lord. This transcendental favor was never bestowed upon the goddess of fortune or
other consorts in the spiritual world. Indeed, never was such a thing even imagined by the most
beautiful girls in the heavenly planets, whose bodily luster and aroma resemble the lotus flower.
Ansd what to speak of worldly women who are very beautiful according to material estimation?"*

   In this verse the word "aìge" means "on the graceful form of the master of Vaikuntha", "çriyaù"
means "of the Lord's dearmost beloved", "nitänta-rateù" means "of the love a girl feels for hewr
beloved", "prasädaù" means "happiness, and {.sy 168}näyam" means "is not". The verse then
continued: "svär-yoñitäà nalina-gandha-rucaà", which means: "If even the goddess of fortune
cannot attain that happiness, then the women of Svarghaloka, whose limbs are like golden lotus
flowers, and who do not even reside in Vaikuntha certainly cannot attain it." Then the words "kuto
'nyäù" mean "Other woemen, who are far away from them certainly cannot attain it." That is the
meaning. Then one may ask: Are there any women who care not bereft of this happiness? The
answer is given in this verse in the passage beginning with the word "räsa" (When Lord Çré Kåñëa
was danciong with the gopés in the räsa-lélä, the gopés were embraced by the arms of the Lord.)
Here the word "asya" means {.sy 168}of the form of Lord Kåñëa, the prine of Vraja". That Goddess
Laksmi yearns to attain the touch of Lord Kåñëa is also confirmed by these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.16.36):


yad-väïchayä çrér lalanäcarat tapaù. . .


   "O Lord, we do not know how the serpent Käliya has attained this great opportunity of being
touched by the dust of Your lotus feet. For this end, the goddess of fortune performed austerities for
centuries, giving up all other desires and taking austere vows."***

   Goddess Lakñmé did not only yearn to attain the love the gopés felt in separation from Lord
Kåñëa, she also yearned to attain the love they felt when they directlyenjoyed pastimes with Him.
What persons like myself say to describe that love? In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.60 the words
"räsotasave 'sya bhuja-daëòa-gåhiöa-kaëöha-labdhäçiñaà ya udagäd" mean "When, in the räsa dance,
Lord Kåñëa embraced the gopés' necks, the gopés felt all their desires were fulfilled". This means the
desire the gopés had long kept hidden in their hearts was now openly attained. That Goddess
Laksmi yearned to attain the gopés' good fortune is also confirmed by theese words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.15.8):


api yat-spåhä çréù

   "You have embraced the young cowherd women between Your two arms--a favor hankered after
by the goddess of fortune herself."***

    In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.60 the word "vraja-sundaréëäm (of the beautiful girls of Vraja)
shows that the gopés are the most beautiful of all girls". That the devotees attain all exalted qualities
is confirmed by these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (5.18.12):


yasyästi bhaktir bhagavaty akiïcanä. . .


   "All the demigods and their exalted qualities, such as religion, knowledge and renunciation,
become manifest in the body of one who has developed unalloyed devotion for the Supreme
Personality of Godhead, Väsudeva."*

   Spiritual love where the devotee loves the Lord as a beloved is the crest jewel of all kinds of
spiritual love. Here two levels of that love, as manifested by Goddess Lakñmé and by the gopés, are
revealed. That this kind of spiritual love for the Lord is the most exalted is not refuted by the
following words spoken by the Lord to Uddhava in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (11.14.15):


na ca saìkarñaëo na çréù


  "My dear Uddhava, neither Lord Brahmä, Lord Çiva, Lord Saìkarñaëa, teh goddess of fortune,
nor indeed My own self are as dear to MKe as you are."***

  These words are only intended to praise devotional service and the devotees in a general way.
They do not mean that Uddhava is in a position superior to Goddess Laksmi and the other devotees
who consider the Lord their beloved. Because the gopés love Lord Kåñëa, the original form of the
Supreme Personality of Godhead, their position is most exalted.
records.content:
Las gopis son las más exaltadas de todos los habitantes de Gokula. Esta verdad se ve en el
Las siguientes palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.87.57-58):
drstvaivam-adi gopinam
krsnavesatma-viklavam uddhavah parama-pritas
ta namasyann idam jagau
"Así, viendo cómo las gopis siempre estaban perturbadas debido a su total absorción en Krsna,
Uddhava estaba sumamente complacido. Deseando ofrecerles todo el respeto, cantó lo siguiente.
etah param tanu-bhrto bhuvi gopa-vadhvo
govinda eva nikhilatmani rudha-bhavah vacanti yad bhava-bhiyo munayo vayam ca
kim brahma-janmabhir ananta-katha-rasasya
"Entre todas las personas de la tierra, solo estas mujeres pastoras han perfeccionado realmente su arte corporal.
vidas, porque han alcanzado la perfección del amor puro por el Señor Govinda. Su amor puro
Es anhelada por aquellos que temen la existencia material, por los grandes sabios y también por nosotros mismos.
Para aquel que ha probado las narraciones del Señor infinito, ¿de qué sirve nacer como un ser humano?
¿Un brahmán de clase alta, o incluso el mismísimo Señor Barhma?
En el segundo de estos dos versículos la palabra "param" significa "solo", "etas tanu-bhrtah" significa
cuyo nacimiento en este mundo ha dado su fruto", akhilatmani" significa "en la Suprema Personalidad de
Divinidad que, aunque rara vez vista en este mundo, está presente como el Alma Suprema en todos los seres vivos.
seres", "govinde" significa la Suprema Personalidad de Dios, que se manifiesta directamente en este
mundo como el príncipe de Gokula", "evam" significa con dulzura así", y "rudha-bhavah" significa
"cuyo amor extático maha-bhava es manifiesto". Las palabras "vacanti yad bhava-bhiyo munayah" significan
Si de alguna manera la descripción de la dulzura del amor extático que alcanza el nivel de maha-
Cuando bhava entre en sus oídos, los sabios que anhelan la liberación de forma ordinaria renunciarán a ella.
deseará y, comprendiendo sus glorias, anhelará alcanzar el amor extático." La palabra "vayam" significa
"Incluso grandes devotos como yo anhelamos alcanzar ese amor. Eso significa que aún no lo hemos alcanzado.
eso. No estamos capacitados para sentir ese amor extático tan dulce." Ese es el significado. Entonces el
El hablante de este verso critica a las personas que no anhelan alcanzar ese amor extático. Dice:
"kim brahma-janmabhir ananta- katha-rasasya", que significa "¿De qué sirve nacer como el
El semidiós Brahma innumerables veces si no podemos saborear el néctar de escuchar los temas del Señor
Krishna, cuyos pasatiempos no tienen fin?" Esta pregunta retórica implica la respuesta: "no hay uso
al nacer como tal Señor Brahma."

records.sourceEnglish:
Uddhava thinks: "For me to aspire to become like the gopés is like a dwarf yearning to catch the
moon. Therefore my only prayer is this: (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.61):


äsäm aho caraëa-reëu-juñäm ahaà syäà
   våndävane kim api gulma-latauñadhénäm
yä dustyajaà sva-janam ärya-pathaà ca hitvä
   bhejur mukunda-padavéà çrutibhir vimågyam


   "The gopés of Våndävana have given up the association of their husbands, sons, and other family

members, who are very difficult to give up, and they have forsaken the path of chastity to take
shelter of tyhe lotus feet of Mukunda, Kåñëa, which one should search for by Vedic knowledge. Oh,
let me be fortunate enough to be one of the bushes, creepers, or herbs in Våndävana, because the
gopés trample them and bless them with the dust of their feet."*

   In this verse Uddhava says: "It is not possible for me to attain even a slight touch of the effulgent
glory of the gopés' great love for Lord Kåñëa. Therefore my desire will be to tak another, a different
birth in this world. If in that birth I still cannot directly attain the touch of the gopés' feet, for what
shall I pray? I will pray: Let me take birth (syäm) even among the undesireable speciies of life,
among the bushes, creepers, or herbs (kim api gulma-latauñadhénäm), for then I will have the4 good
fortune of attaining the touch of the dust of the gopés' feet (äsäm caraëa-reëu)." Here the word {.sy
168}aho" (Oh!) shows that Uddhava's heart is agitated with this desire. Here the question may be
asked: "What is the nature of these gopés?" The answer is given: "Impelled by passionate love, they
have forsaken the path of chastity and rejected the moral codes taught by the Vedas and ordinary
social custon" (yä dustyajaà sva-janam ärya-pathaà ca hitvä). They follow the blissful path of love
for Lord Kåñë, a path all the Çruti-çästras have concluded is the crest jewel of all goals of life
(bhejur mukunda-padavéà çrutibhir vimågyam)." The conclusion, then, of this verse is: "Let us also
reject the path of conventional religion (ärya-patham) and follow the footsteps of the gopés."
records.content:
Uddhava piensa: "Para mí, aspirar a ser como las gopis es como un enano que anhela alcanzar
la luna. Por lo tanto, mi única oración es esta: (srimad-Bhagavatam 10.47.61):
asam aho carana-renu-jusam aham syam
vrndavane kim api gulma-latausadhinam ya dustyajam sva-janam arya-patham ca hitva
bhejur mukunda-padavim srutibhir vimrgyam
"Las gopis de Vrindavana han renunciado a la compañía de sus maridos, hijos y otros
miembros de la familia, que son muy difíciles de abandonar, y han abandonado el camino de la castidad para
Refúgiate en los pies de loto de Mukunda, Krishna, que uno debe buscar mediante el conocimiento védico.
Oh, déjame tener la fortuna de ser uno de los arbustos, enredaderas o hierbas de Vrndavana, porque
Las gopis los pisotean y los bendicen con el polvo de sus pies.
En este verso Uddhava dice: "No me es posible alcanzar ni siquiera un leve roce de la
la gloria resplandeciente del gran amor de las gopis por el Señor Krishna. Por lo tanto, mi deseo será tomar
otro, un nacimiento diferente en este mundo. Si en ese nacimiento aún no puedo alcanzar directamente el
el toque de los pies de las gopis, ¿por qué he de orar? Oraré: Permíteme nacer (syam) incluso entre
las especies indeseables de vida, entre los arbustos, enredaderas o hierbas (kim api gulma-
latausadhinam), porque entonces tendré la4 buena fortuna de alcanzar el contacto con el polvo del
"Los pies de las gopis (asam carana-renu)". Aquí la palabra "aho" (¡Oh!) muestra que el corazón de Uddhava está agitado.
con este deseo. Aquí se puede plantear la pregunta: "¿Cuál es la naturaleza de estas gopis?" La respuesta
Se dice: "Impulsados por un amor apasionado, han abandonado el camino de la castidad y rechazado el
códigos morales enseñados por los Vedas y la costumbre social ordinaria" (yadustyajam sva-janam arya-patham ca
hitva). Siguen el camino dichoso del amor por el Señor Krishna, un camino que todos los sruti-sastras han
"Concluir es la joya suprema de todos los objetivos de la vida (bhejur mukunda-padavim srutibhir vimrgyam)".
La conclusión, pues, de este versículo es: "Rechacemos también el camino de la religión convencional".
(arya-patham) y sigue los pasos de las gopis."

records.sourceEnglish:
Goddess Lakñmé and others find the path of directly enjoying blissful pastimes with Lord Kåñëa
is very difficult to attain. This is revealed in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.62):


yä vai çritärcitam ajädibhir äpta-kämair
   yogeçvarair api sadätmani räsa-goñöhyäm
kåñëasya tad bhagavataù caraëäravindaà
   nyastaà staneñu vijahuù parirabhya täpam


   "The goddess of fortune herself, along with Lord Brahmä and all the other demigods, who are
masters of yogic perfection, can worship the lotus feet of Kåñëa only within her mind. But during
the räsa dance Lord Kåñëa placed His feet upon these gopés' breasts, and by embracing those feet the
gopés gave up all distress."***

   This verse means: "In the assembly of the räsa-dance (räsa-goñöhyäm) embracing (parirabhya)
the indescribably sweet lotus feet (padäravindam) of Lord Kåñëa (çré-kåñëasya), the Supreme
Personality of Godhead (bhagavataù), who manifests all opulences, of which sweetness is the best,
the gopés became free (jahuù) of the great anxiety they felt from not being able to associate with
Lord Kåñëa directly. Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé and other sages expert in the yoga of devotional
service (yogeçvaraiù) worship in their hearts (ätmani) the lotus feet of Lord Kåñëa."

   It is said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.16.36):


yad-väïchayä çrér lalanäcarat tapaù


   "O Lord, we do not know how the serpent Käliya has attained this great opportunity of being
touched by the dust of Your lotus feet. For this end, the goddess of fortune performed austerities for
centuries, giving up all other desires and taking austere vows."***

  In these words it is seen that even Goddess Laksmi has to worship Lord Kåñëa opnly within her
mind. This she always did (sad.ä) from beginningless time. She was never able to approach Lord
Kåñëa directly. That truth is confirmed by the Çruti-çästras and other scriptures.
records.content:
La diosa Lakshmi y otras encuentran el camino para disfrutar directamente de pasatiempos dichosos con el Señor.
Es muy difícil alcanzar a Krishna. Esto se revela en las siguientes palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam.
(10.47.62):
ya vai sritarcitam ajadibhir apta-kamair
yogesvarair api sadatmani rasa-gosthyam krsnasya tad bhagavatah caranaravindam
nyastam stanesu vijahuh parirabhya tapam
"La diosa de la fortuna misma, junto con el Señor Brahma y todos los demás semidioses, que son
Los maestros de la perfección yóguica pueden adorar los pies de loto de Krishna solo en su mente. Pero durante
la danza rasa El Señor Krishna puso Sus pies sobre los pechos de estas gopis, y al abrazar esos pies
Las gopis abandonaron toda aflicción.
Este verso significa: "En la asamblea de la danza rasa (rasa-gosthyam) abrazando (parirabhya)
Los indescriptiblemente dulces pies de loto (padaravindam) del Señor Krishna (sri-krsnasya), el Supremo
Personalidad de Dios (bhagavatah), quien manifiesta todas las opulencias, de las cuales la dulzura es la mejor,
Las gopis quedaron libres (yahuh) de la gran ansiedad que sentían por no poder asociarse con
El Señor Krishna directamente. Srila Sukadeva Gosvami y otros sabios expertos en el yoga devocional.
servicio (yogesvaraih) adoración en sus corazones (atmani) los pies de loto del Señor Krishna."
Se dice en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.16.36):
yad-vachaya srir lalanacarat tapah
"Oh Señor, no sabemos cómo la serpiente Kaliya ha alcanzado esta gran oportunidad de ser
tocada por el polvo de Tus pies de loto. Para este fin, la diosa de la fortuna realizó austeridades.
Durante siglos, renunciaron a todos los demás deseos y tomaron votos austeros."
En estas palabras se ve que incluso la Diosa Lakshmi tiene que adorar al Señor Krishna solo dentro de su interior.
mente. Esto siempre lo hizo (sad.a) desde tiempos inmemoriales. Nunca pudo acercarse al Señor
Krishna directamente. Esa verdad está confirmada por los sruti-sastras y otras escrituras.

records.sourceEnglish:
Humbled by seeing the gopés' glorious status, and feeling himself very unqualified, Uddhava
offers respectful obeisances to the dust of the gopés' feet. He says in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.63):


vande nanda-vraja-stréëäà
   päda-reëum abhikñnaçaù
yäsäà hari-kathodgétaà
   punäti bhuvana-trayam


   "I repeatedly offer my respects to the dust from the feet of the women of Nanda Maharaja's
cowherd village. When these gopés loudly chant the glories of Çré Kåñëa, the vibration purifies the
three worlds."***

   In this verse Uddhava says: "I offer my respectful obeisances (vande) to the dust of the gopés' feet
(päda-reëum)." Then in the second part of the verse he describes the gopés. Uddhava's meaning
here is: "The good fortune we have attained today is very wonderful." Lord Kåñëa Himself describes
the glories of His devotees in these words of Padma Puräëa, Kärttika-mähätmya:


ete hi yädaväù sarve
   mad-gaëä eva bhävini
sarvadä mat-priyä devi
   mat-tulya-guëa-çälinaù


   "O glorious goddess, all the Yädavas are always very dear to Me. They have virtues like My own."

   The Yädavas, who are very dear to Lord Kåñëa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is

confirmed by these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.90.46):


çayyäsanäöanäläpa. . .


   "The Våñëis were so absorbed in Kåñëa consciousness that they forgot their own bodies while
sleeping, sitting, walking, conversing, playing, bathing, and so on."***

   Devotees whose relationship is with other forms of the Lord, forms other than the form of Lord
Kåñëa, are not as glorious as the Yädavas. That amongst the Yädavas and other devotees Uddhava is
very glorious is confirmed by these words spoken by Lord Kåñëa Himself in Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(11.16.29):


tvaà tu bhägavateñv aham


   "O Uddhava, amongst the devotees you are my representative."

   Lord Kåñëa also says in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (11.11.49):


tvaà me bhåtyaù suhåt sakhä


   "O Uddhava, you are My friend, servant, and well-wisher."

   Lord Kåñëa also says in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (3.4.31):


noddhavo 'nv api man-nyünaù


   "Udsdhava is not inferior to Me in any way."*

   Lord Kåñëa also says in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (11.14.15):


na ca saìkarñaëo na çrér
   naivätmä ca yathä bhavän


  "My dear Uddhava, neither Lord Brahmä, Lord Çiva, Lord Saìkarñaëa, the goddess of fortune,
nor indeed My own self are as dear to Me as you."***

   In these and many other statements Lord Kåñëa affirms that Uddhava is exalted amongst the
devotees. Still, Uddhava is very humble when he speaks about the gopés. He is not humble in the

same way about the Lord's queens in Dvärakä. The queens' glory compares to the gopés' glory in the
same way the eye of a person blind from birth compares to the glory of the full moon.
records.content:
Humillado al ver el glorioso estatus de las gopis, y sintiéndose él mismo muy poco capacitado, Uddhava
Ofrece respetuosas reverencias al polvo de los pies de las gopis. Dice en el srimad-Bhagavatam
(10.47.63):
vande nanda-vraja-strinam
pada-renum abhiksnasah yasam hari-kathodgitam
punati bhuvana-trayam

records.sourceEnglish:
That Çré Rädhä is more glorious than the 16,000 queens of Lord Kåñëa, the king of the Yadus, is
confirmed by the queens themselves, who say in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.83.41-43):


na vayaà sädhvi samräjyaà
   svaräjyaà bhaujyam apy uta
vairäjyaà parameñöhyaà ca
   änantyaà vä hareù padam

kämayämaha etasya
  çrémat-päda-rajaù çriyaù
kuca-kuìkuma-gandhäòhyaà
  mürdhnä voòhuà gadä-bhåtaù


   "O saintly lady, we do not desire dominion over the earth, the sovereignty of the King of heaven,
unlimited facility for enjoyment, mystic power, the position of Lord Brahmä, immortality, or even
attainment of the kingdom of God. We simply desire to carry on our heads the glorious dust of Lord
Kåñëa's feet, enriched by the freagrance of kuìkuma from His consort's bosom.***


vraja-striyo yad väïchanti
   pulindyas tåëa-vérudhaù
gävaç cärayato gopäù
   päda-sparçaà mahätmanaù


   "We desire the same contact with the Supreme Lord's feet that the young women of Vraja, the
cowherd boys, and even the aborigine Pulinda women desire-the touch of the dust He leaves on the
plants and grass as He tends His cows."***

   This verse means: "O saintly lady, we do not desire dominion over the earth, or any other
material benefit." Here the word "sämräjyam" means "a kingdom on the earth", "sväräjyam" means
"the kingdom of Indra", {.sy 168}bhojyam" means "the pleasures available in these two kingdoms",
"vairäjyam" means "mystic powers", "and "pärameñöhyam" means "the kingdom of Lord Brahmä".
"Anantyam" here means "the limitless happiness one attains by realizing the Supreme Personality of
Godhead". This limitless happiness is described in the Taittiréya Upaniñad (2.8.2-9), where the
different levels of human happiness, each level of happiness a hundred times greater than the one
below is described. The highest of these levels of happiness is found in realizing the Supreme

Personality of Godhead. In Taittiréya Upaniñad (2.8.9) that limitless happiness is described. That is
the meaning here. What more may be said? The queens say: "We do not desire (na kämayämahe) to
stay near Lord Hari (çré-hareù padam)." Someone may ask: "Thenwhat do you desire to attain?" To
this question the queens answer: "We desire to carry (voòhuà) on our heads (mürdhnä) the dust of
the glorious feet (çrémat-päda-rajaù) of our master, all-knowing Lord Kåñëa (gadä-bhåtaù).
Fuerther, we desire to attain the great treasure present in that dust, the treasure that is the
fragrance of kuìkuma from the goddess of fortune's breast (çriyaù kuca-kuìkuma-gandhäòhyaà)."
   Here someone may protest: "O queens, first you say you do not desire to attain Lord Hari's feet,
and then you say you want to hold the dust of His feet on your heads, dust rich with the fragrance
of kuìkuma from the goddess of fortune's breast. Why do you contradict your own words? If
Rukmiëé, the goddess of fortune, desires, then you will certainly attain your desire. Then you will
indeed attain the dust of the Lord's feet, dust rich with kuìkuma from the most exalted goddess of
fortune's breast. But first please clearly tell us what it is that you desire."
   The answer to this protest is found in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.83.43, where the feet of Lord Kåñëa
(not Lord Näräyaëa) are specifically described. The dust of Lord Kåñëa's feet are also described in
these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.21.17):


pürëäù pulindya urugäya. . .


   "The aborigine women of the Våndävana area become disturbed by lust when they see the grass
marked with reddish kuìkuma
powder. Endowed with the color of Kåñëa's lotus feet, this powder originally decorated the breasts
of His beloveds, and when the aborigine women smear it on their faces and breasts, they give up all
their anxiety."***

   In these quotes it is seen that the gopés of Vraja yearned to attain (yad vänchanti) the dust of
Lord Kåñëa's feet. The present tense is used here (vänchanti) on the assumption that even today
the gopés are not truly separated from Lord Kåñëa. By mentioning the aborigine girls, the queens
hint (in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.83.43) that they themselves should also be qualified to attain the
dust of Lord Kåñëa's feet. Here the words "tåëa-virudhaù" mean the dürvä grass and other plants".
The fragranced of the kunkuma from the goddess of foretune's breast is never absent from Lord
Kåñëa's feet. That is the idea here. Here the word "gavah" means {.sy 168}cows", "carayataù" means
"herding", The cowherd boys (gopäù) are only briefly mentioned here. Although many cowherd
boys, such as the priya-sakhäs and narma-sakhäs, are very close friends of Lord Kåñëa, because they
are males an elaborate description of them here in the midts of a discusion of the gopés is not
appropriate. Even famous Goddess Laksmi cannot attain ord Kåñëa's feet, although she aspires to.
Thismis confirmed in the Näga-patnés' prayers in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.16.36 and also in the words
of Uddhava in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.62. Not even the famous Goddess Rukmiëé can attain the
same kind of association with Lord Kåñëa, for her association with Him is in a different time and
place. Therefore Rukmiëé cannot hope to associate with Lord Kåñëa as the gopés of Vraja do. The
superior status of the gopés is confirmed in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.60. Of Queen Rukmiëé it is
said the Matsya Puräëa:

rukmiëé dväravatyäà tu
   rädhä våndävane vane


   "She who is Rukmiëé in Dvärakä is also Rädhä in Våndävana Forest."

   Vedänta-sütra (1.1.30) and the Ahangrahopasana-sastras declare that the demigod Indra and
Goddess Durgä are in one sense not different from the Supreme Personality of Godhead. In the
same way, in one sense Çré Rädhä is not different from Goddess Lakñmé. The difference is that Çré
Rädhä is the original and complete form of Goddess Lakñmé. This is confirmeed ion the following
words of the Båhad-Gautaméya Tantra:


devé kåñëamayé proktä
   rädhikä. . .


    "The transcendental goddess Çrématé Rädhäräëé is the direct counterpart of Lord Çré Kåñëa. She
is the central figure for all the goddesses of fortune. She possesses all the attractiveness to attract
the all-attractive Supreme Personality of Godhead. She is the primeval internal potency of the
Lord."*

   In the Bahv-åk-pariçiñöa it is said of Çré Rädhä:


rädhayä mädhavo devo
   mädhavenaiva rädhikä


   "Lord Kåñëa always stays with Çré Rädhä. Çré Rädhä always stays with Lord Kåñëa."

   When she appears as Çré Rädhä, the goddess of fortune is most glorious. That is confirmed by
these words. It is also confirmed by the followiong words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.28), which
refer to Çré Rädhä:


anayärädhito nünaà
  bhagavan. . .


   "Certainly this particular gopé has perfectly worshiped the all-powerful Personality of Godhead,
Govinda, since He was so pleased with Her that He abandoned the rest of us and brought Her to a
secluded place."***

   The following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.11) also refer to Çré Rädhä:

apy eëa-patny upagataù. . .


   "O friend, wife of the deer, has Lord Acyuta been here with His beloved, bringing great joy to
your eyes? Indeed, blowing this way is the fragrance of His garland of kunòa flowers, which was
smeared with the kuìkuma from the breasts of His girlfriend when He embraced Her."***

    In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.83.41-43 the Dvaraka queens say: "As the gopés yearn to touch Lord
Kåñëa's feet, so do we." They pray: "May the fragrance of the ecstatic love the gopés' feel be manifest
in us." The Dvärakä queens do not desire only to attain the dust of Lord Kåñëa's feet. They desire to
touch His feet also. Thus the words "vayaà kämayämahe" may refer to the desire expressed in
Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.83.42 or the desire expressed in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.83.43. Thus the
Dvärakä queens' request may be either {.sy 168}We desire to touch Lord Kåñëa's feet." or "We desire
to touch the dust of Lord Kåñëa's feet." Either way, the same result is attained. Therefore these two
requests are not truly different. In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.83.42 the word {.sy 168}etasya" refers to
Lord Kåñëa. What is Lord Kåñëa's nature? In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.83.43 it is said that Lord Kåñëa
is {.sy 168}mahätmanaù". In that word "mahä" means "He who is naturally the greatest of all", and
"ätmanaù" means "He whose nature is fille with handsomeness and all other virtues". Lord Kåñëa's
handsomeness and virtues are seen in these words spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.33.6):


taträtiçuçubhe täbhir
   bhagavän. . .


   "In the midst of the dancing gopés, Lord Kåñëa appeared most brilliant, like an exquisite sapphire
in the midst of golden ornaments."***

   The Çrémad-Bhägavatam verses 10.83.41-43 quoted in the beginning of this anucheda were
spoken by the Dvärakä queens to Draupadé.

Esto lo confirman las propias reinas, que dicen en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.83.41-43):
na vayam sadhvi samrajyam
