cielo, facilidad ilimitada para el disfrute, poder místico, la posición del Señor Brahma, inmortalidad,
o incluso el logro del reino de Dios. Simplemente deseamos llevar sobre nuestras cabezas el glorioso polvo.
de los pies del Señor Krishna, enriquecidos por la fragancia del kunkuma del pecho de Su consorte.
vraja-striyo yad vachanti

"Deseamos el mismo contacto con los pies del Señor Supremo que las jóvenes de Vraja, las
Los pastores jóvenes, e incluso las mujeres aborígenes Pulinda desean el toque del polvo que Él deja en
las plantas y la hierba mientras cuida de sus vacas."
Este versículo significa: "Oh santa señora, no deseamos dominio sobre la tierra, ni sobre ningún otro lugar".
beneficio material." Aquí la palabra "samrajyam" significa "un reino en la tierra", "svarajyam" significa
"el reino de Indra", bhojyam" significa "los placeres disponibles en estos dos reinos",
"vairajyam" significa "poderes místicos" y "paramesthyam" significa "el reino del Señor Brahma".
Aquí, "Anantyam" significa "la felicidad ilimitada que se alcanza al comprender a la Suprema Personalidad".
de la Divinidad". Esta felicidad ilimitada se describe en el Taittiriya Upanisad (2.8.2-9), donde el
diferentes niveles de felicidad humana, cada nivel de felicidad cien veces mayor que el uno
A continuación se describe. El más alto de estos niveles de felicidad se encuentra en la realización de lo Supremo.
Personalidad de Dios. En el Taittiriya Upanishad (2.8.9) se describe esa felicidad ilimitada.
Ese es el significado aquí. ¿Qué más se puede decir? Las reinas dicen: "No deseamos (na
kamayamahe) para permanecer cerca del Señor Hari (sri-hareh padam)." Alguien podría preguntar: "Entonces, ¿qué deseas?"
¿Para alcanzarlo? A esta pregunta las reinas responden: "Deseamos llevar (vodhum) sobre nuestras cabezas.
(murdhna) el polvo de los gloriosos pies (srimat-pada-rajah) de nuestro maestro, el Señor Krishna, que todo lo sabe.
(gada-bhrtah). Además, deseamos alcanzar el gran tesoro presente en ese polvo, el tesoro
esa es la fragancia de kunkuma del pecho de la diosa de la fortuna (sriyah kuca- kunkuma-
gandhadhyam)."
Aquí alguien podría protestar: "Oh reinas, primero decís que no deseáis alcanzar los pies del Señor Hari,
y luego dices que quieres sostener el polvo de Sus pies sobre tus cabezas, polvo rico en
Fragancia de kunkuma del pecho de la diosa de la fortuna. ¿Por qué te contradices?
Si Rukmini, la diosa de la fortuna, lo desea, entonces ciertamente alcanzarás tu deseo. Entonces tú
ciertamente alcanzará el polvo de los pies del Señor, polvo rico en kunkuma del más excelso
Diosa del pecho de la fortuna. Pero primero, por favor, díganos claramente qué es lo que desea.
La respuesta a esta protesta se encuentra en el srimad-Bhagavatam 10.83.43, donde los pies del Señor Krishna
(no el Señor Narayana) se describen específicamente. El polvo de los pies del Señor Krishna también se describe.
En estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.21.17):
purnah pulindya urugaya. . .
"Las mujeres aborígenes de la zona de Vrndavana se perturban por la lujuria cuando ven la hierba
marcado con polvo de kunkuma rojizo. Dotado del color de los pies de loto de Krishna, este polvo
originalmente decoraba los pechos de Sus amadas, y cuando las mujeres aborígenes se lo untaban en sus
rostros y senos, abandonan toda su ansiedad."
En estas citas se ve que las gopis de Vraja anhelaban alcanzar (yad vanchanti) el polvo
de los pies del Señor Krishna. El tiempo presente se usa aquí (vanchanti) bajo el supuesto de que incluso
Hoy en día, las gopis no están realmente separadas del Señor Krishna. Al mencionar a las niñas aborígenes,
Las reinas insinúan (en el srimad- Bhagavatam 10.83.43) que ellas mismas también deberían estar calificadas para
alcanzar el polvo de los pies del Señor Krishna. Aquí las palabras "trna-virudhah" significan la hierba durva y
otras plantas". La fragancia del kunkuma del pecho de la diosa de la fortuna nunca es
ausentes de los pies del Señor Krishna. Esa es la idea aquí. Aquí la palabra "gavah" significa vacas,
"carayatah" significa "pastoreo". Los pastores jóvenes (gopah) solo se mencionan brevemente aquí. Aunque
Muchos pastores jóvenes, como los priya-sakhas y los narma-sakhas, son amigos muy cercanos del Señor.
Krishna, porque son varones, una descripción elaborada de ellos aquí en medio de una discusión de
Las gopis no son apropiadas. Ni siquiera la famosa diosa Lakshmi puede alcanzar los pies del Señor Krishna.
aunque ella aspira a ello. Esto se confirma en las oraciones de las Naga-patnis en el srimad-Bhagavatam.
10.16.36 y también en las palabras de Uddhava en el srimad-Bhagavatam 10.47.62. Ni siquiera el famoso
La diosa Rukmini puede alcanzar el mismo tipo de asociación con el Señor Krishna, por su asociación con
Él está en un tiempo y lugar diferente. Por lo tanto, Rukmini no puede esperar asociarse con el Señor Krishna.
como lo hacen las gopis de Vraja. El estatus superior de las gopis se confirma en el srimad-Bhagavatam.
10.47.60. De la reina Rukmini se dice en el Matsya Purana:
rukmini dvaravatyam tu
Radha Vrndavane Vane
"Aquella que es Rukmini en Dvaraka es también Radha en el bosque de Vrindavana."
El Vedanta-sutra (1.1.30) y los Ahangrahopasana-sastras declaran que el semidiós Indra y
En cierto sentido, la diosa Durga no es diferente de la Suprema Personalidad de Dios. En el mismo sentido,
De alguna manera, en cierto sentido, Sri Radha no es diferente de la Diosa Lakshmi. La diferencia es que Sri Radha
es la forma original y completa de la Diosa Lakshmi. Esto se confirma en las siguientes palabras.
del Brhad-Gautamiya Tantra:
devi krsnamayi prokta
Radhika...
"La diosa trascendental Srimati Radharani es la contraparte directa del Señor Sri Krishna.
Ella es la figura central de todas las diosas de la fortuna. Ella posee todo el atractivo.
para atraer a la Suprema Personalidad de Dios, que es sumamente atractiva. Ella es la potencia interna primordial.
del Señor."
En el Bahv-rk-parisista se dice de Sri Radha:
Radhaya Madhavo Devo
Madhavenaiva Radhika
"El Señor Krishna siempre está con Sri Radha. Sri Radha siempre está con el Señor Krishna."
Cuando aparece como Sri Radha, la diosa de la fortuna es más gloriosa. Eso es confirmado por
estas palabras. También lo confirman las siguientes palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.30.28), que
Consulte a Sri Radha:
anayaradhito nunam
Bhagavan. . .
"Ciertamente, esta gopi en particular ha adorado perfectamente a la todopoderosa Personalidad de Dios.
Divinidad, Govinda, puesto que Él estaba tan complacido con Ella que nos abandonó al resto y nos trajo
La llevé a un lugar apartado."
Las siguientes palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.30.11) también se refieren a sri Radha:
apy ena-patny upagatah. . .
"Oh amiga, esposa del ciervo, ¿ha estado el Señor Acyuta aquí con su amada, trayendo gran alegría?
¿A tus ojos? En efecto, soplando hacia aquí está la fragancia de Su guirnalda de flores de kunda, que
"Quedó manchado con el kunkuma de los pechos de su novia cuando la abrazó."
En el srimad-Bhagavatam 10.83.41-43 las reinas Dvaraka dicen: "Como las gopis anhelan tocar al Señor
"Los pies de Krishna, también nosotros." Oran: "Que la fragancia del amor extático que sienten las gopis sea
se manifiesta en nosotros." Las reinas Dvaraka no desean solo alcanzar el polvo de los pies del Señor Krishna.
Ellos también desean tocar Sus pies. Por lo tanto, las palabras "vayam kamayamahe" pueden referirse al deseo.
expresado en srimad-Bhagavatam 10.83.42 o el deseo expresado en srimad-Bhagavatam 10.83.43.
Así, la petición de las reinas Dvaraka puede ser "Deseamos tocar los pies del Señor Krishna" o "Nosotros
deseo de tocar el polvo de los pies del Señor Krishna." De cualquier manera, se obtiene el mismo resultado.
Por lo tanto, estas dos peticiones no son realmente diferentes. En el srimad-Bhagavatam 10.83.42 la palabra
"etasya" se refiere al Señor Krishna. ¿Cuál es la naturaleza del Señor Krishna? En el srimad-Bhagavatam 10.83.43 es
dijo que el Señor Krishna es mahatmanah". En esa palabra "maha" significa "Aquel que es naturalmente el más grande".
"de todos", y "atmanah" significa "Aquel cuya naturaleza está llena de belleza y todas las demás virtudes".
La belleza y las virtudes del Señor Krishna se ven en estas palabras pronunciadas por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami de
Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.33.6):
tatratisusubhe tabhir
Bhagavan. . .
"En medio de las gopis danzantes, el Señor Krishna apareció resplandeciente, como un ser exquisito
un zafiro en medio de ornamentos dorados."
Los versículos 10.83.41-43 del srimad-Bhagavatam citados al comienzo de este anucheda fueron pronunciados
por las reinas Dvaraka a Draupadi.

records.sourceEnglish:
Çré Rädhä-devé is described in these words of the Adi Puräëa:


trailokye påthivé dhanyä
   tatra våndävanaà punaù
taträpi gopikäù pärtha
   tatra rädhäbhidhä mama

   "O Pärtha, the earth planet is the most fortunate place in the three worlds, for Våndävana forest,
the gopés, and My beloved who bears the name Rädhä all stay there."

   Çré Rädhä-devé is AGAIN described in these words of the Padma Puräëa, Kärttika-mähätmya:


yathä rädhä priyä viñëos
   tasyäù kuëòaà priyaà tathä
sarva-gopéñu saivaikä
   viñëor atyanta-vallabhä


  "Just as Çrématé Rädhäräëé is dear to the Supreme Lord Kåñëa (Viñëu), so Her bathing place
(Rädhä-kuëòa) is equally dear to Kåñëa. Among all the gopés, She alone stands supreme as the
Lord's most beloved."*

  Çré Rädhä's love is the greatest. This is confirmed in the following words of the Agni Puräëa,
Väsanä-bhäçya:


gopyaù papracchur uñasi
   kåñëänucaram uddhavam
hari-lélä-vihäräàç ca
   tatraikäà rädhikäà vinä
rädhä tad-bhäva-samlénä
   väsanäyä virämitä


   "At dawn the gopés asked Kåñëa's servant Uddhava to describe how Kåñëa was enjoying pastimes
without Çré Rädhä. At that moment, overcome with love and yearning to be with Kåñëa, Çré Rädhä
fainted."

   Here the words "väsanäyä virämitä" indicate that Çré Rädhä was in the ninth state of
consciousness. In other words, She was completely overcome. She had no power to continue. That
Çré Rädhä is the best of the gopés is seen in the following words describing the räsa-dance pastime in
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.27):


kasyäù padäni. . .


   "Here we see the footprints of some gopé who must have been walking along with the son of
Nanda Mahäräja. He must have put His arm on Her shoulder, just as an elephant rests His trunk on
the shoulder of an accompanying she-elephant."***

   These words describe Çré Rädhä's supreme good fortune. Çré Rädhä's name is indirectly uttered in
these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.28):


anayärädhito nünaà
   bhagavän harir éçvaraù
yan no vihäya govindaù
   préto yäm anayad rahaù


  "Certainly this particular gopé has perfectly worshiped (ärädhita) the all-powerful Personality of
Godhead, Govinda, since He was so pleased with Her that He abandoned the rest of us and brought
Her to a secluded place."***

   Here the words "anaya bhagavan radhitah" mean {.sy 168}Çré Rädhä brought the Supreme
Personality of Godhead under Her control". The word "nünam" here is used in the sense of making
a guess. Within the word "ärädhitaù" (worshiped) in this verse the name Rädhä is hidden. The
result of Rädhä's worshiping Kåñëa is given in the words beginning with "yan na", the words that
say: "He was so pleased with Her that He abandoned the rest of us and brought Her to a secluded
place." Here the word "govindaù" refers to Lord Kåñëa, the king of Gokula. This verse was spoken by
the vraja-gopés.

Sri Radha-devi es descrita con estas palabras del Adi Purana:
trailokye prthivi dhanya
tatra vrndavanam punah tatrapi gopikah partha
Tatra Radhabhidha Mama
"Oh Partha, el planeta tierra es el lugar más afortunado en los tres mundos, para Vrindavana
El bosque, las gopis y mi amada que lleva el nombre de Radha, todos permanecen allí."
Sri Radha-devi es descrita OTRA VEZ en estas palabras del Padma Purana, Karttika-mahatmya:
Yatha Radha Priya Visnos
tasyah kundam priyam tatha sarva-gopisu saivaika
Visnor Atyanta-Vallabha
"Así como Srimati Radharani es querida por el Señor Supremo Krishna (Vishnu), también lo es su lugar de baño.
(Radha-kunda) es igualmente querido por Krishna. Entre todas las gopis, Ella sola se destaca suprema como la
El más amado del Señor."
El amor de Sri Radha es el más grande. Esto se confirma en las siguientes palabras de Agni.
Purana, Vasana-bhasya:
gopyah papracchur usasi
krsnanucaram uddhavam hari-lila-viharams ca
tatraikam radhikam vina radha tad-bhava-samlina
Vasanaya Viramita
"Al amanecer, las gopis le pidieron al sirviente de Krishna, Uddhava, que describiera cómo Krishna disfrutaba de sus pasatiempos."
sin sri Radha. En ese momento, abrumada por el amor y el anhelo de estar con Krsna, sri Radha
se desmayó."
Aquí las palabras "vasanaya viramita" indican que sri Radha estaba en el noveno estado de
conciencia. En otras palabras, estaba completamente vencida. No tenía poder para continuar. Eso
Sri Radha es la mejor de las gopis, como se ve en las siguientes palabras que describen la danza rasa.
Pasatiempo en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.30.27):
kasyah padani. . .
"Aquí vemos las huellas de alguna gopi que debió haber estado caminando junto al hijo de
Nanda Maharaja. Debió haber puesto su brazo sobre su hombro, tal como un elefante apoya su trompa en
el hombro de una elefanta que la acompañaba."
Estas palabras describen la suprema buena fortuna de Sri Radha. El nombre de Sri Radha se pronuncia indirectamente.
En estas palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.30.28):
anayaradhito nunam
bhagavan harir isvarah yan no vihaya govindah
prito yam anayad rahah
"Ciertamente esta gopi en particular ha adorado perfectamente (aradhita) al todopoderoso
Personalidad de Dios, Govinda, puesto que estaba tan complacido con Ella que nos abandonó al resto.
y la llevó a un lugar apartado."
Aquí las palabras "anaya bhagavan radhitah" significan sri Radha trajo a la Suprema Personalidad de
La divinidad bajo Su control". La palabra "nunam" aquí se usa en el sentido de hacer una suposición. Dentro
La palabra "aradhitah" (adorada) en este verso oculta el nombre de Radha. El resultado de Radha
La adoración a Krishna se da en las palabras que comienzan con "yan na", las palabras que dicen: "Él era tan
Complacido con Ella, Él nos abandonó al resto y la llevó a un lugar apartado." Aquí el
La palabra "govindah" se refiere al Señor Krishna, el rey de Gokula. Este verso fue pronunciado por el vraja-
gopis.

records.sourceEnglish:
The different levels of gopés who love the Supreme Lord in the mood of sweetness, levels that
culimate in the love felt by Çré Rädhä, who has no equal or superior, will be described in this
anuccheda. Considering its causes and effects, scholars learned in ordinary material poetry call this
kind of love {.sy 168}sthäyi-bhäva" (continuous ecstatic love). The causes of sthäyi-bhäva are
vibhäva, anubhäva, and vyabhicäri-bhäva. These bhävas are all part of préti (ecstatic love). Sthäyi-
bhäva is described in these words of the rasa-çästra:


viruddhair aviruddhair vä
   bhävair vicchidyate na yaù
ätma-bhävaà nayaty anyän
   sa sthäyé lavaëäkaraù


  "Ecstatic love that is not diminished by favorable or unfavorable situations is called sthäyi-
bhäva, which is love deep like an ocean."

    Vibhäva and the other parts of love will be discussed later in this book. When sthäyi-bhäva and
its causes are manifest in the context of ecstatic love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead
(bhagavat-préti), then they are called "bhagavat-prétimaya-rasa", or "bhakti-rasa" (the mellows of

devotional service). That the bhävas thus become the rasas is described in the following words of
the rasa-çästra:


bhävä eväbhisampannäù
  prayänti rasa-rüpatäm


   "The bhävas become the rasas."

   Because they do not have the ingredients (sämagré) of the true rasas, the poets who relish the
material rasas (präkåta-rasikas) do not desire to taste the rasas of devotional service (bhakti-rasa).
Their sphere of tasting the rasas is limited to the material demigods or other material persons. The
sämagrés (igredients of the rasas are of three kinds: 1. svarüpa-yuogyatä sämagré, 2. parikara-yogyatä
sämagré, and 3. puruña-yogyatä sämagré. The svarüpa-yuogyatä sämagrés are the ingredients of sthäyi-
bhäva, rati and other sentiemnts when they are manifest in the material rasas. These sentiments
are based on the individual soul's desire to attain happiness for the Supreme Personality of
Godhead, that love brings happiness much greater than the waves of happiness attained by realizing
the impersonal Brahman. Persons in material consciousness cannot understand those sentiments,
which are called yogyatä sämagré. Only spiritual poets and philosophers can understand those
spiritual sentiments. These sentiments arevery beautiful and wonderful. The spiritual sentiments
felt by Çré Prahläda and the other great devotees are called puruña-yogyatä sämagré. Material poets
and philosophers who are not qualified like the great devotees cannot understand these sentiments.
This is described in the following words of Sähitya-darpaëa (3.2):


puëyavantaù pamaëvanti
  yogi-vad rasa-santatim


   "Only saintly devotees can understand the spiritual rasas."

   It is also said in Sähitya-darpaëa (3.8):


na jäyate tad-äsvädo
   vinä raty-ädi-väsanäm


   "Without rati (attraction) and the other sentiments, the taste of the rasas is not manifest."

   In the material rasas one tastes the pleasure of one's own happiness. This is described in the
following words of Sähitya-darpaëa (3.2):


sattvodrekäd akhaëòa-sva-

   prakäçänanda-cin-mayaù
vedyäntara-sparça-çünyo
   brahmäsväda-sahodaraù


   "When the mode of goodness becomes very strong, then limitless spiritual bliss becomes
manifest. When one tastes the bliss of the Supreme, then even the touch of knowledge of anything
else becomes absent. Knowledge of the Supreme and unawareness of anything else are like two
brothers.


lokottara-camatkära-
   präëaù kaiçcit pramätåbhiù
säkäravad abhinnatven-
   äyam äsvädyate rasaù


   "Some great souls know the spoiritual wonders beyond the reach of this world. They taste the
rasas of love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whose form is spiritual."

   Pure spiritual goodness (apräkåta-viçuddha-sattva) enables one to taste the spriitual rasas. This is
described in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (4.3.23):


sattvaà viçuddhaà vasudeva-çabditam. . .


   "I am always engaged in offering obeisances to Lord Väsudeva in pure Kåñëa consciousness.
Kåñëa consciousness is always pure consciousness (viçuddha-sattva), in which the Supreme
Personality of Godhead, known as Väsudeva, is revealed without any covering."*

   Spiritual pure goodness has already been described in the Bhagavat-sandarbha. That the taste of
rasas of love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead is sweeter than the taste of realizing the
impersonal Brahman is confirmed in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (4.9.10):


yä nirvåttis tanu-bhåtäm. . .


   "My Lord, the transcendental bliss derived from meditating upon Your lotus feet or hearing
about Your glories from pure devotees is so unlimited that it is far beyond thwe stage of
brahmänanda, wherein one thinks oneself merged in the impersonal Brahman as one with the
Supreme."*

   Tbis truth is also confirmed by the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (3.15.48):

nätyantikaà vigaëayanty api te prasädam. . .


   "Persons who are very expert and most intelligent in understanding things as they are engage in
hearing narrations of the auspicious activities and pastimes of the Lord, which are worth chanting
and worth hearing. Such persons do not care even for the highest material benediction, namely
liberation, to say nothing of less important other benedictions like the material happiness of the
heavenly kingdom."*

  That the rasas of perceiving the Supreme Personality of Godhead are very wonderful is
confirmed by these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (3.2.12):


vismäpanaà svasya ca saubhagarddheù. . .


   "The Lord appeared in the mortal world by His internal potency, yogamäyä. He came in His
eternal form, which is just suitable for His pastimes. These pastimes were wonderful for everyone,
even for thos proud of their own opulence, including the Lord Himself in His form as the Lord of
Vaikuëöha. Thus His (Çré Kåñëa's) transcendental body is the ornament of all ornaments."*

   The great authors of the past, who knew everything about the spiritual and material rasas, have
throughly explained ths topic of rasa. Rasa was also described in a general way by the author of Çré
Bhagavan-näma-kaumudé. The five rasas were explicitly described by Çréla Çrédhara Svämé in his
commentary on Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.43.17). There he said the word "stréëäm" referred to çåìgära-
rasa, "gopänäm" referred to the sakhä, priya-sakhä, and narma-sakhä friends of thw Lord, among
whom Çrédämä and many others are prominent, "pitroù" referred to the kind devotees in vätsalya-
rasa, "yoginäm" referred to the jïäni-bhaktas in çänta-rasa, {.sy 168}våñëénäm" referred to the
devoteed Våñëis, and "nåëäm" referred ot the people in general who loved the Lord. In this
description all the rasas, beginning with çänta-rasa, are wonderfully described. The rasas are also
explained by Dharma-datta in these words of Sähitya-darpaëa (3.2):


rase säraç camatkäraù
   sarvaträpy anubhüyate
tac-camatkära-säratve
   sarvaträpy adbhuto rasaù
tasmäd adbhutam eväha
   kåté näräyano rasam


   "Wonder is present everywhere in the rasas. The rasas are wonderful everywhere. Therefore,
saintly Näräyuaëa däsa says: the rasas are wonderful."

  Çréla Çrédhara Svami does not show honor to the rasas like raudra-rasa (anger) felt by the

wrestlers and others, for the persons in these rasas act like enemies of the Lord. The philosophers
who know the truths of the spiritual rasas agree with this view. Some philosopghers learned in the
material rasas especially honor sakhya-rasa and vatsalya-rasa. Of this view it is said:


sneha-sthäyi-bhävaù preyän


   "The ecstasy of sthäyi-bhäva is manifest in sakhya-rasa."

   Çåìgära-rasa is described ion these words:


yad eva rocate mahyaà
    tad eva kurute priyä
iti vetti na jänäti
    tat priyaà yat karoti sä


   "Whatever pleases me, my beloved does. I may be aware of her actions or not, but she always acts
to please me."

   Those words described the relationship of husband and wife. The following words describe
sakhya-rasa:


sphuöaà camatkäritatayä
   vatsalaà ca rasaà viduù
sthäyé vatsalatäsyeha
   puträdy-älambanaà matam


   "The sages know that vatsala-rasa is wonderful. In vatsala-rasa sthäyi-bhäva is manifest. Vatsala-
rasa is the love one feels for children and others in a like position."

   The sage Sudeva and others acknowledge vatsala-rasa as one of the bhakti-rasas. Furthermore,
material rati (attraction) and the material rasas may bring pleasure in the beginning, but in the end
they bring suffering. This the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself confirmed in these words of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (11.19.41):


  . . .sukhaà duùkha-sukhätyayaù
duùkham käma-sukhäpekñä


  "Real happiness is to transcend material happiness and unhappiness, and real misery is to be
implicated in searching for sex pleasure."***

  The Supreme (ord describes true peace in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (11.19.36):


çamo man-niñöhatä buddheù


   "True peace is attained when one faithfully rests his intelligence in Me."

   In these weords the Supreme Lord criticizes material pleasures, which bring horrible results.
Even the ordinary people of this world eventually come to hate material pleasures. Criticizing
material so-called pleasures and praising the rasas of love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead,
Çré Närada explains in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (1.5.10-11):


na yad-vacaç citra-padaà harer yaço
   jagat-pavitraà pragåëéta karhicit
tad väyasaà tértham uçanti mänasä
   na yatra haàsä niramanty uçik-kñayäù


   "Those words which do not describe the glories of the Lord, who alone can sanctify the
atmosphere of the whole universe, are considered by saintly persons to be like unto a pilgrimage for
crows. Since the all-perfect persons are inhabitants of the transcendental abode, they do not derive
any pleasure there.*


tad-väg-visargo janatägha-viplavo
   yasmin prati-çlokam abaddhavaty api
nämäny anantasya yaço 'ìkitäni yat
   çåëvanti gäyanti gåëanti sädhavaù


   "On the other hand, that literature which is full of descriptions of the transcendental glories of
the name, fame, forms, pastimes, etc. of the unlimited Supreme Lord is a different creation, full of
transcendental words directed toward bringing about a revolution in the impious lives of this
world's misdirected civilization. Such transcendental literatures, even though imperfectly
composed, are heard, sung, and accepted by purified men who are thoroughly honest."*

   The material rasas are also rejected by Queen rukmiëé, who says in Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.60.45):


tvak-çmaçru-roma-nakha-keça-pinaddham antar
   mäàsästhi-rakta-kåimi-viö-kapha-pitta-vätam
jévac-chavaà bhajati känta-matir vimüòhä

   yä te padäbja-makarandam ajighraté stré


   "A woman who fails to relish the fragranc of the honey of Your lotus feet becomes totally
befooled, and thus she accepts as her husband or lover a living corpse covered with skin, whiskers,
nails, head-hair, and body hair, and filled with flesh, bones, blood, parasites, feces, mucus, bile, and
air."*

   Therefore one should not place his faith in the material rasas, for the material rasas always lead
to a situation filled with horrors. The rasas of love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, on the
other hand, lead to liberation from the material world. If the material reasas lead only to distress
and the spiritual rasas lead to liberation, why then do the foolish people not relish the spiritual
rasas? The answer is given in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.1.4):


nivåtta-tarñair upagéyamänät. . .


    "Glorification of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is performed in the parampara system.
That is, it is conveyed from spiritual master ot disciple. Such gloreification is relished by those no
longer interested in the false, temporary glorification of this cosmic manifestation. Descriptions of
the Lord are the right medicine for the conditioned soul undergoing repeated birth and death.
Therefore, who will cease hearing such glorification of the Lord except a butcher or one who is
killing his own self?"*

   The sweetness of thew spiritual rasas is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.21.19):


aspandanaà gati-matäà pulakas tarüëäm. . .


   "When Lord Kåñëa plays on His flute, the sweet music causes the moving living entities to
become stunned and the nonmoving trees to tremble in ecstasy. These things are certainly very
wonderful."***

   The spiritual rasas of association with Lord Kåñëa brought the devotees back to life. This is
described in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.17.15):


kåñëam sametya labdhehä
   äsan çuñkä nagä api


  "Having regained their vital functions, Yaçodä, Rohiëé, Nanda and all the other cowherd women
and men went up to Kåñna. O descendant of Kuru, even the dried-up trees came back to life."***

  The Puräëa Çrémad-Bhägavatam teaches the rasas of love for the Supreme Personality of
Godhead. This is confirmed by the following words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 1.1.3):


nigama-kalpa-taroù. . .


   "O expert and thoughtful men, rlish Çrémad-Bhägavatam, the mature fruit of the desire tree of
Vedic literatures. It emanated from the lips of Çré Çukadeva Gosvämé. Therefore this fruit has
become even more tasteful, although its nectarean juice weas already relishable for all, including
liberated souls."*

   This verse means: "O auspicious souls learned in the rasas of love for the Supreme Personality of
Godhead, in your hearts please relish the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whioch is the sweet
fruit of desire tree of the Vedas, a tree with many branches and sub-branches that bear all fruits, a
tree that has come to this earth from the spiritual world of Vaikuëöha." Here the word "aho"
ismnused to hint that Çrémad-Bhägavatam enables one to attain what is otherwise unattainable.
The scripture Çrémad-Bhägavatam is desdcriubeed here with the w0ord "rasa" because it is sweet
with the spiritual rasas. It is called Bhägavatam because it describes the rasas of love for Bhagavän
(the Supreme Personality of Godhead). That Çrémad-Bhägavatam is filled with the reasas of love
for the Supreme Personality of Godhead is described in these words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 1.7.7):


yasyäà vai çrüyamäëäyäà. . .


   "Simply by giving aural reception to this Vedic literature (Çrémad-Bhägavatam), the feeling for
loving devotional service to Lord Kåñëa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, sprouts up at once to
extinguish the fire of lamentation, illusion and fearfulness."*

  The word "rasa" is used in relation to the Supreme Personality of Godhead in these words of
Taittiriya Upanisad (2.7.1):


raso vai saù. rasaà hy eväyaà labdhvänandé-bhavati.


  "When one understands the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the reservoir of pleasure (rasa),
Kåñëa, he actually becomes transcendentally blissful."*

   In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 1.1.3 the word "rasikäù" shows that the sages who attained perfection in
ancient times as well as the sages who attained perfection in recent tiomes knew the truth of the
rasas. The word "galitam" shows that the fruit here is perfectly ripe and sweet. Here it is seen that
because it has come from the tree of the scriptures, this fruit is very sweet and delicious. "Rasam"
here shows that this fruit has neither skin nor pit. It has no defect in any way. The words

"bhägavatam nigamasya" here show that Çrémad-Bhägavatam is the best of all the sacred fruits of
the tree of the scriptures. This is so because it teaches the highest goal of life. Even though the
nectar of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is naturally very excellent, it is made even more
excellent in Çrémad-Bhägavatam. This is shown here by the word "çuka". Although the fruit of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam is very wonderful because it has fallen from the kalpa-våkña tree of the
scriptures, it is made even more sweet and nectarean becase it is touched by ther mouth of Çréla
Çukadeva Gosvämé. When it touches Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé's mouth, that fruit becoems sweeter.
When they come from the mouth of a great devotee, descroptions of the Supreme Personality of
Godhead become sweeter. How much more is this true when such descriptions come from the
mouth of Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé, the king of all great devotees? By tasting ther nectar of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam one will never become satiated. His desire to taste it will never become diminished.
Therefore, even after attaining liberation (älayam), one should drink (pibata) the nectar of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam. That even liberated souls are attracted to Çrémad-Bhägavatam is confirmed by Çréla
Çukadeva Gosvämé in the following words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 2.1.9):


pariniñöhito 'pi. . .


   "O saintly king, I was perfectly situated in transcendence, yet I was still attracted by the
delineation of the pastimes of the Lord, who is described by enlightened verses."*

    The sweetness of other things fades in the course of time. The sweetness of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
is not like that. It does not fade. The reasas of love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead are of
two kinds: 1. préty-upayukta and 2. préti-pariëäma. These are described in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (12.3.14-15):


kathä imäs te kathitä mahéyasäà
   vitatya lokeñu yaçaù pareyuñäm
vijïäna-vairägya-vivakñayä vibho
   vaco-vibhütir na tu päramärthyam


   "O mighty Pariksit, I have related to you the narrations of all these great kings, who spread their
fame throughout the world and then departed. My real purpose was to teach transcendental
knowledge and renunciation. Stories of kings lend power and opulence to these narrations but do
not in themselves constitute the ultimate aspect of knwoledge.***


yas tüttama-çloka-guëänuvädaù
   saìgéyate 'bhikñëam amaìgala-ghnaù
tam eva nityaà çåëuyäd abhikñëaà
   kåñëe 'maläà bhaktim abhipsamänaù

   "The person who desires pure devotional service to Lord Kåñëa should hear the narrations of
Lord Uttamaçloka's glorious qualities, the constant chanting of which destoys everything
inauspicious. The devotee should engage in such listening in regular daily assemblies and should
also continue his hearing throughout the day."***

   After describing the rasas in a general way, Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé describes thme in more
detail in the word {.sy 168}amåta". "Amåta" here refers to the nectar of the Lord's pastimes, nectar
described in these owrds of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (12.13.11):


hari-lélä-kathä-vrätä-
   måtänandita-sat-suram


   "Çrémad-Bhägavatam is full of nectarean accounts of Lord Kåñëa's pastimes, which guve ecstasy
ot the
saintly devotees and demigods."

   That narrations of Lord's pastimes are sweet is confirmed by these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(12.4.40):


lélä-kathä-rasa-niñevaëam. . .


   "Narrations of lord Kåñëa's pastimes are sweet like nectar."

   In the word "sat-suram" from Çrémad-Bhägavatam 12.13.11, the word "sat" refers to the ätmäräma
transcendentalists situated in Brahman realization, who are referred to by thew word "satäm" in
Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.12.11, and the word "suram" refers to the devotees who taste only the nectar
of devotional service ot the Lord. In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 1.1.3 the word "amrta-drava" means {.sy
168}the sweetest nectar of the Lord's pastimes". The following exp"lanation may be given: Although
the nectar of love (pritimaya-rasa) for the Supreme Personality of Godhead is the sweetest of all
nectars (sreyah), various levels of that nectar be certainly be distinguished. The taste of the nectar
of the rasas, as described in the word "pibata" is of two kinds, the first of which is the rasas tasted by
the Lord's personal associates who personally participate in the Supreme Lord's pastimes. This
perception of the rasas is the best, because it is direct and confidential (antaraìga). The other
perception of the rasas is tasted y all others. It is indirect and not confidential (bahiraìga). These
two levels of the perception of the nectar of the rasas are both described here by the single word
"pibata". This nectar is like a river flowing from the mouth of Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé. That Çrémad-
Bhägavatam describes the sweetest nectar of love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead is
confirmed by these words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 12.13.15):


sarva-vedänta-säraà hi. . .

. . .tad-rasämåta-tåptasya. . .


   "Çrémad-Bhägavatam is declared to be the essence of all Vedänta philosophy. One who has felt
satisfaction from its nectarean mellow will never be attracted by any other literature."***

   In His commentary Çréla Çrédhara Svami defines the word {.sy 168}bhavukah" in this way:

   " `Bhävukäù' here means `they who are expert at meditating on the nectar rasas'."

   This meditation is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (1.5.19):


smaran mukundäìghry-upagühanaà punar
  vidhätum icchen na rasa-graho janaù

records.sourceEnglish:
Thus joined with vibhäva and its other components, the rasac of love for the Supreme
Personality of Godhead is manifest. They who are learned i n the material rasas shown in dramas
describe four kinds of characters. First is the hero who is primarily served by the rasa. He is the first
character in the drama. Then there is the person who because of being limited, or because of fear or
some other impediment, becomes a follower or servant of the hero. That person, the follower or
servant, is the second kind of character. Then there is a person who, an ordinary person among the
people in general who, because he is unintelligent and needs to accept instructions and orders,
becomes a follower or servant of the hero. That follower or servant is the third kind of character.
Can the follower or servant who is the second character not be intelligent? If he is he becomes the
fourth kind of character. The devotees of the Lord taste the rasas of love for the Supreme
Personality of Godhead. In this way the rasas theytaste are not material in nature. In this way the
rasas of love present in the hearts of this hero and His servants and followers are eternal. They are
perfect and complete. In this way it is demonstrated that the rasas of love for the Supreme
Personality of Godhead are limitless and spiritual in nature. They are not like the material rasas
described in material poems. That is their nature. For example, it is seen that Çré Prahläda, the
vraja-gopés, and many other devotees were completely unaffected by fear, and Çré Vrtra, Çré
Gajendra, Çré Bharata, and other devotees were completely unaffected by the actions of their
previous births. What more need be said? Çré Çukadeva Gosvämé and other devotees were
completely unaffected by the bliss of impersonal Brahman realization. In these ways it should be
known that the love they felt for the Supreme Personality of Godhead was certainly spiritual in

nature. It was not material. Here the älambana (main cause of feeling the rasa of love) is the
Supreme Lord's opulences glories, and virtues, which have no equal or superior. The personal
assaociates of the Lord have spiritual qualities like the Lord's. This truth is proclaimed by the great
dundubhi drums that are the Vedas, Puräëas, and other scriptures. The uddépanas (secondary
causes of feeling the rasa of love) are the things in relation to the Lord. These secondary causes of
rasa are described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (3.15.43):


tasyäravinda-nayanasya. . .
 . . .cakära teñäà
     saìkñobham akñara-juñäm api citta-tanvoù


   "When the breeze carrying the aroma of tulasé leaves from the toes of the lotus feet of the
Supreme Personality of Godhead entered the nostrils of those sages, they experienced a change
both in body and in mind, even though they were attached to the impersonal Brahman
understanding."*

  The Supreme Lord's handsomeness as a cause of rasa is seen in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.44.14):


gopyas tapaù kim acaran. . .


   "What austerities must the gopés have performed! With their eyes they always drink the nectar
of Lord Kåñëa's form, which is the essence of loveliness and is not to be equaled or surpassed. That
loveliness is the only abode of beauty, fame, and opulence. It is self-perfect, ever fresh and
extremely rare.*

   The causes of rasa are also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.29.40):


kä stry aìga. . .
. . .yad go-dvija-druma-mågäù pulakäny abibhran


   "Dear Kåñëa, what woman in all the three worlds wouldn't deviate from religious behavior when
bewildered by the sweet, drawn-out melody of Your flute? Your beauty makes all three worlds
auspicious. Indeed, even the cows, birds, trees and deer manifest the ecstatic symptom of bodily hair
standing on end when they see Your beautiful form."***

   Lord Kåñëa's flute-music as a cause of rasa is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.35.14-
15):

vividha-gopa-caraëeñu vidagdhaù. . .

. . .savanaças tad upadhärya sureçäh
    çakra-sarva-parameñöhi-purogaù
kavaya änata-kandhara-cittäù
    kaçmalaà yayur aniçcita-tattväù


   "O pious mother Yaçodä, your son, who is expert in all the arts of herding cows, has invented
many new styles of flute-playing. When He takes His flute to His bimba-red lips and sends forth the
tones of the harmonic scale in variegated melodies, Brahmä, Siva, Indra and other chief demigods
become confused upon hearing the sound. Although they are the most learned authorities, they
cannot ascertain the essence of that music, and thus they bow down their heads and hearts."***

   That the accidental manifestation of one of the Lord's potencies can become a cause of spiritual
rasa is seen in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.20.31):


prävåt-çriyaà ca täà vékñya
   sarva-käla-sukhävaham
bhagavän püjayäà cakre
   ätma-çakty-upabåàhitam


   "Observing the beauty and opulence of Våndävana's rainy season, a perennial source of great
happiness, the Lord offered all respect to that season, which was expanded from His own internal
potency."***

   Here the clouds and other features of the rainy season bring ecstatis symptoms, like standing up
of the body's hairs.

   It is said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.21.19):


aspandanaà gati-matäà pulakas tarünäm


   "When Lord Kåñëa plays on His flute, the sweet music causes the moving living entities to
become stunned and the nonmoving trees to tremble with ecstasy. These things are certainly very
wonderful."***

   Here even the trees and other like living entities wonderfully become like human beings. Even
grief and other like emotions can help one taste the spiritual rasas. In that greif it is said there may
come madness or other like conditions caused by sorrow and by separation from the Lord. These
emotions can certainly be manifest on the spiritusl platform. The spiritual world is described in
these words of Brahma-saàhitä (5.56-57):

çriyaù käntäù käntaù parama-puruñaù kalpa-taravo
   drumä bhümiç cintämaëi-gaëa-mayé toyam amåtam
kathä gänaà näöyaà gamanam api vaàçé priya-sakhé
   cid-änandaà jyotiù param api tad äsvädyam api ca

sa yatra kñéräbdhiù sravati surabhébhyaç ca su-mahän
   nimeñärdhäkhyo vä vrajati na hi yaträpi samayaù
bhaje çvetadvépaà tam aham iha golokam iti yaà
   vidantas te santaù kñiti-virala-cäräù katipaye


   "I worship thyat transcendental seat, known as Çvetadvépa, where as loving consorts the Lakñmés
in their unalloyed spiritual essence practice the amorous service ofnthe Supreme Lord Kåñëa as
their only lover, where every tree is a transcendental purpose tree, where the sopil is the purpose
gem, all water is nectar, every word is a song, every gait is a dance, the flute is the favorite
attendant, effulgence is full of transcendental bliss, and the supreme spiritual entities are all
enjoyable and tasty, where numberless milk cows always emit transcendental oceans of milk, where
there is eternal existence of transcendental time, who is ever-present and without past or future
and hence is nto subject to the quality of passing away even for the space of half a moment. That
realm is known nas Goloka only to a very few self-realized souls in this world."**

   Here the words "gänaà näöyam" refer to the rasas. The causes that create the rasas of love for
the supreme hero, Lord Kåñëa, rasas that are spiritual and have many spiritual quialities, are called
vibhävas. The vibhävas are described in these words of Sähitya-darpaëa (3.13):


vibhävanaà raty-äder viçeñeëäsvädäìkura-yogyatänayanam. anubhävanam evam-bhütasya raty-
ädeù samantaram eva rasädi-rüpatayä bhävanam. saïcäraëam tathä-bhütasya tasyaiva samyak
cäraëam.


   "Vibhäva makes rati and the other aspects of rasas first appear as a new sprout. Comeing after
vibhäva, anubhäva enables one to directly perceive the nature of rasa. Then saïcäri-bhäva makes
the rasas become active."

    Even material poets who know the material rasas say that happiness can arise out of sorrow. We
also say that spiritual bliss can arise even out of separation from the Lord. Externally the devotee
separated from the Lord may seem to be sorrowful. However, during the anguish of separation the
supremely blissful Lord is always manifest in the devotee's thoughts. Therefore the devotee is also
filled with intense spiritual bliss. In such a situation it is not possible for the devotee to avoid those
two emotions of anguish and bliss. These two emoptions do nto contradict each other. Rather they
are like sweetened hot milk placed before a hungry person. The two features of sweetness and heat
do not negate each other. Rather they compliment each other. In this way the anguish of

separation from the Lord is actually the cause of intense spiritual bliss, just as the shining of the
moon and stars is a source of pleasure. Because it is nourished by the memory of the bliss of directly
associating with the Supreme Lor, the anguish of separation brings bliss with it. In that state of
separatuion the karuëa-rasa (the rasa of a pitiable condition) is manifest. At that time the devotee
yearns to be with the Lord. In this way the manifeastatoon of the rasas of love for ther supreme
hero, Lord Kåñëa, is described. The rasas arise in two primary ways: 1. the love (anuräga) created by
hearing, and 2. the love created by seeing. These are both described in the following words of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.90.26):


çruta-mätro 'pi yaù stréëäà
   prasahyäkarñate manaù
uru-gäyoru-géto vä
   paçyanténäà ca kià punaù


   "The Lord, whom countless songs glorify in countless ways, forcibly attracts the minds of all
women who simply hear about Him. What to speak, then, of those women who see Him
directly?"***

   The arisal of the rasa of love for the Lord is described by Uddhava in the following two verses of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.6.44-45):


tava vikréòitaà brahman. . .


    "My dear Kåñëa, Your pastimes are supremely auspicious for mankind and are an intoxicating
beverage for the ears. Tasting such pastimes, people forget their desires for other things.***
    "My dear Lord, You are the Supreme Soul, and thus You are most dear to us. We are Your
devotees, and how can we possibly reject You or live without You for even a moment? Whether we
ar lying down, sitting, walkign, standing, bathing, enjoying recreation, eating, or doing anything
else, we are constantly engaged in Your service."***

   The anukartä, or follower or servant of the Lord is thus a devotee of the Lord.Non-devotees
cannot become followers or servants of the Lord. The rasas of love for the Lord arise amongst the
devotees. Here the word "anukartä" should not be inter"reted to mean "imitator". It is not possible
for the individual spirit souls to imitate the actions of the Lord. The attempt to imitate the Lord is
against the principles of devotional service. The devotees associate with the Lord and directly
perceive Him, but they never become one with Him. In this way the uddépanas of the rasas, which
arouse the devotees' love, enchance the Lord's pastimes. If the pure devotees sometimes imitate the
Lord, the devotees always think, "the Lord is mine". They never think, "I have become the Lord. I
am the Lord." That kind of imitation is seen in Vasudeva's son Gada and the Lord's other brothers,
who think themselves the Lord's equal. Their sentiments are not against the principles of
devotional service. The ordinary (sämäjika) devtees yearn to attain such a glorious position. In

dåçya-kävyas (staged dramas), the audience sees with their eyes and meditates on the rasas. In
çravya-kävyas (recited narrative poems), the audioence hears the descriptions of the Lord. In this
way the audience meditates on the Lord. The sprout of rati (attraction to the Lord) arises within
them. They attain great love (prema) for the Lord. Melodies in the sixth note may also be a cause
(uddépana) of rasa. This is described in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (6.5.22):


svara-brahmaëi nirbhäta-
   håñékeça-padämbuje
akhaëòaà cittam äveçya
   lokän anucaran muniù


   "The seven musiacl notes-sa, å, gä, ma, pa, dha, and ni-are used in musical instruments, but
originally they come from the Säma Veda. The great sage Närada vibrates sounds describing the
pastimes of the Supreme Lord. By such transcendental vibrations such as Hare Kåñëa, Hare Kåñëa,
Kåñëa Kåñëa, Hare Hare, Hare Räma, Hare Räma, Räma Räma, Hare Hare,, he fixes his mind at
the lotus feet of the Lord. Thus he directly perceives Håñékeça, the master of the senses. After
delivering the Haryaçvas, Närada Muni continued traveling throughout the planetary systems, His
mind always fixed at the lotus feet of the Lord."*

  Prema and the other kinds of ecstatic love (bhävas) create the sämagrés (ingredients of rasa).
This is described in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (7.4.39-41):


kvacid rudati vaikuëöha-
  cintä-çabala-cetasaù. . .

 . . .kvacid utpulakas tuñëém
     äste samsparça-nirvåtaù
aspanda-praëayänanda-
     salilämilitekñaëaù


   "Because of advancement in Kåñëa consciousness, he sometimes cried, sometimes laughed,
sometimes expressed jubilation, and sometimes sang loudly.*
   "Sometimes, upon seeing the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Prahläda Maharaja would loudly
call in full anxiety. He sometimes lost his shyness in jubilation and began dancing in ecstasy, and
sometimes, being fully absorbed in thoughts of Kåñëa, he felt oneness and imitated the pastimes of
the Lord.*
   "Sometimes, feeling the touch of the Lord's lotus hands, he became spiritually jubilant and
remained silent, his hairs standing on end and tears gliding down from his half-closed eyes because
of his love for the Lord."*

   Materialists who relish the material rasas are attracted by something that is imperfect and

incomplete. Persons who taste the rasas of love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead (bhagavat-
préti-rasika) are of two kinds: 1. the devotees who directly participate in the Lord's pastimes (tadéya-
léläntah-päti), and 2. the devotees who aspire to participate in the Lord's pastimes (tadéya-léläntah-
pätitäbhimäna). Because of their past devotional activities, the devotees ion the first group attained
the Lord's direct association. The devotees in the second group are of two kinds: 1. the devotees who
hear description of ther Lord's pastimes with His personal associates, and 2. the devotees who hear
descriptions of the Lord's sweetness and other transcendental qualities. If a devotee in the first of
these two groups desires in the sameee way the personal associates of the Lord desire, then that
devotee eventually becomes the Lord's personal associate. Then that devotee attains the vibhävas
and other elements of rsas manifest in a personal associate of the Lord. How the gopés think is seen
in the following words of Sähitya-darpaëa (3.12):


parasya na parasyeti
   na mameti mameti ca
tad-äsväde vibhävädeù
   paricchedo na vidyate


    "My beloved may be another's husband, or He may not be another's husband. He may be my
husband, or he may not be my husband. When I taste the vibhävas and other elements of the rasas
of love for Him, it makes no difference to me if He is my husband or not."

   If a devotee desires in a way different from the way the Lord's personal associates desire, then
that devotee attains vibhäva, anubhäva, and saïcäri-bhäva that are generally ordinary in nature.
Even when the uddépanas (which arouse the feelings of rasa) are present, that devotee does not
perceive the sweetness of rasa. If a devotee desires ina way that opposes the the way the Lord's
personal associates desire, then, even if the uddépanas of vatsalya-rasa and the other rasas are
present, that devotee will not perceive the different bhävas (ecstasies of love), nor will he perceive
the sweetness of rasa. Now we will discuss the devotees who hear descriptions of the Lord's
sweetness and other transcendental qualities. These devotees are are independent like the Lord's
personal associates who participate in the Lord's pastimes. These devotees have th4e power to
perceive the sweetness of rasa. Now the perfection of the reasas of love for the Supreme Personality
of Godhead will be considered. When love for thweSupreme Personality of Godhead (bhagavat-
préti) is mixed with the vibhävas and other elements of rasa, the result is the rasas of love for the
Supreme Personality of Godhead (bhagavat-prétimaya-rasa). This is described in the following
words of Sähitya-darpaëa (3.15):


yathä khaëòa-marécädénäà sammelanäd apürva iva kaçcid äsvädaù prapänaka-rase saïjäyate.
vibhävädi-sammelanäd ihäpi tathä.


   "As sugar, black pepper, and other ingredients make a drink delightful for the tongue, so the
vibhävas and other elements of rasa make the rasas delightful to taste."

   The sweetness of the Lord is counted among the uddépanas, the secondary elements that help
one to taste the spiritual rasas. The Supreme Lord Himself is the älambana, the primary element
that enables one to taste the spiritual rasas. The älambanas and uddépanas are described in these
words of Agni Puräëa:


vibhävyate hi raty-äder
   yatra yena vibhävyate
vibhävo näma sa devdhä-
   lambanoddépanätmakaù


   "Vibhäva enables one to perceive rati and the other elements of rasa. Vibhäva is of two kinds: 1.
älambana, and 2. uddépana."

   The älambana may be of two kinds: 1. Lord Kåñëa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is
dearly loved by the devotees, and 2. the Lord's devotees, who are filled with lofve for Him. These
two kinds ofälambanas are indicsted in Sanskrit by use of the locative case. Lord Kåñëa as the
älambana is described in these owrds of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (9.24.65):


yasyänanaà makara-kuëòala. . .


   "Kåñëa's face is decorated with ornaments, such as earrings resembling sharks. His ears are
beautiful, His cheeks brilliant, and His smiling attractive to everyone. Whoever sees Lord Kåñëa
sees a festival. His face and body are fully satisfying for everyone to see."*

   Lord Kåñëa as the älambana is also described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.44.14):


gopyas tapaù kim acaran yad amuñya rüpam


   "What austerities must the gopés have performed! With their eyes they always drink the nectar
of Lord Kåñëa's form, which is the essence of loveliness and is not to be equaled or surpassed. That
lovliness is the only abode of beauty, fame, and opulence. It is self-perfect, ever fresh and extremely
rare."*

  As long as Lord Kåñëa's sweetness is not manifest, the individual soul will see his own self as the
most dear and lovable being in the whole world. This is described in the following words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.23.27):


präëa-buddhi-manaù-svätma-

   däräpatya-dhanädayaù
yat-samparkät priyä äsaàs
   tataù ko nv aparaù priyaù


   "It is only by contact with the self that one's vital breath, intelligence, mind, friends, body, wife,
children, wealth and so on are dear. Therefore what object can possibly be more dear than one's
own self?"***

   In this verse the word "sva" means "the pure soul", "ätmä" means "the material body", and "yat-
samparkät" means "because of my contact with that". This verse implies: "As a spirit soul I am full of
spiritual bliss. Therefore I am dear to myself." This verse also implies: "Because I am His part-and-
parcel, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the Supersoul in my heart, is also dear to me." This
verse also implies: "The things in relation to me are also dear to me." Thus the vital breath and
other things are dear because of their relation to the soul. Even when He appears in many different
forms, the Supreme Personality of Godhead is always dear to the individual soul. This is seen in the
following words spoken by Lord Balaräma in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.13.36):


kim etad adbhutam iva
   väsudeve'khilätmani
vrajasya sätmanas tokeñv
   apürvaà prema vardhate


  "What is this wonderful phenomenon? The affection of all the inhabitants of Vraja, including
Me, toward these boys and calves is increasing as never before, just like our affection for Lord
Kåñëa, the Supersoul of all living entities."*

   Lord Kåñëa's own form is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.23.22):


çyämaà hiraëya-paridhià vanamälya-barha-
   dhätu-praväla-naöa-veñam anuvratäàse
vinyasta-hastam itareëa dhunänam abjaà
   karëotpalälaka-kapola-mukhäbja-häsam


   "His complexion was dark blue and His garment golden. Wearing a peacock feather, colored
minerals, sprigs of flower buds, and a garland of forest flowers and leaves, He was dressed just like a
dramatic dancer. He rested one hand upon the shoulder of a friend and the with the other twirled a
lotus. Lilies graced His ears, His hair hung down over His cheeks, and His lotuslike face was
smiling."***

  The words of this verse imply: "Will you not become wonderfully attracted to these features of
Lord Kåñëa?" Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.23.27, quoted in this anuccheda, was spoken by Lord Kåñëa to

the yajïa-patnés.

realización. De estas maneras debe saberse que el amor que sentían por la Suprema Personalidad

tasyaravinda-nayanasya. . .

"Cuando la brisa trae el aroma de las hojas de tulasi desde los dedos de los pies de loto de la
La Suprema Personalidad de Dios entró por las fosas nasales de aquellos sabios, y experimentaron un cambio.

La belleza del Señor Supremo como causa de rasa se ve en estas palabras del srimad-

gopyas tapah kim acaran. . .

de la forma del Señor Krishna, que es la esencia de la hermosura y no debe ser igualada ni superada.

y extremadamente raro.

ka stry anga. . . . . .yad go-dvija-druma-mrgah pulakany abibhran
"Querido Krishna, ¿qué mujer en los tres mundos no se desviaría del comportamiento religioso cuando...

"Se les eriza el vello al ver tu hermosa figura."
La música de flauta del Señor Krishna como causa de rasa se ve en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam.
(10.35.14-15):
vividha-gopa-caranesu vidagdhah. . .
. . .savanasas tad upadharya suresah
sakra-sarva-paramesthi-purogah kavaya anata-kandhara-cittah
kasmalam yayur aniscita-tattvah
"Oh piadosa madre Yasoda, tu hijo, que es experto en todas las artes del pastoreo de vacas, ha inventado
muchos estilos nuevos de tocar la flauta. Cuando Él lleva su flauta a sus labios rojos como el bimba y envía
los tonos de la escala armónica en melodías variadas, Brahma, Siva, Indra y otros principales
Los semidioses se confunden al oír el sonido. Aunque son las autoridades más sabias,
No pueden comprender la esencia de esa música, y por eso inclinan la cabeza y el corazón.

El rasa espiritual se observa en las siguientes palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.20.31):
pravrt-sriyam ca tam viksya
sarva-kala-sukhavaham bhagavan pujayam cakre
atma-sakty-upabrmhitam
"Observando la belleza y la opulencia de la temporada de lluvias de Vrindavana, una fuente perenne de gran
felicidad, el Señor ofreció todo respeto a esa temporada, que fue expandida desde Su propio interior
potencia."
Aquí las nubes y otras características de la temporada de lluvias traen síntomas de éxtasis, como estar de pie
desde el vello corporal.
Se dice en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.21.19):
aspandanam gati-matam pulakas tarunam
"Cuando el Señor Krishna toca su flauta, la dulce música hace que los seres vivos en movimiento...
quedar aturdidos y los árboles inmóviles temblar de éxtasis. Estas cosas son ciertamente muy
maravilloso."
Aquí, incluso los árboles y otros seres vivos similares se convierten maravillosamente en seres humanos.
El dolor y otras emociones similares pueden ayudar a uno a saborear los rasas espirituales. En ese dolor se dice
Puede sobrevenir la locura u otras afecciones similares causadas por el dolor y por la separación del Señor.
Estas emociones ciertamente pueden manifestarse en la plataforma espiritual. El mundo espiritual es
descrito en estas palabras del Brahma-samhita (5.56-57):
sriyah kantah kantah parama-purusah kalpa-taravo
druma bhumis cintamani-gana-mayi toyama amrtam katha ganam natyam gamanam api vamsi priya-sakhi
cid-anandam jyotih param api tad asvadyam api ca
sa yatra ksirabdhih sravati surabhibhyas ca su-mahan
nimesardhakhyo va vrajati na hola yatrapi samayah bhaje svetadvipam tam aham iha golokam iti yam
vidantas te santah ksiti-virala-carah katipaye
"Yo adoro el trono trascendental Thyat, conocido como Svetadvipa, donde como consortes amorosos los
Las Lakshmis, en su esencia espiritual pura, practican el servicio amoroso del Señor Supremo.
Krishna como su único amante, donde cada árbol es un árbol de propósito trascendental, donde el sopil es
la gema del propósito, toda el agua es néctar, cada palabra es una canción, cada andar es una danza, la flauta es
el asistente favorito, el resplandor está lleno de dicha trascendental y la espiritualidad suprema
Las entidades son todas agradables y sabrosas, donde innumerables vacas lecheras siempre emiten trascendental
océanos de leche, donde existe la existencia eterna del tiempo trascendental, que está siempre presente y
sin pasado ni futuro y por lo tanto no está sujeto a la cualidad de desaparecer incluso para el espacio
de medio instante. Ese reino es conocido como Goloka solo por unas pocas almas autorrealizadas en este
mundo."
Aquí las palabras "ganam natyam" se refieren a los rasas. Las causas que crean los rasas del amor.
para el héroe supremo, el Señor Krishna, rasas que son espirituales y tienen muchas cualidades espirituales,
se llaman vibhavas. Los vibhavas se describen en estas palabras de Sahitya-darpana (3.13):
vibhavanam raty-ader visesenasvadankura-yogyatanayanam. anubhavanam evam-bhutasya raty-adeh
samantaram eva rasadi-rupataya bhavanam. sacaranam tatha-bhutasya tasyaiva samyak caranam.
"Vibhava hace que rati y los otros aspectos de los rasas aparezcan primero como un nuevo brote. Al venir
Después de vibhava, anubhava permite percibir directamente la naturaleza de rasa. Luego sacari-bhava
hace que los rasas se activen."
Incluso los poetas materialistas, que conocen los rasas materiales, dicen que la felicidad puede surgir del dolor.
También decimos que la dicha espiritual puede surgir incluso de la separación del Señor. Externamente,
El devoto separado del Señor puede parecer triste. Sin embargo, durante la angustia de
La separación del Señor supremamente dichoso siempre se manifiesta en los pensamientos del devoto. Por lo tanto,
El devoto también está lleno de una intensa dicha espiritual. En tal situación no es posible
el devoto para evitar esas dos emociones de angustia y dicha. Estas dos emociones no
se contradicen entre sí. Más bien son como leche caliente endulzada puesta delante de una persona hambrienta.
Las dos características de dulzura y picante no se anulan entre sí. Al contrario, se complementan.
De esta manera, la angustia de la separación del Señor es en realidad la causa de una intensa espiritualidad.

Se manifiesta una condición lamentable. En ese momento, el devoto anhela estar con el Señor. De esta manera
Se describe la manifestación de los rasas del amor por su héroe supremo, el Señor Krishna.
Los rasas surgen de dos maneras principales: 1. el amor (anuraga) creado por la audición, y 2. el amor creado

El anukarta, o seguidor o sirviente del Señor, es por lo tanto un devoto del Señor. No devotos

devotos. Aquí la palabra "anukarta" no debe interpretarse como "imitador". No es

Los rasas, que despiertan el amor de los devotos, realzan los pasatiempos del Señor. Si los devotos puros
A veces imitan al Señor, los devotos siempre piensan: "El Señor es mío". Nunca piensan: "Yo

"A veces, al sentir el toque de las manos de loto del Señor, se llenaba de júbilo espiritual y

Los priti-rasika) son de dos tipos: 1. los devotos que participan directamente en los pasatiempos del Señor

(tadiya-lilantah-patitabhimana). Debido a sus actividades devocionales pasadas, los devotos en el
El primer grupo alcanzó la asociación directa con el Señor. Los devotos del segundo grupo son de dos

cualidades. Si un devoto del primero de estos dos grupos desea de la misma manera la personal
Si un devoto desea algo, entonces eventualmente se convierte en el asociado personal del Señor.
Entonces ese devoto alcanza los vibhavas y otros elementos de los rasas que se manifiestan en un ser personal.

parasya na parasyeti

"Mi amado puede ser el marido de otra, o puede que no sea el marido de otra. Puede que sea mi
esposo, o puede que no sea mi esposo. Cuando pruebo los vibhavas y otros elementos de los rasas
Por el amor que le tengo, me da igual si es mi marido o no."
Si un devoto desea algo de una manera diferente a como lo desean los asociados personales del Señor,
entonces ese devoto alcanza vibhava, anubhava y sacari-bhava que son generalmente ordinarios en
naturaleza. Incluso cuando los uddipanas (que despiertan los sentimientos de rasa) están presentes, ese devoto no
no percibir la dulzura del rasa. Si un devoto desea de una manera que se opone a la forma en que el
Los asociados personales del Señor desean, entonces, incluso si los uddipanas de vatsalya-rasa y los demás
están presentes los rasas, de modo que el devoto no percibirá los diferentes bhavas (éxtasis del amor), ni
¿Percibirá él la dulzura del rasa? Ahora hablaremos de los devotos que escuchan descripciones de
la dulzura del Señor y otras cualidades trascendentales. Estos devotos son independientes como
los asociados personales del Señor que participan en los pasatiempos del Señor. Estos devotos tienen el
poder para percibir la dulzura del rasa. Ahora la perfección de los rasas del amor por el Supremo
Se tendrá en cuenta la Personalidad de Dios. Cuando el amor por la Suprema Personalidad de Dios
(bhagavat-priti) se mezcla con los vibhavas y otros elementos de rasa, el resultado son los rasas de
amor por la Suprema Personalidad de Dios (bhagavat-pritimaya-rasa). Esto se describe en el
Las siguientes palabras de Sahitya-darpana (3.15):
yatha khanda-maricadinam sammelanad apurva iva kascid asvadah prapanaka-rase sajayate. vibhavadi-
sammelanad ihapi tatha.
"Así como el azúcar, la pimienta negra y otros ingredientes hacen que una bebida sea deliciosa para el paladar, así también
Los vibhavas y otros elementos del rasa hacen que los rasas sean deliciosos al paladar."
La dulzura del Señor se cuenta entre los uddipanas, los elementos secundarios que ayudan
uno para saborear los rasas espirituales. El Señor Supremo mismo es el alambana, el elemento primario.
que permite saborear los rasas espirituales. Los alambanas y uddipanas se describen en estos
Palabras del Agni Purana:
vibhavyate hola raty-ader
yatra yena vibhavyate vibhavo nama sa devdha-
lambanoddipanatmakah
"Vibhava permite percibir rati y los demás elementos de rasa. Vibhava es de dos
tipos: 1. alambana y 2. uddipana."
El alambana puede ser de dos tipos: 1. El Señor Krishna, la Suprema Personalidad de Dios, quien es
muy amados por los devotos, y 2. los devotos del Señor, que están llenos de amor por Él.
Estos dos tipos de alambanas se indican en sánscrito mediante el uso del caso locativo. El Señor Krishna como
El alambana se describe en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (9.24.65):
yasyananam makara-kundala. . .
"El rostro de Krishna está decorado con adornos, como pendientes que se asemejan a tiburones. Sus orejas son
hermoso, Sus mejillas brillantes, y Su sonrisa atractiva para todos. Quienquiera que vea al Señor Krishna
ve un festival. Su rostro y su cuerpo son completamente satisfactorios para que todos los vean."
El Señor Krishna, como el alambana, también es descrito en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.44.14):
gopyas tapah kim acaran yad amusya rupam
¡Qué austeridades debieron haber realizado las gopis! Con sus ojos siempre beben el néctar.

Esa hermosura es la única morada de belleza, fama y opulencia. Es perfecta en sí misma, siempre fresca y
extremadamente raro."
Mientras la dulzura del Señor Krishna no se manifieste, el alma individual verá su propio ser.

"Solo mediante el contacto con uno mismo se puede alcanzar el aliento vital, la inteligencia, la mente, los amigos,
El cuerpo, la esposa, los hijos, la riqueza, etc., son valiosos. Por lo tanto, ¿qué objeto puede ser más valioso?
¿Más que uno mismo?
En este versículo la palabra "sva" significa "el alma pura", "atma" significa "el cuerpo material" y

queridos para mí." Este versículo también implica: "Las cosas relacionadas conmigo también me son queridas." Así, el
El aliento vital y otras cosas son valiosas por su relación con el alma. Incluso cuando Él
La Suprema Personalidad de Dios aparece en muchas formas diferentes, pero siempre es querida por los demás.
alma individual. Esto se observa en las siguientes palabras pronunciadas por el Señor Balarama en el Srimad-Bhagavatam.

kim etad adbhutam iva

Mi afecto por estos niños y terneros crece como nunca antes, al igual que nuestro cariño por el Señor.
Krishna, el Alma Suprema de todos los seres vivos."
La propia forma del Señor Krishna se describe en estas palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.23.22):

Las palabras de este verso implican: "¿No te sentirás maravillosamente atraído por estos rasgos?"

records.sourceEnglish:
The devotees dear to the Lord are described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (1.18.13):


tulayäma lavenäpi. . .


   "The value of a moment's association with the devotee of the Lord cannot be compared to the
attainment of heavenly planets or liberation from matter, and what to speak of worldly
benedictions in the form of material prosperity, which are for those who are meant for death."*

   In this way it is seen that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is the object of love (viñaya) and
He is also the primary cause (älambana) that makes the devotees fall in love with Him. By following
the path that begins with hearing about the Lord, the devotees attain love (préti) for Him. The
word "viñaya" may mean either the person who loves or the person who is loved. It is said in Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (1.16.5-6):


tat kathyatäà mahä-bhäga
   yadi kåñëa-kathäçrayam
athaväsya padämbhoja-
   makaranda-lihäà satäm


  "Please describe all these incidents if they realte to the topics of Lord Kåñëa. The devotees of the
Lord are accustomed to licking up the honey available from the lotus feet of the Lord."*

    By associating with the Supreme Lord, one falls in love with Him. In this way the Supreme
Personality of Godhead is the primary cause (älambana) of ecstatic love for Him. The secondary
causes (uddépana) of ecstatic love are different. The Lord's dear devotees, who are of two kinds,
namely the devotees who have the same desire (saväsana) and the devotees who have different
desires (bhinna-väsana), are also objects (viñaya) of ecstatic love. The devotees are also the
reservoirs of love (ädhära) for the Lord. However, one's material friends and kinsmen are not the
causes of attaining love ofr Lord Kåñëa. Indeed, the devotees do not pray to attain love for their
friends and kinsmen. Rthaer they pray only to love the Supreme Lord. That they do not pray to
attain love for their friends and kinsmen is seen in these words of Queen Kunté in Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (1.8.41):


atha viçveça viçvätman

   viçva-mürte sva-kesu me
sneha-päçam imaà chindhi
   dådhaà päëdusu våsëisu


   "O Lord of the universe, soul of the universe, O personality of the form of the universe, please,
therefore, sever my tie of affection for my kinsmen, the Paëòavas and the Vrñëis."*

bendiciones en forma de prosperidad material, destinadas a aquellos que están destinados a la muerte."

Siguiendo el camino que comienza con escuchar acerca del Señor, los devotos alcanzan el amor (priti) por Él.

tat kathyatam maha-bhaga
yadi krsna-kathasrayam athavasya padambhoja-
makaranda-liham satam
"Por favor, describa todos estos incidentes si se relacionan con los temas del Señor Krishna. Los devotos
Los seguidores del Señor están acostumbrados a lamer la miel disponible de los pies de loto del Señor."
Al asociarse con el Señor Supremo, uno se enamora de Él. De esta manera, el Supremo
La personalidad de Dios es la causa principal (alambana) del amor extático por Él. La secundaria
Las causas (uddipana) del amor extático son diferentes. Los amados devotos del Señor, que son de dos tipos,
es decir, los devotos que tienen el mismo deseo (savasana) y los devotos que tienen diferentes
Los deseos (bhinna-vasana) son también objetos (visaya) de amor extático. Los devotos también son los
depósitos de amor (adhara) por el Señor. Sin embargo, los amigos materiales y los parientes no son los
causas de alcanzar el amor por el Señor Krishna. De hecho, los devotos no rezan para alcanzar el amor por su
amigos y parientes. O bien, solo rezan para amar al Señor Supremo. Que no rezan para
El amor que sienten por sus amigos y parientes se ve reflejado en estas palabras de la reina Kunti en el srimad-
Bhagavatam (1.8.41):
atha visvesa visvatman
visva-murte sva-kesu me sneha-pasam imam chindhi
drdham pandusu vrsnisu
"Oh Señor del universo, alma del universo, oh personalidad de la forma del universo,
Por lo tanto, les ruego que rompan el vínculo afectivo que me une a mis parientes, los Pandavas y los Vrsnis."
