de la varilla de batir y comenzó a impedir que batiera."
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
Vätsalya-rasa is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.45.2-10):


uväca pitaräv etya
   sägrajah sätvatarñabhaù
praçrayävanataù préëann
   amba täteti sädaram. . .

. . .iti mäyä-mauñyasya


  "Lord Kåñëa, the greatest of the Sätvatas, approached His parents with His elder brother.
Humbly bowing His head and gratifying them by respectfully addressing them as `My dear mother'

and `My dear father', Kåñëa spoke as follows.***
    " `Dear father, because of Us, your two sons, you and mother Devaké always remained in anxiety
and could never enjoy Our childhood, boyhood, or youth.***
    " `Deprived by fate, We could not live with you and enjoy the pampered happiness most children
enjoy in their parents' home.***
    " `With one's body one can acquire all goals of life, and it is one's parents who give the body birth
and sustenance. Therefore no mortal man can repay his debt to his parents, even if he serves them
for a full lifetime of a hundred years.***
    " `A son who, though able to do so, fails to provide for his parents with hsi physical resources and
wealth is forced after his death to eat his own flesh.***
    " `A man who, though able to do so, fails to support his elderly parents, chaste wife, young child,
or spiritual master, or who neglects a brähmaëa or anyone who comes to him for shelter, is
considered dead, though breathing.***
    "Thus We have wasted all these days, unable as We were to properly honor you because Our
minds were always disturbed by fear of Kaàsa.***
    " `Dear father and mother, please forgive Us for not serving you. We are not independent and
have been greatly frustrated by cruel Kaàsa.'***
    "Thus beguiled by the words of Lord Hari, the Supreme Soul of the universe, who by his internal
illusory potency appeared to be a human, His parents joyfully raised Him up on their laps and
embraced Him."***

   In these verses the word "pitarau" (parents) refers to Çré Devaké and Vasdueva, and the word
"préëan" means "delighting". These verses were spoken by Çré ÿa Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 226-229


   Lord Kåñëa's childhood restlessness is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.8.25):


çåìgy-aìgi-daàñöry-asi-jäla-dvija-kaëöakebhyaù
   kréòä-paräv ati-calau sva-sutau niñeddhum
gåhyäni kartum api yatra na taj-jananyau
   sekäta äpatur alaà manaso 'navastham


   "When Mother Yaçodä and Rohiëé were unable to protect the babies from calamities threatened
by horned cows, by fire, by animals with claws and teeth such as monkeys, dogs, and cats, and by
thorns, swords, and other weapons on the ground, they were always in anxiety, and their household
engagements were disturbed. At that time they were fully equipoised in the transcendental ecstasy
known as the distreess of material affection, for this was aroused within their minds."*

   Lord Kåñëa's childhood restlessness is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.8.28-
29):

kåñëasya gopyo ruciraà
   vékñya kaumära-cäpalam
çåìvantyaù kila tan-mätur
   iti hocuù samägataù


   "Observing the very attractive childish restlessness of Kåñëa, all the gopése in the neighborhood,
to hear about Kåñëa's activities again and again, would approach Mother Yaçodä ans speak to her as
follows."*


vatsän muïcan kvacid asamaye. . .


   " `Our dear friend Yaçodä, your son sometimes comes to our houses before the milking of the
cows and releases the calves, and when the master of the house becomes angry, your son merely
smiles. Sometimes He devises some process by which He steals palatavble curd, butter, and milk,
which He then eats and drinks. When the monkeys assemble, He divides it with them, and when
the monkeys have their bellies so full that they won't take any more, He breaks the pots.
Sometimes, if He gets no opportunity to stral butter and milk from a house, He will be angry at the
householders, and for His revenge He will agitate the small children by pinching them. Then, when
they begin crying, Kåñëa will go away.' "*

   The word "gopyaù" (gopés) here refers to Mother Yaçodä's friends and Lord Kåñëa's aunts. In
other situations in this rasa Lord Kåñëa manifests humility, shyness, speaking sweet words, honesty,
generosity and other virtues. These virtues are seen in the following description of Lord Kåñëa's
pastimes at the pilgrimage to Kurukñetra in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.82.34):


kåñëa-rämau pariñvajya
   pitaräv abhivadya ca. . .


   "O hero of the Kurus, Kåñëa and Balaräma embraced Their foster parents and bowed down to
them, bu Their throats were so choked up with tears of love that the two Lords could say
nothing."***

   In His childhood Lord Kåñëa was very forceful and arrogant when He stopped the Indra-yajïa.
Still, His actions delighted His parents and superiors. Lord Kåñëa's handsomeness and auspicious
features gradually increased until they reached their apex in His full-blown youth (pürëa-kaiçora).
The growing-up of Lord Kåñëa is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.8.21 and 26):


kälena vrajatälpena

   gokule räma-keçavau
jänubhyäà saha päëibhyäà
   ri\ìgamänau vijahratuù


  "After a short time passed, both brothers, Räma and Kåñëa, began to crawl on the ground of
Vraja with the strength of Their hands and knees and thus enjoy Their childhood play."*


kälenälpena räjarñe
   rämaù kåñëaç ca gokule
aghåñöa-jänubhiù padbhir
   vicakramatur aïjasä


  "O King Parékñit, within a very short time both Räma and Kåñëa began to walk very easily in
Gokula on Their legs, by Their own strength, without the need to crawl."*

  The meaning of these verses is clear. These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
El Vatsalya-rasa también se observa en estas palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.45.2-10):
Uvaca pitarav etya
sagrajah satvatarsabhah prasrayavanatah prinann
amba tateti sadaram. . .
. . .iti maya-mausyasya
"El Señor Krishna, el más grande de los Satvatas, se acercó a Sus padres con Su hermano mayor.
Inclinando humildemente la cabeza y complaciéndolas al dirigirse a ellas respetuosamente como "Mi querida madre".
y 'Mi querido padre', Krishna habló de la siguiente manera.
"`Querido padre, por nuestra culpa, tus dos hijos, tú y la madre Devaki siempre permanecieron ansiosos y
Nunca pudimos disfrutar de nuestra infancia, niñez o juventud.
"Privados por el destino, no pudimos vivir con ustedes y disfrutar de la felicidad consentida que la mayoría de los niños
disfrutar en casa de sus padres.
"Con el cuerpo se pueden alcanzar todas las metas de la vida, y son los padres quienes dan el cuerpo.
nacimiento y sustento. Por lo tanto, ningún hombre mortal puede pagar su deuda a sus padres, incluso si
Les sirve durante toda una vida de cien años.
"Un hijo que, aunque capaz de hacerlo, no provee a sus padres con sus recursos físicos.
y la riqueza se ve obligada, tras su muerte, a comerse su propia carne.
"Un hombre que, aunque capaz de hacerlo, no logra mantener a sus ancianos padres, a su casta esposa, a sus jóvenes
niño, o maestro espiritual, o quien descuide a un brahmán o a cualquiera que venga a él en busca de refugio, es
Se le considera muerto, aunque respira.
"Así hemos desperdiciado todos estos días, incapaces como estábamos de honrarte debidamente porque nuestras mentes
Siempre les perturbaba el miedo a Kamsa.
"`Queridos padre y madre, por favor perdónanos por no serviros. No somos independientes y tenemos
Me siento muy frustrado por la cruel Kamsa.
"Así, seducidos por las palabras del Señor Hari, el Alma Suprema del universo, quien por su interior
La potencia ilusoria parecía ser un ser humano, sus padres lo levantaron alegremente en sus regazos y
lo abrazó."
En estos versículos la palabra "pitarau" (padres) se refiere a sri Devaki y Vasdueva, y la palabra
"prinan" significa "deleite". Estos versos fueron pronunciados por Sri La Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
Lord Kåñëa's graudally growing-up is also described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.15.1):


tataç ca paugaëòa-vayaù-çritau vraje
   babhüvatus tau paçu-päla-sammatau


   "When Lord Räma and Lord Kåñëa attained the age of paugaëòa [six to ten] while living in
Våndävana, the cowherd men allowed Them to take up the task of tending the cows. Engaging thus
in the company of Their friends, the two boys rendered the land of Våndävana most auspicious by
imprinting upon it the marks of Their lotus feet."***

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
El crecimiento gradual del Señor Krishna también se describe en estas palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam.
(10.15.1):
tatas ca pauganda-vayah-sritau vraje
babhuvatus tau pasu-pala-sammatau
"Cuando el Señor Rama y el Señor Krishna alcanzaron la edad de pauganda [de seis a diez años] mientras vivían en
Vrndavana, los pastores les permitieron asumir la tarea de cuidar las vacas. De esta manera, se dedicaron a
En compañía de sus amigos, los dos muchachos hicieron que la tierra de Vrndavana fuera sumamente auspiciosa.
imprimiendo en ella las marcas de sus pies de loto."
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
Lord Kåñëa's birth was already described. Lord Kåñëa's activities include His birth pastimes and
His childhood pastimes. Lord Kåñëa's birth pastimes are described in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.5.1):

nandas tv ätmaja utpanne. . .


   "Nanda Mahäräja was naturally very magnanimous, and when Lord Çré Kåñëa appeared as his
son, he was overwhelmed with jubilation."*

   Lord Kåñëa's childhood pastimes are described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.8.22-
24):


täv aìghri-yugmam anukåñya sarésåpantau
   ghoña-praghoña-ruciraà vraja-kardameñu
tan-näda-håñöa-manasäv anusåtya lokaà
   mugdha-prabhétavad upeyatur anti mätroù. . .


   "When Kåñëa and Balaräma, with the strength of Their legs, crawled in the muddy places
created in Vraja by cow dung and cow urines, Their crawling resembled the crawling of serpents,
and the sound of Their ankle bells was very charming. Very much pleased by the spound of other
people's ankle bells, They used to follow these people as if going to Their mothers, but when They
saw that these were other people, They became afraid and returned to Their real mothers, Yaçodä
and Rohiëé.*
   "Dressed with muddy earth mixed with cow dung and cvow urine, the babies looked very
beautiful, and when They went to Their mothers, both Yaçodä and Rohiëé picked Them up with
great affection, embraced Them, and allowed Them to suck the milk flowing from their breasts.
While sucking the breast, the babies smiled, and Their small teeth were visible. Their mothers,
upon seeing those beautiful teeth, enjoyed great transcendental bliss.*


yarhy aìganä-darçanéya-kumära-liläv
   antar-vraje tad abalä pragåhéta-pucchaiù
vatsair itas tata ubhäv anukåñyamänau
   pekñantya ujjhita-ghrä jahåñur hasantyaù


   "Within the house of Nanda Mahäräja the cowherd ladies would enjoy seeing the pastimes of the
babies Räma and Kåñëa. The babies would catch the ends of the calves' tails, and the calves would
drag Them here and there. When thre ladiers saw these pastimes, they certainly stopped their
household activities and laughed and enjoyed the incidents."*

  The meaning of these verses is clear. These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
El nacimiento del Señor Krishna ya fue descrito. Las actividades del Señor Krishna incluyen sus pasatiempos de nacimiento.
y sus pasatiempos infantiles. Los pasatiempos del nacimiento del Señor Krishna se describen en estas palabras del srimad-
Bhagavatam (10.5.1):
nandas tv atmaja utpanne. . .
"Nanda Maharaja era naturalmente muy magnánimo, y cuando el Señor Sri Krishna apareció como su hijo,
Estaba desbordado de júbilo.
Los pasatiempos infantiles del Señor Krishna se describen en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.8.22-
24):
tav anghri-yugmam anukrsya sarisrpantau
ghosa-praghosa-ruciram vraja-kardamesu tan-nada-hrsta-manasav anusrtya lokam
mugdha-prabhitavad upeyatur anti matroh. . .
"Cuando Krishna y Balarama, con la fuerza de sus piernas, se arrastraron por los lugares fangosos
Creados en Vraja por estiércol y orina de vaca, su arrastrarse se asemejaba al arrastrarse de las serpientes,
y el sonido de sus campanillas de tobillo era muy encantador. Muy complacido por el sonido de los demás
las campanillas de tobillo de la gente, Solían seguir a estas personas como si fueran a sus madres, pero cuando
Vieron que eran otras personas, se asustaron y regresaron con sus verdaderas madres.
Yasoda y Rohini.
"Vestidos con tierra fangosa mezclada con estiércol de vaca y orina de vaca, los bebés se veían muy hermosos,
y cuando fueron con sus madres, tanto Yasoda como Rohini los recogieron con gran cariño,
Las abrazó y les permitió mamar la leche que fluía de sus pechos. Mientras mamaban
Los bebés sonrieron y sus pequeños dientes eran visibles. Sus madres, al ver esos pechos, sonrieron y sus madres, al ver a sus madre pequeños dientes fueron visibles.
Dientes hermosos, disfruté de una gran dicha trascendental.
yarhy angana-darsaniya-kumara-lilav
antar-vraje tad abala pragrhita-pucchaih vatsair itas tata ubhav anukrsyamanau
peksantya ujjhita-ghra jahrsur hasantyah
"Dentro de la casa de Nanda Maharaja, las mujeres pastoras disfrutaban viendo los pasatiempos de los
los bebés Rama y Krishna. Los bebés se agarraban a los extremos de las colas de los terneros, y los terneros...
Las arrastran de aquí para allá. Cuando las tres damas vieron estos pasatiempos, ciertamente dejaron de hacerlo.
realizaban actividades domésticas y reían y disfrutaban de los incidentes."
El significado de estos versos es claro. Estos versos fueron pronunciados por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
In this context the word "ädi" (beginning with) means "beginning with the paugaëòa years (six
until ten). Here the parahpernalia of the Lord's pastimes include his garments, clay pots, and other
things. Different specific times include Lord Kåñëa's birthday and other like times. Lord Kåñëa's
birthday celebration is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.7.4):


kadäcid autthänika-kautukäplave
   janmarkña-yoge samaveta-yoñitäm
väditra-géta-dvija-mantra-väcakaiç
   cakära sünor abhiñecanaà saté


   "When Mother Yaçodä's baby was slanting His body to attempt to rise and turn around, this
attempt was observed by a Vedic ceremony. In such a ceremony, called utthäna, which is performed
when a child is due to leave the house for the first time, the child is properly bathed. Just after
Kåñëa turned three months old, mother Yaçodä celebrated this ceremony with other women of the
neighborhood. On that day there was a conjunction of the moon with the constellation Rohiëé. As
the brähmaëas joined by chanting Vedic hymns and professional musicians also took part, this
great ceremony was observed by mother Yaçodä."*

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
En este contexto, la palabra "adi" (que comienza con) significa "que comienza con los años pauganda (seis)".
hasta las diez). Aquí, los parahpernalia de los pasatiempos del Señor incluyen sus vestiduras, vasijas de barro y
otras cosas. Diferentes momentos específicos incluyen el cumpleaños del Señor Krishna y otros momentos similares. Señor
La celebración del cumpleaños de Krishna se describe en estas palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.7.4):
kadacid autthanika-kautukaplave
janmarksa-yoge samaveta-yositam vaditra-gita-dvija-mantra-vacakais
cakara sunor abhisecanam sati
"Cuando el bebé de la Madre Yasoda estaba inclinando su cuerpo para intentar levantarse y darse la vuelta, esto
El intento fue observado mediante una ceremonia védica. En dicha ceremonia, llamada utthana, que se realiza
Cuando un niño está a punto de salir de casa por primera vez, se le baña adecuadamente.
Después de que Krishna cumplió tres meses, la madre Yasoda celebró esta ceremonia con otras mujeres de
el vecindario. Ese día hubo una conjunción de la luna con la constelación Rohini.
A medida que los brahmanas se unieron cantando himnos védicos y los músicos profesionales también participaron, esto
La madre Yasoda presenció una gran ceremonia.
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
Among the anubhävas are the udbhäsvaras. Among the udbhäsvaras is lälana (doting parental
love), which is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.15.44-46):


tayor yaçodä-rohiëyau
   putrayoù putra-vatsale
yathä-kämaà yathä-kälaà
   vyadhattäà paramäçiñaù


   "Mother Yaçodä and mother Rohiëé, acting most affectionately toward their two sons, offered all
the best things to Them in response to Their every desire and at the various appropriate.***


gatädhväna-çramau tatra
   majjanonmardanädibhiù
névéà vasitvä ruciräà
   divya-srag-gandha-maëòitau

   "By being bathed and massaged, the two young Lords were relieved of the weariness caused by
walking on the country roads. Then They were dressed in attractive robes and decorated with
transcendental garlands and fragrances.***


janany-upahåtaà präçya
   svadv annam upalatitau
saàviçya vara-çayyäyäà
   sukhaà suñupatur vraje


   "After dining sumptuously on the delicious food given Them by Their mothers and being
pampered in various ways, the two brothers lay down upon Their excellent beds and happily went
to sleep in the village of Vraja."***

  The meaning of these verses is clear. These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Entre los anubhavas se encuentran los udbhasvaras. Entre los udbhasvaras se encuentra lalana (padre cariñoso).
amor), que se describe en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.15.44-46):
Taylor Yasoda-Rohinyau
putrayoh putra-vatsale yatha-kamam yatha-kalam
vyadhattam paramasisah
"La madre Yasoda y la madre Rohini, mostrando el mayor cariño hacia sus dos hijos, ofrecieron
todas las mejores cosas para Ellos en respuesta a cada uno de Sus deseos y en los diversos momentos apropiados.
gatadhvana-sramau tatra
majjanonmardanadibhih nivim vasitva ruciram
divya-srag-gandha-manditau
"Al ser bañados y masajeados, los dos jóvenes lores se aliviaron del cansancio causado por
caminando por los caminos rurales. Luego se vistieron con túnicas atractivas y se adornaron con
Guirnaldas y fragancias trascendentales.
janany-upahrtam prasya
svadv annam upalatitau samvisya vara-sayyayam
sukham susupatur vraje
"Después de cenar suntuosamente con la deliciosa comida que les dieron sus madres y estar
mimados de diversas maneras, los dos hermanos se acostaron en sus excelentes camas y se fueron felices a
dormir en el pueblo de Vraja."
El significado de estos versos es claro. Estos versos fueron pronunciados por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
The udbhäsvara of çiro-ghräëa (smelling the head) is described in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.6.43):


nandaù sva-putram ädäya
  pretyägatam udära-dhéù
mürdhny upaghräya paramäà
  mudaà lebhe kurüdvaha


  "O Mahäräja Parékñit, best of the Kurus, Nanda Mahäräja was very liberal and simple. He
immediately took his son Kåñëa on his lap as if Kåñëa had returned from death, and by formally
smelling his son's head, Nanda Mahäräja undoubtedly enjoyed transcendental bliss."*

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
El udbhasvara de siro-ghrana (oler la cabeza) se describe con estas palabras de srimad-
Bhagavatam (10.6.43):
nandah sva-putram adaya
pretyagatam udara-dhih murdhny upaghraya paramam
mudam lebhe kurudvaha
"Oh Maharaja Pariksit, el mejor de los Kurus, Nanda Maharaja era muy liberal y sencillo. Él
inmediatamente tomó a su hijo Krsna en su regazo como si Krsna hubiera regresado de la muerte, y al formalmente
Al oler la cabeza de su hijo, Nanda Maharaja sin duda experimentó una dicha trascendental.
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
The udbhäsvara of äçirväda (speaking blessings) is described in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.5.12):


tä äçiñaù prayuïjänäç

   ciraà pähéti bälake
haridra-cürëa-tailädbhiù
   siïcantyo 'janam ujjaguù


   "Offering blessings to the newborn child, Kåñëa, the wives and daughters of the cowherd men
said, `May you become the king of Vraja and long maintain all its inhabitants.' They sprinkled a
mixture of turmeric powder, oil, and water upon the birthless Supreme Lord and offered prayers."*

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
El udbhasvara de asirvada (pronunciar bendiciones) se describe en estas palabras de srimad-
Bhagavatam (10.5.12):
ta asisah prayunjanas
ciram pahiti balake haridra-curna-tailadbhih
sincantyo 'janam ujjaguh
"Ofreciendo bendiciones al niño recién nacido, Krishna, las esposas e hijas de los pastores de vacas
dijeron: «Que te conviertas en el rey de Vraja y mantengas a todos sus habitantes por mucho tiempo». Rociaron un
"Se vertió una mezcla de cúrcuma en polvo, aceite y agua sobre el Señor Supremo sin nacimiento y se ofrecieron oraciones."
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
The udbhäsvara of hitopadeça-däna (giving auspicious advice) is described in these words of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.11.15):


kåñëa kåñëäravindäkña
   täta ehi stanaà piba
alaà vihäraiù kñut-kñäntaù
   kréòä-çränto 'si putraka


   "Mogher Yasoda said: My dear son Kåñëa, lotus-eyed Kåñëa, come here and drink the milk of my
breast. My dear darling, You must be very tired because of hunger and the fatigue of playing so long.
There is no need to play any more."*

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
El udbhasvara de hitopadesa-dana (dar consejos auspiciosos) se describe en estas palabras de
Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.11.15):
krsna krsnaravindaksa
tata ehi stanam piba alam viharaih ksut-ksantah
krida-sranto 'si putraka
"Mogher Yasoda dijo: Mi querido hijo Krishna, Krishna de ojos de loto, ven aquí y bebe la leche de mi
pecho. Mi querido amor, debes estar muy cansado por el hambre y el cansancio de jugar tanto.
largo. Ya no hay necesidad de jugar más."
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
All these activitirs are performed by the many kinds of devotees in vatsalya-rasa, but they are
especially performed by Lord Kåñëa's parents. For His benefit, Lord Kåñëa's parents also rebuke
Him. An example of this is seen in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.8.32-34):


ekadä kréòamänäs te
   rämädyä gopa-därakaù
kåñëo mådaà bhakñitavän
   iti mätre nyavedayan


   "One day while Kåñëa was playing with His small playmates, including Balaräma and the other

sons of the gopas, all His friends came together and lodged a complaint to Mother Yaçodä. `Mother,'
they submitted, "Kåñëa has eaten earth.'*


sä gåhitvä kare kåñëam
   upalabhya haitaiñiëé
yaçodä bhaya-sambhränta-
   prekñaëäkñam abhäñata


   "Upon hearing this from Kåñëa's playmates, mother Yaçodä, who was always full of anxiety over
Kåñëa's welfare,, picked Kåñëa up with her hands to look into His mouth and chastise Him. Her eyes
fearful, she spoke to her son as follows.*


kasmän mådam ädantätman
   bhavän bhakñitavän rahaù
vadanti tävakä hy ete
   kumäräs te 'grajo 'py ayam


   "Dear Kåñëa, why are You so restless that You have eaten dirt in a solitary place? This complaint
has been lodged against You by all Your playmates, including Your elder brother, Balaräma. How is
this?"*

  The meaning of these verses is clear. These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Todas estas actividades son realizadas por los muchos tipos de devotos en vatsalya-rasa, pero ellos
son realizadas especialmente por los padres del Señor Krishna. Para Su beneficio, los padres del Señor Krishna también
Reprenderlo. Un ejemplo de esto se ve en las siguientes palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.8.32-34):
ekada kridamanas te
ramadya gopa-darakah krsno mrdam bhaksitavan
iti matre nyavedayan
"Un día, mientras Krishna jugaba con sus pequeños compañeros de juego, entre ellos Balarama y los demás
Los hijos de los gopas, todos sus amigos se reunieron y presentaron una queja a la Madre Yasoda.
—Madre —respondieron—, Krishna ha comido tierra.
sa grhitva kare krsnam
upalabhya haitaisini yasoda bhaya-sambhranta-
preksanaksam abhasata
"Al escuchar esto de los compañeros de juego de Krsna, la madre Yasoda, que siempre estaba llena de ansiedad por
El bienestar de Krishna, lo tomó con sus manos para mirarlo en la boca y reprenderlo.
Con los ojos llenos de miedo, le habló a su hijo de la siguiente manera.
Kasman Mrdam Adantatman
bhavan bhaksitavan rahah vadanti tavaka hy ete
kumaras te 'grajo 'py ayam
"Querido Krishna, ¿por qué estás tan inquieto que has comido tierra en un lugar solitario?
Todos tus compañeros de juego, incluido tu hermano mayor, han presentado una queja contra ti.
Balarama. ¿Qué tal esto?
El significado de estos versos es claro. Estos versos fueron pronunciados por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
An example of what happened to child Kåñëa after He broke the yogurt-pot is seen in these
words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.9.11-12):


kåtägasaà taà prarudantam akñiëé
   kasantam anjan-mañiëé sva-päëinä
udvékñamäëaà bhaya-vihvalekñaëaà
   haste gåhétvä bhiñayanty avägurat


   "When caught by mother Yaçodä, Kåñëa became more and more afraid and admitted to being an
offender. As she looked upon Him, she saw that He was crying, His tears mixing with the black
ointment around His eyes, and as He rubbed His eyes with His hands, He smeared the ointment all
over His face. Mother Yaçodä, catching her beautiful son by the hand, mildly began to chastise
Him."*

tyaktvä yañtià sutaà bhétaà
   vijïäyärbhaka-vatsa la
iyeña kila taà baddhuà
   dämnätad-vérya-kovidä


    "Mother Yaçodä was always overwhelmed by intense love for Kåñëa, not knowing who Kåñëa was
or how powerful He was. Because of maternal affection for Kåñëa, she never even cared to know
who He was. Therefore, when she saw that her son had become excessively afraid, she threw the
stick away and desired to bind Him so that He would not commit any further naughty activities."*

  The meaning of these verses is clear. These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 239 and 240


   Wishing only His welfare and happiness, the devotees in vätsalya-rasa discipline Kåñëa, give Him
bitter-tasting medicine, and perform other like activities. An example of these activities is seen in
the following wrds of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.9.5):


tam aìkam ärüdham apäyayat stanaà
   sneha-snutaà sa-smitam ékñaté mukham
atåptam utsåjya javena sä yayäv
   utsicyamäne payasi tv adhiçrite


   "Mother Yaçodä then embraced Kåñëa, allowed Him to sit down on her lap, and began to look
upon the face of the Lord with great love and affection. Because of her intense affection, milk was
flowing from her breast. But when she saw that the milk pan on the oven was boiling over, she
immediately left her son to take care of the overflowing milk, although the child was not yet fully
satisfied with drinking the milk of His mother's breast."*

  These devotees are also described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.14.35):


yad-dhämärtha-suhåt-priyätma-tanaya-präëäçayas tvat-kåte


   "My Lord, sometimes I am puzzled as to how Your Lordship will be able to repay, in gratitude, the
devotional service of these residents of Våndävana. Although I know that You are the supreme
source of all benediction, I am puzzled to know how You will be able to repay all the service that
You are receiving from these residents of Våndävana. I think of how You are so kind, so

magnanimous, that even Pütanä, who came to cheat You by dressing herself as a very affectionate
mother, was awarded liberation and the actual post of a mother. And other demons belonging to
the same family, such as Aghäsura and Bakäsura, were also favored with liberation. Under the
circumstances, I am puzzled. These residents of Våndävana have given You everything: Their
bodies, their minds, their love, their homes. Everything is being utilized for Your purpose. So how
will You be able to repay their debt? You have already given Yourself to Pütanä! I surmise that You
shall ever ever remain a debtor to the residents of Våndävana, bein unable to repay their loving
service."*

   Here we see Mother Yaçodä is eager to protect the wealth in her house. Cowherd people are
naturally very determined to attain great wealth in milk and milk-products. Mother Yaçodä was
eager to protect her wealth of milk. Still, this eagerness only nourished her love for Lord Kåñëa in
vätsalya-rasa. As waves increase the ocean, so these activities increased her love for her son. In her
heart she did not think of protecting her own wealth. She only thought: "This is what I must do
now". In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.9.5 the word "sneha-snutam" shows that she had deep love for her
son. Even when her son broke the yogurt pots, she had only a dim reflection of anger. In her heart
she was delighted and amused by her son's mischief. This is seen in the following words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.9.7):


uttärya gopé suçåtaà payaù punaù
   praviçya sandåçya ca dadhy-amatrakam
bhagnaà vilokya sva-sutasya karma taj
   jahäsa taà cäpi na tatra paçyaté


  "Mother Yaçodä, after taking down the hot milk from the oven, returned to the churning spot,
and when she saw that the container of yogurt was broken and that Kåñëa was not present, she
concluded that the breaking of the pot was the work of Kåñëa.* Seeing this, she smiled."

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Un ejemplo de lo que le sucedió al niño Krishna después de que rompió el recipiente de yogur se ve en estas palabras.
del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.9.11-12):
krtagasam tam prarudantam aksini
kasantam anjan-masini sva-panina udviksamanam bhaya-vihvaleksanam
prisa grhitva bhisayanty avagurat
"Cuando fue atrapado por su madre Yasoda, Krishna sintió cada vez más miedo y admitió ser un
ofensor. Al mirarlo, vio que lloraba, sus lágrimas se mezclaban con la oscuridad.
ungüento alrededor de sus ojos, y mientras se frotaba los ojos con sus manos, untó el ungüento por todo
sobre su rostro. La madre Yasoda, tomando a su hermoso hijo de la mano, comenzó a reprenderlo suavemente.
A él."
tyaktva yastim sutam bhitam
vijnayarbhaka-vatsa la iyesa kila tam baddhum
damnatad-virya-kovida
"La Madre Yasoda siempre estuvo abrumada por un intenso amor por Krishna, sin saber quién era Krishna o
cuán poderoso era Él. Debido al afecto maternal por Krishna, ella nunca se preocupó por saber quién era Él.
Así era. Por lo tanto, cuando vio que su hijo tenía demasiado miedo, tiró el palo.
y deseaba atarlo para que no cometiera más actos indebidos."
El significado de estos versos es claro. Estos versos fueron pronunciados por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
Even when he is in distress, a devotee in vätsalya-rasa may pretend to smile in order to reassure
Lord Kåñëa. An example of this is seen in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.11.6):


ulükhalaà vikarñantaà
   dämnä baddhaà svam ätmajam
vilokya nandaù prahasad-
   vadano vimumoca ha

    "When Nanda Mahäräja saw his own son bound with ropes to the wooden mortar and dragging
it, he smiled and released Kåñëa from His bonds."*

   An alternate reading here is "prahasad-vadanam" (Lord Kåñëa weas smiling). This verse was
spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Incluso cuando está angustiado, un devoto en vatsalya-rasa puede fingir sonreír para poder
tranquilizar al Señor Krishna. Un ejemplo de esto se ve en las siguientes palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam.
(10.11.6):
ulukhalam vikarsantam
damna baddham svam atmajam vilokya nandah prahasad-
vadano vimumoca ha
"Cuando Nanda Maharaja vio a su propio hijo atado con cuerdas al mortero de madera y arrastrándolo,
Él sonrió y liberó a Krishna de sus ataduras.
Una lectura alternativa aquí es "prahasad-vadanam" (el Señor Krishna sonríe). Este verso fue
hablado por srila sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
A devotee in vätsalya-rasa may fear that calamities brought by wicked people or other sources
may harm Lord Kåñëa. An example of this is seen in these words spoken by Devaké in Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.3.29):


janma te mayy asau päpo
   mä vidyän madhusüdana
samudvije bhavad-dhetoù
   kaàsäd aham adhéra-dhéù


   "O Madhusüdana, because of Your apperance I am becoming more and more anxious in fear of
Kaàsa. Therefore, please arrange for that sinful Kaàsa to be unable to understand that You have
taken birth from my womb."*

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çré Devaké.
records.content:
Un devoto en vatsalya-rasa puede temer las calamidades traídas por personas malvadas u otras fuentes.
puede dañar al Señor Krishna. Un ejemplo de esto se ve en estas palabras pronunciadas por Devaki en el srimad-
Bhagavatam (10.3.29):
janma te mayy asau papo
ma vidyan madhusudana samudvije bhavad-dhetoh
kamsad aham adhira - dhih
"Oh Madhusudana, debido a Tu aparición me siento cada vez más ansioso por el temor a
Kamsa. Por lo tanto, por favor, haz que ese pecador Kamsa no pueda comprender que Tú tienes
nacido de mi vientre."
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por Sri Devaki.

records.sourceEnglish:
This fear is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.8.25):


çåìgy-aìgi-daàñöry-asi-jäla-dvija. . .


   "When Mother Yaçodä and Rohiëé were unable to protect the babies from calamities threatened
by horned cows, by fire, by animals with claws and teeth such as monkeys, dogs, and cats, and by
thorns, swords, and other weapons on the ground, they were always in anxiety, and their household
engagements were disturbed. At that time they were fully equipoised in the transcendental ecstasy
known as the distreess of material affection, for this was aroused within their minds."*

   For Lord Kåñëa's welfare a devotee in vätsalya-rasa may worship the demigods or other exalted
beings. An example of this is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.5.16):

tais taiù kämair adénätmä
   yathocitam apüjayat
viñëor ärädhanärthäya
   sva-putrasyodayäya ca


    "The great-minded Mahäräja Nanda gave clothing, ornaments, and cows in charity to the
cowherd men in order to please Lord Viñëu, and thus he improved the condition of his own son in
all respects."*

   Here Nanda Maharaja thought: "By these activities Lord Viñëu will be pleased. When He is
pleased then good will come to my son." Thinking in this way, Nanda properly performed these
activities of worship. That is the meaning here. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Este temor también se observa en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.8.25):
srngy-angi-damstry-asi-jala-dvija. . .
"Cuando la Madre Yasoda y Rohini no pudieron proteger a los bebés de las calamidades amenazantes
por vacas con cuernos, por fuego, por animales con garras y dientes como monos, perros y gatos, y por
espinas, espadas y otras armas en el suelo, siempre estaban ansiosos, y su hogar
Los compromisos se vieron interrumpidos. En ese momento estaban completamente equilibrados en el éxtasis trascendental.
conocida como la angustia del afecto material, pues esta se despertaba en sus mentes."
Para el bienestar del Señor Krishna, un devoto en vatsalya-rasa puede adorar a los semidioses u otros seres exaltados.
seres. Un ejemplo de esto se ve en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.5.16):
tais taih kamair adinatma
yathocitam apujayat visnor aradhanarthaya
sva-putrasyodayaya ca
"El magnánimo Maharaja Nanda dio ropa, adornos y vacas como acto de caridad al pastor de vacas."
hombres para complacer al Señor Visnu, y así mejoró la condición de su propio hijo en todo
saludos."
Aquí Nanda Maharaja pensó: "Con estas actividades el Señor Visnu estará complacido. Cuando Él esté
"Me alegra que mi hijo esté contento." Pensando de esta manera, Nanda realizó correctamente estas
actividades de adoración. Ese es el significado aquí. Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
Seeing a display of Lord Kåñëa's extraordinary power, a devotee in vätsalya-rasa may think the
power came not from Kåñëa, but from some other source instead. An example of this is seen in the
following words spoken by Lord Kåñëa's parents in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.7.31):


aho batäty-adbhutam eña rakñasä
  bälo nivåttià gamito 'bhyagät punaù
hiàsraù sva-päpena vihiàsitaù khalaù
  sädhuù samatvena bhayäd vimucyate


   "It is most astonishing that although this innocent child was taken away by the Räkñasa to be
eaten, He has returned without having been killed or even injured. Because this demon was
envious, cruel, and sinful, he has been killed for his own sinful activities. This is the law of nature.
An innocent devotee is always protecvted by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and a sinful
person is always vanquished for his sinful life."*

  Lord Kåñëa's prents thought in this way. Lord Kåñëa's mother spoke these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.8.40):


kià svapna. . .


   "(Mother Yaçodä began to argue with herself:) Is this a dream, or is it an illusory creation by the
external energy? Has this been manifested by my own intelligence, or is it some mystic power of my
child?"*

   After seeing Lord Kåñëa manifest the entire material universe within His abdomen, Mother
Yaçodä could not believe that this was a display of her son's great power. She assumed that He had
no power to manifest this vision. (She assumed that the vision of the universal form was caused by
the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is different from her son.) She thought in Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.8.41):


atho yathävan na vitarka-gocaram. . .


   "Therefore let me surrender to the Supreme Personality of Godhead and offer my obeisances
unto Him, who is beyond the conception of human speculation, the mind, activities, words, and
arguments, who is the original cause of this cosmic manifestation, by whom the entire cosmos is
maintained, and by whom we can conceive of its existence. Let me simply offer my obeisances, for
He is beyond my contemplation, speculation, and meditation. He is beyond all of my material
activities."*

   Here Mother Yaçodä assumes that this vision of the universal form was caused by the Supreme
Personality of Godhead (who is different from her son). To become free from seeing this fearful
vision, she takes shelter of the Supreme Lord's lotus feet. Then she thought (Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.8.42):


ahaà mamäsau. . .


   "It is by the influence of the Supreme Lord's mäyä that I am wrongly thinking that Nanda
Mahäräja is my husband, that Kåñëa is my son, and that because I am the queen of Nanda
Mahäräja, all the wealth of cows and calves are my possessions and all the cowherd men and their
wives are my subjects. Actually, I also am eternally subordinate to the Supreme Lord. He is my
ultimate shelter."*

  With these words Mother Yasoda firmlytakes shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
Speaking the words "Nanda Mahäräja is my husband, that Kåñëa is my son," she refers to Lord
Kåñëa, who was then before her eyes. Then she says: "I am bewildered (kumatiù) by these many
manifestations of the universal form (yan-mäyayä)." Then she says: "the Supreme Personality of
Godhead (saù) is the goal of my life (gatiù). There Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé explained (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.8.43):


itthaà vidita-tattväyam. . .


   "Mother Yaçodä, by the grace of the Lord, could understand the real truth. But then again, the
supreme master, by the influence of the internal potency, Yogamäyä, inspired her to become
absorbed in intense maternal affection for her son."*

   Here the word "tattva" reefers to her son. Here the words "sa éçvaraù" refer to Lord Kåñëa's
feature as the supreme controller.In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.8.42 the words "pranatasmi tat-padam"
mean "Let me simply offer obeisances, for He is beyond my contemplation". In Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.8.43 the words "vaiñävéà mäyäm" may mean "the Supreme Lord's internal potency", or they may
also mean "the Supreme Lord's mercy". The it is explained in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.8.45):


trayyä copaniñadbhiç ca. . .


  "The glories of the Supreme Personality of Godhead are studied through the three Vedas, the
Upaniñads, the literature of saìkhya-yoga, and other Vaiñëava literature, yet mother Yaçodä
considered the Supreme Person her ordinary child."*

   It is also said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.9.21):


näyaà sukhäpo bhagavän. . .


   "The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kåñëa, the son of mother Yaçodä, is accessible to
devotees engaged in spontaneous loving service, but He is not as easily accessible to mental
speculators, to those striving for self-realization by severe austerities and penances, or to those who
consider the body the same as the self."*

   It these words the Çrémad-Bhägavatam sings thre glories of Mother Yaçodä. It is also said in
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.46.18-19):


api smarati naù kåñëaù. . .


   "Does Kåñëa remember us? Does He remember His mother and His friends and well-wishers?
Does He remember the cowherds and their village of Vraja, of which He is thr master? Does He
remember the cows, Våndävana forest, and Govardhana Hill?***


apy äyaçyati govindaù. . .


   "Will Govinda return even once to see His family? If He ever does, we may then glance upon His
beautiful face, with its beautiful eyes, nose, and smile."***

  After Nanda Mahäräja had spoken these words, Uddhava, following the way of this world, to
console him spoke these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.46.30):

yuväà çläghyatamau nünam. . .


   "O respectful Nanda, certainly you and mother Yaçodä are the most praiseworthy persons in the
entire world, since you have developed such a loving attitude toward Lord Näräyaëa, the spiritual
master of all living beings."***

   Even as Uddhava spoke these words of praise, Nanda's remained convinced that Kåñëa was his
son and not the Supreme Personality of Godhead. He could nto be moved from that idea. Then it is
said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.46.44):


evaà niçä sa bhruvator vyatétä
   nandasya kåñëänucarasya räjan. . .


   "While Kåñëa's messenger continued speaking with Nanda, the night ended, O king. The women
of the cowherd village rose from bed and, lighting lamps, worshiped their household deities. Then
they began churning yogurt into butter."***

   In this way Uddhava spoke many words to console Nanda Maharaja, who was griving in
separation from Kåñëa. No matter what Uddhava said, Nanda remained always convinced that
Kåñëa was his son and not the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The truth of Uddhava's words,
that Lord Kåñëa is indeed the original form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is elaboratedly
explained in the Kåñëa-sandarbha. Even at Kuruksetra, when a great host of saintly devotees
affirmed that Lord Kåñëa is indeed the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Nanda and Yaçodä
remained unconvinced. They continued to believe that Kåñëa was only their son. This is seen in
the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.82.35):


täv ätmäsanam äropya
   bähubhyäà parirabhya ca
yaçodä ca mahä-bhägä
   sutau vijahatuù çucaù


  "Raising their two sons onto their laps and holding Them in their arms, Nanda and saintly
mother Yaçodä forgot their sorrow."***

  It is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.66):


manaso våttayo naù syuù. . .

  "May our thoughts always take shelter of Kåñëa's lotus feet, may our words always chant His
names, and may our bodies always bow down to Him and serve Him."***

   Even though the truth that Çré Kåñëa is the all-powerful Supreme Personality of Godhead was
again and again proved to him, Nanda Mahäräja continued to believe Kåñëa was only his son and
nothing more. These words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.66) Nanda spoke to Uddhava mean: "We
pray that birth after birth we may love Kåñëa." This prayer of love spoken by Nanda is filled with
anuräga love. Loev is not absent from it. Then it is said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.65):


taà nirgataà samäsädya
   nänopäyana-pänayaù
nandädayo 'nurägeëa
   prävocann açru-locanäù


  "As Uddhava was about to leave, Nanda and the others approached him bearing various items of
worship. With tears in their eyes they addressed him as follows."***

   In these verses it is seen that Nanda and Yaçodä are filled with anuräga ecstatic love for Lord
Kåñëa. Their devotion to the Lord is not in the mood of awe and veneration, the mood of
appreciating Lord Kåñëa's supreme power and opulence. Here Uddhava thinks: "Although I am far
from attaining this kind of good fortune, I still pray that someday I will attainj this kind of ecstatic
love. I pray this love will nto be denied to me." With a voice choked with emotion Uddhava prays
in this way. Praying that in some other lifetime he may some day attain this kind of anuräga
ecstatic love, Uddhava says (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.67):


karmabhir bhramyamänänäm. . .


   "Wherever we are made to wander about this world by the Supreme Lord's will, in accordance to
the reactions to our fruitive work, may our good works and charity always grant us love for Lord
Kåñëa."***

   Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.66 may be interpreted in two ways. It may be interpreted to refer to
vätsalya-rasa alone, or it may also be interpreted to refer to the other rasas also. Here the phrase
beginning with the word "päda" (taking shelter of Kåñëa's feet) is considered appropriate in vätsalya-
rasa because Nanda Mahäräja feels great anguish because he cannto associate with Kåñëa who has
gone to a faraway country. A similar situation in karuëa-rasa is seen in the story of Mahäräja
Citraketu. Here the word "prahvana" means "bowing down". In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.67 the
word "éçvare" is used, as it was used before, as an affectionate term used to address a child. It is
sometimes used in that way in this world. These are included amongst the udbhäsvaras. Now the
sättvika-bhävas will be considered. Of these there are eight, as were described before. For Lord
Kåñëa's mother there is a ninth sättvika-bhäva, which is milk flowing from her breasts. Now the

saïcäri-bhävas will be considered. These are: 1. thoseborn from the pastimes Lord Kåñëa directly
performs, and 2. those born from the pastimes of power and opulence manifest with thr aid of Lord
Kåñëa's pastime potency. The first of these is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.8.34):


kasmän mådam ädantätman. . .


   "Dear Kåñëa, why are You so restless that You have eaten dirt in a solitary place? This complaint
has been lodged against You by all Your playmates, including Your elder brother, Balaräma. How is
this?"***

   This is an example of Lord Kåñëa's restlessness. The second of these saïcäri-bhävas (those
pastimes of power and opulence manifest with the aid of Lord Kåñëa's pastime potency) is seen in
these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.8.37):


sä tatra dadåçe viçvam. . .


    "When Kåñëa opened His mouth wide by the order of Mother Yaçodä, she saw within His mouth
all moving and nonmoving entities, outer space, and all directions, along with mountains, islands,
oceans, the surface of the earth, the blowing wind, fire, the moon, and stars. She saw the planetary
systems, water, light, air, sky, and creation by transformation of akaìkära. She also saw the senses,
the mind, sense perception, and the three qualities goodness, passion, and ignorance. She saw the
time allotted for the living entities, she saw natural instinct and the reactions of karma, and she
saw desires and different varieties of bodies, moving and nonmoving. Seeing all these aspects of the
cosmic manifestation, along with herself and Våndävana-dhäma, she became doubtful and fearful of
her son's nature."*

  In this passage is seen Mother Yaçodä's wonder and doubt. Here the sthäyi-bhäva is vätsalya-rasa.
This sthäyi-bhäva is seen in these owrds of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.8.23):


tan-mätarau nija-sutau ghåëayä snuvantyau
   paìkäìga-räga-ruciräv upagåhya dorbhyäm
dattvä stanaà prapibatoù sma mukhaà nirékñya
   mugdha-smitälpa-daçanaà yayatuù pramodam


   "Dressed with muddy earth muxed with cow dung and cow urine, the babies looked very
beautiful, and when They went to Their mothers, both Yaçodä and Rohiëé picked Them up with
great affection, embraced Them, and allowed Them to suck the milk flowing from their breasts.
While sucking the breast, the babies smiled, and Their small teeth were visible. Their mothers,
upon seeing those beautiful teeth, enjoyed great transcendental bliss."*

   In this verse the word "tan-mätarau" means {.sy 168}the mothers of Kåñëa and Balaräma", and
"ghåëayä" means "with compassion". Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.8.23 was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva
Gosvämé.
records.content:
Al ver una demostración del extraordinario poder del Señor Krishna, un devoto en vatsalya-rasa puede pensar:
El poder no provenía de Krishna, sino de alguna otra fuente. Un ejemplo de esto se ve en
Las siguientes palabras pronunciadas por los padres del Señor Krishna en el Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.7.31):
aho bataty-adbhutam esa raksasa
balo nivrttim gamito 'bhyagat punah himsrah sva-papena vihimsitah khalah
sadhuh samatvena bhayad vimucyate
"Es sumamente asombroso que, aunque este niño inocente fue llevado por los Raksasa para ser
comido, ha regresado sin haber sido asesinado ni siquiera herido. Porque este demonio fue
Envidioso, cruel y pecador, ha sido asesinado por sus propias actividades pecaminosas. Esta es la ley de
naturaleza. Un devoto inocente siempre está protegido por la Suprema Personalidad de Dios, y un
"La persona pecadora siempre es vencida por su vida pecaminosa."
Los padres del Señor Krishna pensaban de esta manera. La madre del Señor Krishna pronunció estas palabras de srimad-
Bhagavatam (10.8.40):
Kim Svapna...
"(La madre Yasoda comenzó a discutir consigo misma:) ¿Es esto un sueño o una creación ilusoria?
¿Por la energía externa? ¿Se ha manifestado esto por mi propia inteligencia, o es algún tipo de misticismo?
¿El poder de mi hijo?
Después de ver al Señor Krishna manifestar todo el universo material dentro de su abdomen, Madre
Yasoda no podía creer que aquello fuera una demostración del gran poder de su hijo. Ella asumió que Él
no tenía poder para manifestar esta visión. (Ella asumió que la visión de la forma universal era
causado por la Suprema Personalidad de Dios, que es diferente de su hijo.) Ella pensó en
Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.8.41):
atho yathavan na vitarka-gocaram. . .
"Por lo tanto, permítanme rendirme a la Suprema Personalidad de Dios y ofrecer mis reverencias."
a Él, que está más allá de la concepción de la especulación humana, la mente, las actividades, las palabras y
argumentos, quién es la causa original de esta manifestación cósmica, por quien todo el cosmos es
mantenido, y por quien podemos concebir su existencia. Permítanme simplemente ofrecer mis reverencias, por
Él está más allá de mi contemplación, especulación y meditación. Él está más allá de toda mi comprensión material.
actividades."
Aquí la Madre Yasoda supone que esta visión de la forma universal fue causada por el Ser Supremo.
Personalidad de Dios (que es diferente de su hijo). Para liberarse de ver esto temible
visión, se refugia en los pies de loto del Señor Supremo. Entonces pensó (srimad-Bhagavatam
10.8.42):
aham mamasau. . .
"Es por la influencia de la maya del Señor Supremo que estoy pensando erróneamente que Nanda
Maharaja es mi esposo, que Krsna es mi hijo, y que porque soy la reina de Nanda Maharaja,
Toda la riqueza de vacas y terneros son mis posesiones y todos los pastores y sus esposas son
mis súbditos. En realidad, yo también estoy eternamente subordinado al Señor Supremo. Él es mi supremo.
refugio."
Con estas palabras, la Madre Yasoda se refugia firmemente en la Suprema Personalidad de Dios.
Al pronunciar las palabras "Nanda Maharaja es mi esposo, ese Krishna es mi hijo", se refiere al Señor
Krishna, que estaba entonces ante sus ojos. Entonces ella dice: "Estoy desconcertada (kumatih) por estos muchos
manifestaciones de la forma universal (yan-mayaya)." Luego dice: "la Suprema Personalidad de
La divinidad (sah) es el objetivo de mi vida (gatih). Allí Srila Sukadeva Gosvami explicó (srimad-
Bhagavatam 10.8.43):
ittham vidita-tattvayam. . .
"La madre Yasoda, por la gracia del Señor, pudo comprender la verdadera verdad. Pero luego,
El maestro supremo, por la influencia de la potencia interna, Yogamaya, la inspiró a convertirse en
"Absorta en un intenso afecto maternal por su hijo."
Aquí la palabra "tattva" se refiere a su hijo. Aquí las palabras "sa isvarah" se refieren al Señor Krishna.
característica como el controlador supremo. En el srimad-Bhagavatam 10.8.42 las palabras "pranatasmi tat-padam"
significa "Permítanme simplemente ofrecer reverencias, pues Él está más allá de mi contemplación". En el srimad-Bhagavatam
10.8.43 las palabras "vaisavim mayam" pueden significar "la potencia interna del Señor Supremo", o pueden
También significa "la misericordia del Señor Supremo". Esto se explica en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.8.45):
Trayya Copanisadbhis ca. . .
"Las glorias de la Suprema Personalidad de Dios se estudian a través de los tres Vedas, el
Los Upanishads, la literatura del sankhya-yoga y otra literatura vaisnava, sin embargo, la madre Yasoda
consideraba a la Persona Suprema como su hijo común."
También se dice en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.9.21):
nayam sukhapo bhagavan. . .
"La Suprema Personalidad de Dios, Krishna, el hijo de la madre Yasoda, es accesible a
devotos comprometidos en servicio amoroso espontáneo, pero Él no es tan fácilmente accesible a los devotos mentales
especuladores, a aquellos que se esfuerzan por la autorrealización mediante severas austeridades y penitencias, o a
aquellos que consideran que el cuerpo es lo mismo que el yo."
En estas palabras el srimad-Bhagavatam canta las tres glorias de la Madre Yasoda. También se dice en
Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.46.18-19):
api smarati nah krsnah. . .
¿Se acuerda Krishna de nosotros? ¿Se acuerda de su madre, de sus amigos y de quienes le desean lo mejor?
¿Recuerda a los pastores y su aldea de Vraja, de la cual Él es el amo? ¿Lo recuerda?
las vacas, el bosque de Vrndavana y la colina Govardhana?
apy ayasyati govindah. . .
¿Volverá Govinda siquiera una vez para ver a su familia? Si alguna vez lo hace, entonces podremos echar un vistazo a
Su hermoso rostro, con sus hermosos ojos, nariz y sonrisa."
Después de que Nanda Maharaja pronunció estas palabras, Uddhava, siguiendo el camino de este mundo,
Para consolarlo, pronunció estas palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.46.30):
yuvam slaghyatamau nunam. . .
"Oh respetuosa Nanda, ciertamente tú y la madre Yasoda sois las personas más dignas de alabanza en el mundo.
mundo entero, ya que has desarrollado una actitud tan amorosa hacia el Señor Narayana, el espiritual
amo de todos los seres vivos."
Mientras Uddhava pronunciaba estas palabras de alabanza, Nanda seguía convencido de que Krishna era suyo.
hijo y no la Suprema Personalidad de Dios. No se le podía apartar de esa idea. Entonces es
Dicho en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.46.44):
evam nisa sa bhruvator vyatita
nandasya krsnanucarasya rajan. . .
"Mientras el mensajero de Krishna seguía hablando con Nanda, la noche terminó, oh rey. Las mujeres de
Los pastores de la aldea se levantaron de sus camas y, encendiendo lámparas, adoraron a sus deidades domésticas.
Comenzaron a batir el yogur para convertirlo en mantequilla.
De esta manera, Uddhava pronunció muchas palabras para consolar a Nanda Maharaja, quien sufría por la separación.
de Krishna. Sin importar lo que dijera Uddhava, Nanda siempre estuvo convencido de que Krishna era su hijo.
y no la Suprema Personalidad de Dios. La verdad de las palabras de Uddhava, que el Señor Krishna es
De hecho, la forma original de la Suprema Personalidad de Dios se explica detalladamente en el
Krsna-sandarbha. Incluso en Kuruksetra, cuando una gran multitud de devotos santos afirmaron que el Señor
Krishna es en efecto la Suprema Personalidad de Dios, Nanda y Yasoda permanecieron sin estar convencidos.
continuaron creyendo que Krishna era solo su hijo. Esto se ve en las siguientes palabras de Srimad:
Bhagavatam (10.82.35):
tav atmasanam aropya
bahubhyam parirabhya ca yasoda ca maha-bhaga
sutau vijahatuh sucah
"Alzando a sus dos hijos en sus regazos y sosteniéndolos en sus brazos, Nanda y la santa
La madre Yasoda olvidó su dolor.
También se observa en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.47.66):
manaso vrttayo nah syuh. . .
Que nuestros pensamientos siempre encuentren refugio en los pies de loto de Krishna, que nuestras palabras siempre canten Su nombre.
nombres, y que nuestros cuerpos siempre se inclinen ante Él y le sirvan."
Aunque la verdad de que Sri Krishna es la Suprema Personalidad de Dios todopoderosa era
Una y otra vez se le demostró, Nanda Maharaja continuó creyendo que Krishna era solo su hijo y
nada más. Estas palabras (srimad-Bhagavatam 10.47.66) que Nanda le dirigió a Uddhava significan: "Oramos para que
nacimiento tras nacimiento podemos amar a Krishna." Esta oración de amor pronunciada por Nanda está llena de anuraga
amor. Loev no está ausente de él. Entonces se dice en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.47.65):
tam nirgatam samasadya
nanopayana-panayah nandadayo 'nuragena
pravocann asru-locanah
"Cuando Uddhava estaba a punto de irse, Nanda y los demás se acercaron a él portando varios objetos de
adoración. Con lágrimas en los ojos, se dirigieron a él de la siguiente manera."
En estos versos se ve que Nanda y Yasoda están llenos de un amor extático anuraga por
Señor Krishna. Su devoción al Señor no es en el estado de ánimo de asombro y veneración, sino en el estado de ánimo de
apreciando el poder supremo y la opulencia del Señor Krishna. Aquí Uddhava piensa: "Aunque estoy lejos de
Alcanzar este tipo de buena fortuna, sigo rezando para que algún día logre este tipo de
Amor extático. Ruego que este amor no me sea negado." Con la voz quebrada por la emoción.
Uddhava reza de esta manera. Rezando para que en alguna otra vida pueda algún día alcanzar este tipo de...
Del amor extático anuraga, Uddhava dice (srimad-Bhagavatam 10.47.67):
karmabhir bhramyamananam. . .
"Dondequiera que se nos haga vagar por este mundo por la voluntad del Señor Supremo, de acuerdo con
Que las reacciones a nuestra obra fruitiva, que nuestras buenas obras y caridad nos concedan siempre amor por el Señor
Krishna."
El srimad-Bhagavatam 10.47.66 puede interpretarse de dos maneras. Puede interpretarse como una referencia a
vatsalya-rasa solamente, o también puede interpretarse que se refiere a los otros rasas también. Aquí el
Se considera apropiada la frase que comienza con la palabra "pada" (refugiarse a los pies de Krishna).
en vatsalya-rasa porque Nanda Maharaja siente una gran angustia porque no puede asociarse con
Krishna, que se ha ido a un país lejano. Una situación similar en karuna-rasa se ve en la historia.
del Maharaja Citraketu. Aquí la palabra "prahvana" significa "inclinarse". En el srimad-Bhagavatam
10.47.67 La palabra "isvare" se usa, como se usaba antes, como un término cariñoso utilizado para
dirigirse a un niño. A veces se usa de esa manera en este mundo. Estos se incluyen entre los
udbhasvaras. Ahora se considerarán los sattvika- bhavas. De estos hay ocho, como fueron
descrito anteriormente. Para la madre del Señor Krishna hay un noveno sattvika-bhava, que es la leche que fluye.
de sus pechos. Ahora se considerarán los sancari-bhavas. Estos son: 1. aquellos nacidos de los
1. Pasatiempos que el Señor Krishna realiza directamente, y 2. aquellos nacidos de los pasatiempos del poder y la opulencia.
manifestado con la ayuda de la potencia de los pasatiempos del Señor Krishna. El primero de estos se ve en estas palabras.
del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.8.34):
Kasman Mrdam Adantatman. . .
"Querido Krishna, ¿por qué estás tan inquieto que has comido tierra en un lugar solitario?
Todos tus compañeros de juego, incluido tu hermano mayor, han presentado una queja contra ti.
Balarama. ¿Qué tal esto?
Este es un ejemplo de la inquietud del Señor Krishna. El segundo de estos sancari-bhavas (aquellos
pasatiempos de poder y opulencia que se manifiestan con la ayuda de la potencia de pasatiempos del Señor Krishna) se ve en
Estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.8.37):
sa tatra dadrse visvam. . .
"Cuando Krishna abrió su boca de par en par por orden de la Madre Yasoda, ella vio dentro de su boca todo
entidades móviles y no móviles, el espacio exterior y todas las direcciones, junto con montañas, islas,
los océanos, la superficie de la tierra, el viento que sopla, el fuego, la luna y las estrellas. Ella vio el
sistemas planetarios, agua, luz, aire, cielo y creación por transformación de akankara. Ella también
vio los sentidos, la mente, la percepción sensorial y las tres cualidades bondad, pasión y
ignorancia. Ella vio el tiempo asignado a las entidades vivientes, vio el instinto natural y el
reacciones del karma, y vio deseos y diferentes variedades de cuerpos, en movimiento y sin movimiento.
Al ver todos estos aspectos de la manifestación cósmica, junto con ella misma y Vrndavana-dhama, ella...
Comenzó a dudar y a temer la naturaleza de su hijo.
En este pasaje se ve el asombro y la duda de la Madre Yasoda. Aquí el sthayi-bhava es vatsalya-
rasa. Este sthayi-bhava se ve en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.8.23):
tan-matarau nija-sutau ghrnaya snuvantyau
pankanga-raga-rucirav upagrhya dorbhyam dattva stanam prapibatoh sma mukham niriksya
mugdha-smitalpa-dasanam yayatuh pramodam
"Vestidos con tierra fangosa mezclada con estiércol y orina de vaca, los bebés parecían muy
hermosas, y cuando fueron con sus madres, tanto Yasoda como Rohini las recogieron con gran alegría.
Con afecto, los abrazó y les permitió mamar la leche que fluía de sus pechos. Mientras
Al mamar del pecho, los bebés sonreían y sus pequeños dientes eran visibles. Sus madres, al...
Al ver esos hermosos dientes, experimenté una gran dicha trascendental."
En este verso la palabra "tan-matarau" significa las madres de Krsna y Balarama", y "ghrnaya"
significa "con compasión". El Srimad-Bhagavatam 10.8.23 fue hablado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
Vätsalya-rasa is wonderful with many vibhävas and other bhävas. Even before the devotees have
seen Lord Kåñëa for the first time, these ecstasies are manifest. This is seen in the following words
of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.5.9):


gopyaç cäkarëya muditä
   yaçodäyäù sütodbhavam
ätàanaà bhüñayäà cakrur
   vasträkalpäïjanädibhiù


   "The gopé wives of the cowherd men were very pleased to hear that mother Yaçodä had given
birth to a son, and they began to decorate themselves very nicely with proper dresses, ornaments,
black ointment for the eyes, and so on."*

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Vatsalya - rasa es maravilloso con muchos vibhavas y otros bhavas. Incluso antes de los devotos
Cuando uno ve al Señor Krishna por primera vez, estos éxtasis se manifiestan. Esto se observa en el
Las siguientes palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.5.9):
gopyas cakarnya mudita
yasodayah sutodbhavam atmanam bhusayam cakrur
vastrakalpanjanadibhih
"Las esposas gopis de los pastores se alegraron mucho al saber que la madre Yasoda había dado
nacimiento de un hijo, y comenzaron a adornarse muy bien con vestidos apropiados, adornos,
ungüento negro para los ojos, y cosas por el estilo."
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
After the devotees attain Lord Kåñëa's direct association the ecstasies of vätsalya-rasa become
perfectly manifest. They are seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.5.12):


ta äçiñaù. . .


   "Offering blessings to the newborn child, Kåñëa, the wives and the daughters of the cowherd
men said, `May You become the king of Vraja and logn maintain all its inhabitants.' They sprinkled
a mixture of turmeric powder, oil, and water upon the birthless Supreme Lord and offered their
prayers."*

   When the devotees become separated from Lord Kåñëa, the ecstasies of vätsalya-rasa are also
seen. An example is given in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.46.27-28):


iti saàsmåtya saàsmåtya
    nandaù kåñëänurakta-dhéù

aty-utkaëöho 'bhavat tüñëéà
   prema-prasara-vihvalaù


   "Thus intensely remembering Kåñëa again and again, Nanda Mahäräja, his mind completely
attached to the Lord, felt extreme anxiety and fell silent, overcome by the strength of his love.***


yaçodä varëyamänäni
   putrasya caritäni ca
çåëvaty açruni aväsräkñét
   sneha-snuta-payodharä


   "As mother Yaçodä heard the descriptions of her son's activities, she poured out her tears, and
milk flowed from her breasts out of love."***

  The meaning of Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.46.27-28 is clear. These verses were spoken by Çréla
Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 247 and 248


   After being separated from Him, when they again meet Kåñëa, the devotees in vätsalya-rasa are
very pleased. This is seen in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.82.35):


täv ätmäsanam äropya


  "Raising their two sons onto their laps and holding Them in their arms, Nanda and saintly
mother Yaçodä forgot their sorrow."***

   These ecstasies are also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.84.66):


nandas tu sakhyuù priya-kåt
   premëä govinda-rämayoù
adya sva iti mäsäàs trén
   yadubhir mänito 'vasat


   "And on his part, Nanda was also full of affection for his friend Vasudeva. Thus during the
following days Nanda would repeatedly announce, `I will be leaving later today' and `I will be
leaving tomorrow'. But out of love for Kåñëa and Balaräma he remained there for three more
months, honored by all the Yadus."***

   In this verse it is said: "But out of love for Kåñëa and Balaräma he remained there for three more
months." For three months he would repeatedly announce, `I will be leaving later today' and `I will
be leaving tomorrow'." Overcome with bliss, Nanda felt those three months apss as if they were only
two days. Someone may ask: "What did he do as he resided there?" The answer is given here in the
words: "Nanda was also full of affection for his friend Vasudeva." This means that when Vasudeva
was present Nanda did not act as if Kåñëa were his son. Neither did he attempt to take Kåñëa back
with him to Vraja. Then it is said here: "Nanda was honored by all the Yadus." Afterward Nanda
was again separated from Lord Kåñëa. This is described in the following words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.84.67-69):


tataù kämaiù püryamänaù
   sa-vrajaù saha-bandhavaù
parärdhyäbharaëa-kñauma-
   nänänarghya-paricchadaiù

vasudevograsenabhyäà
   kåñëoddhava-balädibhiù
dattam ädäya paribarhaà
   yäpito yadubhir yayau


   "Then, after Vasudeva, Ugrasena, Kåñëa, Uddhava, Balaräma, and others had fulfilled his desires
and presented him with precious ornaments, fine linen, and varieties of priceless household
furnishing, Nanda Mahäräja accepted all these gifts and took his leave. Seen off by all the Yadus, he
departed with his family members and the residents of Vraja.***


nando gopas ca gopyaç ca
  govinda-caraëämbuje
manaù kñiptaà punar hartum
  anéçä mathuräà yayau


   "Unable to withdraw their minds from Lord Govinda's lotus feet, where they had surrendered
them, Nanda and the cowherd men and women returned to Mathurä."***

   In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.84.67 the word "kämaiù" means "with the desires that begin with the
desire that Kåñëa would return to Vraja", and the word "püryamänaù" means "satisfied by Lord
Kåñëa". It was Lord Balaräma who returned to Vraja. In describing that pastime Çréla Çukadeva
Gosvämé said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.65.6):


kåñëe kamala-paträkñe
   sanyastäkhila-rädhasaù

   "The cowherds had dedicated everything to lotus-eyed Kåñëa."***

   Çréla Çrédhara Svämé comments:

   "In this verse the word `kåñëe' means `for the purpose of attaining Lord Kåñëa's association', and `
sanyastäkhila-rädhasaù' means `they renounced everything'."

   In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.84.67-69 it is said: {.sy 168}With great love Vasudeva and the others
gave gifts of many ornaments." Here the word "äpitaù" means {.sy 168}escorted by a great army".
Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.84.69 describes the great love the people of Vraja felt for Lord Kåñëa.
Whent hey had returned to Mathurä, the cowherd people again yearned for Lord Kåñëa's
association. Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.84.66-69 was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Después de que los devotos alcanzan la asociación directa del Señor Krishna, los éxtasis de vatsalya-rasa
Se manifiestan perfectamente. Se ven en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.5.12):
ta asisah. . .
"Ofreciendo bendiciones al niño recién nacido, Krishna, a las esposas y a las hijas del pastor de vacas."
Los hombres dijeron: «Que te conviertas en el rey de Vraja y mantengas a todos sus habitantes por siempre».
roció una mezcla de cúrcuma en polvo, aceite y agua sobre el Señor Supremo sin nacimiento y ofreció
sus oraciones."
Cuando los devotos se separan del Señor Krishna, los éxtasis de vatsalya-rasa también se desvanecen.
visto. Un ejemplo se da en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.46.27-28):
iti samsmrtya samsmrtya
nandah krsnanurakta-dhih aty-utkantho 'bhavat tusnim
prema-prasara-vihvalah
"Así, recordando intensamente a Krishna una y otra vez, Nanda Maharaja, su mente completamente
Apegada al Señor, sintió una angustia extrema y guardó silencio, abrumada por la fuerza de su amor.
Yasoda Varnyamanani
putrasya caritani ca srnvaty asruni avasraksit
sneha-snuta-payodhara
"Cuando la madre Yasoda escuchó las descripciones de las actividades de su hijo, derramó sus lágrimas,
y la leche brotó de sus pechos por amor."
El significado de srimad-Bhagavatam 10.46.27-28 es claro. Estos versos fueron pronunciados por srila
Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
It was after these pastimes that the citizens of Dvärakä spoke these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(1.11.9):


yarhy ambujäkñäpasasära bho bhavän
   kurün madhün vätha suhåd-didåkñayä


    "O lotus-eyed Lord, whenever You go away to Mathurä-Våndävana or Hastinäpura to meet Your
friends and relatives, every moment of Your absence seems like a million years. O infallible one, at
that time our eyes become useless, as if bereft of sun."*

   In Çré Kåñëa-sandarbha (Anuccheda 174) it was explained that Lord Kåñëa resides in Vraja
eternally in His aprakaöa (unmanifest) form, and therefore they people of vraja are never truly
separated from Him. Their desire to associate with Him is always satisfied. In this way vätsalya-rasa
has been described.
   Now sakhya-rasa will be described. In this rasa the älambana is Lord manifest as a friend. The
viñaya is Lord Kåñëa. The äsraya is the friends who aprticipate in Lord Kåñëa's glorous pastimes. In
this rasa the Lord sometimes manifests a form-armed form and other times manifests a humanlike
form. The four-armed form is described by Arjuna in these words of Bhagavad-gétä (11.46):


tenaiva rüpeëa catur-bhujena
   sahasra-bäho bhava viçva-mürte


   "O universal form, O thousand-armed Lord, I wish to see You in Your four-armed form."*

   Afterward, when Lord Kåñëa's humanlike form was manifest, Arjuna said in Bhagavad-gétä
(11.51):


dåñövedaà mänuñaà rüpaà
   tava saumyaà janärdana
idäném asmi samvåttaù
   sa-cetaù prakåtià gataù


   "When Arjuna saw Kåñëa in His origina form, he said: O Janärdana, seeing this humanlike form,
so very beautiful, I am now composed in mind, and I am restored to my original nature."*

   Amongst the devotees in sakhya-rasa are the mitras, suhåts, and sakhäs. Among the suhåts, Çré
Bhimasena and Çré Draupadé are prominent. Among the sakhäs, Çrémän Arjuna and Çrédämä Vipra
are prominent. In Gokula the gopa Çrédämä is prominent. These great devotees are glorified in
Çrémad-Bhägavatam and other scriptures. In the Agama-sastras, Vasudämä, Kiìkini, and other
devotees in sakhya-rasa are described. In the Bhaviñya Puräëa's description of pastimes of wrestling,
the names of some devotees in sakhya-rasa are given in these words:


subhadra-maëòalébhadra-
   bhadravardhana-gobhaöäù
yakñendrabhaöaù. . .


   "Subhadra, Maëòalébhadra, Bhadravardhana, Gobhaöa, and Yakñendrabhaöa participated in
these pastimes."

  The gopas in sakhya-rasa are also described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.12.2):


tenaiva säkaà påthukäù sahasraçaù. . .


    "At that time, hundreds and thousands of cowherd boys came out of their respective homes in
Vrajabhümi and joined Kåñëa, keeping before them their hundreds and thousands of groups of
calves. The boys were very beautiful, and they were equipped with lunch bags, bugles, flutes, and
sticks for controlling the calves."*

  These gopas were all Lord Kåñëa's equals. It is said in the scriptures:


gopaiù samäna-guëa-çéla-vayo-viläsa-vañaiç ca

   "In their qualities, character, age, pastimes, and garments, the gopa boys were like Kåñëa."

   Of the gopas it is also said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.18.11):


gopa jäti-praticchannä. . .


   "O King, demigods disguised themselves as members of the cowherd community and, just as
dramatic dancers praise another dancer, worshiped Kåñëa and Balaräma, who were also appearing
as cowherd boys."***

    This verse has been explained in Çré Kåñëa-sandarbha, Anuccheda 117. The gopas' great learning
is seen in these words they spoke in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.23.8):


déksäyäù paçu-saàsthäyäù. . .


   "Except during the interval between the initiation of the performer of a sacrifice and the actual
sacrifice of the animal, O most pure brähmaëas, it is not contaminating for even the initiated to
partake of food, at least in sacrifices other than the Sauträmaëi."***

   The gopas' expert artistic skill is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.18.13):


kvacin nåtyatsu cänyeñu. . .


   "While the other boys were dancing, O King, Kåñëa and Balaräma would sometimes accompany
them with song and instrumental music, and sometimes the two Lords would praise the boys, saying,
``Very good! Very good!' "***

   In these words Lord Kåñëa Himself praised the gopas' glorious qualities. The gopas are of three
kinds: 1. sakhä (ordinary friends), 2. priya-sakhä (more confidential friends), and 3. priya-narma-
sakhä (intimate friends). The gopa Çrédämäa and the other gopas enjoy very sweeet pastimes with
Lord Kåñëa. They are described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.12.11):


itthaà satäà. . .


   "In this way, all the cowherd boys used to play with Kåñëa, who is the source of the Brahman
effulgence for jïänés desiring to merge into that effulgence, who is the Supreme Personality of
Godhead for devotees who have accepted eternal servitorship, and who for ordinary persons is but
another ordinary child. The cowherd boys, having accumulated the results of pious activities for
many lives, were able to associate in this way with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. How can

one explain their great fortune?"*

   In this rasa lord Kåñëa is the älambana. Lord Kåñëa as the älambana is described in these words
of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.21.5):


barhäpéòaà naöa-vara-vapuù. . .


   "Wearing a peacock-feather ornament upon His head, blue karnikära flowers on His ears, a
yellow garment as brilliant as gold, and the Vaijayanté garland, Lord Kåñëa exhibited His
transcendental form as the greatest of dancers as He entered the forest of Våndävana, beautifying it
with the marks of His footprints. He filled the holes of His flute with the nectar of His lips, and the
cowherd boys sang His glories."***

   Mow the uddépanas in this rasa will be considered. Amongst these uddépanas are included the
following transcendental qualities: loving friendship, straightforwardness, gratitude, intelligence,
learning, glory, expert skill, heroism, strength, tolerance, mercy, and giving delight to the people.
Also included amongst these uddépanas are youthful handsomeness, all-auspicious bodily features,
and other qualities. For the suhåt friends the qualities beginning with straightforwardness are
prominent. For the sakhä friends the qualities beginning with handsomeness and skill are
prominent. For the mitra friends the qualities beginning with straightforwardness, handsomeness,
and skill are prominent. The suhåt, sakhä, and mitra kinds of friendship are mentioned by
lamenting Arjuna in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (1.15.4):


sakhyaà maitréà sauhådaà ca. . .


  "Remembering Lord Kåñëa and His well wishes, benefactions, intimate familial relations and His
chariot driving, Arjuna, overwhelmed and breathing very heavily, began to speak."***

   Lord Kåñëa's friendly affection for the gopas is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.13.13 and 16):


tän dåsövä bhaya-santrastän
   üce kåñëo'sya bhé-bhayam
miträëy äçän mä viramate-
   häneñye vatsakän aham


   "When Kåñëa saw that His friends the cowherd boys were frightened, He, the fierce controller
even of fear itself, said, just to mitigate their fear, `My dear friends, do not stop eating. I shall bring
your calves back to this spot by personally going after them Myself.' "***

tato vatsän adåñövaitya
   puline 'pi ca vatsapän
ubhäv api vane kåñëo
   vicikäya samantataù


   "Thereafter, when Kåñëa was unable to find the calves, He returned to the bank of the river, but
there He was also unable to see the cowherd boys. Thus He began to search for both the calves and
the boys, as if He could not understand what had happened."*

   The meaning of these verses (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.13.13 and 16) is clear. These verses were
spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Fue después de estos pasatiempos que los ciudadanos de Dvaraka pronunciaron estas palabras de srimad-
Bhagavatam (1.11.9):
yarhy ambujaksapasasara bho bhavan
kurun madhun vatha suhrd-didrksaya
"Oh Señor de ojos de loto, siempre que te vayas a Mathura-Vrindavana o Hastinapura para encontrarte con Tu
Amigos y familiares, cada momento de Tu ausencia parece un millón de años. ¡Oh infalible!
En ese momento nuestros ojos se vuelven inútiles, como si estuvieran privados de sol.
En el sri Krsna-sandarbha (Anuccheda 174) se explicó que el Señor Krsna reside en Vraja.
eternamente en Su forma aprakata (no manifestada), y por lo tanto, la gente de vraja nunca es verdaderamente
separados de Él. Su deseo de asociarse con Él siempre se satisface. De esta manera vatsalya-
Se ha descrito el rasa.
Ahora se describirá el sakhya-rasa. En este rasa, el alambana es el Señor manifestado como un amigo.
Visaya es el Señor Krishna. Asraya son los amigos que participan en los gloriosos pasatiempos del Señor Krishna.
En este rasa, el Señor a veces manifiesta una forma armada y otras veces manifiesta una forma humana.
forma. Arjuna describe la forma de cuatro brazos con estas palabras del Bhagavad-gita (11.46):
tenaiva rupena catur-bhujena
sahasra-baho bhava visva-murte
"Oh forma universal, oh Señor de mil brazos, deseo verte en tu forma de cuatro brazos."
Después, cuando la forma humana del Señor Krishna se manifestó, Arjuna dijo en el Bhagavad-gita
(11.51):
drstvedam manusam rupam
tava saumyam janardana idanim asmi samvrttah
sa-cetah prakrtim gatah
"Cuando Arjuna vio a Krishna en su forma original, dijo: Oh Janardana, viendo esta forma semejante a la humana,
Es tan hermoso, ahora estoy en paz y he recuperado mi naturaleza original."
