"Cuando el Señor Sri Krishna estaba bailando con las gopis en el rasa-lila, las gopis fueron abrazadas por
los brazos del Señor. Este favor trascendental nunca fue otorgado a la diosa de la fortuna o
otros consortes en el mundo espiritual. De hecho, jamás se imaginó algo así por parte de los más
Hermosas muchachas en los planetas celestiales, cuyo brillo corporal y aroma se asemejan a la flor de loto.
¿Y qué decir de las mujeres mundanas que son muy bellas según los estándares materiales?
Las gopis son glorificadas nuevamente en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.44.14):
gopyas tapah kim acaran yad amusya rupam. . .
¡Qué austeridades debieron haber realizado las gopis! Con sus ojos siempre beben el néctar.
de la forma del Señor Krishna, que es la esencia de la hermosura y no debe ser igualada ni superada.
Esa hermosura es la única morada de belleza, fama y opulencia. Es perfecta en sí misma, siempre fresca y
extremadamente raro."
Este versículo dice: "Las gopis contemplaron la forma del Señor Krishna, que no tiene igual ni igual.
superadas". Las gopis son glorificadas nuevamente en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.44.15):
ya dohane 'vahanane mathanopalepa. . .
. . .dhanya vraja-striya urukrama-citta-yanah
"Las damas de Vraja son las mujeres más afortunadas porque, con sus mentes completamente enfocadas,
a Krsna y sus gargantas siempre ahogadas por las lágrimas, constantemente cantan sobre Él mientras
ordeñar las vacas, aventar el grano, batir la mantequilla, recoger estiércol de vaca para combustible, montar en columpios,
cuidando a sus bebés que lloraban, rociando el suelo con agua, limpiando sus casas y
y así sucesivamente. Gracias a su elevada conciencia de Krishna, adquieren automáticamente todas las cosas deseables."
En este versículo la palabra "urukrama-citta-yanah" significa "aquellos cuyo carro es el todopoderoso".
mente". Esto significa que dondequiera que fueran sus mentes, ellos, cabalgando en el carro de la mente, estaban
capaz de ir." Una lectura alternativa nos da "cinta-yanah" en lugar de "citta-yanah". El significado,
Sin embargo, permanece igual. El srimad-Bhagavatam 10.44.15 fue pronunciado por las mujeres de la ciudad de Mathura.

records.sourceEnglish:
In this way the great glory of the gopés' love for Lord Kåñëa is seen. Their love is gloriosu because
it is forbidden, because it is love for a paramour (parakéya). Even in ordinary affairs of the materuial
world, this kind of forbidden love is understood to be very intense. The author Bharata explains:


bahu väryate yataù khalu
   yatra pracchanna-kämukatvaà ca
yä ca mitho durlabhatä
   sä paramä manmathasya ratiù


   "The highest amorous pleasure is attained when love is forbidden, when the lovers must conceal
their love, when the lovers rarely meet."

   The author Rudra explains:


vämatä durlabhatvaà ca
   stréëäà ya ca niväraëä
tad eva païca-bäëasya
   manye paramam äyudham


  "Contrariness, difficulty of attainment, and rejection by women I consider Kämadeva's greatest
weapons."

   The author Viñëu-gupta explains:


yatra niñedha-viçeñaù
   su-durlabhatvaà ca yan mågäkñéëäm
tatraiva nägaräëäà
   nirbharam äsajjate hådayam


   "When love is forbidden and the doe-eyed beloved is difficult to attain, then the passionate
lover's heart becomes very attached to his beloved."

   Some gopé girls prayed to Goddess Katyayani that they might attain Lord Kåñëa as their
husband. Their desire to attain Him was very strong. Because Kåñëa was unattainable for them,
their love for Him was very great. The greatness oftheir love is described in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.83.43):


vraja-striyo yad väïchanti. . .


   "We desire the same contact with the Supreme Lord's feet that thr young women of Vraja, the
cowherd boys, and even the aborigine Pulinda women desire-the touch of the dust He leaves on the
plants and grass as He tends His cows."***

   Their love is also described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.58):


väïchanti yad bhava-bhiyaù. . .


   "Among all persons on earth, these cowherd women alone have actually perfected their
embodied lives, for they have achieved the perfection of unalloyed love for Lord Govinda. Their
pure love is hankered after by those who fear material existence, by great sages, and by ourselves as
well. For one who has tasted the narrations of the infinite Lord, what is the use of taking birth as a
high-class brähmaëa, or even as Lord Barhmä himself?"***

   Still, the gs' intesne desire to attain Lord Kåñëa was not born merely because they were
forbidden to associate with Him. They certrainly did not wish to be forbidden or to have so many
obstacles placed befope them. Rather they loved Him in spite of being so strongly forbidden, This is
described in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.61):


yä dustyajam. . .

    "The gopés of Våndävana have given up the association of their husbands, sons, and other family
members, who are very difficult to give up, andf they have forsaken the path of chastity to take
shelter of tyhe lotus feet of Mukunda, Kåñëa, which one should search for by Vedic knowledge. Oh,
let me be fortunate enough to be one of the bushes, creepers, or herbs in Våndävana, because the
gopés trample them and bless them with the dust of their feet."*

   As a wild elephant cannot be stopped, so the gopés' passionate love for Kåñëa could not be
stopped. Although the gopés were all forbidden in the smae way to associate with Lord Kåñëa, still
they each had a different intensity of love for Him. Of them all Rädhä had the greatest love. She
had the greatest power to bring Lord Kåñëa under Her control. The supremely exalted position of
Çré Rädhä's love is indirectly described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.28):


anayärädhito nünam. . .


   "Certainly this particular gopé has perfectly worshiped the all-powerful Personality of Godhead,
Govinda, since He was so pleased with Her that He abandoned the rest of us and brought Her to a
secluded place."***

   In tyhis way the gopés' love for Lord Kåñëa blossomed. It was as if they had been bitten by the
black snake of love for Kåñëa. They did not associate with Kåñëa as a wife associates with her
husband. Rather they passionately loved Kåñëa as a girl loves her paramour. This kind of love is
criticized in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.7-8):


niùsvaà tyajanti gaëikä. . .


   "Prostitutes abandon a penniless man."***


järä bhuktvä ratäà striyam


   "A lover abandons the woman he has enjoyed, even though she remains attached to him."***

   It is said that girls who love someone other than their husbands (parakéya) are fallen and worthy
of contempt. This is true for girls who take shelter of individual souls who live in the material
world. The situation of such girls is abominable. However these defects asnd criticisms do not apply
to the gopés. This truth is seen in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.35):

gopénäà tat-paténäà ca. . .


   "He who lives as the overseeing witness within the gopés and their husbands, and indeed within

all embodied living beings, assumes forms in this world to enjoy transcendental pastimes."***

   From the material point of view it seemed that the gopés had husbands other than Kåñëa.
However, from the spiritual point of view these so-called husbands did not exist. In the Kåñëa-
sandarbha it has already been shown that the gopés' so-called husbands were in truth only a display
manifested from Lord Kåñëa's internal potency. Therefore it is Lord Kåñëa Himself who is
ultimately the gs only true husband. The gopés' exalted position, which has so equal or superior, is
described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.58):


etäù paraà tanu-bhåtaù. . .


   "Among all persons on earth, these cowherd women alone have actually perfected their
embodied lives, for they have achieved the perfection of unalloyed love for Lord Govinda. Their
pure love is hankered after by those who fear material existence, by great sages, and by ourselves as
well. For one who has tasted the narrations of the infinite Lord, what is the use of taking birth as a
high-class brähmaëa, or even as Lord Barhmä himself?"***

   The gopés' glories are also described in these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi:


neñöä yad aìgini rase kavibhiù paroòhä
   tad gokulämbuja-dåçäà kulam antareëa
äçaàsayä rasa-vidher avatäritänäà
   kaàsäriëä rasika-maëòala-çekhareëa


   "Philosophers do not praise adultery. However, they do praise the pastimes Lord Kåñëa, the
crown of all rasikas, enjoys with Gokula's lotus-eyed girls, girls who descended to this world to enjoy
nectar pastimes with Him."

   The gopés did not have even a dim reflection of contact with their so-called husbands. This is
seen in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.37):


näsüyan khalu kåñëäya
   mohitäs tasya mäyayä
manyamänäù sva-pärçva-sthän
   svän svän därän vrajaukasaù


  "The cowherd men, bewildered by Kåñëa's illusory potency, thought their wives had remained
home at their sides. Thus they did not harbor any jealous feelings against Him."***

   The gopés are eternally dear to Lord Kåñëa. They are His consorts eternally. This verse explains:

"The cowherd men, bewildered by Kåñëa's illusory potency, thought their wives had remained home
at their sides. Thus they did not harbor any jealous feelings against Him."*** This verse was spoken
by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
De esta manera se ve la gran gloria del amor de las gopis por el Señor Krishna. Su amor es glorioso.
porque está prohibido, porque es amor por un amante (parakiya). Incluso en asuntos cotidianos.
En el mundo material, este tipo de amor prohibido se entiende como muy intenso. El autor
Bharata explica:
bahu varyate yatah khalu
yatra pracchanna-kamukatvam ca ya ca mitho durlabhata
sa parama manmathasya ratih
"El mayor placer amoroso se alcanza cuando el amor está prohibido, cuando los amantes deben
"Ocultan su amor, cuando los amantes rara vez se encuentran."
El autor Rudra explica:
vamata durlabhatvam ca
strinam ya ca nivarana tad eva panca-banasya
manye paramam ayudham
"La contradicción, la dificultad de alcanzarla y el rechazo por parte de las mujeres considero que Kamadeva
las mejores armas."
El autor Visnu-gupta explica:
Yatra Nisedha-Visesah
su-durlabhatvam ca yan mrgaksinam tatraiva nagaranam
nirbharam asajjate hrdayam
"Cuando el amor está prohibido y la amada de ojos grandes es difícil de alcanzar, entonces la apasionada
El corazón del enamorado se apega mucho a su amada.
Algunas niñas gopi rezaron a la Diosa Katyayani para poder alcanzar al Señor Krishna como su
esposo. Su deseo de alcanzarlo era muy fuerte. Porque Krishna era inalcanzable para ellos,
Su amor por Él era muy grande. La grandeza de su amor se describe en estas palabras de
Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.83.43):
vraja-striyo yad vanchanti. . .
"Deseamos el mismo contacto con los pies del Señor Supremo que las jóvenes de Vraja, las
Los pastores jóvenes, e incluso las mujeres aborígenes Pulinda desean el toque del polvo que Él deja en
las plantas y la hierba mientras cuida de sus vacas."
Su amor también se describe en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.47.58):
vanchanti yad bhava-bhiyah. . .
"Entre todas las personas de la tierra, solo estas mujeres pastoras han perfeccionado realmente su arte corporal.
vidas, porque han alcanzado la perfección del amor puro por el Señor Govinda. Su amor puro
Es anhelada por aquellos que temen la existencia material, por los grandes sabios y también por nosotros mismos.
Para aquel que ha probado las narraciones del Señor infinito, ¿de qué sirve nacer como un ser humano?
¿Un brahmán de clase alta, o incluso el mismísimo Señor Barhma?
Sin embargo, el intenso deseo de los gs de alcanzar al Señor Krishna no nació simplemente porque estaban
Prohibido asociarse con Él. Ciertamente no deseaban que se les prohibiera o tener tantos
obstáculos puestos delante de ellos. Más bien lo amaron a pesar de estar tan fuertemente prohibido, esto
Se describe en las siguientes palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.47.61):
ya dustyajam. . .
"Las gopis de Vrindavana han renunciado a la compañía de sus maridos, hijos y otros
miembros de la familia, que son muy difíciles de abandonar, y si han abandonado el camino de la castidad
para refugiarse en los pies de loto de Mukunda, Krishna, que uno debe buscar según los védicos.
conocimiento. Oh, déjame tener la fortuna de ser uno de los arbustos, enredaderas o hierbas en
Vrindavana, porque las gopis los pisotean y los bendicen con el polvo de sus pies."
Así como a un elefante salvaje no se le puede detener, el amor apasionado de las gopis por Krishna no podía ser detenido.
se detuvo. Aunque a todas las gopis se les prohibió de la misma manera asociarse con el Señor Krishna,
Sin embargo, cada uno de ellos tenía una intensidad de amor diferente por Él. De todos ellos, Radha tenía el más grande.
amor. Ella tenía el mayor poder para someter al Señor Krishna a Su control. El supremamente exaltado
La posición del amor de Sri Radha se describe indirectamente en estas palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam.
(10.30.28):
anayaradhito nunam. . .
"Ciertamente, esta gopi en particular ha adorado perfectamente a la todopoderosa Personalidad de Dios.
Divinidad, Govinda, puesto que Él estaba tan complacido con Ella que nos abandonó al resto y nos trajo
La llevé a un lugar apartado."
De esta manera, el amor de las gopis por el Señor Krishna floreció. Fue como si hubieran sido mordidas por
la serpiente negra del amor por Krsna. No se asociaron con Krsna como una esposa se asocia con
su esposo. Más bien, amaban apasionadamente a Krishna como una chica ama a su amante. Este tipo de amor
Se critica en las siguientes palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.47.7-8):
nihsvam tyajanti ganika. . .
"Las prostitutas abandonan a un hombre sin un centavo."
jara bhuktva ratam striyam
"Un amante abandona a la mujer con la que ha tenido relaciones, aunque ella siga apegada a él."
Se dice que las chicas que aman a alguien que no es su marido (parakiya) están caídas y
digno de desprecio. Esto es cierto para las chicas que se refugian en almas individuales que viven en el
mundo material. La situación de estas chicas es abominable. Sin embargo, estos defectos y críticas
No se aplican a las gopis. Esta verdad se ve en las siguientes palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam.
(10.33.35):
gopinam tat-patinam ca. . .
"Aquel que vive como testigo supervisor dentro de las gopis y sus maridos, y en verdad
Dentro de todos los seres vivos encarnados, se adoptan formas en este mundo para disfrutar de pasatiempos trascendentales."
Desde el punto de vista material, parecía que las gopis tenían maridos distintos de Krishna.
Sin embargo, desde el punto de vista espiritual, estos supuestos maridos no existían. En el Krsna-
sandarbha ya se ha demostrado que los supuestos maridos de las gopis eran en realidad solo un
Exhibición manifestada desde la potencia interna del Señor Krishna. Por lo tanto, es el Señor Krishna mismo quien es
en última instancia el único esposo verdadero de las gopis. La posición exaltada de las gopis, que tiene tan igual o superior,
Se describe en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.47.58):
etah param tanu-bhrtah. . .
"Entre todas las personas de la tierra, solo estas mujeres pastoras han perfeccionado realmente su arte corporal.
vidas, porque han alcanzado la perfección del amor puro por el Señor Govinda. Su amor puro
Es anhelada por aquellos que temen la existencia material, por los grandes sabios y también por nosotros mismos.
Para aquel que ha probado las narraciones del Señor infinito, ¿de qué sirve nacer como un ser humano?
¿Un brahmán de clase alta, o incluso el mismísimo Señor Barhma?
Las glorias de las gopis también se describen en estas palabras de Ujjvala-nilamani:
nesta yad angini rase kavibhih parodha
tad gokulambuja-drsam kulam antarena asamsaya rasa-vidher avataritanam
kamsarina rasika-mandala-sekharena
"Los filósofos no alaban el adulterio. Sin embargo, sí alaban los pasatiempos del Señor Krishna, el
corona de todos los rasikas, disfruta con las chicas de ojos de loto de Gokula, chicas que descendieron a este mundo para
Disfruta de momentos dulces y placenteros con Él."
Las gopis no tenían ni el más mínimo contacto con sus supuestos maridos.
Esto se observa en las siguientes palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.33.37):
nasuyan khalu krsnaya
mohitas tasya mayaya manyamanah sva-parsva-sthan
svan svan daran vrajaukasah
"Los pastores, desconcertados por la potencia ilusoria de Krishna, pensaron que sus esposas habían permanecido
en casa a su lado. Por lo tanto, no albergaban celos contra Él.
Las gopis son eternamente queridas por el Señor Krishna. Son Sus consortes eternamente. Este verso
explica: "Los hombres pastores, desconcertados por la potencia ilusoria de Krsna, pensaron que sus esposas tenían
permanecieron en casa a su lado. Por lo tanto, no albergaron ningún sentimiento de celos contra Él." Esto
El verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
In this way it is seen that the gopés' love for Lord Kåñëa is most exalted. The spiritual forms of
Lord Kåñëa and the gopés are described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.29.43):


täbhiù sametäbhir udära-ceñöitaù. . .


   "Among the assembled gopés, the infallible Lord Kåñëa appeared just like the moon surrounded
by stars. He whose activifies are so magnanimous made their faces blossom with His affectionate
glances, and His broad smiles revealed the effulgence of His jasmine-bud-like teeth."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
De esta manera se ve que el amor de las gopis por el Señor Krishna es sumamente elevado. El espiritual
Las formas del Señor Krishna y las gopis se describen en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.29.43):
tabhih Sametabhir udara-cestitah. . .
"Entre las gopis reunidas, el infalible Señor Krishna apareció como la luna que las rodeaba.
por las estrellas. Aquel cuyas activismos son tan magnánimos hizo florecer sus rostros con Su afecto
Sus miradas, y sus amplias sonrisas, revelaban el resplandor de sus dientes, semejantes a capullos de jazmín."
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
The spiritual forms of Lord Kåñëa and the gopés are again described in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.33.6):


taträtiçuçubhe täbhir
   bhagavän devaké-sutaù
madhye maëénäà haimänäà
   mahä-marakato yathä


   "In the midst of the dancing gopés, Lord Kåñëa appeared most brilliant, like an exquisite sapphire
in the midst of golden ornaments."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Las formas espirituales del Señor Krishna y las gopis se describen nuevamente en estas palabras del srimad-
Bhagavatam (10.33.6):
tatratisusubhe tabhir
bhagavan devaki-sutah madhye maninam haimanam
maha-marakato yatha
"En medio de las gopis danzantes, el Señor Krishna apareció resplandeciente, como un ser exquisito
un zafiro en medio de ornamentos dorados."
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
The spiritural powers and glories and virtues of Lord Kåñëa and the gopés are described in these
words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.32.10):

täbhir vidhüta-çokäbhir
   bhagavän acyuto våtah
vyarocatädhikaà täta
   puruñaù çaktibhir yatha


   "Encircled by the gopés, who were now relieved of all distress, Lord Acyuta, the Supreme
Personality of Godhead, shone forth splendidly. My dear King, Kåñëa thus appeared like the
Supersoul encircled by His spiritual potencies."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Los poderes espirituales, las glorias y las virtudes del Señor Krishna y las gopis se describen en
Estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.32.10):
tabhir vidhuta-sokabhir
bhagavan acyuto vrtah vyarocatadhikam tata
purusah saktibhir yatha
"Rodeado por las gopis, que ahora estaban libres de toda angustia, el Señor Acyuta, el Supremo
La Personalidad de Dios resplandeció espléndidamente. Mi querido Rey, Krishna apareció así como la
El Alma Suprema rodeada por Sus potencias espirituales."
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
The transcendental artistic genius of Lord Kåñëa and the gopé is described in these words of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.7-8):


päda-nyäsair bhuja-vidhutibhiù. . .


   "As the gopés sang in praise of Kåñëa, their feet danced, their hands gestured, and their eyebrows
moved with playful smiles. With their braids and belts tied tight, their waists bending, their faces
perspiring, the garments on their breasts moving this way and that, and their earrings swinging on
their cheeks, Lord Kåñëa's young consorts shone like streaks of lightning in a mass of clouds.***


uccair jagur nåtyamänä
   rakta-kaëöhyo rati-priyäù
kåñëäbhimarça-muditä
   yad-gétenedam ävrtam


  "Eager to enjoy conjugal love, their throats colored with various pigments, the gopés sang loudly
and danced. They were overjoyed by Kåñëa's touch, and they sang songs that filled the entire
universe."***

    In this verse the word "idam" (this) refers to the universe. This verse says that the gopés' songs
filled the entire universe. In the Saìgéta-sära itis said:


tävanta eva rägä syur
   yävatyo jéva-jätayaù
teñu ñoòaça-sähasré

   purä gopé-kåtä varä


   "The rägas number 16,000, as many as there are species of life. The gopés sang songs in all these
rägas."

  At the end of this book it is said that these rägas are seen in Svargaloka and the other higher
material planets.
records.content:
El genio artístico trascendental del Señor Krishna y la gopi se describe en estas palabras de
Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.33.7-8):
pada-nyasair bhuja-vidhutibhih. . .
"Mientras las gopis cantaban en alabanza de Krishna, sus pies danzaban, sus manos gesticulaban y sus
Las cejas se movían con sonrisas juguetonas. Con sus trenzas y cinturones bien ajustados, sus cinturas arqueadas,
sus rostros sudaban, las prendas sobre sus pechos se movían de un lado a otro, y sus pendientes
Balanceándose sobre sus mejillas, las jóvenes consortes del Señor Krishna brillaban como rayos en una multitud.
de nubes.
Uccair Jagur Nrtyamana
rakta-kanthyo rati-priyah krsnabhimarsa-mudita
yad-gitenedam avrtam
Ansiosas por disfrutar del amor conyugal, con sus gargantas teñidas de diversos pigmentos, las gopis cantaban.
gritaban y bailaban. Estaban rebosantes de alegría por el toque de Krishna y cantaban canciones que llenaban el
universo entero."
En este versículo la palabra "idam" (este) se refiere al universo. Este versículo dice que las gopis
Las canciones llenaban todo el universo. En el Sangita-sara se decía:
tavanta eva raga syur
yavatyo jiva-jatayah tesu sodasa-sahasri
pura gopi-krta vara
"Los ragas suman 16.000, tantos como especies de vida existen. Las gopis cantaron canciones en todos ellos.
estos ragas."
Al final de este libro se dice que estos ragas se ven en Svargaloka y los demás
planetas de mayor materialidad.

records.sourceEnglish:
The gopés' songs are also described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.9):


käcit samaà mukundena
   svara jätér amiçritäù
unninye püjitä tena
   préyatä sädhu sädhv iti
tad eva dhruvam unninye
   tasyai mänaà ca bahv adät


   "One gopé, joining Lord Mukunda in His singing, sang pure melodious tones that rose
harmoniously above His. Kåñëa was pleased and showed great appreciation for her performance,
saying `Excellent! Excellent!' Then another gopé repeated the same melody, but in a special metrical
pattern, and Kåñëa praised her also."***

   In this verse the word "svaräù" means the scale of seven notes beginning with the sixth note",
and {.sy 168}jätayaù" means "the räga that comes from that scale". Here "amisritah" means that
because Kåñëa and the gopés were very expert, the melodies they sang did not become mixed. The
melodies remained pure, and "unninye" means "the melodies were gloriously sung". The gopés sang
together with Lord Kåñëa, Kåñëa whose melodies even Brahmä, Çiva, Indra and all the demigods
have no power to understand. The singing of Kåñëa and the gopés was equal. The singing of one did
not dominate the singing of the other. The words "püjitä tena" mean "with their treble voices the
gopés worshiped Lord Kåñëa". Here the word "dhruvam" means "a gopé sang a melody in the dhruva
rhythm, and "tasyai mänam adät" means "Lord Kåñëa praised her". This verse was spoken by Çréla
Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 285 and 286


   Among the ordinary (sämänya) conjugal lovers of Lord Kåñëa, Kubjä is the most exalted. Among
the queens married (svakéya) to Lord Kåñëa, Çré Rukmiëé and Çré Satyabhämä are mosty exalted.

They are described in the following words of Hari-vaàça:


kuöumbasyeçvaré cäséd
   rukmiëé bhéñmakätmajä
satyabhämottamä stréëäà
   saubhägye cädhikäbhavat


  "Bhéñmaka's daughter, Rukmiëé, is the controller of Lord Kåñëa's household. Satyabhämä is the
most fortunate of Lord Kåñëa's wives."

  The most exalted of the goddesslike gopés of Vraja are described in these words of the Bhaviñya
Puräëa, Uttara-khaëòa:


gopälé pälikä dhanyä
   viçäkhä dhyäna-niñöhikä
rädhänurädhä somäbhä
   tärakä daçamé tathä


  "The ten most prominent gopés are Gopälé, Pälikä, Dhanyä, Viçäkhä, Dhyäna-niñöhikä, Rädhä,
Anurädhä, Somäbhä, and Tärakä."

   Here the words "tärakä daçamé" mean "the tenth gopé is named Tärakä". In ther Skanda Purana,
Prahlada-samhita the four gopés Lalitä, Çaibyä, Padmä, and Bhadrä are included amongst the most
prominent gopés. In other places in the scriptures Candrävalé is also included amongst the
prominent gopés. The Somäbhä mentioned in the previous quote from the Bhaviñya Puräëa is the
same as Candrävalé. In the Agama-çästras it is said:


pramadä-çata-koöibhir äkulitaù


   "Lord Kåñëa is surrounded by hundreds and millions of beautiful gopés."

  Amongst all the gopés, Rädhä is the most important. It is because of her great love that Lord
Kåñëa disappeared from the räsa dance. This has already been described in the Çré Kåñëa-sandarbha
(Anuccheda 189). Rädhä is celebrated in all the scriptures. In the Gopäla-täpané Upaniñad she is
known by the name Gändharvikä.

   Lord Kåñëa's beloveds are of three kinds: 1. mugdhä (meek), 2. madhyä (niteermediate), and 3.
pragalbhä (arrogant). They are also of three ages: 1. nava-yauavana (new youth), 2. spañöa (clearly
manifested youth), and 3. (samyag-yauvana (fully blossomed youth). According to these different
ages different kinds of activities are manifested. The age of samyag-yuavana is sixteen years. It is

not older than that. This is seeen in the following words of the Gautaméya Tantra:

kanyäbhir dvy-añöa-varñäbhiù


   "Lord Kåñëa is surrounded by sixteen-year-old gopés."

   The termperments of the Lord's beloveds are of three kinds: 1. dhérä (peaceful), 2. adhérä
(agitated), and 3. miçra-guëä (a mixture of peace and agitation). Their love for Lord Kåñëa they are
also of three kinds: 1. çreñöhä (best), 2. samä (intermediate), and 3. laghu (least).
   In their pastimes with Lord Kåñëa, His beloveds are in the following eight situations: 1.
abhisärikä (meeting Kåñëa ina rendezvous), 2. väsaka-sajjä (dressing in fine garments and
ornaments to prepare for a rendezvous with Kåñëa), 3. utkaëöhitä (yearning to meet Kåñëa at the
rendezvous), 4. khaëòitä (jilted by Kåñëa), 5. vipralabdhä (separated from Kåñëa), 6. kalahäntaritä
(feuding with Kåñëa), 7. proñita-preyasé (separated from Kåñëa because He has gone to a faraway
place), and 8. svädhéna-bhartåkä (dominating Kåñëa). In their realtions with each other, Lord
Kåñëa's beloveds have four kinds of natures: 1. sädåçya (alike), kiïcit-sädåçya (somewhat alike), 3.
aspañöa-sädåçya (not clearly alike), and 4. virodhi (opposed). These four natures are manifest as the
following four kinds of relationships: 1. sakhé (friend), 2. suhåt (well-wisher), 3. taöasthä (neutral
person), and prätipakñiké (rival). In this way the Lord's beloveds have different natures. A sakhé
spoke these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.1):


apy eëa-patné. . .tanvan dåçäà sakhi su-nirvåtim


   "O friend, wife of the deer, has Lord Acyuta been here with His beloved, bringing great joy to
your eyes? Indeed, blowing this way is the fragrance of His garland of kunòa flowers, which was
smeared with the kuìkuma from the breasts of His girlfriend when He embraced Her."***

   Here the words "tanvan dåçäà sakhi su-nirvåtim" (O friend, has Lord Acyuta been here with His
beloved, bringing great joy to your eyes?) were spoken by the gopés because they yearned to see Lord
Kåñëa. Here the word "sakhi" (O friend) shows that the gopés imagined the deer to be like them,
delighted by the sight of Lord Kåñëa. In this way they imagined that the deer were their friends.
Here the word "käntä" means "the great good fortune of Lord Kåñëa's girlfriend", "kula-pateù" means
"of Lord Kåñëa", and "käntäìga-saìge" means "delighted by the fragrance of the two lovers'
embraces". The pleasures Rädhä and Kåñëa enjoy in Their pastimes are described in these words of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.12):


bähuà priyäàsa. . .


     "O trees, we see that you are bowing down. When the younger brother of Räma walked by here,
followed by intoxicated bees swarming around the tulasé maïjarés decorating His garland, did He
acknowledge your obeisances with His affectionate glances? He must have been resting His arm on

the shoulder of His beloved and carrying a lotus flower in His free hand."***

   A suhåt (well-wisher) spoke these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.28):


anayärädhito nünaà
   bhagavan harir isvaraù
yan no vihäya govindaù
   préto yäm amayad rahaù


   "Certainly this particular gopé has perfectly worshiped the all-powerful Personality of Godhead,
Govinda, since He was so pleased with Her that He abandoned the rest of us and brought Her to a
secluded place."***

  Because she praises Çré Rädhä's good fortune, the gopé who speak this verse is a suhåt. After
hearing a sakhé speak Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.30.11, a The taöasthä (neutral person) spoke these
words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.13):


påcchatemä latä bähün
   apy äçliñöä vanaspateù
nünaà tat-karaja-spåñöä
   bibhraty utpulakäny aho


   "Let us ask these creepers about Kåñëa. Even though they are embracing the arms of their
husband, this tree, they certainly must have been touched by Kåñëa's fingernails, since out of joy
they are manifesting eruptions on their skin."***

  After hearing a suhåt speak Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.30.28, a taöasthä spoke these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.30.29):


dhanyä aho amé alyaù. . .


  "O girls! The dust of Govinda's lotus feet is so sacred that even Brahmä, Çiva and the goddess
Ramä take that dust upon their heads to dispel sinful reactions."***
records.content:
Los cantos de las gopis también se describen en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.33.9):
kacit samam mukundena
svara jatir amisritah unninye pujita tena
priyata sadhu sadhv iti tad eva dhruvam unninye
tasyai manam ca bahv adat
"Una gopi, uniéndose al Señor Mukunda en su canto, cantó tonos puros y melodiosos que se elevaban
armoniosamente por encima de Él. Krishna se complació y mostró gran aprecio por su actuación.
diciendo "¡Excelente! ¡Excelente!" Luego otra gopi repitió la misma melodía, pero en un tono especial.
patrón métrico, y Krishna también la alabó."
En este versículo, la palabra "svarah" significa la escala de siete notas que comienza con la sexta.
nota", y jatayah" significa "el raga que proviene de esa escala". Aquí "amisritah" significa que
Debido a que Krishna y las gopis eran muy expertas, las melodías que cantaban no se mezclaban.
Las melodías permanecieron puras, y "unninye" significa "las melodías fueron cantadas gloriosamente". Las gopis cantaron
junto con el Señor Krishna, Krishna cuyas melodías incluso Brahma, Shiva, Indra y todos los semidioses tienen
ningún poder para entender. El canto de Krishna y las gopis era igual. El canto de uno no
dominan el canto del otro. Las palabras "pujita tena" significan "con sus voces agudas el
Las gopis adoraban al Señor Krishna". Aquí la palabra "dhruvam" significa "una gopi cantaba una melodía en el dhruva".
ritmo, y "tasyai manam adat" significa "El Señor Krishna la alabó". Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila
Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
A prätipakñiké (rival) spoke these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.30):

tasyä amüni naù kñobham-
   kurvanty uccaiù padäni yat
yaikäpahåtya gopénäà
   raho bhuìkte 'cyutädharam


   "These footprints of that special gopé greatly disturb us. Of all the gopés, She alone was taken
away to a secluded place, where She is enjoying the lips of Kåñëa."***
   The gopé who spoke this verse clearly displayed her envy of the gopé taken away by Lord Kåñëa.
In the pastime of capturing the pärijäta-tree, a pastime described in the Hari-vaàça and other
scriptures, Satyabhämä envied Çré Rukmiëé in the same way the gopé who spoke Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.30.30 envied the gopé taken away by Lord Kåñëa. The meaning of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam

tasya amuni nah ksobham-
kurvanty uccaih padani yat yaikapahrtya gopinam
raho bhunkte 'cyutadharam
"Estas huellas de esa gopi tan especial nos perturban profundamente. De todas las gopis, solo ella era...
La llevaron a un lugar apartado, donde disfruta de los labios de Krishna.
La gopi que recitó este verso mostró claramente su envidia hacia la gopi que fue llevada por el Señor.
Krishna. En el pasatiempo de capturar el árbol parijata, un pasatiempo descrito en el Hari-vamsa y
En otras escrituras, Satyabhama envidiaba a Sri Rukmini de la misma manera que la gopi que hablaba srimad-

De Srila Jiva Gosvami

records.sourceEnglish:
Here someone may protest: "It is not possible that the devotees of the Lord can be rivals of each
other. That is a horrible idea. It is said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.29.48):


täsäà tat-saubhaga-madam. . .


   " `Lord Keçava, seeing the gopés too proud of their good fortune, wanted to relieve them of this
pride and show them further mercy. Thus He immediately disappeared.'***

   "In this way it is seen that the Supreme Personality of Godhead wishes to cast far away all envy,
lust, and pride. Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé here uses the word `daurätmya' (wickedness) to describe
those vices."

   To this protest I reply: If sometimes the Lord's devotees are rivals of each other that is only to
nourish their love for the Lord and to nourish the Lord's pastimes. The Lord reveals His pastimes so
the souls may attain love for Him. This is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.36):


bhajate tädåçéù kréòä
  yäù çrutva tat-paro bhavet


   "When the Lord assumes a humanlike body to show mercy to His devotees, He engages in such
pastimes as will attract those who hear about them to become dedicated to Him."***

   Indeed, in çåìgära-rasa (the mellow of conjugal love), the rasa is noursihed by a wonderful
display of spiritual envy, lust, and pride. This truth is confirmed by the great philosophers. The
Supreme Lord personally accepts it in His pastimes. As the hero loved by His beloveds, the Supreme
Lord manifests four features: 1. dakñiëa (pleasing), 2. anuküla (a faithful lover), 3. çaöha (a cheat),
and 4. dhåñöa (bold and dominating). The Lord's pastime potency (lélä-çakti) manifests these various
features in the presence of the Lord's beloveds. In this way these features are seen. However, when
they are separated from the Lord, the Lord's beloveds feel great distress. In that state of calamity
they all feel friendship for each other. This is seen in the following words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.30.40):

anvicchantyo bhagavato
  märgaà gopyo 'vidüritaù
dadåçuù priya-viçleñan
  mohitäà duùkhitäà sakhém


   "WhiIe continuing to search out Kåñëa's path, the gopés discovered their unhappy friend close
by. She was bewildered by separation from Her lover."***

    In this verse the gopés' feelingsof friendship for each other is manifested. Lord Kåñëa manifests
this pastime of being separated from Him in order that the gopés' thirst to attain Him may very
quickly increase. In this way the gopés' love for Lord Kåñëa, the crest jewel of amorous heroes,
increases. That this is the true reason Lord Kåñëa arranges that His devotees be separated from Him
is confirmed by Lord Kåñëa Himself in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.32.20):


nähaà tu sakhyo bhajato 'pi jantün. . .


   "But the reason I do not immediately reciprocate the affection of living beings even when they
worship Me, O gopés, is that I want to intensify their loving devotion. They then become like a poor
man who has gained some wealth and then lost it, and who thus becomes so anxious about it that he
can think of nothing else."***

   These pastimes are the Supreme Lord's attempt to make the gopés free offalse pride. This is seen
in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.48, which was quoted above. In that verse the word {.sy 168}prasamaya"
means "to make them free of false pride", and the word "prasadaya" means "to give them mercy,
mercy that took the form of making them thirst after attaining Him". In this way the gopés' good
ofrtune (tat-subhaga) is seen. The word "prasädäya" may also be interpreted to mean "to satisfy the
gopés' passioante desires, Lord Kåñëa enjoyed the räsa dance pastime", and the word {.sy
168}prasädäya" may also be interpreted to mean "to delight the gopés, Lord Kåñëa enjoyed the räsa-
dance pastime". The word "daurätmya" here means "separated fropm Lord Kåñëa, the gopés became
depressed at heart". {.sy 168}Daurätmya" here does not mean "wickedness" because this passage
describes pastimes of transcendental love. Çréla Çyukadeva Gisvämé, the king of sages, then gave
this description in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.41):


tayä kathitam äkarëya. . .


   "She told them how Mädhava had given Her much respect, but how She then suffered dishonor
because of Her misbehavior. The gopis were extremely amazed to hear this."***

   Actually there was nothing wrong with that gopés' pride. This is seen in the following words of

Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.34):


reme tayä svätma-rata
   ätmärämo 'py akhaëòitaù
käminäà darçayan dainyaà
   stréëäà caiva durätmatäm


   "Lord Kåñëa enjoyed with that gopé although He enjoys only within, being self-satisfied and
complete in Himself. Thus by contrast He showed the wretchedness of ordinary lusty men and
hardhearted women."***

   In this verse the word "svätma-rataù" means {.sy 168}self-satisfied", "ätmärämaù" means "who
enjoys pastimes", and "apy akhaëòitaù reme" means {.sy 168}attached to that particular gopé, He
enjoyed pastimes with Her". Someone may ask: "Why was Lord Kåñëa so attached to that one gopé?
Why did He enjoy pastimes with Her?" The answer is given here in this verse, Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.30.35. It is also said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (1.7.10):


ittham-bhüta-guëo hariù


   "The Supreme Personality of Godhead possesses transcendental qualities."

   As the Supreme Personality of Godhead possesses transcendental qualities, so does the gopé (Çré
Rädhä) mentioned in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.30.34. Her quality is that She is filled with love for
Lord Kåñëa. Here it is specifically said that Her love is pure spiritual love. It is not material lust.
Spiritual love is very powerful and glorious. Still, this gopé's spiritual love may superfically seem like
material lust, and in this way it may manifest what seems to be material pride and material passion.
Thus this gopé reveals a kind of love that seems to be like the wretchedness (dainyam) of lusty
women, a wretchedness that is well known in this material world. Thus this gopés manifests
stubbornness, willfulness, and a personality that tries to dominate Her beloved. With this beloved
Lord Kåñëa enjoys pastimes (reme). Or, these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam may be interpreted in a
different way. They may be interpreted to mean "With these pastimes the Lord shows how
wretched and insignificant are materialistic mn who try to enjoy amorous pastimes with lusty
women in the material world. Manifesting the glory of His pastimes, the Lord shows how wretched
and devoid of true nectar are the activities (dainyam) of lusty men (käminam) and how wretched is
the nature (durätmatäm) of materialistic women (stréëäm) who do not worship the Supreme Lord."
The great glory of the gopés' pastimes with Lord Kåñëa is also seen in these words of scripture:


darçayad vidhu-paräjayaà ramä-vaktram ullasati dhüta-läïchanam


   "As the goddess of fortune enjoys pastimes with the Supreme Lord, the spotless moon of her face,

a moon that defeats all other moons, shines with bliss."

   Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.30.34 discussed in these words was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Aquí alguien podría protestar: "No es posible que los devotos del Señor puedan ser rivales de
el uno al otro. Esa es una idea horrible. Se dice en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.29.48):
tasam tat-saubhaga-madam. . .
"El señor Kesava, al ver que las gopis estaban demasiado orgullosas de su buena fortuna, quiso liberarlas de
este orgullo y mostrarles más misericordia. Así, Él desapareció inmediatamente.
"De esta manera se ve que la Suprema Personalidad de Dios desea alejar a todos
envidia, lujuria y orgullo. Srila Sukadeva Gosvami aquí usa la palabra `dauratmya' (maldad) para
describe esos vicios."
A esta protesta respondo: Si a veces los devotos del Señor son rivales entre sí, eso es
solo para alimentar su amor por el Señor y para alimentar los pasatiempos del Señor. El Señor revela Su
pasatiempos para que las almas puedan alcanzar el amor por Él. Esto se ve en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam.
(10.33.36):
bhajate tadrsih krida
yah srutva tat-paro bhavet
"Cuando el Señor asume un cuerpo humano para mostrar misericordia a sus devotos, se dedica a tales cosas."
pasatiempos que atraerán a quienes oigan hablar de ellos a consagrarse a Él."
En efecto, en srngara-rasa (el dulzor del amor conyugal), el rasa se nutre de una maravillosa
Exhibición de envidia espiritual, lujuria y orgullo. Esta verdad es confirmada por los grandes filósofos.
El Señor Supremo personalmente lo acepta en Sus pasatiempos. Como el héroe amado por Sus amados, el
El Señor Supremo manifiesta cuatro características: 1. daksina (agradable), 2. anukula (un amante fiel), 3.
satha (un tramposo), y 4. dhrsta (audaz y dominante). La potencia de los pasatiempos del Señor (lila-sakti)
manifiesta estas diversas características en presencia de los amados del Señor. De esta manera,
Se ven características. Sin embargo, cuando se separan del Señor, los amados del Señor se sienten muy
angustia. En ese estado de calamidad, todos sienten amistad entre sí. Esto se observa en el
Las siguientes palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.30.40):
anvicchantyo bhagavato
margam gopyo 'viduritah dadrsuh priya-vislesan
mohitam duhkhitam sakhim
"Mientras seguían buscando el camino de Krishna, las gopis descubrieron a su infeliz amigo cerca
Ella estaba desconcertada por la separación de su amante.
En este verso se manifiestan los sentimientos de amistad entre las gopis. Señor Krishna
manifiesta este pasatiempo de estar separadas de Él para que las gopis tengan sed de alcanzarlo.
puede aumentar muy rápidamente. De esta manera el amor de las gopis por el Señor Krishna, la joya suprema del amor
héroes, aumenta. Que esta es la verdadera razón por la que el Señor Krishna dispone que Sus devotos sean
La separación de Él es confirmada por el mismo Señor Krishna en estas palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam.
(10.32.20):
naham tu sakhyo bhajato 'pi jantun. . .
"Pero la razón por la que no correspondo inmediatamente al afecto de los seres vivos, incluso cuando
Me adoran, oh gopis, porque quiero intensificar su amorosa devoción. Entonces se convierten en
como un hombre pobre que ha ganado algo de riqueza y luego la ha perdido, y que por eso se angustia tanto por
que no puede pensar en nada más."
Estos pasatiempos son el intento del Señor Supremo de liberar a las gopis del falso orgullo. Esto es
visto en srimad-Bhagavatam 10.29.48, que fue citado anteriormente. En ese verso la palabra prasamaya"
significa "liberarlos del falso orgullo", y la palabra "prasadaya" significa "darles misericordia,
misericordia que tomó la forma de hacerlas sedientas de alcanzarlo". De esta manera, el bien de las gopis
Se observa ofrtune (tat-subhaga). La palabra "prasadaya" también puede interpretarse como "para satisfacer".
los deseos apasionados de las gopis, el Señor Krishna disfrutaba del pasatiempo de la danza rasa", y la palabra
"prasadaya" también puede interpretarse como "para deleitar a las gopis, el Señor Krishna disfrutó del rasa-
pasatiempo de danza". La palabra "dauratmya" aquí significa "separadas del Señor Krishna, las gopis se convirtieron
deprimido de corazón". Dauratmya" aquí no significa "maldad" porque este pasaje describe
pasatiempos del amor trascendental. Srila Syukadeva Gisvami, el rey de los sabios, entonces dio esto
Descripción en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.30.41):
taya kathitam akarnya. . .
"Les contó cómo Madhava le había mostrado mucho respeto, pero cómo luego sufrió deshonra."
Debido a su mal comportamiento, las gopis quedaron sumamente asombradas al oír esto.
En realidad, no había nada malo en el orgullo de esa gopi. Esto se ve reflejado en las siguientes palabras.
del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.30.34):
reme taya svatma-rata
atmaramo 'py akhanditah kaminam darsayan dainyam
strinam caiva duratmatam
"El Señor Krishna disfrutó con esa gopi aunque Él disfruta solo en su interior, estando satisfecho consigo mismo y
completo en sí mismo. Así, por contraste, mostró la miseria de los hombres comunes y fuertes y
mujeres de corazón duro."
En este versículo la palabra "svatma-ratah" significa autosatisfecho", "atmaramah" significa "quien disfruta
pasatiempos", y "apy akhanditah reme" significa apegado a esa gopi en particular, Él disfrutaba de pasatiempos
con Ella". Alguien podría preguntar: "¿Por qué el Señor Krishna estaba tan apegado a esa gopi? ¿Por qué disfrutaba tanto de ella?".
¿pasatiempos con Ella? La respuesta se da aquí en este verso, srimad-Bhagavatam 10.30.35. Es
También se dice en el srimad-Bhagavatam (1.7.10):
ittham-bhuta-guno harih
"La Suprema Personalidad de Dios posee cualidades trascendentales."
Así como la Suprema Personalidad de Dios posee cualidades trascendentales, también las posee la gopi.
(Sri Radha) mencionada en el Srimad-Bhagavatam 10.30.34. Su cualidad es que está llena de amor.
para el Señor Krishna. Aquí se dice específicamente que Su amor es puro amor espiritual. No es
lujuria material. El amor espiritual es muy poderoso y glorioso. Aun así, el amor espiritual de esta gopi
puede parecer superficialmente lujuria material, y de esta manera puede manifestar lo que parece ser
orgullo material y pasión material. Así, esta gopi revela un tipo de amor que parece ser como
la miseria (dainyam) de las mujeres lujuriosas, una miseria que es bien conocida en este material.
mundo. Por lo tanto, esta gopis manifiesta terquedad, obstinación y una personalidad que intenta
dominar a Su amado. Con este amado Señor Krishna disfruta de pasatiempos (reme). O, estas palabras de
El srimad-Bhagavatam puede interpretarse de una manera diferente. Puede interpretarse como "Con
Estos pasatiempos el Señor muestra cuán miserables e insignificantes son los hombres materialistas que intentan
Disfrutar de pasatiempos amorosos con mujeres lujuriosas en el mundo material. Manifestando la gloria de Su
pasatiempos, el Señor muestra cuán miserables y carentes de verdadero néctar son las actividades (dainyam) de
hombres lujuriosos (kaminam) y cuán miserable es la naturaleza (duratmatam) de las mujeres materialistas (strinam)
quienes no adoran al Señor Supremo." La gran gloria de los pasatiempos de las gopis con el Señor Krishna es
También se ve en estas palabras de las Escrituras:
darsayad vidhu-parajayam rama-vaktram ullasati dhuta-lanchanam
"Mientras la diosa de la fortuna disfruta de pasatiempos con el Señor Supremo, la luna inmaculada de su
rostro, una luna que vence a todas las demás lunas, brilla con dicha."
El srimad-Bhagavatam 10.30.34 discutido en estas palabras fue pronunciado por srila sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
In this way the älambana of srngara-rasa has been described. Now the uddépanas will be
described. Included among the uddépanas are Lord Kåñëa's qualities, such as His ability to charm
women (näré-moahana-çélatva), The handsome charm of His bodily color, sweetness, fragrance,
touch, sound, auspicious qualities, and new youthfulness (avayava-varëa-rasa-gandha-sparça-çabda-
sal-lakñaëa-nava-yauvanänäà kamanéyatä), His being always new and fresh (nitya-nütanatva), His
making the gopés fall in love with Him (abhivyakta-bhävatva), His being controlled by His devotees'
love (prema-vaçyatva), and His genius (saubuddhya-pratibhätva). His ability to charm women is
described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.21.12):


kåñëaà nirékñya vanitotsava-rüpa-çélam. . .


    "Kåñëa's beauty and character create a festival for all women. Indeed, when the demigods' wives
flying in airplanes with their husbands catch sight of Him and hear His resonant flute-song, their
hearts are shaken by Cupid, and they become so bewildered that the flowers fall out of their hair
and their belts loosen."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by the goddesslike gopés of Vraja.


Anucchedas 290-294


    Lord Kåñëa's being eternally new and fresh is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(1.11.34):


yadyapy asau pärçva-gataù. . .


  "Although Lord Çré Kåñëa was constantly by their sides, as well as exclusively alone, His feet
appeared to them to be newer and newer. The goddess of fortune, although by nature always restless
and moving, could not quit the Lord's feet. So what woman can be detached from those feet, having
once taken shelter of them?"***

   Now Lord Kåñëa's quality of making the gopés fall in love with Him will be described. The pürva-
räga (first stages of that love) is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.31.2):

çarad-udäçaye sädhu jäta-sat-
   sarasijodara-çré-muñä dåçä
surata-nätha te 'çulka-däsikä
   vara-da nighnato neha kim vadhaù


   "O Lord of love, in beauty Your glance excels the whorl of the finest, most perfec fly formed
lotus within the autumn pond. O bestower of benedictions, You are killing the maidservants who
have given themselves to You freely, without any price. Isn't this murder?"***

   In this verse the words "dåçä surata-nätha" mean "O Lord who with Your glance beg to
enjoyamorous pastimes", "vara-prada" means "O Lord who at the end of our worship of Goddess
Kätyäyané granted the boon we prayed to attain", "dåçä açulka-däsikä" mean {.sy 168}without giving
any money to purchase us, simply by casting Your love-filled galnce on us, You turned us into Your
slavea", and "nighnato neha kim vadhaù" mean "did You not murder us women?" In this way this
verse shows that simply with His glance Lord Kåñëa enchanted the gopés. He enchanted them in
two ways: 1. He enchanted them with His form and qualities (svarüpa), and 2. He enchanted them
with His activities others have no power to perform (duñkara-kriyä). In this verse these two ways of
enchantement are both described. Lord Kåñëa's enchanting the gopés is also described in these
words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.31.8):


madhurayä girä valgu-väkyayä
   budha-manojïayä puñkarekñaëa
vidhi-karér imä véra muhyatér
   adhara-sédhunäpyäyayasva naù


   "O lotus-eyed one, Your sweet voice and charming words, which attract the minds of the
intelligent, are bewildering us more and more. Our dear hero, please revive Your maidservants with
the nectar of Your lips."***

   In this verse the word "madhurayä" means {.sy 168}with the sweetness of Your form", "valgu-
väkyayä" means "with the sweetness of Your words", and {.sy 168}budha-manojïayä" means "which
charm the hearts of the intelligent". In this way Lord Kåñëa's sweetness is manifest. Lord Kåñëa's
enchanting the gopés is also described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.31.10):


prahasitaà priya-prema-vékñaëaà
   viharaëaà ca te dhyäna-maìgalam
rahasi saàvido yä hådi spåçaù
   kuhaka no manaù kñobhayanti hi


  "Your smiles, Your sweet, loving glances, the intimate pastimes and confidential talks we enjoyed

with You--all these are auspicious to meditate upon, and they touch our hearts. But at the same
time, O deceiver, they very much agitate our minds."***

  In this verse the word "samvidaù" means {.sy 168}joking words".

   Lord Kåñëa's enchanting the gopés is also described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.31.12):


dina-parikñaye néla-kuntalair
   vanaruhänanaà bibhrad ävåtam
ghana-rajasvalaà darçayan muhur
   manasi naù smaram vira yacchasi


   "At the end of the day You repeatedly show us Your lotus face, covered with dark blue locks of
hair and thickly powdered with dust. Thus, O hero, You arouse lusty desires in our minds."***

   In this verse the word "muhuù" means "again and again". Lord Kåñëa's enchanting the gopés is
also described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.31.16-17):


pati-sutänvaya-bhrätå-bändhavän
   ativilaìghya te 'nty acyutagataù
gati-vidas tavodgéta-mohitäù
   kitava yoñitaù kas tyajen niçi


   "Dear Acyuta, You know very well why we have come here. Who but a cheater like You would
abandon young women who come to see Him in the middle of the night, enchanted by the loud
song of His flute? Just to see You, we have completely rejected our husbands, children, ancestors,
brothers and other relatives.***


rahasi saàvidaà håc-chayodayam
   prahasitänanaà prema-vékñaëam
brhad-uraù çriyo vékñya dhäma te
   muhur ati-spåhä muhyate manaù


   "Our minds are repeatedly bewildered as we think of the intimate conversations we had with
You in secret, feel the rise of lust in our hearts and remember Your smiling lace, Your loving
glances and Your broad chest, the resting place of the goddess of fortune. Thus we experience the
most severe hankering for You."***

  In these verses the words "gati-vidas tavodgéta-mohitäù" mean "You played on Your flute, a flute

that well knows how to bring us under its spell". These verses were spoken by the gopés to the
Supreme Personality of Godhead, who at that moment was not visible before them.
records.content:
De esta manera se ha descrito el alambana de srngara-rasa. Ahora se presentarán los uddipanas.
descrito. Entre los uddipanas se incluyen las cualidades del Señor Krishna, como su capacidad para encantar
mujeres (nari-moahana-silatva), El hermoso encanto de Su color corporal, dulzura, fragancia, tacto,
sonido, cualidades auspiciosas y nueva juventud (avayava-varna-rasa-gandha-sparsa-sabda-sal-
laksana-nava-yauvananam kamaniyata), Su ser siempre nuevo y fresco (nitya-nutanatva), Su hacer
Las gopis se enamoran de Él (abhivyakta-bhavatva), siendo Él controlado por el amor de sus devotos.
(prema-vasyatva), y Su genio (saubuddhya-pratibhatva). Su habilidad para encantar a las mujeres es
descrito en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.21.12):
krsnam niriksya vanitotsava-rupa-silam. . .
"La belleza y el carácter de Krishna crean un festival para todas las mujeres. De hecho, cuando los semidioses...
Las esposas que vuelan en avión con sus maridos lo divisan y oyen su flauta resonante.
canción, sus corazones son sacudidos por Cupido, y se quedan tan desconcertados que las flores caen de
"Se les afloja el pelo y los cinturones."
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por las gopis de Vraja, semejantes a diosas.

records.sourceEnglish:
Lord Kåñëa's enchanting the gopés in the stage of pürva-räga (beginning of love) is described in
these words of Skanda Puräëa, Revä-khaëòa, Tulasé-stava:


gaväà hitäya tulasi
   gopénäà rati-hetave
våndävane tvaà väpitä
   sevita viñëunä svayam


   "To bring auspiciousness to the cows, as well as to make the gopés fall in love with Him, Lord
Viñëu personally plants You in Våndävana and serves you, O Goddess Tulasé."
   Lord Kåñëa's enhcanting the gopés while directly enjoying pastimes them is described in these
words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.29.42):


iti viklavitaà täsäm. . .


   "Smiling upon hearing these despondent words from the gopis, Lord Kåñëa, the supreme master
of all masters of mystic yoga, mercifully enjoyed with them, although He is self-satisfied."***

   In this verse the word "prahasya" (smiling) describes how Lord Kåñëa enchanted the gopés.

  Lord Kåñëa enchanting the gopés as He enjoyed pastimes with them is again described in these
words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.29.43, 44, and 46):


täbhiù sametäbhir udära-ceñöitaù. . .
 . . .udära-häsa-dvija-kunda-dédhatiù


   "Among the assembled gopés, the infallible Lord Kåñëa appeared just like the moon surrounded
by stars. He whose activities are so magnanimous made their faces blossom with His affectionate
glances, and His broad smiles revealed the effulgence of His jasmine-bud-like teeth.***


upagéyamänaù. . .udgäyan

  "As the gopés sang His praises, that leader of hundreds of women sang loudly in reply. He moved
among them, wearing His Varjayanté garland, beautifying the Våndävana forest.***


bähu-prasära. . .


   "Kåñëa threw His arms around the gopés and embraced them. He aroused Cupid in the beautiful
young ladies of Vraja by touching their hands, hair, thighs, belts, and breasts, by playfully
scratching them with His fingernails, and also by joking with them, glancing at them, and laughing
with them. In this way the Lord enjoyed His pastimes."***

   In this way is described Lord Kåñëa's quality of making the gopés fall in love with Him.

    Now will be considered Lord Kåñëa's quality of controlled by His devotees' love (prema-
vaçyatva). This quality is of two kinds: 1. being controlled by the love of devotees other than His
beloveds (premäntareëa), and 2. being controlled by the love of His beloveds (preyasé-premëä). The
first of these (being controlled by the love of devotees other than His beloveds) is seen in these
words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.35.20):


narma-daù praëayiëäà vijahära


    "O sinless Yaçodä, your darling child, the son of Mahäräja Nanda, has festively enhanced His
attire with a jasmine garland, and He is now playing along the Yamunä in the company of the cows
and cowherd boys, amusing His dear companions. The gentle breeze honors Him with its soothing
fragrance of sandalwood, while the various Upadevas, standing on all sides like panegyrists, offer
their music, singing and gifts of tribute."***

   Now the second of these (being controlled by the love of His beloveds) will be considered. This
quality when manifested in the stage of pürva-räga is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.53.2):


tathäham api tac-citto
   nidräà ca na labhe niçi


   "Just as Rukmiëé's mind is fixed on Me, My mind is fixed on her. I can't even sleep at night."***

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by the Supreme Personality of
Godhead to Rukmiëé's messenger.


Anucchedas 296 and 297

   Lord Kåñëa's being controlled by the love of His beloveds in the stage of pürva-räga is also seen
in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.29.1):


bhagavän api tä rätréù
   çäradotphulla-mallikaù
vékñya rantuà manaç cakre
   yoga-mäyäm upäçritah


   "Çré Kåñëa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, full in all opulences, yet upon seeing those
autumn nights scented with blossoming jasmine flowers, He turned His mind toward loving affairs.
To fulfill His purposes He employed His internal potency."***

   In this verse the word "yoga-mäyäm upäçritaù" means "taking shelter of yoga-mäyä, which fulfills
the numberless desires of numberless gopés."

   Lord Kåñëa's being controlled by the love of His beloveds as He directly enjoys pastimes with
them is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.29.42):


iti viklavitaà täsäà
    çrutvä yogeçvareçvaraù
prahasya sa-dayaà gopér
    ätmärämo py aréramat


   "Smiling upon hearing these despondent words from the gopis, Lord Kåñëa, the supreme master
of all masters of mystic yoga, mercifully enjoyed with them, although He is self-satisfied."***

   In this verse the word "viklavitam" means {.sy 168}the gs' appeals of love", "sadayam" means {.sy
168}merciful because He was controlled by their love", {.sy 168}ätmärämo 'pi" means "even though
He was self-satisfied, He could see the great virtue of their love for Him". The word "ätmäräma" (self-
satisfied is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (1.7.10):

ätmärämäç ca munayaù. . .
 . . .ittham-bhüta-guëo hariù


   "All different varieties of ätmärämas [those who take pleasure in ätmä, or spirit self], especially
those established on the path of seff-realization, though freed from all kinds of material bondage,
desire to render unalloyed devotional service unto the Personality of Godhead. This means that the
Lord possesses transcendental qualities and therefore can attract everyone, including liberated
souls."*

  The two verses Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.1 and 10.29.42 were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva
Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 298 and 299


   Lord Kåñëa's being controlled by the love of His beloveds as He directly enjoys pastimes with
them is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.23):


reme svayaà sva-ratir atra gajendra-lélaù


   "My dear King, in the water Kåñëa found Himself being splashed on all sides by the laughing
gopés, who looked at Him with love. As the demigods worshiped Him by showering flowers from
their airplanes, the self-satisfied Lord took pleasure in playing like the king of the elephants."***

    In this verse the word "sva-ratiù" means {.sy 168}Lord Kåñëa who loved (rati) the gopés (sva)".
Lord Kåñëa's being controlled by the love of His beloveds as He directly enjoys pastimes with them
is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.20):


täsäà rati-vihäreëa


   "Seeing that the gopés were fatigued from conjugal enjoyment, my dear King, merciful Kåñëa
lovingly wiped their faces with His comforting hand."***

   This pastime is also seen in these words of Viñëu Puräëa (5.13.54):


gopé-kapola-saàçleña. . .


   "Lord Kåñëa wiped the gopés' cheeks."

   Lord Kåñëa's pastimes with the gopés are also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.33.16):


evaà pariñvaìga-karäbhimarça-
   snigdhekñaëoddama-vilasa-hasaiù
reme rameço vraja-sundarébhir
   yathärbhakaù sva-pratibimba-vibhramaù

   "In this way Lord Kåñëa, the original Lord Näräyaëa, master of the goddess of fortune, took
pleasure in the company of the young women of Vraja by embracing them, caressing them and
glancing lovingly at them as He smiled His broad, playful smiles. It was just as if a child were playing
with his own reflection."***

   Here the word "rameça" means "the controller of Goddess Lakñmé". This verse says: "by embracing
them, caressing them and glancing lovingly at them, Lord Kåñëa enjoyed pastimes with the gopés".
In this way Lord Kåñëa was controlled by the gopés' love. Here is given the example of a
childplaying with his reflection. As a child plays with his reflection, so Lord Kåñëa enjoyed pastimes
beginnign with singing and dancing with the gopés. In this activities it is seen that Lord Kåñëa and
the gopés were deeply attached to each other.
records.content:
Se describe cómo el Señor Krishna encanta a las gopis en la etapa de purva-raga (el comienzo del amor).
en estas palabras de Skanda Purana, Reva-khanda, Tulasi-stava:
gavam hitaya tulasi
gopinam rati-hetave vrndavane tvam vapita
sevita visnuna svayam
"Para traer buena fortuna a las vacas, así como para hacer que las gopis se enamoren de Él,
El Señor Vishnu te planta personalmente en Vrindavana y te sirve, oh Diosa Tulasi."
El Señor Krishna encantando a las gopis mientras disfruta directamente de sus pasatiempos se describe en estos
Palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.29.42):
iti viklavitam tasam. . .
"Sonriendo al oír estas palabras de desánimo de las gopis, el Señor Krishna, el maestro supremo,
De todos los maestros del yoga místico, disfrutó misericordiosamente con ellos, aunque Él es autosatisfecho."
En este verso, la palabra "prahasya" (sonriente) describe cómo el Señor Krishna encantó a las gopis.
El Señor Krishna encantando a las gopis mientras disfrutaba de pasatiempos con ellas se describe nuevamente en estos
Palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.29.43, 44 y 46):
tabhih Sametabhir udara-cestitah. . . . . .udara-hasa-dvija-kunda-didhatih
"Entre las gopis reunidas, el infalible Señor Krishna apareció como la luna que las rodeaba.
por las estrellas. Aquel cuyas actividades son tan magnánimas hizo florecer sus rostros con Su afectuosa
Sus miradas, y sus amplias sonrisas, revelaban el resplandor de sus dientes, semejantes a capullos de jazmín.
upagiyamanah. . .udgayan
"Mientras las gopis cantaban sus alabanzas, aquella líder de cientos de mujeres cantó en voz alta en respuesta.
Se movía entre ellos, luciendo su guirnalda de Varjayanti, embelleciendo el bosque de Vrindavana.
bahu-prasara. . .
"Krishna rodeó con sus brazos a las gopis y las abrazó. Despertó a Cupido en la hermosa
jóvenes de Vraja tocándoles las manos, el pelo, los muslos, los cinturones y los pechos, de forma juguetona
arañándolos con sus uñas, y también bromeando con ellos, mirándolos y riendo.
con ellos. De esta manera el Señor disfrutaba de sus pasatiempos.
De esta manera se describe la cualidad del Señor Krishna de hacer que las gopis se enamoren de Él.
Ahora se considerará la cualidad del Señor Krishna controlada por el amor de Sus devotos (prema-
vasyatva). Esta cualidad es de dos tipos: 1. estar controlado por el amor de devotos distintos a
Sus amados (premantarena), y 2. ser controlado por el amor de Sus amados (preyasi-premna).
El primero de estos (ser controlado por el amor de devotos que no son Sus amados) se ve en
Estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.35.20):
narma-dah pranayinam vijahara
"Oh, Yasoda, inocente, tu amado hijo, el hijo del Maharaja Nanda, ha realzado festivamente Su
ataviado con una guirnalda de jazmines, y ahora está jugando a orillas del Yamuna en compañía de las vacas.
y los muchachos pastores, entreteniendo a sus queridos compañeros. La suave brisa lo honra con su suave
fragancia de sándalo, mientras los diversos Upadevas, de pie a todos lados como panegiristas, ofrecen
su música, su canto y sus ofrendas de homenaje."
Ahora bien, se considerará el segundo de estos (ser controlado por el amor de sus amados).
Esta cualidad, cuando se manifiesta en la etapa de purva-raga, se observa en estas palabras de srimad-
Bhagavatam (10.53.2):
tathaham api tac-citto
nidram ca na labhe nisi
"Así como la mente de Rukmini está fija en Mí, mi mente está fija en ella. Ni siquiera puedo dormir a las
noche."
El significado de este versículo es claro. Este versículo fue pronunciado por la Suprema Personalidad de Dios.
La divinidad al mensajero de Rukmini.

records.sourceEnglish:
Then it is said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.25):


evaà çaçäìkäàçu-viräjitä niçäù
    sa satya-kämo 'nuratäbalä-gaëaù
siñeva ätmany avaruddha-saurataù
    sarväù çarat-kävya-kathä-rasäçrayäh


   "Although the gopés were firmly attached to Lord Kåñëa, whose desires are always fulfilled, the
Lord was not internally affected by any mundane sex desire. Still, to perform His pastimes the Lord
took advantage of all those moonlit autumn nights, which inspire poetic descriptions of
transcendental affairs."***

    In this verse the word "evam" means "as was previously described", "anuratäbalä-gaëaù" means
{.sy 168}the gopés who loved Kåñëa eternally", "saù" means "Çré Kåñëacandra", "ätmany avaruddha-
saurataù" means "whose thoughts were filled with flirting and various amorous pastimes", "satya-
kämaù" means {.sy 168}whose love is never wrong", "çarat-kävya-kathä-rasäçrayäù" means "nectar
poems in relation to autumn", "sarväù" means "them all", and "siñeve" means "He utilized". The wird
"çarat" here may also mean "for an entire year". The word {.sy 168}çaçäìkäàçu-viräjitä" (moonlit
nights) further describes this pastime. The Lord's amorous pastimes are also seen in the following
owrds of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.58):


evaà saurata-samläpaiù. . .


  "And so the self-satisfied Supreme Lord of the universe enjoyedwith the goddess of fortune,
engaging her in lovers' talks and thus imitating the ways of human society."***

   This verse describes Lord Kåñëa's pastimes of joking with Rukmiëé. The word "saurata" here has
the same meaning it had in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.33.25. Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.33.25 was spoken
by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Entonces se dice en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.33.25):
evam sasankamsu-virajita nisah
sa satya-kamo 'nuratabala-ganah siseva atmany avaruddha-sauratah
sarvah sarat-kavya-katha-rasasrayah
"Aunque las gopis estaban firmemente unidas al Señor Krishna, cuyos deseos siempre se cumplen,
El Señor no se vio afectado internamente por ningún deseo sexual mundano. Aun así, para realizar Sus pasatiempos
El Señor aprovechó todas esas noches de otoño iluminadas por la luna, que inspiran descripciones poéticas de
asuntos trascendentales."
En este versículo la palabra "evam" significa "como se describió anteriormente", "anuratabala-ganah" significa
las gopis que amaron a Krsna eternamente", "sah" significa "sri Krsnacandra", "atmany avaruddha-sauratah"
significa "cuyos pensamientos estaban llenos de coqueteo y diversos pasatiempos amorosos", "satya-kamah" significa
cuyo amor nunca se equivoca", "sarat-kavya-katha- rasasrayah" significa "poemas de néctar en relación con
otoño", "sarvah" significa "todos ellos", y "siseve" significa "Él utilizó". La palabra "sarat" aquí puede
también significa "durante todo un año". La palabra sasankamsu-virajita" (noches de luna) describe además
este pasatiempo. Los pasatiempos amorosos del Señor también se ven en las siguientes palabras de srimad-
Bhagavatam (10.60.58):
evam saurata-samlapaih. . .
"Y así, el autosatisfecho Señor Supremo del universo disfrutó con la diosa de la fortuna,
Entablando conversaciones amorosas con ella e imitando así las costumbres de la sociedad humana."
Este verso describe los pasatiempos del Señor Krishna bromeando con Rukmini. La palabra "saurata" aquí
tiene el mismo significado que tenía en srimad-Bhagavatam 10.33.25. srimad-Bhagavatam 10.33.25 fue pronunciado
Por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
In the matter of His relationship with the gopés Lord Kåñëa Himself declares in Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.32.22):


na päraye 'ham. . .


  "I am not able to repay My debt for your spotless service, even within a lifetime of Brahmä. Your
connection with Me is beyond reproach. You have worshiped Me, cutting off all domestic ties,
which are difficult to break. Therefore please let your own glorious deeds be your compensation."*

   Lord Kåñëa's separation from the gopés when He went to live in a faraway place is described in
these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.46.1-4):


våñëénäà pravaro mantré
    kåñëasya dayitaù sakhä
çiñyo båhaspateù säkñäd
    uddhavo buddhi-sattamaù


    "The supremely intelligent Uddhava was the best counselor of the Våñëi dynasty, a beloved
friend of Lord Çré Kåñëa, and a direct disciple of Båhaspati.***


tam äha bhagavän preñöhaà
   bhaktam ekäntinaà kvacit
gåhétvä päëinä päëià
   prapannärti-haro hariù


  "The Supreme Lord Hari, who relieves the distress of all who surrender to Him, once took the
hand of His fully devoted, dearmost friend Uddhava and addressed him as follows.***


gacchoddhava vrajaà saumya
   pitror nau prétim ävaha
gopénäà mad-viyogädhià

   mat-sandeçair vimocaya


   "Dear gentle Uddhava, go to Vraja and give pleasure to Our parents. And also relieve the gopés,
suffering in separation from Me, by giving them My message.***


tä man-manaskä mat-präëä
   mad-arthe tyakta-daihikäù


  "The minds of those gopés are always absorbed in Me, and their very lives are ever devoted to Me.
For My sake they have abandoned everything related to their bodies."***

  This pastime is also described in the Skanda Puräëa, Prahläda-saàhitä, Dvärakä-mähätmya,
where Çrémän Uddhava tells the gopés:


bhagavän api däçarhaù
   kandarpa-çara-péòitaù
na bhuìkte na çvapiti ca
   cintayan vo hy ahar-niçam


  "Wounded by Kämadeva's arrow, Lord Kåñëa thinks of you gopés day and night. He neither eats
nor sleeps."

   Most of the princesses married by Lord Kåñëa had previously been gopés in Vraja. As time passed
in separation from Kåñëa, they became those princesses to save themselves from committing suicide
in despair. This is described in the following words of Padma Puräëa:


kaiçora gopa-kanyäs tä
   yauvane räja-kanyakäù


   "The girls who in the beginning of their youth had been gopés at the later stage of their youth
became princesses."

   That the Lord's beloveds are inclined to commit suicide rather than live without Lord Kåñëa is
seen in these words spoken by Queen Rukmiëé in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.52.43):


yarhy ambujäkña na labheya bhavat-prasädaà
   jahyäm asün vrata-kåçän çata-janmabhiù syät

  "O lotus-eyed one, if I cannot obtain Your mercy, I shall simply give up my vital force, which will
have become weak from severe penances I will perform. Then, after hundreds of lifetimes of
endeavor, I may obtain Your mercy."***
records.content:
En lo que respecta a Su relación con las gopis, el Señor Krishna mismo declara en el srimad:
Bhagavatam (10.32.22):
na paraye 'ham. . .
"No soy capaz de saldar mi deuda por vuestro servicio intachable, ni siquiera en el transcurso de la vida de Brahma."
Tu unión conmigo es intachable. Me has adorado, cortando todos los lazos familiares,
que son difíciles de romper. Por lo tanto, que vuestras propias y gloriosas hazañas sean vuestra recompensa."
Se describe la separación del Señor Krishna de las gopis cuando se fue a vivir a un lugar lejano.
En estas palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.46.1-4):
vrsninam pravaro mantri
krsnasya dayitah sakha sisyo brhaspateh saksad
uddhavo buddhi-sattamah
"El sumamente inteligente Uddhava fue el mejor consejero de la dinastía Vrsni, un hombre muy querido
Amigo del Señor Sri Krishna y discípulo directo de Brhaspati.
Tam Aha Bhagavan Prestham
bhaktam ekantinam kvacit grhitva panina panim
prapannarti-haro harih
"El Señor Supremo Hari, que alivia la angustia de todos los que se rinden a Él, una vez tomó el
de la mano de su devoto y más querido amigo Uddhava y se dirigió a él de la siguiente manera.
gacchoddhava vrajam saumya
pitror nau pritim avaha gopinam mad-viyogadhim
estera-sandesair vimocaya
"Querido y gentil Uddhava, ve a Vraja y dale alegría a Nuestros padres. Y también alivia el
gopis, sufriendo en separación de Mí, al darles Mi mensaje.
ta man-manaska mat-prana
mad-arthe tyakta-daihikah
"Las mentes de esas gopis están siempre absortas en Mí, y sus vidas mismas están siempre consagradas a Mí.
Por mí. Por mi causa han abandonado todo lo relacionado con sus cuerpos.
Este pasatiempo también se describe en el Skanda Purana, Prahlada-samhita, Dvaraka-mahatmya,
donde sriman Uddhava les dice a las gopis:
Bhagavan Api Dasarhah
kandarpa-sara-piditah na bhunkte na svapiti ca
cintayan vo hy ahar-nisam
"Herido por la flecha de Kamadeva, el Señor Krishna piensa en vosotras, gopis, día y noche. Ni come ni muere
ni duerme."
La mayoría de las princesas con las que se casó el Señor Krishna habían sido previamente gopis en Vraja. Con el tiempo
pasaron separadas de Krsna, se convirtieron en esas princesas para salvarse de cometer
Suicidio por desesperación. Esto se describe en las siguientes palabras del Padma Purana:
kaisora gopa-kanyas ta
Yauvane Raja-Kanyakah
"Las muchachas que al principio de su juventud habían sido gopis en la etapa posterior de su
Las jóvenes se convirtieron en princesas."
Que los amados del Señor se inclinan a cometer suicidio antes que vivir sin el Señor Krishna
Esto se ve reflejado en estas palabras pronunciadas por la reina Rukmini en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.52.43):
yarhy ambujaksa na labheya bhavat-prasadam
jahyam asun vrata-krsan sata-janmabhih syat
"Oh, tú de ojos de loto, si no puedo obtener Tu misericordia, simplemente renunciaré a mi fuerza vital,
que se habrán debilitado por las severas penitencias que realizaré. Luego, después de cientos de
Tras toda una vida de esfuerzo, espero obtener Tu misericordia."

records.sourceEnglish:
Amongst the uddépanas is Lord Kåñëa's caste status. Lord Kåñëa's caste as a gopa is described in
these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.35.14):


vividha-gopa-caraëeñu vidagdho
   veëu-vädya urudhä. . .


   "O pious mother Yaçodä, your son, who is expert in all the arts of herding cows, has invented
many new styles of flute-playing. When He takes His flute to His bimba-red lips and sends forth the
tones of the harmonic scale in variegated melodies, Brahmä, Siva, Indra and other chief demigods
become confused upon hearing the sound. Although they are the most learned authorities, they
cannot ascertain the essence of that music, and thus they bow down their heads and hearts."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by the goddesslike gopés of Vraja.
records.content:
Entre los uddipanas se encuentra el estatus de casta del Señor Krishna. La casta del Señor Krishna como gopa se describe
En estas palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.35.14):
vividha-gopa-caranesu vidagdho
venu-vadya urudha. . .
"Oh piadosa madre Yasoda, tu hijo, que es experto en todas las artes del pastoreo de vacas, ha inventado
muchos estilos nuevos de tocar la flauta. Cuando Él lleva su flauta a sus labios rojos como el bimba y envía
los tonos de la escala armónica en melodías variadas, Brahma, Siva, Indra y otros principales
Los semidioses se confunden al oír el sonido. Aunque son las autoridades más sabias,
No pueden comprender la esencia de esa música, y por eso inclinan la cabeza y el corazón.
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por las gopis de Vraja, semejantes a diosas.

records.sourceEnglish:
Lord Kåñëa's caste as one of the Yädavas, a kñatriya, is seen in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.90.20):


megha çrémäàs tvam asi dayito yädavendrasya nünam. . .


   "O revered cloud, you are indeed dear to the chief of the Yadus, who bears the mark of Çrévatsa.
Like us, you are bound to Him by love and are meditating upon Him. Your heart is distraught with
great eagerness, as our hearts are, and as you remember Him again and again you shed a torrent of
tears. Association with Kåñëa brings such misery!"***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by the Lord's queens.
records.content:
La casta del Señor Krishna como uno de los Yadavas, un kshatriya, se ve en estas palabras del srimad-
Bhagavatam (10.90.20):
megha srimams tvam asi dayito yadavendrasya nunam. . .
"Oh venerada nube, eres verdaderamente querida por el jefe de los Yadus, que lleva la marca de
srivatsa. Al igual que nosotros, estás unido a Él por amor y meditas en Él. Tu corazón está
angustiados con gran anhelo, como lo están nuestros corazones, y como lo recuerdas una y otra vez,
Derramé un torrente de lágrimas. ¡La asociación con Krishna trae tanta miseria!
El significado de este versículo es claro. Este versículo fue pronunciado por las reinas del Señor.

records.sourceEnglish:
Now Lord Kåñëa's activities (kriyä) will be considered. The Lord's activities are of two kinds: 1.
bhäva-sambandhiné (activities of love), and 2. sväbhävika-vinodamaya (pastimes that come from

His own nature). The first of these two kinds of activities (activities of love) is described in these
words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.29.4):


niçamya gétaà tad anaìga-vardhanam. . .
