lo han hecho y muestran Su misericordia tomando la mano de Vaidarbhi.
evam prema-kala-baddha
vadanti sma puraukasah
"Unidos por un amor creciente, los habitantes de la ciudad hablaron de esta manera."
En estos versículos se ve que hay muchos tipos diferentes de personas, personas con diferentes
pensamientos y deseos, personas que ni siquiera tienen el más mínimo contacto con la calificación para disfrutar
Pasatiempos en srngara-rasa con el Señor Krsna como su amado, todavía sienten deleite (anumodana) en su
corazones cuando el Señor Krishna disfruta del pasatiempo de casarse con la princesa Rukmini. Aquí la palabra prema-kala-
"baddhah" significa "sus corazones unidos por un poco de amor, estaban encantados". Aunque era
solo una pequeña partícula de amor, y aunque la gente no era refinada ni sofisticada, ellos
aún se sentía feliz en el corazón. Al mismo tiempo, nació el tipo de amor más glorioso.
dentro de ellos. La luna llena regia del amor extático surgió dentro de ellos. De esta manera, el tipo más grande
Una alegría inmensa apareció en sus corazones. Estos versos fueron pronunciados por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
An example of the devotees who directly enjoy amorous pastimes with Lord Kåñëa is seen in
these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.11-12):


apy eëa-patny upagataù priyayeha gätrais
   tanvan dåçäà sakhi su-nirvåtim acyuto vaù
käntäìga-saìga-kuca-kuìkuma-raïjitäyäù
   kunda-srajaù kula-pater iha väti gandhaù


   "O friend, wife of the deer, has Lord Acyuta been here with His beloved, bringing great joy to
your eyes? Indeed, blowing this way is the fragrance of His garland of kunòa flowers, which was
smeared with the kuìkuma from the breasts of His girlfriend when He embraced Her.***


bähuà priyäàsa upadhäya gåhéta-padmo
  rämänujas tulasikali-kulair madandhaiù
anvéyamäna iha vas taravaù praëämaà
  kià väbhinandati caran praëayävalokaiù


     "O trees, we see that you are bowing down. When the younger brother of Räma walked by here,
followed by intoxicated bees swarming around the tulasé maïjarés decorating His garland, did He
acknowledge your obeisances with His affectionate glances? He must have been resting His arm on
the shoulder of His beloved and carrying a lotus flower in His free hand."***

   Here the word "ena-patni" means "O beautiful-eyed wife of the deer". Here the gopés imagine
that the doe is like a human being, like the gopés themselves, and thus is the wife of a deer. The

word "sakhi" means {.sy 168}you have attained my friendship because of your good fortune, which I
will soon describe". "Priyayä acyutaù" means {.sy 168}Çré Kåñëa accompanied by His beloved".
"Gätraiù" means "Their limbs entwined in an embrace". {.sy 168}Vaù" means "ofe persons like
tyourselves", {.sy 168}dåçäm" means "of the eyes", "sunirvåtim" means "the spiritual bliss born from
seeing Lord Kåñëa", "tanvan" means "granting the best of all", and "upagataù" means "did He come
near you?" Here the wives of the deer may ask: "How can you know if Lord Kåñëa was here?" Fearing
the does might speak those words, the gopés speak the second half (beginning with the word känta)
of this verse, where, speaking words that indirectly praise the divine couple's amorous pastimes,
they describe the symptoms of Lord Kåñëa's presence. ere the word "kula-pateù" means "the tilaka
mark decorating the family of Vraja's king", "kunda-srajaù gandhaù" means "the fragrance of the
jasmine garland", and "iha väti" means "is blown here by the breeze". What is the garland like? It is
described here in the words "käntäìga-saìga-kuca-kuìkuma-raïjitäyäù", which mean "reddened
with kuìkuma from the limbs of His passionate and all-virtuous beloved". The gopés say: "We think
that you, who perceive everything here, might have smelled this fragrance as you walked near
Them."
    Fearing this doe is concealing the joy she feels on seeing the divine couple and the grief she feels
by separation from Them, and thinking the doe must certainly have seen the divine couple, the
gopés joyfully describe a specific pastime the divine couple might have enjoyed at that time. Then,
seeing the bent-down trees, and thinking them servants now bowing down before them, the gopés
ask the trees if they had the good fortune of seeing the divine couple. In this way the gopés spoke
Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.30.12. In that verse the word "anviyamanah" means "being followed", "caran
praëayävalokaiù" means {.sy 168}enjoying pastimes of mutual loving glances", "vaù praëämaà kià
väbhinandati" means "did He respectfully ackowledge your obeisances?" Here the gopés mean to say:
{.sy 168}Rapt in enjoying pastim,es with His beloved, did Lord Kåñëa greet you? We do not think He
did." These verses were spoken by Çré Rädhä's girlfriends.
records.content:
Un ejemplo de los devotos que disfrutan directamente de pasatiempos amorosos con el Señor Krishna se ve en
Estas palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.30.11-12):
apy ena-patny upagatah priyayeha gatrais
tanvan drsam sakhi su-nirvrtim acyuto vah kantanga-sanga-kuca-kunkuma-ranjitayah
kunda-srajah kula-pater iha vati gandhah
"Oh amiga, esposa del ciervo, ¿ha estado el Señor Acyuta aquí con su amada, trayendo gran alegría?
¿A tus ojos? En efecto, soplando hacia aquí está la fragancia de Su guirnalda de flores de kunda, que
Quedó manchado con el kunkuma de los pechos de su novia cuando la abrazó.
bahum priyamsa upadhaya grhita-padmo
ramanujas tulasikali-kulair madandhaih anviyamana iha vas taravah pranamam
kim vabhinandati caran pranayavalokaih
"Oh árboles, vemos que os inclináis. Cuando el hermano menor de Rama pasó por aquí,
seguido de abejas ebrias pululando alrededor de los tulasi manjaris que decoraban Su guirnalda, ¿acaso Él
¿Reconoció tus reverencias con sus miradas afectuosas? Debió haber estado apoyando su brazo en
sobre el hombro de su amada y portando una flor de loto en su mano libre."
Aquí la palabra "ena-patni" significa "Oh, hermosa esposa del ciervo". Aquí las gopis imaginan
que la cierva es como un ser humano, como las propias gopis, y por lo tanto es la esposa de un ciervo.
La palabra "sakhi" significa que has alcanzado mi amistad debido a tu buena fortuna, la cual yo
pronto describirá". "Priyaya acyutah" significa sri Krsna acompañado de Su amado". "Gatraih" significa
"Sus miembros entrelazados en un abrazo". Vah" significa "de personas como ustedes", drsam" significa "de
los ojos", "sunirvrtim" significa "la dicha espiritual nacida de ver al Señor Krishna", "tanvan" significa
"otorgando lo mejor de todo", y "upagatah" significa "¿se acercó a ti?" Aquí las esposas de los
Los ciervos pueden preguntar: "¿Cómo puedes saber si el Señor Krishna estuvo aquí?" Temiendo que las ciervas pudieran decir esas palabras,
Las gopis recitan la segunda mitad (que comienza con la palabra kanta) de este verso, donde, hablando
palabras que indirectamente alaban los pasatiempos amorosos de la pareja divina, describen los síntomas de
La presencia del Señor Krishna. Aquí la palabra "kula-pateh" significa "la marca tilaka que decora a la familia de
El rey de Vraja", "kunda-srajah gandhah" significa "la fragancia de la guirnalda de jazmín", e "iha
"vati" significa "es traído aquí por la brisa". ¿Cómo es la guirnalda? Se describe aquí en el
palabras "kantanga-sanga-kuca-kunkuma-ranjitayah", que significan "enrojecido con kunkuma de las extremidades
de su amado apasionado y virtuoso". Las gopis dicen: "Pensamos que tú, que percibes
Todo lo que hay aquí, es posible que hayas percibido este aroma al pasar cerca de ellos."
Temiendo que esta cierva esté ocultando la alegría que siente al ver a la pareja divina y el dolor que siente.
siente por separación de Ellos, y pensando que la cierva ciertamente debe haber visto a la pareja divina,
Las gopis describen con alegría un pasatiempo específico que la pareja divina pudo haber disfrutado en aquel momento.
Entonces, al ver los árboles doblados y pensando que eran sirvientes que ahora se inclinaban ante ellos, el
Las gopis preguntan a los árboles si tuvieron la fortuna de ver a la pareja divina. De esta manera,
Las gopis hablaron el srimad-Bhagavatam 10.30.12. En ese verso, la palabra "anviyamanah" significa "ser".
seguido", "caran pranayavalokaih" significa disfrutar de pasatiempos de miradas amorosas mutuas", "vah
"pranamam kim vabhinandati" significa "¿Él reconoció respetuosamente tus reverencias?" Aquí las gopis
Queremos decir: ¿Te saludó el Señor Krishna absorto en disfrutar de pasatiempos con sus amados? No lo sabemos.
"Creo que sí." Estos versos fueron recitados por las novias de Sri Radha.

records.sourceEnglish:
Beginning with älambana and ending with sthäyi-bhäva, srngara-rasa has thus been described.
Srngara-rasa has two divisions: 1. vipralambha (separation), and 2. sambhoga (enjoyment).
Vipralambha means "attainment (lambha) of distance (vipra)". Vipralambha is described in these
words of
Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-prakaraëa, Texts 1-2:


yünor ayuktayor bhävo
  yuktayor vätha yo mithaù

abhéñöäliìganädénäm
   anävaptau prakåñyate
sa vipralambho vijïeyaù
   sambhogonnati-kärakaù

   "Vipralambha (love-in-separation) is of two kinds: 1. yünor ayuktayor bhäva (love-in-separation
of the youthful couple who have not yet directly met each other), and 2. yünor yuktayor bhava
(love-in-separation of the youthful couple who have already met each other).
   "The yearning to embrace and enjoy amorous pastimes on the part of the couple who have not
yet met becomes the source of their intense pleasure."

   The exalted nature of vipralambha is described in these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-
prakaraëa, Text 3:


na vinä vipralambhena
   sambhogaù puñöim açnute
käñäyite hi vasträdau
   bhüyän rägo vivardhate


   "Just as one cannot redden cloth or some other object without the use of red dye, in the same
way the happiness of conjugal love cannot reach its fullness without there having been separation
of the lovers."

   This truth is confirmed by Lord Kåñëa Himself in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.32.20):


nähaà tu sakhyo bhajato 'pi jantün. . .


   "But the reason I do not immediately reciprocate the affection of living beings even when they
worship Me, O gopés, is that I want to intensify their loving devotion. They then become like a poor
man who has gained some wealth and then lost it, and who thus becomes so anxious about it that he
can think of nothing else."***

   Lord Kåñëa also confirms this truth in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.34-35):


yat tv ahaà bhavaténäà vai
   düre värte priyo dåçam
manasaù sannikarñärthaà
   mad-anudhyäna-kämyayä


   "But the actual reason why I, the beloved object of your sight, have stayed far away from you is
that I wanted to intensify your meditation upon Me and thus draw your minds closer to Me.***


yathä düra-care preñöhe

    mana äviçya vartate
stréëäà ca na tathä cetaù
    sannikåñöe 'kñi-gocare


   "When her lover is far away, a woman thinkñ of him more than when he is present before
her."***

    Vipralambha has four divisions: 1. pürva-räga (before the lovers have met), 2. mäna (jealous
anger), 3. prema-vaicittya (sorrow), and 4. praväsa (the beloved lives in a faraway place). Sambhoga
is defined as the love when the two lovers enjoy (sambhoga) together. Sambhoga is described in
these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Sambhoga-prakaraëa, Text 1:


daåsanäliìganädénäm
   änukülyän niñevayä
yünor ulläsam ärohan
   bhävaù sambhoga éryate


   "That state which, by glances, embraces, and other activities brings pleasure to the youthful
divine couple is called sambhoga."

   As was described before, vipralambha is divided into four parts, which begin with pürva-räga.
pürva-räga is described in these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-prakaraëa, Text 5:


ratir yä saìgamät pürvaà
   darçana-çravaëädi-jä
tayor unmélati präjïaiù
   pürva-rägaù sa ucyate


  "That love born from seeing, hearing, or other kinds of contact before the couple have actually
met is called pürva-räga by the wise."

   Pürva-räga is seen in the following description of Queen Rukmiëé in Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.52.23):


sopaçrutya mukundasya
   rüpa-vérya-guëa-çriyaù
gåhägatair géyamänäs
   taà mene sadåçaà patim

   "Hearing of the beauty, prowess, transcendental character, and opulencer of Mukunda from
visitors to the palace who sang His praises, Rukmiëé decided that He would be the perfect husband
for her."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Así se ha descrito el srngara-rasa, que comienza con alambana y termina con sthayi-bhava.
Srngara-rasa tiene dos divisiones: 1. vipralambha (separación) y 2. sambhoga (disfrute).
Vipralambha significa "logro (lambha) de distancia (vipra)". Vipralambha se describe en estos
palabras de Ujjvala-nilamani, srngara-prakarana, Textos 1-2:
yunor ayuktayor bhavo
yuktayor vatha yo mithah
abhistalinganadinam
anavaptau prakrsyate sa vipralambho vijneyah
sambhogonnati-karakah
"Vipralambha (amor en separación) es de dos tipos: 1. yunor ayuktayor bhava (amor en separación)
separación de la pareja joven que aún no se ha conocido directamente), y 2. yunor
yuktayor bhava (amor en separación de la pareja joven que ya se ha conocido).
"El anhelo de abrazar y disfrutar de pasatiempos amorosos por parte de la pareja que aún no se ha conocido
se convierte en la fuente de su intenso placer."
La naturaleza exaltada de vipralambha se describe en estas palabras de Ujjvala-nilamani, srngara-
prakarana, Texto 3:
na vina vipralambhena
sambhogah pustim asnute kasayite hola vastradau
Bhuyan Rago Vivardhate
"Así como no se puede enrojecer una tela u otro objeto sin usar tinte rojo, del mismo modo
de manera que la felicidad del amor conyugal no puede alcanzar su plenitud sin que haya habido separación
de los amantes."
Esta verdad es confirmada por el Señor Krishna mismo en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.32.20):
naham tu sakhyo bhajato 'pi jantun. . .
"Pero la razón por la que no correspondo inmediatamente al afecto de los seres vivos, incluso cuando
Me adoran, oh gopis, porque quiero intensificar su amorosa devoción. Entonces se convierten en
como un hombre pobre que ha ganado algo de riqueza y luego la ha perdido, y que por eso se angustia tanto por
que no puede pensar en nada más."
El Señor Krishna también confirma esta verdad en estas palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.47.34-35):
yat tv aham bhavatinam vai
dure varte priyo drsam manasah sannikarsartham
mad-anudhyana-kamyaya
"Pero la verdadera razón por la que yo, el objeto amado de tu mirada, me he mantenido lejos de ti
Es que quería intensificar vuestra meditación sobre Mí y así acercar vuestras mentes a Mí.
yatha dura-care presthe
mana avisya vartate strinam ca na tatha cetah
sannikrste 'ksi-gocare
"Cuando su amante está lejos, una mujer piensa más en él que cuando lo tiene presente."
Vipralambha tiene cuatro divisiones: 1. purva-raga (antes de que los amantes se hayan encontrado), 2. mana (celos
ira), 3. prema-vaicittya (tristeza) y 4. pravasa (el ser amado vive en un lugar lejano).
Sambhoga se define como el amor cuando los dos amantes disfrutan (sambhoga) juntos. Sambhoga es
descrito en estas palabras de Ujjvala-nilamani, Sambhoga-prakarana, Texto 1:
darsanalinganadinam
anukulyan nisevaya yunor ullasam arohan
bhavah sambhoga iryate
"Ese estado que, mediante miradas, abrazos y otras actividades, brinda placer a los jóvenes.
La pareja divina se llama sambhoga."
Como se describió anteriormente, vipralambha se divide en cuatro partes, que comienzan con purva-raga.
purva-raga se describe en estas palabras de Ujjvala-nilamani, srngara-prakarana, Texto 5:
ratir ya sangamat purvam
darsana-sravanadi-ja tayor unmilati prajnaih
purva-ragah sa ucyate
"Ese amor que nace de ver, oír u otro tipo de contacto antes de que la pareja se haya casado
"Lo que realmente se encuentra es llamado purva-raga por los sabios."
Purva-raga se observa en la siguiente descripción de la reina Rukmini en el srimad-Bhagavatam.
(10.52.23):
sopasrutya mukundasya
rupa-virya-guna-sriyah grhagatair giyamanas
tam mene sadrsam patim
"Escuchar sobre la belleza, la destreza, el carácter trascendental y la opulencia de Mukunda de
Tras escuchar a los visitantes del palacio cantar sus alabanzas, Rukmini decidió que Él sería el esposo perfecto.
para ella."
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
Now the pürva-räga of the vraja-gopés will be considered. Although in some special
circumstances sambhoga is manifest even in Lord Kåñëa's early childhood (bälya), in general the
pastimes where Lord Kåñëa is the gopés' paramour arwe manifested in Lord Kåñëa's kaiçora (11-15
years) age. This is seen in the following words of Bhaviñya Puräëa's description of Kärttika-vrata:


bälye 'pi bhagavän kåñëaù
   kaiçoraà rüpam äçritaù


   "Even in His early childhood Lord Kåñëa manifested the same enchanting handsome form He
later manifested as a teenager (kaiçora)."

   This means that the form manifest in Lord Kåñëa's kaiçora's age is also manifest, although
hidden, in His other ages as well. Therefore the manifestation of sambhoga in these other ages is
not inappropriate. By the Lord's great power His kaiçora form may be manifested even in His
childhood, even when He was only six-years old. In trhis way even at that young age pürva-räga was
manifest. Pürva-räga is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.20.45):


äçliñya sama-çétosnaà
   prasüna-vana-märutam
janäs täpaà jahur gopyo
   na kåñëa-håta-cetasaù


   "Except for the gopés, whose hearts had been stolen by Kåñëa, the people could forget their
suffering by embracing the wind coming from the flower-filled forest. This wind was neither hot
nor cold."***

   Here the words "gopyo na jahuù" mean "the gopés did not leave". They did not leave because
their hearts were stolen by Kåñëa (kåñëa-håta-cetasaù). In this way it is seen that they were
tormented by separation from Kåñëa. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 372 and 373

   The gopés' pürva-räga love for Lord Kåñëa is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.21.1-19):


itthaà çarat-svaccha-jalaà
   padmäkara-su-gandhinä
nyaviçad väyunä vätaà
   sa-go-gopälako vanam


   "Thus the Våndävana forest was filled with transparent autumnal waters and cooled by breezes
perfumed with the fragrance of lotus flowers growing in the clear lakes. The infallible Lord,
accompanied by His cows and cowherd boyfriends, entered that Våndävana forest.***


kusumita-vanaraji-suñmi-bhånga-
   dvija-kula-ghuñöa-saraù-sarin-mahédhram
madhupatir avagähya cärayan gäù
   saha-paçu-päla-balaç cuküja venum


   "The lakes, rivers and hills of Våndävana resounded with the sounds of maddened bees and
flocks of birds moving about the flowering trees. In the company of the cowherd boys and Balaräma,
Madhupati [Sré Kåñëa] entered that forest, and while herding the cows He began to vibrate His
flute.***


tad vraja-striya äçrutya
   venu-gétaà smarodayam
käçcit parokñaà kåñëasya
   sva-sakhibhyo nvavarëayan


   "When the young ladies in the cowherd village of Vraja heard the song of Kåñëa's flute, which
arouses the influence of Cupid, some of them privately began describing Kåñëa's qualities to their
intimate friends.***


tad varëayitum ärabdhäh
   smarantyaù kåñëa-ceñöitam
nasakan smara-vegena
   vikñipta-manaso nåpa

  "The cowherd girls began to speak about Kåñëa, but when they remembered His activities, O
King, the power of Cupid disturbed their minds, and thus they could not speak.***


barhäpéòaà naöa-vara-vapuù karëayoù karëikäraà
   bibhrad väsaù kanaka-kapiçaà vaijayantéà ca mäläm
randhrän veëor adhara-sudhayäpürayan gopa-våndair
   våndaraëyam sva-pada-ramaëam pravisad gita-kirtiù


   "Wearing a peacock-feather ornament upon His head, blue karëikära flowers on His ears, a
yellow garment as brilliant as gold, and the Vaijayanté garland, Lord Kåñëa exhibited His
transcendental form as the greatest of dancers as He entered the forest of Våndävana, beautifying it
with the marks of His footprints. He filled the holes of His flute with the nectar of His lips, and the
cowherd boys sang His glories.***


iti veëu-ravaà räjan
    sarva-bhüta-manoharam
çrutvä vraja-striyaù sarvä
    varëayantyo 'bhirebhire


   "O King, when the young ladies in Vraja heard the sound of Kåñëa's flute, which steals the minds
of all living beings, they all embraced one another and began describing it.***


çré-gopya ücuù

akñaëvatäà phalam idaà na paraà vidämaù
   sakhyaù paçün anuviveçayator vayasyaiù
vaktraà vrajeça-sutayor anuveëu juñöam
   yair vä nipétam anurakta-kaöäkña-mokñam


   "The cowherd girls said: O friends, those eyes that see the beautiful faces of the sons of Mahäräja
Nanda are certainly fortunate. As these two sons enter the forest, surrounded by Their friends,
driving the cows before Them, They hold Their flutes to Their mouths and glance lovingly upon
the residents of Våndävana. For those who have eyes, we think there is no greater object of
vision.***


cüta-praväla-barha-stabakotpaläbja-
   mälänupåkta-paridhäna-vicitra-veçau
madhye virejatur alaà paçu-päla-goñöhyäà
   raìge yathä naöa-varau kvaca gayamanau

   "Dressed in a charming variety of garments, upon which Their garlands rest, and decorating
Themselves with peacock feathers, lotuses, lilies, newly grown mango sprouts and clusters of flower
buds, Kåñëa and Balaräma shine forth magnificently among the assembly of cowherd boys. They
look just like the best of dancers appearing on a dramatic stage, and sometimes They sing.***


gopyaù kim äcarad ayaà kuçalaà sma veëur
   dämodarädhara-sudhäm api gopikänäm
bhuìkte svayaà yad avaçiñöa-rasaà hradinyo
   håñyat-tvaco 'çru mumucus taravo yathäryäh


   "My dear gopés, what auspicious activities must the flute have performed to enjoy the nectar of
Kåñëa's lips independently and leave only a taste for us gopés, for whom that nectar is actually
meant! The forefathers of the flute, the bamboo trees, shed tears of pleasure. His mother, the river
on whose bank the bamboo was born, feels jubilation, and therefore her blooming lotus flowers are
standing like hair on her body.***


vrndävanaà sakhi bhuvo vitanoti kértim. . .


    "O friend, Våndävana is spreading the glory of the earth, having obtained the treasure of the
lotus feet of Kåñëa, the son of Devaké. The peacocks dance madly when they hear Govinda's flute,
and when other creatures see them from the hilltops, they all become stunned.***


dhanyäù sma muòha-gatayo 'pi hariëya etäù. . .


   "Blessed are all these foolish deer because they have approached Mahäräja Nanda's son, who is
gorgeously dressed and is playing on His flute. Indeed, both the doe and the bucks worship the Lord
with looks of love and affection.***


kåñëaà nirékñya. . .


    "Kåñëa's beauty and character create a festival for all women. Indeed, when the demigods' wives
flying in airplanes with their husbands catch sight of Him and hear His resonant flute-song, their
hearts are shaken by Cupid, and they become so bewildered that the flowers fall out of their hair
and their belts loosen.***


gävaç ca kåñëa-mukha. . .

    "Using their upraised ears as vessels, the cows are drinking the nectar of the flute-song flowing
out of Kåñëa's mouth. The calves, their mouths full of milk from their mothers' moist nipples, stand
stdl as they take Govinda within themselves through their tearfilled eyes and embrace Him within
their hearts.***


präyo batämba vihagä munayaù. . .


   "O mother, in this forest all the birds have risen onto the beautiful branches of the trees to see
Kåñëa. With closed eyes they are simply listening in silence to the sweet vibrations of His flute, and
they are not attracted by any other sound. Surely these birds are on the same level as great
sages.***


nadyas tadä tad upadhärya. . .


   "When the rivers hear the flute-song of Kåñëa, their minds begin to desire Him, and thus the
flow of their currents is broken and their waters are agitated, moving around in whirlpools. Then
with the arms of their waves the rivers embrace Muräri's lotus feet and, holding on to them, present
offerings of lotus flowers.***


dåçövätape vraja-paçün. . .


   "In the company of Balaräma and the cowherd boys, Lord Kåñëa is continually vibrating His
flute as He herds all the animals of Vraja, even under the full heat of the summer sun. Seeing this,
the cloud in the sky has expanded himself out of love. He is rising"***


pürëäù pulindyaù. . .


   "The aborigine women of the Våndävana area become disturbed by lust when they see the grass
marked with reddish kuìkuma
powder. Endowed with the color of Kåñëa's lotus feet, this powder originally decorated the breasts
of His beloveds, and when the aborigine women smear it on their faces and breasts, they give up all
their anxiety.***


hantäyam adrir abalä. . .

   "Of all the devotees, this Govardhana Hill is the best! O my friends, this hill supplies Kåñëa and
Balaräma, along with Their calves, cows and cowherd friends, with all kinds of necessities-water for
drinking, very soft grass, caves, fruits, flowers and vegetables. In this way the hill offers respects to
the Lord. Being touched by the lotus feet of Kåñëa and Balaräma, Govardhana Hill appears very
jubilant.***


gä gopakaiù. . .


   "My dear friends, as Kåñëa and Balaräma pass through the forest with Their cowherd friends,
leading Their cows, They carry ropes to bind the cows' rear legs at the time of milking. When Lord
Kåñëa plays on His flute, the sweet music causes the moving living entities to become stunned and
the nonmoving trees to tremble with ecstasy. These things are certainly very wonderful."***

    In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.21.1-19 the word "ittham" (thus) means "as was described in the
previous chapter", and the words "kusumitam" (filled with flowers) and {.sy 168}vanam" (forest) also
mean "as was described in the previous chapter". The word "vanam" means "the forest in that place",
"çuñmi" means "wild", "tad-vraja. . .venu-gitam asrutya" means "hearing the music of Lord Kåñëa's
flute", "paeroksam anvavarnayan" means "in a secluded place they shyly described their love for
Lord Kåñëa. It was not appropriate to describe these feelings in the presence of their elders. The
gopés concealed all this from their elders' knowledge."We may note that here it is said they
described their love for Lord Kåñëa, but they did not say that He had yet become their lover. The
words "tad varnayitum nasakan" mean "they had no power to describe those confidential topics".
The reason they had no power to describe them is given in the words {.sy 168}smarantyaù"
(remembering) and "smara-vegena" (by the power of Cupid). Then in the next verse (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.21.5) the gopés describe the previously revealed activities of Lord Kåñëa. Here the
words "adhara-sudhaya" (with the nectar of His lips) refers to Lord Kåñëa's playing the flute. By
directly seeing Lord Kåñëa in this way the gopés became enchanted. Thus they had no power to
speak (nasakan). They wildly embraced each other (abhirebhire).
    Although they had no power to describe their love for Lord Kåñëa, the gopés still spoke (sri-
gopya ucuh). There weretwo reasons they could not remain silent. The first reason is, even they did
not understand that they were overcome by the great power of their ecstatic love for Lord Kåñëa.
The second reason is they did understand how they were overcome by their ecstatic love for Lord
Kåñëa. The first of these reasons is seen in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.21.7. This verse has a second
interpretation. Here the words It may also be interpreted to mean "The gopas drink the nectar of
the face of Lord Kåñëa, the younger (anu) of the two princes of Vraja (vrajesa-sutayoh), a face
where the flute is placed". The second reason is seen in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.21.8-9. Thus in the
first part (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.21.7) of the gopés' explanation they attaempted to keep their real
feelings hidden, and in the second part (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.21.8-9) of their statement they
found that they had no power to conceal their true felings. In the passage begionning with Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.21.13 the gopés desrcibed their feelings in a more circumspect, a hidden way.
Concluding this chapter of Çrémad-Bhägavatam, Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé says (Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.21.20):

evaà-vidhä bhagavato
   yä våndävana-cäriëaù
varnayantyo mitho gopyaù
   kréòäs tan-mayatäà yayuù


  "Thus narrating to one another the playful pastimes of the Supreme Personality of Godhead as
He wandered about in the Våndävana forest, the gopés became fully absorbed in thoughts of
Him."***

   Here the word "tan-mayatäm" means "they became rapt in thinking of Lord Kåñëa". This means
they became like a rake who always thinks of women. These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva
Gosvämé.
records.content:
Ahora se considerará el purva-raga de las vraja-gopis. Aunque en algunos casos especiales
Las circunstancias sambhoga se manifiestan incluso en la primera infancia del Señor Krishna (balya), en general
pasatiempos donde el Señor Krishna es el amante de las gopis arwe manifestado en el kaisora del Señor Krishna (11-15
años) edad. Esto se observa en las siguientes palabras de la descripción de Karttika en el Bhavisya Purana:
vrata:
balye 'pi bhagavan krsnah
Kaisoram Rupam Asritah
"Incluso en su temprana infancia, el Señor Krishna manifestó la misma forma encantadora y hermosa que más tarde mostró.
se manifestó como adolescente (kaisora)."
Esto significa que la forma manifestada en la era de Kaisora del Señor Krishna también se manifiesta, aunque
oculto, también en Sus otras edades. Por lo tanto, la manifestación de sambhoga en estas otras edades es
No es inapropiado. Por el gran poder del Señor, Su forma kaisora puede manifestarse incluso en Su
infancia, incluso cuando solo tenía seis años. De esta manera, incluso a esa corta edad purva- raga
se manifestó. Purva-raga se describe en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.20.45):
aslisya sama-sitosnam
prasuna-vana-marutam janas tapam jahur gopyo
na krsna-hrta-cetasah
"Excepto por las gopis, cuyos corazones habían sido robados por Krishna, la gente podía olvidar sus
sufriendo al abrazar el viento que venía del bosque lleno de flores. Este viento no era ni caliente
ni frío."
Aquí las palabras "gopyo na jahuh" significan "las gopis no se fueron". No se fueron porque
Sus corazones fueron robados por Krsna (krsna-hrta-cetasah). De esta manera se ve que fueron
atormentado por la separación de Krishna. Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
The pürva-räga of the unmarried gopé girls is also described in the Tenth Canto, 22nd chapter of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam, which begins with these words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.1):


hemante prathame mäsi
   nanda-vraja-kumärikäù
cerur haviñyaà bhuïjänäù
   kätyäyany-arcana-vratam


  "During the first month of the winter season, the young unmarried girls of Gokula observed the
vow of worshiping goddess Kätyäyané. For the entire month they ate only unspiced khichré."***

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
El purva-raga de las muchachas gopis solteras también se describe en el capítulo 22 del décimo canto.
del srimad-Bhagavatam, que comienza con estas palabras (srimad-Bhagavatam 10.22.1):
hemante prathame masi
nanda-vraja-kumarikah cerur havisyam bhunjanah
katyayany-arcana-vratam
"Durante el primer mes de la temporada de invierno, las jóvenes solteras de Gokula observaron
el voto de venerar a la diosa Katyayani. Durante todo el mes solo comieron khichri sin especias."
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
Sending a love-letter (käma-lekhä) is one of the activities of pürva-räga. An example of a love-
letter is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.52.37):


çrutvä guëän bhuvana-sundara çåëvatäà te. . .


  "Çré Rukmiëé said (in her letter read by the brahmana): O beauty of the worlds, having heard of

Your qualities, which enter the ears of those who hear and remove their bodily distress, and havong
alos heard of Your beauty, which fulfills all the visual desires of those who see, I have fixed my
shameless mind upon You, O Kåñëa."***

   After pürva-räga comes sambhoga. Sambhoga has four parts: 1. sandarçana (gazing), 2. saïjalpa
(conversation), 3. samsparça (touching), and 4. samprayoga (union). Sandarçana means "gazing". An
example of sambhoga characterized by gazing and touching is seen in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.52.54-55):


saivaà çanaiç calayaté cala-padma-koçau
   präptià tadä bhagavataù prasamékñamänä
utsärya väma-karajair alakän apäìgaiù
   präptan hriyaikñata nåpän dadåçe 'cyutaà ca

täà räja-kanyäà ratham ärurukñatéà
   jahära kåñëo dviñatäà samékñatäm


   "On the pretext of the procession, Rukmiëé displayed her beauty for Kåñëa alone. Slowly she
advanced the two moving lotus-whorls of her feet, awaiting the arrival of the Supreme Lord. With
the fingernails of her left had she pushed some strands of hair away from her facw and shyly looked
from the corners of her eyes

at the kings standing before her. At that moment she saw Kåñëa. Then, while His enemies looked
on, the Lord seized the princess, who was eager to mount His chariot."***

  These verses mean: "She shyly waited for the arrival of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
She looked at the kings standing before her. Then, with an agitated heart, she saw the infallible
Supreme Lord." These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 376-378


    An example in sambhoga of gazing and conversation in relation to the unmarried girls of Vraja
is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.52.55):


täsäà väsäàsy upädäya
   népam äruhya satvaraù
hasadbhiù prahasan bälaiù
   parihäsam uväca ha


  "Taking the girls' garments, He (Kåñëa) quickly climbed to the top of the kadamba tree. Then, as
He laughed loudly and His companions also laughed, He addressed the girts jokingly."***

   Here it may be said that although the gopés already had very exalted love for Lord Kåñëa, Lord
Kåñëa still manifested this joking pastime to openly display that love and to enjoy a certain kind of
loving pastime with them. Scholars learned in rasa-çästra yearn to relish this display of the gopés'
love. In this pastime Lord Kåñëa does not touch the gopés or enjoy other kinds of sambhoga pastimes
with them. This kind of pürva-rasa is called "lajjä-ccheda" (breaking the shyness). It is one of the
different kinds of sambhoga. These different kinds of sambhoga are described in these words of

Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-bheda-prakaraëa, Text 66:


nayana-prétiù prathamaà
   cintä-saìgas tato 'tha saìkalpaù
nidrä-cchedas tanutä
   viñaya-nivåttis trapä-näçaù
unmädo mürchä måtir
   ity etäù smara-daçä daçaiva syuù


   "Some other authorities list the stage of sambhoga in this way: 1. nayana-préti (falling in love by
seeing the beloved), 2. cintä (thinking of the beloved), 3. saìkalpa (deciding to pursue the beloved),
4. nidrä-ccheda (loss of sleep), 5. tanutä (becoming emaciated), viñaya-nivåtti (becoming oblivious
to everything except the beloved), 7. trapä-näça (destroying shyness), 8. unmäda (becoming wild), 9.
mürchä (fainting), and 10. måti (death)."

   This condition of breaking shyness is the most exalted state in anuräga. Even when they accept
death, the last of these ten states, the gopés do not abandon their shyness. To relish this kind of
anuräga (breaking the gopés' shyness), Lord Kåñëa arranged these joking pastimes. In these pastimes
Lord Kåñëa said to the gopés (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.11):


na mayodita-pürvaà vä
   anrtam tad ime viduù


   "I have never before spoken a lie, and these boys know it. Therefore, O slender-waisted girls,
please come forward, either one by one or all together, and pick out your clothes."***

   That the gopés' love for Lord Kåñëa is never broken and remained unchanged in every situation
(even when Lord Kåñëa laughed at them) is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (01.229):


hasadbhiù. . .


   "Lord Kåñëa laughed loudly and His companions also laughed,"

  Here the word "bäla" indicated Lord Kåñëa's friends. Only persons who are Lord Kåñëa's friends
may touch His body. Other's cannot. Lord Kåñëa friends are described in these words of Gautaméya
Tantra, Prathamävaraëa-püjä:


däma-sudäma-vasudäma-
  kiìkiëér gandha-puñpakaiù

antaùkaraëa-rüpäs te
   kåñëasya parikértitäù
ätmäbhedena te püjyä
   yathä kåñëas tathaiva te


   "With fragrant flowers Dämä, Sudämä, Vasudämä, and Kiìkiëé worshiped Lord Kåñëa. These
boys were all praised by Lord Kåñëa Himself. These boys all know Lord Kåñëa's heart. Their hearts
are not different from Lord Kåñëa's heart. As Lord Kåñëa is worthy of worship, so are they."

   Because these pastimes of Lord Kåñëa's relishing the gopés' anuräga love for Him are confidential,
Lord Kåñëa pretended these activities were all a joke. This joking pretense is not incompatible with
these pastimes. On the contrary, Lord Kåñëa joking enhances the bliss of the pastimes. The great
sage Sukadeva Gosvami describes Lord Kåñëa's purpose in performing these activities. The sage
explains (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.18):


bhagavän ähatä vékñya
   çuddha-bhäva-prasäditaù
skandhe nidhäya väsäàsi
   prétaù proväca sa-smitam


   "When the Supreme Lord saw how the gopés were struck with embarrassment, He was satisfied
by their pure loving affection. Putting their clothes on His shoulder, the Lord smiled and spoke to
them with affection."***

   In this verse the word "ähatäù" means {.sy 168}approached". Or, "ähaöaù" may also mean {.sy
168}Although they had renounced almost all shyness, because of their feminine nature a small
fragment of shyness remained. Because of this remaining shyness they gently bent their bodies."
The word "çuddha-bhäva-prasäditaù" means "pleased at heart by relishing the gopés' splendid love,
love that showed their longing to be with Him and their being enchanted by Him".
   The next verse explains (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.19):


yüyaà vivasträ yad apo dhåta-vratäù. . .


   "(Lord Kåñëa said:) You girls bathed naked while executing your vow, and that is certainly an
offense against the demigods. To counteract Your sin you should offer obeisances while placing
your joined palms above your heads. Then you should take back your lower garments."***

   In order to see the last remnants of the gopés' shyness come to their final end Lord Kåñëa spoke
these joking words. The next verse explains (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.20):

ity acyutena. . .


   "Thus the young girls of Våndävana, considering what Lord Acyuta had told them, accepted that
they had suffered a falldown from their vow by bathing naked in the river. But they still desired to
successfully complete their vow, and since Lord Kåñëa is Himself the ultimate result of all pious
activities, they offered their obeisances to Him to cleanse away all their sins."***

   In this way Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé, the king of sages, reveals first the gopés'being enchanted by
Lord Kåñëa and their longing to associatte with Him, and then their obedience to His command. In
the next verse Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé explains (Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.22.22):


dåòhaà pralabdhäs trapayä ca häpitäù
   prastobhitäù kréòana-vac ca käritah
vasträëi caiväpahåtäny athäpy amum-
   tä näbhyasüyan priya-saìga-nirvrtäh


   "Although the gopés had been thoroughly cheated, deprived of their modesty, ridiculed and made
to act just like toy dolls, ana although their clothing had been stolen, they did not feel at all
inimical toward Sré Kåñëa. Hather, they were simply joyful to have this opportunity to associate
with their beloved."***

   In the verse the word "dåòham" means {.sy 168}greatly", and "pralabdhäù" means "cheated". The
cheating of the gopés is described here in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.19. "Trapayä häpitäù" means
"deprived of their modesty". This is descibed in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.10. "Prastobhitäù' here
means "mocked". Lord Kåñëa mocked the gopés in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.10. Lord Kåñëa's
making the gopés act like toy dolls is desscribed in His making them stand with folded palms on the
pretext of performing atonement. Even though Lord Kåñëa cheated them and teased them in many
ways, the gopés did not find fault with Lord Kåñëa. On the contrary. It is said here that even though
He had stolen their garments, the gopés did not feel eneimical toward Lord Kåñëa. On the contrary.
They were plunged into bliss because they had an opportunity to associate with their beloved.
These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 379-382


   Because they were brähmaëés, the yajïa-patnés were not qualified to associate with with Lord
Kåñëa as the gopés did. Still, the yajïa-patnés did have an ecstatic sentiment that was something like
pürva-räga. Gazing at Lord Kåñëa and conversing with Him, they experienced something in some
ways like sambhoga. They experienced sambhogäbhäsa (the reflection of sambhoga). After the
winter season had ended and summer had come, Lord Kåñëa's pastimes with the yajna-patnés
became visible. The beginning of these pastimes is desacribed in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam

(10.22.29):

atha gopaiù parivåto
   bhagavän devaké-sutaù
vrndävanäd gato düraà
   cärayan gäù sahägrajah


   "Some time later Lord Kåñëa, the son of Devaké, surrounded by His cowherd friends and
accompanied by His elder brother, Balaräma, went a good distance away from Våndävana, herding
the cows."***

   This verse means: "After Lord Kåñëa had given His mercy to the unmarried girls of Vraja, a
summer day came". That the day was a summer day distinguishes this pastime from the previous
pastime (which occurred in the winter). On this day Lord Kåñëa was accompanied by Lord
Balaräma. That is indicated here by the word "sägrajaù" (with His elder brother). Here the phrase "a
good distance away from Våndävana" indicates that Kåñëa and the boys were in the hilly part of
Kämyavana. That they were in the hills is seen by the fact that they decorated their bodies with
mineral pigments from the hills. That place is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.22.36):


tarüëäà namra-çäkhänäà
   madhyato yamunäà gatah


   "Thus moving among the trees, whose branches were bent low by their abundance of twigs,
fruits, flowers and leaves, Lord Kåñëa came to the Yamunä River."***

   With Vraja to their south and the Yamunä to the west, they entered a clearing to enjoy
pastimes. To the south was Mathurä City, and to the north was the place where some yäjïika-
brähmaëas lived. The home of these brahmana's was near King Kaàsa's palace. That is seen in
these words describing the thoughts of these brähmaëas (Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.23.52):


kaàsäd bhétä na cäcalan


   "Thus reflecting on the sin they had committed by neglecting Lord Kåñëa, they (the yäjïika-
brähmaëas) became very eager to see Him. But being afraid of King Kaàsa, they did not dare go to
Vraja."***

   In this way it is seen that those brähmaëas did not go to meet Lord Kåñëa. The summer qualities
of that day are described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.22.30):

nidäghärkätape tigme
   chäyäbhiù sväbhir ätmanaù
atapatrayitan vikñya
   drumän äha vrajaukasaù


   "When the sun's heat became intense, Lord Kåñëa saw that the trees were acting as umbrellas by
shading Him, and thus He spoke as follows to His boyfriends."***

   In this verse the phrase "nidäghärkätape tigme" is a locative absolute. The yajna-patnis'
sambhogäbhäsa (reflection of sambhoga) is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.23.21-23):


yamunopavane 'çoka-
   nava-pallava-mandite
vicarantaà våtaà gopaih
   sägrajaà dadåçuù striyaù


   "Along the river Yamunä, within a garden decorated with buds of açoka trees, they caught sight
of Him strolling along in the company of the cowherd boys and His elder brother, Balaräma.***


çyämaà hiraëya-paridhià vanamälya-barha-
   dhätu-praväla-naöa-veñam anuvratäàse
vinyasta-hastam itareëa dhunänam abjaà
   karëotpalälaka-kapola-mukhäbja-häsam


   "His complexion was dark blue and His garment golden. Wearing a peacock feather, colored
minerals, sprigs of Mower buds, and a garland of forest flowers and leaves, He was dressed just like a
dramatic dancer. He rested one hand upon the shoulder of a friend and with the other twirled a
lotus. Lilies graced His ears, His hair hung down over His cheeks, and His lotuslike face was
smiling."***


präyaù-çruta-priyatamodaya-karëa-pürair
   yasmin nimagna-manasas tam athäkñi-randhraiù
antaù praveçya su-ciraà parirabhya täpaà
   präjïaà yathäbhimatayo vijahur narendra


   "O ruler of men, for a long time those brahmana ladies had heard about Kåñëa, their beloved,
and His glories had become the constant ornaments of their ears. Indeed, their minds were always
absorbed in Him. Through the apertures of their eyes they now forced Him to enter within their

hearts, and then they embraced Him within for a long time. In this way they fionally gave up the
pain of separation from Him, just as sagesa give up the anxiety of false ego by embracing their
innermost consciousness."***

   In this verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.23.23) the word {.sy 168}abhimatayaù" means: "false ego",
and the phrase {.sy 168}prajnam tapam vijahuù" means "as the sages, situated in spiritual trace,
become free of all sufferings, so these women also became free of all sufferings".

   One of those brähmaëés, becoming free of their previous disqualifications, attained in her heart
pürva-räga love for Lord Kåñëa and then enjoyed sambhoga pastimes with Him, pastimes that begin
with touching Him. This attainment of hers is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.23.35):


tatraikä vidhåtä bharträ
   bhagavantaà yathä-çrutam
hådopaguhya vijahau
   dehaà karmänubandhanam


   "One of ther ladies had been forcibly kept back by her husband. When she heard the others
describe the Supreme Lord Kåñëa, she embraced him within her heart and gave up her material
body, the basis of bondage to material activity."***

  When she gave up the brahmana body she had attained by past karma, then he disqualification
was destroyed and she was able to embrace Lord Kåñëa in her heart. In that way she attained Lord
Kåñëa's association. This is described in these words of Bhagavad-gétä (8.6):


yaà yaà väpi smana bhävam. . .


   "Whatever state of being one remembers when he quits this body, O son of Kunté, that state he
will attain without fail."*

   The statement that she attained Lord Kåñëa's association means that she attained the form of a
gopé. She did not attain the form of a brähmaëé and in that form associate with Lord Kåñëa. That
Lord Kåñëa's close associates were all cowherd people is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.23.37):


evaà lélä-nara-vapuù. . .


  "Thus the Supreme Lord, appearing like a human being to perform His pastimes, imitated the
ways of human society. He enjoyed pleasing His cows, cowherd boyfriends and cowherd girlfriends

with His beauty, words, and actions."***

   In this verse it is said that Lord Kåñëa enjoyed pleasing the cows and cowherd people. He did not
enjoy pastimes with others, at least not in the land of Vraja. In Vraja that yajïa-patné could not
enjoy pastimes with Lord Kåñëa without becoming a gopé. She thus entered the Vraja that is not
manifested in the material world. In that unmanifested Vraja Lord Kåñëa enjoys many different
pastimes, pastimes without limit. This is explained in the Kåñëa-sandarbha. Therefore there is
nothing wrong in her death. She yearned to attain Lord Kåñëa. With a great effort she struggled to
attain Him. In that way she attained a very exalted relationship (rasa) with Him. Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.23.35 quoted above was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Enviar una carta de amor (kama-lekha) es una de las actividades de purva-raga. Un ejemplo de una
La carta de amor se ve reflejada en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.52.37):
srutva gunan bhuvana-sundara srnvatam te. . .
"Sri Rukmini dijo (en su carta leída por el brahmán): Oh belleza de los mundos, habiendo escuchado
de Tus cualidades, que entran en los oídos de los que oyen y les quitan sus aflicciones corporales, y
Habiendo oído también de Tu belleza, que satisface todos los deseos visuales de quienes la ven, he
He fijado mi mente desvergonzada en Ti, oh Krishna."
Después de purva-raga viene sambhoga. Sambhoga tiene cuatro partes: 1. sandarsana (mirar), 2. sanjalpa
(conversación), 3. samsparsa (tocar) y 4. samprayoga (unión). Sandarsana significa "mirar fijamente". Un
Un ejemplo de sambhoga caracterizado por la mirada y el tacto se ve en estas palabras de srimad-
Bhagavatam (10.52.54-55):
saivam sanais calayati cala-padma-kosau
praptim tada bhagavatah prasamiksamana utsarya vama-karajair alakan apangaih
praptan hriyaiksata nrpan dadrse 'cyutam ca
tam raja-kanyam ratham aruruksatim
jahara krsno dvisatam samiksatam
"Con el pretexto de la procesión, Rukmini mostró su belleza solo para Krishna. Lentamente ella
Avanzó los dos remolinos de loto móviles de sus pies, esperando la llegada del Señor Supremo. Con
Las uñas de su mano izquierda apartaron algunos mechones de cabello de su rostro y tímidamente
miró de reojo
De Srila Jiva Gosvami
Sri Priti-sandarbha
a los reyes que estaban frente a ella. En ese momento vio a Krishna. Entonces, mientras Sus enemigos observaban,
El Señor tomó a la princesa, que ansiaba subir a su carro.
Estos versículos significan: "Ella esperó tímidamente la llegada de la Suprema Personalidad de Dios.
Miró a los reyes que estaban frente a ella. Entonces, con el corazón agitado, vio al infalible
"Señor Supremo." Estos versos fueron pronunciados por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
In the autumn after (Lord Çré Kåñëa's pastime of stealing the gopés' garments) all the vraja-gopés
enjoyed sambhoga pastime with Lord Kåñëa, pastimes born of the gopés' purva-raga love for Him,
pastimes that begin with gazing at Lord Kåñëa. These sambhoga pastimes are described (in the
scriptures). Although the unmarried girls of Vraja had already attained Lord Kåñëa's association,
theydid not feel fulfilled. Their purva-raga love for Him had still not attained its full nature. Still,
at least one gopés had enjoyed pastimes with Lord Kåñëa, as is seen in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.21.17):


pürëäù pulindyaù. . .


   "The aborigine women of the Våndävana area become disturbed by lust when they see the grass
marked with reddish kuìkuma
powder. Endowed with the color of Kåñëa's lotus feet, this powder originally decorated the breasts
of His beloveds, and when the aborigine women smear it on their faces and breasts, they give up all
their anxiety."***

   Still, many other gopés had not yet even touched Lord Kåñëa. This is seen in these words spoken
by the gopés in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.29.36):


yarhy ambujäkña. . .


    "O lotus-eyed one, the goddess of fortune considers it a festive occasion whenever she touches
the soles of Your lotus feet. You are very dear to the residents of the forest, and therefore we will
also touch those lotus feet. From that time on we will be unable even to stand in the presence of
any other man, for we will have been fully satisfied by You."***

   When the gopés first heard Lord Kåñëa's flute-music they at first tried to supress the ecstatic

emotions that came to overwhelm them. From this it may be seen that they had not yet directly
enjoyed sambhoga pastimes with Him. Also, because they had not yet enjoyed sambhoga pastimes
with Him, Lord Kåñëa at first rejected them, and they then appealed to Him. These pastimes are
seen in Çrémad-Bhägavatam, Canto 10, Chapter 29, in the passage that begins with these words
(Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.4):


niçamya gétaà tad anaìga-vardhanaà
   vraja-striyaù kåñëa-gåhéta-mänasäù
äjagmur anyonyam alakñitodyamäù
   sa yatra känto java-lola-kundaläù


   "When the young women of Våndävana heard Kåñëa's flute song, which arouses romantic
feelings, their minds were captivated by the Lord. They went to where their lover waited, each
unknown to the others, moving so quickly that their earrings swung back and forth."***

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
En el otoño siguiente (al pasatiempo del Señor Sri Krishna de robar las vestimentas de las gopis) todo el vraja-
Las gopis disfrutaban del pasatiempo sambhoga con el Señor Krishna, pasatiempos nacidos del amor purva-raga de las gopis por
Él, pasatiempos que comienzan con la contemplación del Señor Krishna. Estos pasatiempos sambhoga se describen (en el
escrituras). Aunque las muchachas solteras de Vraja ya habían alcanzado la compañía del Señor Krishna,
No se sentían satisfechos. Su amor purva-raga por Él aún no había alcanzado su plena naturaleza.
Sin embargo, al menos una gopi había disfrutado de pasatiempos con el Señor Krishna, como se ve en estas palabras de
Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.21.17):
purnah pulindyah. . .
"Las mujeres aborígenes de la zona de Vrndavana se perturban por la lujuria cuando ven la hierba
marcado con polvo de kunkuma rojizo. Dotado del color de los pies de loto de Krishna, este polvo
originalmente decoraba los pechos de Sus amadas, y cuando las mujeres aborígenes se lo untaban en sus
rostros y senos, abandonan toda su ansiedad."
Sin embargo, muchas otras gopis ni siquiera habían tocado al Señor Krishna. Esto se ve en estas palabras.
pronunciado por las gopis en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.29.36):
yarhy ambujaksa. . .
"Oh, tú de ojos de loto, la diosa de la fortuna considera una ocasión festiva cada vez que toca el
las plantas de Tus pies de loto. Eres muy querido para los habitantes del bosque, y por lo tanto te amaremos.
también toca esos pies de loto. Desde ese momento en adelante seremos incapaces incluso de estar de pie en presencia de
cualquier otro hombre, porque contigo ya estaríamos plenamente satisfechos."
Cuando las gopis escucharon por primera vez la música de flauta del Señor Krishna, al principio intentaron suprimirla.
emociones extáticas que llegaron a abrumarlos. De esto se puede ver que aún no habían
directamente disfrutaron de pasatiempos de sambhoga con Él. Además, porque aún no habían disfrutado de sambhoga
Pasatiempos con Él, el Señor Krishna al principio los rechazó, y luego le rogaron.
Los pasatiempos se ven en el srimad-Bhagavatam, Canto 10, Capítulo 29, en el pasaje que comienza con
Estas palabras (srimad-Bhagavatam 10.29.4):
nisamya gitam tad ananga-vardhanam
vraja-striyah krsna-grhita-manasah ajagmur anyonyam alaksitodyamah
sa yatra kanto java-lola-kundalah
"Cuando las jóvenes de Vrindavana oyeron el canto de flauta de Krishna, que despierta sentimientos románticos,
Sus mentes estaban cautivadas por el Señor. Fueron a donde su amado los esperaba, cada uno sin saberlo.
Los demás se movían tan rápido que sus pendientes se balanceaban de un lado a otro.
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
Jealous anger (mäna) may bring separation (vipralambha) of Lord Kåñëa and His beloved. This is
seen in the following words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-bheda-prakaraëa (Text 93):


aher iva gatiù premëä
   sva-bhäva-kuöilä bhavet
ato hetor ahetoç ca
   yünor mäna udaïcati


   "The progress of loving affairs between young couples is by nature crooked, like the movement of
a snake. Becuase of this, two types of nager arise between young couples-anger with cause and anger
without cause."*

   Jealous anger without a cause is described in these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-bheda-
prakaraëa (Text 70):


ahetur neti nety ukter
   hetor yan mäna ucyate
asya praëaya eva syän
   mänasya padam uttamam

  "When without any cause the beloved says `No. No.' and rejects the lover, this is called jealous
anger (mäna). This is the highest state of loving jealous anger."

   Jealous anger is thus with a cause and without a ccause. Jealous anger with a cause is described in
these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-bheda-prakaraëa (Text 71):


hetur érñyä-vipakñäder
   viçiñöye preyasä kåte
bhävaù praëaya-mukhyo 'yam
   érñyä-mänatvam åcchati


   "When the lover gives special attention to a certain beloved, then all the rivals of the beloved
become jealous. In this way what was once love becomes jealous anger. This is anger with cause."

  Jealous anger is also described in these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-bheda-prakaraëa
(Text 72):


snehaà vinä bhayaà na syän
   nerñyä ca praëayaà vinä
tasmän mäna-prakäro 'yaà
   dvayoù prema-prakäçakaù


   "Without love there cannot be fear (for the loss of the beloved), and without love there cannot
be jealousy. For this reason fear and jealousy may be manifestations of love."

   Jealous anger is seen in the following words of Hari-vaàça, Viñëu-parva (66.4 and 65.50):


ruñitäm iva täà devéà
   snehät saìkalpayann iva
bhéta-bhéto 'ti-çanakair
   viveça yadu-nandanaù

rüpa-yauvana-sampannä
   sva-saubhägyena garvitä
abhimänavaté devé
   çrutvaiverñyä-vaçaà gatä


   "As He slowly entered the palace, Lord Kåñëa, who is feared by fear itself, and who is the
descendent of Maharaja Yadu, lovingly meditated on His angry queen Satyabhämä."

  "Meanwhile, hearing (how her rival Rukmiëé had attained a pärijäta flower from Indraloka),
Queen Satyabhämä, who was very proud of her opulent beauty and youthfulness, bexcame
overwhelmed with jealous anger."

   When the beloved suspects the lover no longer loves her, then jealous anger with cause is
manifest. Lord Kåñëa enjoys teasing His beloved in this way (to make her angry because she
suspects He no longer loves her). An example of such teasing is seen in these words Lord Kåñëa
spoke to Queen Rukmiëé (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.29):


tvad-vacaù çrotu-kämena
   kñvelyäcaritam aìgane


   "I only spoke in jest, dear lady, because I wanted to hear what you would say."***

Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.30):


mukhaà ca prema-samrambha-
  sphuritädharam ékñitum. . .


   "I wanted to see your face with lips trembling in loving anger, the reddish corners of your eyes
throwing sidelong glances and the line of your beautiful eyebrows knit in a frown."***

  Queen Rukmiëé refuted Lord Kåñëa's teasing arguments by speaking these words (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.60.40):


jäòyaà vacas tava gadägraja. . .


   "My Lord, as a lion drives away lesser animals to claim his proper tribute, You drove off the
assembled kings with the resounding twang of Your Çärìga bow and then claimed me, Your fair
share. Thus it is sheer foolishness, my dear Gadägraja, for You to say You took shelter in the ocean
out of fear of those kings."***

   Lord Kåñëa's teasing words in the pastime were proper, for they were meant only to increase His
beloved's love for Him. Such words are approved by ancient and modern poets and philosophers.
Now jealous anger in the mood of worship, which is called {.sy 168}ädaraëéya-mäna", will be
considered. When, during the räsa dance, at the time of their first intimate meeting, Lord Kåñëa
abandoned all the gopés and remained hidden from their sight, the gopés became slightly angry with
Him. This is seen in the passage beginning with these words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.32.15):

sabhäjayitvä tam anaìga-dépanaà
   sahäsa-lélekñaëa-vibhrama-bhruvä
saàsparçanenäìka-kåtäìghri-hastayoù
   saàstutya iñat kupita babhasire


   "Sré Kåñëa had awakened romantic desires within the gopés, and they honored Him by glancing
at Him with playful smiles, gesturing amorously with their eyebrows, and massaging His hands and
feet as they held them in their laps. Even while worshiping Him, however, they felt somewhat
angry, and thus they addressed Him as follows."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadwva Gosvämé.
records.content:
La ira celosa (mana) puede traer separación (vipralambha) del Señor Krishna y su amada.
se ve en las siguientes palabras de Ujjvala-nilamani, srngara-bheda-prakarana (Texto 93):
aher iva gatih premna
sva-bhava-kutila bhavet ato hetor ahetos ca
yunor mana udancati
"El progreso de las relaciones amorosas entre parejas jóvenes es por naturaleza tortuoso, como el movimiento
de una serpiente. Debido a esto, surgen dos tipos de enojo entre las parejas jóvenes: enojo con causa
y enojo sin causa."
La ira celosa sin causa se describe en estas palabras de Ujjvala-nilamani, srngara-bheda-
prakarana (Texto 70):
ahetur neti nety ukter
hetor yan mana ucyate asya pranaya eva syan
manasya padam uttamam
"Cuando sin motivo alguno el amado dice 'No. No.' y rechaza al amante, esto se llama
ira celosa (mana). Este es el estado más elevado de ira celosa amorosa."
La ira celosa, por lo tanto, tiene una causa y carece de causa. La ira celosa con causa es
descrito en estas palabras de Ujjvala-nilamani, srngara-bheda-prakarana (Texto 71):
hetur irsya-vipaksader
visistye preyasa krte bhavah pranaya-mukhyo 'yam
irsya-manatvam rcchati
"Cuando el amante presta especial atención a un ser querido, entonces todos los rivales del
El ser amado se vuelve celoso. De esta manera, lo que una vez fue amor se convierte en ira celosa. Esta es la ira con
causa."
La ira por celos también se describe en estas palabras de Ujjvala-nilamani, srngara-bheda-prakarana.
(Texto 72):
sneham vina bhayam na syan
nersya ca pranayam vina tasman mana-prakaro 'yam
dvayoh prema-prakasakah
"Sin amor no puede haber temor (por la pérdida del ser amado), y sin
no pueden ser celos. Por esta razón, el miedo y los celos pueden ser manifestaciones de amor.
La ira celosa se observa en las siguientes palabras del Harivamsa, Visnu-parva (66.4 y 65.50):
rusitam iva tam devim
snehat sankalpayann iva bhita-bhito 'ti-sanakair
Vivesa Yadu-Nandanah
rupa-yauvana-sampanna
sva-saubhagyena garvita abhimanavati devi
srutvaiversya-vasam gata
"Mientras entraba lentamente al palacio, el Señor Krishna, a quien el miedo mismo infunde temor, y quien es el
Descendiente del Maharajá Yadu, meditaba con amor sobre su iracunda reina Satyabhama."
"Mientras tanto, al oír (cómo su rival Rukmini había obtenido una flor de parijata de Indraloka), la reina
Satyabhama, que estaba muy orgullosa de su opulenta belleza y juventud, se sintió abrumada por
ira celosa."
Cuando la amada sospecha que el amante ya no la ama, entonces la ira celosa con causa es
manifiesto. El Señor Krishna disfruta molestando a su amada de esta manera (para hacerla enojar porque ella
sospecha que ya no la ama). Un ejemplo de tal burla se ve en estas palabras Señor Krishna
habló con la reina Rukmini (srimad-Bhagavatam 10.60.29):
tvad-vacah srotu-kamena
ksvelyacaritam angane
"Solo lo dije en broma, querida señora, porque quería oír lo que usted diría."
Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.60.30):
mukham ca prema-samrambha-
sphuritadharam iksitum. . .
"Quería ver tu rostro con los labios temblando de amorosa ira, las comisuras rojizas de tus
tus ojos lanzaban miradas de reojo y la línea de tus hermosas cejas se fruncía en un ceño fruncido.
La reina Rukmini refutó los argumentos burlones del Señor Krishna pronunciando estas palabras (srimad-
Bhagavatam 10.60.40):
jadyam vacas tava gadagraja. . .
"Mi Señor, como un león ahuyenta a los animales inferiores para reclamar su tributo adecuado, Tú ahuyentaste a los
Reunió a reyes con el resonante sonido de tu arco sarnga y luego me reclamó, tu bella
compartir. Por lo tanto, es una pura tontería, mi querido Gadagraja, que digas que te refugiaste en el
océano por miedo a esos reyes."
Las palabras burlonas del Señor Krishna en el pasatiempo eran apropiadas, pues solo tenían como objetivo aumentar
El amor de su amada por Él. Estas palabras son avaladas por poetas y filósofos antiguos y modernos.
Ahora se considerará la ira celosa en el estado de ánimo de adoración, que se llama "adaraniya-mana".
Cuando, durante la danza rasa, en el momento de su primer encuentro íntimo, el Señor Krishna abandonó
Todas las gopis y permaneció oculto de su vista, las gopis se enojaron un poco con Él. Esto
Se observa en el pasaje que comienza con estas palabras (srimad-Bhagavatam 10.32.15):
sabhajayitva tam ananga-dipanam
sahasa-lileksana-vibhrama-bhruva samsparsanenanka-krtanghri-hastayoh
samstutya isat kupita babhasire
"Sri Krishna había despertado deseos románticos en las gopis, y ellas lo honraron mirándolo fijamente.
a Él con sonrisas juguetonas, haciendo gestos amorosos con sus cejas y masajeando Sus manos y
pies mientras los sostenían en sus regazos. Sin embargo, incluso mientras lo adoraban, sentían algo
enojados, y así se dirigieron a Él de la siguiente manera."
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadwva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
By speaking words of praise the lover may pacify the beloved's anger. An example of this may be
seen in these words of praise spoken by Lord Kåñëa to the gopés (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.32.21-22):


evaà mad-arthojjhita-loka-veda-
   svänäà hi vo mayy anuvåttaye 'baläù
mayäparokñaà bhajatä tirohitaà
   masuyitum marhatha tat priyam priyah


   "My dear girls, understanding that simply for My sake you had rejected the authority of worldly
opinion, of the Veòas and of your relatives, I acted as I did only to increase your attachment to Me.
Even when I removed Myself from your sight by suddenly disappearing, I never stopped loving you.
Therefore, My beloved gopés, please do not harbor any bad feelings toward Me, your beloved.***


na päraye 'haà niravadya-saàyujäm. . .


  "I am not able to repay My debt for your spotless service, even within a lifetime of Brahmä. Your
connection with Me is beyond reproach. You have worshiped Me, cutting off all domestic ties,
which are difficult to break. Therefore please let your own glorious deeds be your
compensation."***

  The meaning of these verses is clear. These verses were spoken by the Supreme Personality of
Godhead.
records.content:
Al pronunciar palabras de elogio, el amante puede apaciguar la ira del amado. Un ejemplo de esto puede ser...
se puede ver en estas palabras de alabanza pronunciadas por el Señor Krishna a las gopis (srimad-Bhagavatam 10.32.21-
22):
evam mad-arthojjhita-loka-veda-
svanam hola vo mayy anuvrttaye 'balah mayaparoksam bhajata tirohitam
masuyitum marhatha tat priyam priyah
"Mis queridas hijas, entendiendo que simplemente por mi causa habíais rechazado la autoridad de
opinión mundana, de los Vedas y de tus parientes, actué como lo hice solo para aumentar tu
apego a Mí. Incluso cuando me aparté de tu vista desapareciendo repentinamente, nunca
Dejé de amarte. Por lo tanto, mis amadas gopis, por favor no guarden ningún resentimiento hacia Mí.
tu amado.
na paraye 'ham niravadya-samyujam. . .
"No soy capaz de saldar mi deuda por vuestro servicio intachable, ni siquiera en el transcurso de la vida de Brahma."
Tu unión conmigo es intachable. Me has adorado, cortando todos los lazos familiares,
que son difíciles de romper. Por lo tanto, que vuestras propias y gloriosas hazañas sean vuestra recompensa."
El significado de estos versículos es claro. Estos versículos fueron pronunciados por la Suprema Personalidad de Dios.
