records.sourceEnglish:
Another example of the gopés greeting a messenger from Lord Kåñëa is seen in these words of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.65.9):


gopyo hasantyaù papracchü
   räma-sandarçanädåtäù
kaccid äste sukhaà kåñëaù
   pura-stré-jana-vallabhaù


  "Honored to have the personal audience of Lord Balaräma, the young gopés smiled and asked
Him: `Is Kåñëa, the darling of city women, living happily."***

  In this verse the word "hasantyaù" means "with smiles mixed with love and anger, smiles that
mock Lord Kåñëa". This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 403-413


   In Uddhava's presence the gopés spoke wildly. This is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.47.11):


käcin madhukaraà dåñövä
   dhyäyanté kåñëa-saìgamam
priya-prasthäpitaà dütaà
   kalpayitvedam abravét


   "One of the gopés, while meditating on Her previous association with Kåñëa, saw a honeybee
before Her and imagined it to be a messenger sent by Her beloved. Thus She spoke as follows."***

   In this verse the word "käcit" (a certain gopé, refers to Çré Rädhä". This is explained in the
Väsanä-bhäñya commentary. This truth is also seen in the Daçama-öippané commentary of Çréla
Sanätana Gosvämé. In the following eigth verses (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.12-19), angry Çré Rädha'
speaks wildly. She says (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.12):

madhupa kitava-bandho. . .


   "O honeybee, O friend of a cheater, don't touch My feet with your whiskers, which are smeared
with the kuìkuma that rubbed onto Kåñëa's garland when it was crushed hy the breasts of a rival
lover! Let Kåñëa satisfy the women of Mathurä. One who sends a messenger like you will certainly
be ridiculed in the Yadus' assembly."***

   Then She explains the reason for Her anger in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.13):


sakåd adhara-sudhäm. . .


   "After making us drink the enchanting nectar of His lips only once, Kåñëa suddenly abandoned
us, just as you might quickly abandon some flowers. How is, then, that Goddess Padmä willingly
serves His lotus feet? Alas! The answer must certainly be that her mind has been stolen away by His
deceitful words."***

  In this verse Çré Rädha' criticizes Her rival, Goddess Padmä. In the next verse She rejects the
words of praise brought by the messenger. She says (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.14):


kim iha. . .


   "O bee, why do you sing here so much about the Lord of the Yadus, in front of us homeless
people? These topics are old news to us. Better you sing about that friend of Arjuna in front of His
new girlfriends, the burning desire in whose breasts He has now relieved. Those ladies will surely
give you the charity you are begging."***

   In this verse the word "vijaya" means "Lord Kåñëa, who brings all others under His control",
"sakhä" means "your friend", "sakhénäm" means "of the women of Mathurä", and "prasaìgaù" means
"songs that bring one under their control". The gopés here say: "These songs are faulty because they
make us attached to Kåñëa. Even if you take that fault away, these topics still make us wretched and
miserable. This proves that Kåñëa is completely merciless." The gopés say in the next verse (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.47.15):


divi bhuvi. . .


   "In heaven, on earth, or in the subterranean sphere, what woman is unavailable to Him? He
simply arches His eyebrows and smiles with deceptive charm, and they all become His. The supreme
goddess herself worships the dust of His feet, so what is our position in comparison? But at least

those who are wretched can chant His name, Uttamaùsloka."***

   In this verse the word "api ca" means "nevertheless", "kåpaëa-pakñe" means "wretched persons
like us", "and "uttama-çloka-çabdaù" means the sound of Lord Kåñëa's name may be present". Here
the gopés hint: "Because He will not allow us to see Him, He is not merciful, and because He is not
merciful, He should not be called by the name Uttamaçloka".
   Thinking the bee's gentle humming to be a host of flattering words from Lord Kåñëa, Çré Rädha'
says in the next verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.16):


visåja çirasi. . .


   "Keep your head off My feet! I know what you're doing. You expertly learned diplomacy from
Mukunda, and now you come as His messenger with flattering words. But he abandoned those who
fro His sake alone gave up their children, husbands, and all other relations. He's simply ungrateful.
Why should I make up with Him now?"***

  With love and anger criticizing Lord Kåñëa, Çré Rädha' admitShe cannot stop talking of Him.
Then She finds fault with Him. She says (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.17):


mågayur iva. . .


   "Like a hunter He cruelly shot the king of the monkeys with arrows. Because He was conquered
by a woman, He disfigured another woman who came to Him with lusty desires. And even after
consuming the gifts of Bali Maharaja, He bound him up with ropes as if he were a crow. So let us
give up all frindship with this dark-compexioned boy, even if we can't give up talking about
Him."***

   Here the word "asita" means "Kåñëa, who is black because of all these misdeeds" and "sakhyaiù"
means with loving friendship". Again and again She affirms that Kåñëa should be rejected. She
again finds fault with Kåñëa when She speaks the next verse of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.18):


yad-anucarita. . .


    "To hear about the pastimes that Kåñëa regularly performs is nectar fro the ears. For those who
relish just a single drop of that nectar, even once, their dedication to material duality is ruined.
Many such persons have suddenly given up their wretched homes and families and, themselves
becoming wretched, traveled here to Våndävana to wander about like birds, begging for their
living."***

   In this verse the word "karna-piyusa" means "these topics may be nectar for the ears, but they are

not nectar for the heart". They are sweet only in the beginning. The words "vidhüta-dvandva-
dharmä vinañöäù" mean "at the end these topics make one almost unconscious". "Iha" means "in
Våndävana", "vihaìgäù" means "parrots and other birds", "bhikñu-caryäà caranti" means "they
follow the activities of the sannyasis, which means they ignore their material bodies and other
material things. It is seen that they act in this way". That is the meaning here.

   Then Çré Rädha' laments in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.19):


vayam åtam iva. . .


   "Faithfully taking His deceitful words as true, we became just like the black deer's foolish wives,
who trust the cruel hunter's song. Thus we repeatedly felt the sharp pain of lust cause by the touch
of His nails. O messenger, please talk about something besides Kåñëa."***

   Then, fearing that Her harsh and angry words spoken in these eight verses will chase the
messenger away, Çré Rädha' tries to end Her quarrel with Lord Kåñëa. She says in the next verse of
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.20):


priya-sakha. . .


   "O friend of My dear one, has My beloved sent you here again? I should honor you, friend, so
please choose whatever boon you wish. But why have you came back to take us to Him, whose
conjugal love is so difficult to give up? After all, gentle bee, His consort is the goddess Çré, as she is
always with Him, staying upon His chest."***

   With words of crooked irony Çré Rädha' speaks the second half of this verse. Here the word
"dvandva" means "amorous pastimes"". The reason amorous pastimes with Kåñëa are difficult to give
up is given in the word "satatam" (Goddess Lakñmé always on Lord Kåñëa's chest). Here, speaking
words of love and anger, Çré Rädha' imagines that the Çrévatsa line on Lord Kåñëa's chest is actually
Goddess Lakñmé. At the end of this passage Çré Rädha' humbly speaks these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.47.21):


api bata. . .


   "O Uddhava! It is indeed regrettable that Kåñëa resides in Mathurä. Does He remember His
father's household affairs and His friends, the cowherd boys? O great soul! Does He ever talk about
us, His maidservants? When will He lay on our heads His aguru-scented hand? "***

   The messenger (Uddhava, sent by Lord Kåñëa consoled the gopés in two ways: 1. by praising
them, and 2. by speaking Lord Kåñëa's message to them. He praised them in these words of Çrémad-

Bhägavatam (10.47.23):


aho yüyaà sma pürëärthäù. . .


   "Certainly you gopés are all-successful and are universally worshiped because you have dedicated
your minds in this way to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Väsudeva."***

  Uddhava's repeating Lord Kåñëa's message is discussed in Kåñëa-sandarbha (Anuccheda 155)¾
That message is given in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.29):


bhavaténäà viyogo me. . .


   "The Supreme Lord said: You are never actually separated from Me, for I am the soul of all
creation. Just as the elements of nature-ether, air, fire, water, and earth-are present in every created
thing, so I am present within everyuone's mind, life-air, and senses, and also within the physical
elements and the modes of material nature."***

  These words describe Lord Kåñëa's eternal pastimes with the people of Vraja in the eternal
Våndävana in another manifestation (in the spiritual sky). These words also describe the
meditational process of jïäna-yoga, by which the people of this world may obtain relief from
material sufferings. However, the teaching of jïäna-yoga do not bring peace to the gopés. Lord
Kåñëa then explains in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.34):


yat tö ahaà bhavaténäà vai. . .


   "But the actual reason why I, the beloved object of your sight, have stayed far away from you is
that I wanted to intensify your meditation upon Me and thus draw your minds closer to Me."***

   Lord Kåñëa also explains in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.37):


yä mayä kréòatä rätryäm. . .


   "Although some gopés had to remain in the cowherd village and so could not join the räsa dance
to sport with Me at night in the forest, they were nonetheless fortunate. Indeed, they attained Me
by thinking of My glorious pastimes."***

  Further explaining the meaning of the words He spoke in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.34, Lord
Kåñëa says in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.82.41):

api smaratha naù sakhyaù
   svänäm artha-cikérñayä
gatän. . .


   "My dear girlfriends, do you still remember Me? It was for My relatives' sake that I stayed away so
long, intent on destroying my enemies."***

   By describing his purpose (in staying way, Lord Kåñëa's intention to increase the gopés' feelings
of happiness and love for Him. This is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.53):


tatas täù kåñëa-sandeçair
   vyapeta-viraha-jvaräù
uddhavaà püjayäà cakrur
   jïätvätmänam adhokñajam


  "Lord Kåñëa's messages having relieved their fever of separation, the gopés then worshipped
Uddhava, recognizing him as nondifferent from their Lord, Kåñëa."***

  In this verse the word "vyapeta-viraha-jvaräù" means "by hearing of Lord Kåñëa's return and by
hearing of other topics also, the gopés became pacified". In this context the gopés asked (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.47.40):


kaccid gadägrajaù saumya. . .


   "Gentle Uddhava, is the elder brother of Gada now bestowing on the city women the pleasure
that actually belongs to us? We suppose those ladies worship Him with generous glances full of
affectionate, shy smiles."***

   In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.53 the word "ätmänam" means "because he was a messenger sent by
Kåñëa, Uddhava was able to know what was in Lord Kåñëa's heart", and "adhokñajam" means "the
gopés thought Uddhava was Lord Kåñëa Himself". Because they thought he was Lord Kåñëa, the
gopés worshiped Uddhava (uddhavaà püjayäà cakruù). The idea that Uddhava was Lorrd Kåñëa
Himself is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.46.14):


tam ägatam samägamya
   kåñëasyänucaraà priyam
nandaù prétaù pariñvajya
   väsudeva-dhiyärcayat

  "As sson as Uddhava arrived in Nanda Mahäräja's home, Nanda came forward to meet him. The
cowherd king embraced him in great happiness and worshipped him as nondifferent from Lorrd
Väsudeva."***

  This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvnamni.


Anucchedas 414-421


  Lord Balaräma's carrying a message from Lord Kåñëa in Dvärakä is seen in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.65.16):


saìkarñaëas täù kåñëasya
   sandeçair hådayaìgamaiù
säntvayäm äsa bhagavän
   nänänunaya-kovidaù


  "The Supreme Loord Balaräma, the attractoir of all, being expert at various kinds of conciliation,
consoled the gopés by relaying to them the confidential messages Lord Kåñëa had sent with Him.
These messages deeply touched the gopés' hearts."***

  After this message the gopés enjoyed sambhoga pastimes with Lord Kåñëa, directlyseeing Him at
Kurukñetra. Those pastimes are described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.82.39):


gopyaç ca kåñëam upalabhya ciräd abhiñöaà
   yat-prekñaëe dåçiñu pakñma-kåtaà çapanti
dågbhir hådé-kåtam alaà parirabhya sarväs
   tad-bhävam äpur api nitya-yujaà duräpam


   "While gazing at their beloved Kåñëa, the young gopés used to condemn the creator of their
eyelids (which would momentarily block their vison of Him). Now, seeing Kåñëa again after such a
long separation, with their eyes they took Him into their hearts, and there they embraced Him to
their full satisfaction. In this way they became totally absorbed in ecstatic meditation on Him,
although those who constantly practice mystic yoga find such absorption difficult to achieve."***

   After in this way describing the condition of the gopés' hearts, Çrémad-Bhägavatam explains the
gopés' ecstatic love for Lord Kåñëa in these words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.82.40):


bhagaväàs täs tathä-bhütä

   viviktä upasaìgataù
äçliñyanamayaà prñövä
   prahasann idam abravét


    "The Supreme Lord approached the gopés in a secluded place as they stood in their ecstatic
trance. After embracing each of them and inquiring about their well-being, He laughed and spoke
as follows."***

   Agitating the gopés' hearts, Lord Kåñëa made the gopés forgive his offenses. His smile was
glorious. Then He consoled the gopé with these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.82.41):


api smaratha naù sakhyaù
   svänäm artha-cikérñayä
gatäàç cérayatan chatru-
   pakña-kñäpaëa-cetasaù


   "My dear girlfriends, do you still remember Me? It was for My relatives' sake that I stayed away so
long, intent on destroying my enemies."***

   In this verse Lord Kåñëa says: "Please do not remember Me with anger. Then, to show that He is
indeed faultless, Lord Kåñëa says: "It was for My relatives' sake that I stayed away so long, intent on
destroying my enemies." Here the word "svanam" means "of My father, the king of Vraja, and also of
My kinsmen, the Yädavas". Thess words may also hint: "These two sides of the family (Kåñëa's
kinsmen in Vraja and Dvärakä, were both part of the Yädava dynasty". Then Lord Kåñëa explains
why He was so long in returning to Vraja. He says: "I was intent on destroying my enemies". These
words hint: "From now only you will enjoyMy company (sambhoga, without interruption".

   Fearing the gopés may remain dissatisfied at heart, Lord Kåñëa comforted them by explaining
that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is the ultimate independent controller of everyone. He
said (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.82.42):


apy avadhyayathäsman svid
   akåta-jïäviçaìkayä
nünaà bhütäni bhagavän
   yunakti vinuyakti ca


  "Do you perhaps think I'm ungrateful and thus hold Me in contempt? After all, it is the Supreme
Lord who brings living beings together and then separates them."***

   Fearing that the gopés might reply: "You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead", Lord Kåñëa
explains: "Your separation from Me gave birth to great love for Me in your hearts. This is not

against your actual desire." Lord Kåñëa told them in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.82.44):


mayi bhaktir hi bhütänäm
   amåtatväya kalpate
diñöyä yad äsén mat-sneho
   bhavaténäà mad-äpanaù


   "Rendering devotional service to Me qualifies any living being for eternal life. But by your good
fortune you have developed a special loving attitude toward Me, by which you have attained
Me."***

   Çrédhara Svämé comments on this verse:

  "This verse means: `Rendering devotional service to Me qualifies any living being for eternal life.
But by your good fortune you have developed a special loving attitude toward Me." The question
may be asked: `Why is this so?' The answer is given here in the words: `You have attained Me'."

   Then, in order to console the gopés and reassure them they they indeed have attained His
association, Lord Kåñëa explains to them that because He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead
manifest in a humanlike form. He explains to the gopés that He is present everywhere and He is the
shelter in which everything rests. He tells them in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.82.45-46):


ahaà hi sarva-bhütänäm. . .


   "Dear ladies, I am the beginning and end of all created beings and exist both within and without
them, just as the elements ether, water, earth, air, and fire are the beginning and end of all material
objects and exist both within and without them."*
   "In this way all created beings reside within the basic elements of creation, while the spirit souls
pervade the creation, remaining in their own true identity. You should see both of these-the
material creation and the self-as manifest within Me, the imperishable Supreme Truth."***

   In the description of the Lord's Dämodara pastimes it is also said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.9.13-
14):


na cäntar na bahir yasya. . .


   "The Supreme Personality of Godhead has no beginning and no end, no exterior and no interior,
no front and no rear. In other words, He is all-pervading. Because He is not under the influence of
the element of time, for Him there is no difference between past, present and future. He exists in
His own transcendental form at all times. Being absolute, beyond relativity, He is free from

distinctions between cause and effect, although He is the cause and effect of everything. That
unmanifested person, who is beyond the perception of the senses, had now appeared as a human
child, and mother Yaçodä, considering Him her own ordinary child, bound Him to the wooden
mortar with a rope."*

   In these two verses are described some of Lord Kåñëa's eternal pastimes in Våndävana with the
people of Vraja, pastimes also revealed in the Kåñëa-sandarbha, Anucchedas 174-175. Those
pastimes are also considered here. The gopés were able to see Lord Kåñëa as the Supreme. That is
described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.82.47):


adhyätma-çikñayä. . .


   "Having thus been instructed by Kåñëa in spiritual matters, the gopés were freed from all tinges
of false ego because of their incessant meditation upon Him. And with their deepening absorption
in Him, they came to understand Him fully."***
   In this verse the word "ätma" refers to Lord Kåñëa, and the word "siksaya" means "by His
instruction". Their bodies old and worn by meditating on Lord Kåñëa in the mood of separation, the
gopés then could see Lord Kåñëa in that way. Some thinkers interpret Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.82.45
in this way: "According to ordinary perception it seems that Lord Kåñëa is here preaching the
philosophy of Brahman, but that philosophy is not the true meaning of His words here. When
Rukmé was disfigured Lord Balaräma preached to Çré Rukmiëé what also seemed to be the
philosophy of Brahman. However, because Rukmiëé was directly enjoying pastimes with Lord
Kåñëa, that preaching of Lord Balarama's was only a specific pastime meant to look like the
activities of an ordinary person in this world. In the same way Lord Kåñëa's preaching of this
philosophy to the gopés is also only a pastime. Actually the gopés yearned to enjoy pastimes with
Lord Kåñëa directly in His spiritual form. This is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.82.48):


ähus ca te nalina-näbha padäravindaà


   "Dear Lord whose navel is just like a lotus flower, Your lotus feet are the only dhelter for those
who have fallen into the deep well of material existence. Your feet are worshiped and meditated
upon by great mystic yogis and highly learned philosophers. We wish that these lotus feet may also
be awakened within our hearts, although we are ordinary persons engaged in household affairs."***

   In this verse the gopés say: "Dear Lord whose navel is just like a lotus flower, may Your lotus feet
be awakened within the hearts of us, who are overcome by always meditating on You. Following
Your instructions, the peaceful-hearted kings of yoga meditate on Your feet in their hearts." An
explanation of this verse may be seen in the Kåñëa-sandarbha, Anuccheda 170. This verse was
spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Otro ejemplo de las gopis saludando a un mensajero del Señor Krishna se ve en estas palabras de
Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.65.9):
Gopyo Hasantyah Papracchu
rama-sandarsanadrtah kaccid aste sukham krsnah
pura-stri-jana-vallabhah
"Honradas de tener la audiencia personal del Señor Balarama, las jóvenes gopis sonrieron y preguntaron
Él: «¿Está Krishna, el favorito de las mujeres de la ciudad, viviendo feliz?»
En este versículo la palabra "hasantyah" significa con sonrisas mezcladas con amor y enojo, sonrisas que
"Búrlate del Señor Krishna". Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
In this way the truth of sambhoga, which consists of seeing, touching, and conversing with Lord
Kåñëa, is revealed. Lord Kåñëa stayed at Kurukñetra for three months. Then He and the gopés were
again separated. After that there were not again separatyion between them. After that they
enjoyed sambhoga pastimes together. The conclusion of these pastimes is described in the following
words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.83.1):


tathänugåhya bhagavän
   gopénäà sa gurur gatiù


   "Thus Lord Kåñëa, the spiritual master of the gopés and the very purpose of their life, showed
them His mercy. He •
then met with Yudhiñöhira and all His other relatives and inquired from them about their
welfare."***

   This verse explains that the gopés attained the desire they expressed in Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.82.48. This is seen in this verse, which explains that Lord Kåñëa gave His mercy (anugåhya, to
them. This verse also affirms that they attained Lord Kåñëa, who is their eternal destination
(gatiù). This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
De esta manera la verdad de sambhoga, que consiste en ver, tocar y conversar con
El Señor Krishna se revela. El Señor Krishna permaneció en Kurukshetra durante tres meses. Luego Él y las gopis
fueron separados de nuevo. Después de eso no hubo más separación entre ellos. Después de eso ellos
Disfrutaron juntos de pasatiempos relacionados con el sambhoga. La conclusión de estos pasatiempos se describe a continuación.
Palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.83.1):
tathanugrhya bhagavan
gopinam sa gurur gatih
"Así, el Señor Krishna, el maestro espiritual de las gopis y el propósito mismo de su vida,
les mostró Su misericordia. Luego se reunió con Yudhisthira y todos Sus demás parientes y les preguntó
les preocupa su bienestar."
Este verso explica que las gopis alcanzaron el deseo que expresaron en el srimad-Bhagavatam.
10.82.48. Esto se ve en este versículo, que explica que el Señor Krishna le dio Su misericordia (anugrhya) a
ellos. Este versículo también afirma que alcanzaron al Señor Krishna, quien es su destino eterno.
(gatih). Este verso fue pronunciado por srila sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
All of this is revealed in a passage from the Padma Puräëa, Uttara-khaëòa, a passage quoted in
Kåñëa-sandarbha, Anuccheda 176. In that pasasage it is said that Lord Kåñëa left Dvärakä and
returned to Våndävana. There, visible to everyone, even the ordinary people of this world, He
enjoyed pastimes for two months. After that Lord Kåñëa gave the people of Våndävana eternal
samyoga pastimes with Him, although those pastimes were not visible to ordinary people. Lord
Kåñëa clearly exlained all this to Uddhava in Çrémad-Bhägavatam's Eleventh Canto. There Lord
Kåñëa sais (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.12.10-11):


rämeëa särdhaà mathuräà praëéte. . .


   "The residents of Våndävana, headed by the gopés, were always completely attached to Me with
deepest love. Therefore, when My uncle Akrüra brought My brother Balaräma and Me to the city
of Mathurä, the residents of Våndävana suffered extreme mental distress because of separation from
Me and could not find any other source of happiness."***

täs täù kñapäù. . .


   "Dear Uddhava, all of those nights that the gopés spent with Me, their most dearly beloved, in
the land of Våndävana seemed to them to pass in less than a moment. Bereft of My association,
however, the gopés felt that those same nights dragged on forever, as if each night were equal to a
day of Brahmä."***

  After that time there was no further separation of Lord Kåñëa and the people of Våndävana.
After that time the people of Våndävana always enjoyed the bliss of Lord Kåñëa's association. Lord
Kåñëa described this truth in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (11.12.12-13):


tä nävidan mayy anuñaìga-baddha-dhiyaù. . .


   "My dear Uddhava, just as great sages in yoga trance merge into self realization like rivers
merging into the ocean, and are thus not aware of material names and forms, similarly the gopés
were so completely attached to Me within their minds that they could not think of their own
bodies, or of this world, or of their future lives. Their entire consciousness was simply bound up in
Me.***
   "All those hundreds of thousands of gopés, understanding Me to be their most charming lover
and ardently desiring Me in that way, were unaware of my actual position. Yet by intimately
associating with Me, the gopés attained Me, the Supreme Absolute Truth."***

    In these verses the word "anu" means "after the great separation", and "sanga-baddha-dhiyah"
means "their hearts were overcome with bliss", and navidan" means "they were bewildered with joy".
In that state it was as if they had become onbe with Lord Kåñëa. An example to explain that state is
given here in the phrase beginning with the words "just as great sages in yoga trance". A different
interpretation of Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.12.13 has already been given in Kåñëa-sandarbha,
Anuccheda 177. What the gopés attained (präpuù, is described in this verse. It is briefly described
there. There it is said: "The gopés attained Me, the Supreme Brahman, who am named Kåñëa." Here
Lord Kåñëa hints: "Unaware of My true nature, that I am eternally the object of their love, the gopés
attained Me as their paramour (järam). Then, desiring Me as their husband, they eventually
attained Me as their husband (ramaëam)." In this way it is seen that the gopés' relationship with
Lord Kåñëa after some time becomes parakéyäbhäsa (the faint reflection of the love a girl has for
her paramour). All this is explained in that passage of Kåñëa-sandarbha, Anuccheda 177. My
glorious master, Çréla Rüpa Gosvämé explains in Ujjvala-nélamaëi (Näyikä-bheda-prakaraëa, Text
3):


neñöä yad aëgini rase kavibhiù paroòhä
   tad gokulämbuja-dåçäà kulam antareëa
äçaàsayä rasa-vidher avitäritänäà

  kaàsäriëä rasika-maëòala-çekhareëa


   "The lotus-eyed gopés of Gokula descended to this material world to enjoy amorous pastimes with
Kåñëa, the crest jewel of those expert at relishing transcendental mellows, and the enemy of King
Kaàsa. Except for those gopés, learned scholars and philosophers do not consider amorous affairs
between a married woman and a paramour to be good or auspicious."

   The scriptures explain that this was the activity at the time of Lord Kåñëa's descent to this
world. The conclusion of all this is found in Çréla Rüpa Gosvämé's Lalita-Mädhava (7.18), where it is
said:


dagdhaà hanta dadhänayä vapuù. . .


  "O moon-faced one, My dear friend ahs again come to Me. My desire to see Him scorched My
body and wounded My heart with a monsoohn of pain. My life-breeath yearns to meet Him in
Våndävana and enjoy pastimes with Him in a cottage by the Yamunä's shore."

    When the mistaken idea that He is their paramour is destroyed, then the gopés enjoy the full
bliss of perfect sambhoga pastimes with Lord Kåñëa. In this way vipralam,bha is divided into four
parts and sambhoga is also divided into four parts. In sambhoga are many different pastimes, such as
lélä-cauryam (playful theft), saëgänam (singing and music), räsa (the räsa dance), jala-kréòä (water
pastimes), and våndävana-vihära (pastimes in Våndävana forest). An example of playful theft is
seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.22.9):


täsäà väsäàsy upädäya
   népam äruhya satvaraù. . .


   "Taking the girls' garments, He quickly climbed to the top of a kaòamba tree. Then, as He
laughed loudly and His companions also laughed, He addressed the girls jokingly."***

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Todo esto se revela en un pasaje del Padma Purana, Uttara-khanda, un pasaje citado
en Krsna-sandarbha, Anuccheda 176. En ese pasaje se dice que el Señor Krsna dejó Dvaraka y
Regresó a Vrindavana. Allí, a la vista de todos, incluso de la gente común de este mundo, Él
disfrutaron de pasatiempos durante dos meses. Después de eso, el Señor Krishna le dio a la gente de Vrindavana la eternidad.
Pasatiempos de samyoga con Él, aunque esos pasatiempos no eran visibles para la gente común. Señor Krishna
explicó claramente todo esto a Uddhava en el undécimo canto del srimad-Bhagavatam. Allí el Señor Krishna dijo:
(Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.12.10-11):
ramena sardham mathuram pranite. . .
"Los residentes de Vrindavana, encabezados por las gopis, siempre estuvieron completamente unidos a Mí con
amor más profundo. Por lo tanto, cuando mi tío Akrura nos trajo a mi hermano Balarama y a mí a la ciudad de
Mathura, los residentes de Vrindavana sufrieron una angustia mental extrema debido a la separación de Me
y no pudo encontrar ninguna otra fuente de felicidad."
tas tah ksapah. . .
"Querido Uddhava, todas esas noches que las gopis pasaron conmigo, su más amado,
En la tierra de Vrndavana les pareció pasar en menos de un instante. Privados de Mi compañía,
Sin embargo, las gopis sentían que esas mismas noches se prolongaban eternamente, como si cada noche fuera igual a
un día de Brahma."
Después de ese momento, no hubo más separación entre el Señor Krishna y la gente de Vrindavana.
A partir de entonces, la gente de Vrindavana siempre disfrutó de la dicha de la compañía del Señor Krishna.
El Señor Krishna describió esta verdad en estas palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam (11.12.12-13):
ta navidan mayy anusanga-baddha-dhiyah. . .
"Mi querido Uddhava, así como los grandes sabios en trance de yoga se funden en la autorrealización como ríos
fusionándose con el océano, y por lo tanto no son conscientes de los nombres y formas materiales, de manera similar las gopis
estaban tan completamente apegados a Mí en sus mentes que no podían pensar en sí mismos.
cuerpos, o de este mundo, o de sus vidas futuras. Toda su consciencia estaba simplemente ligada
arriba en mí.
"Todos esos cientos de miles de gopis, entendiéndome como su amante más encantador y
Deseándome ardientemente de esa manera, desconocían mi posición real. Sin embargo, al íntimamente
Al asociarse conmigo, las gopis me alcanzaron, a Mí, la Suprema Verdad Absoluta."
En estos versículos la palabra "anu" significa "después de la gran separación" y "sanga-baddha-dhiyah"
significa "sus corazones fueron invadidos por la dicha", y "navidan" significa "fueron desconcertados por
alegría". En ese estado era como si se hubieran unido al Señor Krishna. Un ejemplo para explicar eso
El estado se da aquí en la frase que comienza con las palabras "igual que los grandes sabios en trance de yoga". A
En Krsna-sandarbha ya se ha dado una interpretación diferente del srimad-Bhagavatam 11.12.13.
Anuccheda 177. Lo que las gopis alcanzaron (prapuh) se describe en este versículo. Se describe brevemente.
descrito allí. Allí se dice: "Las gopis me alcanzaron, al Brahman Supremo, que soy llamado
Krishna." Aquí el Señor Krishna insinúa: "Sin ser consciente de Mi verdadera naturaleza, que Yo soy eternamente el objeto de
su amor, las gopis me alcanzaron como su amante (jaram). Entonces, deseándome como su esposo,
"Finalmente me alcanzaron como su esposo (ramanam)". De esta manera se ve que las gopis...
La relación con el Señor Krishna después de algún tiempo se convierte en parakiyabhasa (el débil reflejo de la
amor que una chica siente por su amante). Todo esto se explica en ese pasaje del Krsna-sandarbha,
Anuccheda 177. Mi glorioso maestro, srila Rupa Gosvami explica en Ujjvala-nilamani (Nayika-bheda-
prakarana, Texto 3):
nesta yad angini rase kavibhih parodha
tad gokulambuja-drsam kulam antarena asamsaya rasa-vidher avitaritanam
kamsarina rasika-mandala-sekharena
"Las gopis de ojos de loto de Gokula descendieron a este mundo material para disfrutar de pasatiempos amorosos."
con Krsna, la joya suprema de aquellos expertos en saborear los placeres trascendentales, y el enemigo de
Rey Kamsa. Excepto aquellas gopis, los eruditos y filósofos no consideran amorosos.
Las relaciones entre una mujer casada y un amante se consideran buenas o auspiciosas.
Las escrituras explican que esta era la actividad en el momento del descenso del Señor Krishna a este mundo.
mundo. La conclusión de todo esto se encuentra en el Lalita-Madhava (7.18) de Srila Rupa Gosvami, donde
Se dice:
dagdham hanta dadhanaya vapuh. . .
"Oh, tú, rostro de luna, mi querido amigo ha vuelto a mí. Mi deseo de verlo quemó mi cuerpo.
y hirió mi corazón con un monzón de dolor. Mi aliento de vida anhela encontrarse con Él en Vrindavana y
Disfrutar de momentos de ocio con Él en una cabaña a orillas del Yamuna."
Cuando se destruye la idea errónea de que Él es su amante, entonces las gopis disfrutan de la plenitud.
la dicha de los pasatiempos perfectos de sambhoga con el Señor Krishna. De esta manera, vipralam,bha se divide en cuatro
partes y sambhoga también se divide en cuatro partes. En sambhoga hay muchos pasatiempos diferentes, como
como lila-cauryam (robo lúdico), sanganam (canto y música), rasa (la danza rasa), jala-krida
(pasatiempos acuáticos) y vrndavana-vihara (pasatiempos en el bosque de Vrndavana). Un ejemplo de juego
El robo se ve reflejado en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.22.9):
tasam vasamsy upadaya
nipam aruhya satvarah. . .
"Tomando las prendas de las niñas, trepó rápidamente a la copa de un árbol kadamba. Entonces, mientras Él
Se rió a carcajadas y sus compañeros también rieron. Se dirigió a las chicas en tono de broma.
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
An example of singing and music is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.9):


käcit samaà mukundena. . .

   "One gopé, joining Lord Mukunda in His singing, sang pure melodious tones that rose
harmoniously above His. Kåñëa was pleased and showed great appreciation for her performance,
saying `Excellent! Excellent!' Then another gopé repeated the same melody, but in a special metrical
pattern, and Kåñëa praised her also."***

   Another example of singing and music is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.34.20-
21):


kadäcid atha govindo
   rämaç cädbhuta-vikramaù
vijahratur vraje rätryäà
   madhya-gau vraja-yoñitäm


   "Once Lord Govinda and Lord Räma, the performers of wonderful feats, were playing in the
forest at night with the young girls of Vraja.***


upagéyamänau lalitaà
   stré janair baddha-sauhådaiù
sö-alaìkåtänuliptäìgau
   sragvinau virajo-'mbarau


   "Kåñëa and Balaräma wore flower garlands and spotless garments, and Their limbs were
beautifully decorated and anointed. The women sang Their glories in a charming way, bound to
Them by affection."***

   In general the Holi festival is celebrated in this way. Thus, to celebrate the Holi festival, Lord
Kåñëa and His brother, Lord Balaräma, enjoyed singing and many other pastimes with a host of girls
in Vraja. This pastime is also described in the Bhaviñya Puräëa, Uttara-khaëòa. Even today, the
people of India celebrate the Holi festival in this way. It is said in that passage of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.34.22):


niçä-mukhaà mänayantäv
   uditoòupa-tärakam. . .


   "The two Lords praised the nightfall, signaled by the rising of the moon and the appearance of
stars, a lotus-scented breeze and bees intoxicated by the fragrance of jasmine flowers."***

  The bliss of this festival, which occurs on the full-moon day of the month of Phälguna, after the
winter has ended, is described in this verse. Lord Kåñëa enjoyed this festival with His joyful friend
Lord Balaräma. In some texts of Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.34.20 the passage reads "vane rätryäm"

instead of "vraje rätryäm". In this reading the forest is described as the forest of Vraja. These verses
were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 425-427


   The räsa dance pastime is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.2):


taträrabhata govindo
   räsa-kréòäm anuvrataiù. . .


   "There on the Yamunä's banks Lord Govinda then began the pastime of the räsa dance in the
company of those jewels among women, the faithful gopés, who joyfully linked their arms
together."***

   The Lord's water-pastimes are seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.23):


so 'mbhasy alaà yuvatibhiù pariñicyamänaù. . .


   "My dear King, in the water Kåñëa found Himself being splashed on all sides by the laughing
gopés, who looked at Him with love. As the demigods worshiped Him by showering flowers from
their airplanes, the self-satisfied Lord took pleasure in playing like the king of the elephants."***

   Lord Kåñëa's pastimes in Våndävana forest are seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.33.24):


tatas" ca kåñëopavane jala-sthala-
   prasüna-gandhänila juñöa-dik-tate. . .


   "Then the Lord strolled through a small forest on the bank of the Yamunä. This forest was filled
to its limits with breezes carrying the fragrances of all the flowers growing on the land and in the
water. Followed by His entourage of bees and beautiful women, Lord Kåñëa appeared like an
intoxicated elephant with his she-elephants."***

   The meaning of these verses is clear. These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Un ejemplo de canto y música se puede ver en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.33.9):
kacit samam mukundena. . .
"Una gopi, uniéndose al Señor Mukunda en su canto, cantó tonos puros y melodiosos que se elevaban
armoniosamente por encima de Él. Krishna se complació y mostró gran aprecio por su actuación.
diciendo "¡Excelente! ¡Excelente!" Luego otra gopi repitió la misma melodía, pero en un tono especial.
patrón métrico, y Krishna también la alabó."
Otro ejemplo de canto y música se ve en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.34.20-
21):
kadacid atha govindo
ramas cadbhuta-vikramah vijahratur vraje ratryam
madhya-gau vraja-yositam
"Una vez, el Señor Govinda y el Señor Rama, los autores de hazañas maravillosas, estaban jugando en el
El bosque por la noche con las jóvenes de Vraja.
upagiyamanau lalitam
stri janair baddha-sauhrdaih sv-alankrtanuliptangau
sragvinau virajo-'mbarau
"Krsna y Balarama llevaban guirnaldas de flores y vestiduras inmaculadas, y sus miembros estaban
bellamente decoradas y ungidas. Las mujeres cantaban Sus glorias de una manera encantadora, unidas a Ellos.
por afecto."
En general, el festival Holi se celebra de esta manera. Por lo tanto, para celebrar el festival Holi,
El Señor Krishna y su hermano, el Señor Balarama, disfrutaban cantando y realizando muchos otros pasatiempos con una multitud de
chicas en Vraja. Este pasatiempo también se describe en el Bhavisya Purana, Uttara-khanda. Incluso hoy en día,
El pueblo de la India celebra el festival Holi de esta manera. Se dice en ese pasaje del srimad-
Bhagavatam (10.34.22):
nisa-mukham manayantav
uditodupa-tarakam. . .
"Los dos señores elogiaron el anochecer, anunciado por la salida de la luna y la aparición
de estrellas, una brisa con aroma a loto y abejas embriagadas por la fragancia de las flores de jazmín."
La dicha de este festival, que tiene lugar el día de luna llena del mes de Phalguna, después
El invierno ha terminado, se describe en este verso. El Señor Krishna disfrutó de esta festividad con Sus
alegre amigo Señor Balarama. En algunos textos del srimad- Bhagavatam 10.34.20 el pasaje dice "vano
ratryam" en lugar de "vraje ratryam". En esta lectura, el bosque se describe como el bosque de
Vraja. Estos versos fueron pronunciados por srila sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
The Lord's amorous pastimes with the gopés are seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.29.46):


bähu-prasära-parirambha-karälakoru-névé. . .


   "There Kåñëa threw His arms around the gopés and embraced them. He aroused Cupid in the
beautiful young ladies of Vraja by touching their hands, hair, thighs, belts, and breasts, by playfully
scratching them with His fingernails, and also by joking with them, glancing at them, and laughing
with them. In this way the Lord enjoyed pastimes."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.
records.content:
Los pasatiempos amorosos del Señor con las gopis se ven reflejados en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam.
(10.29.46):
bahu-prasara-parirambha-karalakoru-nivi. . .
"Allí Krishna rodeó con sus brazos a las gopis y las abrazó. Despertó a Cupido en el
hermosas jóvenes de Vraja al tocar sus manos, cabello, muslos, cinturones y senos, por
rascándoles juguetonamente con sus uñas, y también bromeando con ellos, mirándolos de reojo,
y riendo con ellos. De esta manera el Señor disfrutaba de sus pasatiempos.
El significado de este verso es claro. Este verso fue pronunciado por Srila Sukadeva Gosvami.

records.sourceEnglish:
At the conclusion of the descriptioon of Lord Kåñëa's amorous pastimes in the räsa dance it is
said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.25):


evaà çaçäìkäàçu-viräjitä niçäù. . .


   "Although the gopés were firmly attached to Lord Kåñëa, whose desires are always fulfilled, the
Lord was not internally affected by any mundane sex desire. Still, to perform His pastimes the Lord
took advantage of all those moonlit autumn nights, which inspire poetic descriptions of
transcendental affairs."***

   Lord Kåñëa's pastimes with Çré Rädhä, who is thhe crest jewel of all fortunate girls, are described
in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.27-34):


kasyäù padäni caitäni
   yätäyä nanda-sünunä
aàsa-nyasta-prakoñöhäyäù
   kareëoù kariëä yathä


   "Here we see the footprints of some gopé who must have been walking along with the son of
Nanda Mahäräja. He must have put His arm on Her shoulder, just as an elephant rests His trunk on
the shoulder of an accompanying she-elephant."***


anayärädhito nünaà
  bhagavän harir éçvaraù

yan no vihäya govindaù
   préto yäm amayad rahaù


   "Certainly this particular gopé has perfectly worshiped the allpowerful Personality of Godhead,
Govinda, since He was so pleased with Her that He abandoned the rest of us and brought Her to a
secluded place."***


dhanyä aho amé alyo
   govindäìghry-abja-reëavaù
yän brahmeçau ramä devé
   dadhur mürdhny agha-nuttaye


  "O girls! The dust of Govinda's lotus feet is so sacred that even Brahmä, Siva and the goddess
Ramä take that dust upon their heads to dispel sinful reactions."***


tasyä amüni naù kñobham-
   kurvanty uccaiù padäni yat
yaikäpahåtya gopénäà
   dhanaà bhuìkte 'cyutädharam

na lakñyante padäny atra
   tasyä nünaà tåëäìkuraiù
khidyat-sujätäìghri-talam
   unnénye preyaséà priyah


   "These footprints of that special gopé greatly disturb us. Of all the gopés, She alone was taken
away to a secluded place, where She is enjoying the lips of Kåñëa. Look, we can't see Her footprints
over here! It's obvious that the grass and sprouts were hurting the tender soles of Her feet, and so
the lover lifted up His beloved."***


imäny adhika-magnäni
   padäni vahato vadhüm
gopyaù paçyata kåñëasya
   bhäräkräntasya käminaù
aträvaropitä käntä
   puñpa-hetor mahätmanaù


   "Please observe, my dear gopés, how in this place lusty Kåñëa's footprints are pressed more deeply
into the ground. Carrying the weight of His beloved must have been difficult for Him. And over

here that intelligent boy must have put Her down to gather some flowers.***


atra prasünävacayaù
   pnya-rthe preyasä kåtaù
prapadäkramana ete
   paçyatäsakale pade


   "Just see how in this place dear Kåñëa collected flowers for His beloved. Here He has left the
impression of only the front part of His feet because He was standing on His toes to reach the
flowers."***


keça-prasädhanaà tö atra
   käminyäù käminä krtam
täni cüòayatä käntäm
   upaviñöam iha dhruvam


  "Certainly Kåñëa sat down here with His girlfriend to arrange Her hair. The lusty boy must have
made a crown for that Iusty girI out of the flowers He had collected."***

   In this passage Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.3027 is spoken by all the gopés, 10.30.28 is spoken by Çré
Rädhä's friends, 10.30.29 is spoken by the gopés who are neither friends nor enemies, 10.30.30 is
spoken by Çré Rädhä's rivals, the second stanza (beginning with the words "na lakñyate, of 10.30.30 is
spoken by Çré Rädhä's friends, who speak these words to torment Çré Rädhä's rivals, 10.30.31 is
spoken by the rivals who cannot bear Çré Rädhä's good fortune, the last two lines (beginning with
the word "aträvaropitä, of 10.30.31 and 10.30.32 are spoken by by Çré Rädhä's friends, the first two
lines of 10.30.33 are spoken by Çré Rädhä's rivals, and the last two lines of 10.30.33 are spoken by Çré
Rädhä's friends. In this way Çré Rädhä's friends and rivals describe the pastimes of Çré Çré Rädha'-
Kåñëa. It is also said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.26):


vilokyärtäù samabruvan


   "The gopés began following Kåñëa's path, as shown by His many footprints, but when they saw
that these prints were thoroughly intermixed with those of His dearmost consort, they became
perturbed and spoke as follows."***

  All the gopés spoke these words. Filled with lonmgings, all the gopés wandered (in the forest).
The passage quoted above (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.30.2*-34, was spoken by the vraja-gopés.

   The pastimes of Çré Rädha' had already been hinted at in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.30.11-12):

apy eëa-patni. . .


   "O friend, wife of the deer, has Lord Acyuta been here with His beloved, bringing great joy to
your eyes? Indeed, blowing this way is the fragrance of His garland of kunòa flowers, which was
smeared with the kuìkuma from the breasts of His girlfriend when He embraced Her.***
   "O trees, we see that you are bowing down. When the younger brother of Räma walked by here,
followed by the intoxicated bees swarming around the tulasé maïjarés decorating His garland, did
He acknowledge your obeisances with His affectionate glances? He must have been resting His arm
on the shoulder of His beloved and carrying a lotus flower in His free hand."***

   The reader may study these verses to see the pastimes of Çré Çré Rädhä-Kåñëa.


Epilogue


   Many verses of Çrémad-Bhägavatam's Tneth Canto we have not elaborately explained here. The
devotees who yearn to taste the nectar of the rasas may study the explanations Çréla Çrédhara Svämé
has given in His Daçama-öippané commentary. Following his explanations, we have explained the
verses of Çrémad-Bhägavatam.


älébhiù paripälitaù pravalitaù sänandam älokitaù
   pratyäçaà sumanaù-phalodaya-vidhau sämodam äsväditaù
våndäraëya-bhuvi prakäça-madhuraù sarvätiçäyi-çriyä
   rädhä-mädhavayoù pramodayatu mäm ulläsa-kalpa-drumaù


   May the glorious kalpa-våkña tree of Çré Çré Rädha'-Mädhava, a tree surrounded by hosts of
bumblebees that are Çré Rädhä's gopé freinds, a tree delightful to see, a tree that fills the directions
with the sweet fragrance of its sumanù flowers, a tree that manifests in the land of Våndävana the
sweetness of the greatest beauty and handsomeness, fill me with delight.


tädåça-bhävaà bhävaà
   prathayitum iha yo 'vatäram äyätaù
ä-durjana-gaëa-çaraëaà
   sa jayati caitanya-vigrahaù kåñëaù


   Glory to Lord Kåñëa, who is the shelter of everyone, including even the most fallen and wicked,
and who, manifesting the form of Lord Caitanya, descended to this world to widely distribute the
gift of ecstatic spiritual love.

Thus ends Çré Préti-sandarbha

El Señor no se vio afectado internamente por ningún deseo sexual mundano. Aun así, para realizar Sus pasatiempos

descrito en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.30.27-34):

En este pasaje srimad-Bhagavatam 10.3027 es hablado por todas las gopis, 10.30.28 es hablado por

Todas las gopis pronunciaron estas palabras. Llenas de longanimings, todas las gopis vagaron (en el

Epílogo

anucchedas 78-80), in the description
of the four Kumäras' seeing Vaikuëöha, and in Çré Vyäsa's and Çré Närada's conversation about the
relative importance of impersonal Brahman and the Supreme Personality of Godhead. In Çrémad-
•ŠBhägavatam (3.15.43) it is said of the Four Kumäras:


tasyäravinda-nayanasya. . .


   "When the breeze carrying the aroma of tulasé leaves from the toes of the lotus feet of the
Personality of Godhead entered the nostrils of those sages, they experienced a change both in body
and mind, even though they were attached to the impersonal Brahman understanding."*

   That the Supreme Personality of Godhead is superior to the impersonal Brahman is hinted in
these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (1.5.4):


jijïäsitam adhétaà ca. . .


   "You have fully delineated the subject of impersonal Brahman as well as the knowledge derived
therefrom. Why should you be despondent in spite of all this, thinking that you are undone, my
dear prabhu?"*

  The superiority of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is also confirmed by these words of
Dhruva Mahäräja (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 4.9.10):


yä niåvrtis tanu-bhåtäm. . .


   "My Lord, the transcendental bliss derived from meditating upon Your lotus feet or hearing
about Your glories from pure devotees is so unlimited that it is far beyond the stage of
brahmänanda, where one thinks himself merged in the impersonal Brahman as one with the
Supreme. Since brahmänanda is also defeated by the transcendental bliss derived from devotional
service, then what to speak of the temporary blissfulness of elevating oneself to the heavenly
planets, which is ended by the separating sword of time? Although one may be elevated to the
heavenly planets, he falls down in due course of time."*

   About the author of Çrémad-Bhägavatam it is said (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 12.12.69):


svasukha-nibhåta-cetäs tad-vyudastänya-bhävaù. . .


    "I offer my respectful obeisances unto Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé, the son of Vyäsadeva. He is the
destroyer of all sinful reactions and is full in self-realization and bliss. Because of this, he has no
other desire. Still, he was attracted by the transcendental pastimes of the Supreme Personality of
Godhead, and out of compassion for the people, he described the transcendental historical
literature called Çrémad-Bhägavatam. This is compared to the light of the Absolute Truth."*

   In Bhagavad-gétä (18.54) the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself declares:


brahma-bhütaù prasannätmä. . .


   "One who is thus transcendentally situated at once realizes the Supreme Brahman. He never
laments nor desires to have anything. He is equally disposed to every living entity. In that state he
attains pure devotional service unto Me."*

    Simply by seeing the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Çré Prahläda became free from all sins.
Fiorst he saw the impersonal Brahman, then he saw the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and then
he became filled with transcendental bliss. In this way he attained the supreme goal of life. Of him
it is said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (7.9.6):


sa tat-kara-sparça-dhutäkhiläçubhaù
   sapady abhivyakta-parätma-darçanaù
tat-päda-padmaà hådi nirvåto dadhau
   håñyat-tanuù klinna-kåd-açru-locanaù


  "By the touch of Lord Nåsiàhadeva's hand on Prahläda Mahäräja's head, Prahläda was
completely freed of all material contaminations and desires, as if he had been thoroughly cleansed.
Therwefore he at once became transcendentally situated, and all the symptoms of ecstasy became
manifest in his body. His heart filled with love, and his eyes with tears, and thus he was able to
completely capture the lotus feet of the Lord within the core of his heart."*

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

Anucchedas 103 and 104


   Here someone may protest: "Is it not true that the sages who yearn after liberation and who have
already attained liberation are glorified in all the scriptures? How can the devotees be superior to
them? Why would the sages desire anything but liberation?" To answer this protest, Uddhava speaks
these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.59):


kvemäù striyo vana-carér vyabhicära-duñöäù
  kåñëe kva caiña paramätmani rüòha-bhäväù
nanv éçvaro 'nubhajato 'viduño 'pi säkñäc
  chreyas tanoty agada-räja ivopayuktaù


   "How amazing it is that these simple women who wander about the forest, seemingly spoiled by
improper behavior, have achieved the perfection of unalloyed love for Kåñëa, teh Superme Soul!
Still, it is true that the Supreme Lord Himself awards His blessings even to an ignorant worshiper,
just as the best medicine works even when taken by a person ignorant of its ingredients."***

   In these verses, from beginning to end, Çrémän Uddhava's great devotion to the Lord is clearly
seen. Here someone may protest that the gopés' relationship with Lord Kåñëa was adulterous and
therefore immoral. This protest is answered by these words spoken at the conclusion of the

description of the räsa dance (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.33.35):


gopénäà tat-paténäà ca
   sarveñäm eva dehinäm
yo 'ntaç carati so 'dhyakñaù
   kréòaneneha deha-bhäk


    "He who lives as the overseeing witness within the gopés and their husbands, and indeed within
all embodied living beings, assumes forms in this world to enjoy transcendental pastimes."***

   The idea of wicked-hearted men that the gopés acted immorally in their relationship with Lord
Kåñëa is refuted by this verse, by the word "paramätmani" (the Supreme Personality of Godhead) in
Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.59, and also by these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.61):


ärya-pathaà ca hitvä. . .


    "The gopés of Våndävana have given up the association of their husbands, sons, and other family
members, who are very difficult to give up, andf they have forsaken the path of chastity to take
shelter of tyhe lotus feet of Mukunda, Kåñëa, which one should search for by Vedic knowledge. Oh,
let me be fortunate enough to be one of the bushes, creepers, or herbs in Våndävana, because the
gopés trample them and bless them with the dust of their feet."*

   Now is not the right time to refute the mistaken idea that the gopés acted immorally. Later in
this book we will proove that the gopés acted rightly. In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.58 and 59 the
words "kvemäù striyo vana-caréù" mean "what is the status of the women who enjoyed pastimes in
Våndävana forest and took shelter of Lord Kåñëa?" In these verse the words "kva vyabhicära-duñöäù
bhava-bhiyo vayam" mean {.sy 168}and what is the status of us, sages who have not attained exalted
spiritual love and who are not attached to Lord Kåñëa, are afraid of material existence?" The
meaning here is: {.sy 168}The difference bewteen us and the gopés is very great." Here the question
may be asked: "Why does such a great difference exist?" The answer is given here in the words {.sy
168}eña paramätmani rüòha-bhäväù", which mean "In the gopés is seen great ecstatic love (mahä-
bhäva) for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is worshiped by everyone and who is the
abode of all desires. That same ecstatic love is not seen n us." If this is so, then the following
question may be asked: If you do not directly see Lord Kåñëa's glorious qualities, qualities that made
the gopés fall in love with Him, then how will you attain that ecstatic love even if you yearn to
attain it? This quesyion is answered in this verse in the passage beginning with the word "nanu"
(the Supreme Lord Himself awards His blessings even to an ignorant worshiper, just as the best
medicine works even when taken by a person ignorant of its ingredients.) Here the word "aviduñaù"
means {.sy 168}the Lord Hismelf makes this love spontaneously manifest within me." That is the
example given here. Uddhava declares in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.47.27):

viraheëa mahä-bhäga
   mahän me 'nugrahah kåtaù


   "You have rightfully claimed the privilege of unalloyed love for the transcendental Lord, O most
glorious gopés. Indeed, by exhibiting your love for Kåñëa in separation from Him, you have shown
me great mercy7"***

   Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.59 may also be interpreted in a different way, in a way that sternly
rebukes ladies who, although very faithful to their husbands, are averse to the rasas of devotional
service. In the first interpretation of this verse the words "kvemah striah" referred to the gopés, who
enjoy pastimes in Våndävana forest. The second interpretation of this verse is based on the
asumption that an "a" was originally present before the word "vana-carih" and then elided by
sandhi. Thus the word was originally "avana-carih", which would mean "women who are not like
the gopés". Such materialistic women are described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (5.18.19):


striyo vratais tvä. . .



   "My dear Lord, You are certainly the fully independent master of all the senses. Therefore all
women who worship You by strictly observing vows because they wish to acquire a husband to
satisfy their senses are surely under illusion. They do not know that such a husband cannot actually
give protection to them or their children. Nor can he protect their wealth or duration of life, for he
himself is dependent on time, fruitive results and the modes of nature, which are all subordinate to
You."*

   These words were spoken by Çrématé Lakñmé--devé in the midst of Çrémad-Bhägavatam's
description of Kutmäla-varña. In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.59 the words "imäù striyo vyabhicära-
duñöäù kåñëe kva paramätmani" may then be interpreted to mean "What is the status of women who
are averse to Kåñëa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead?" The meaning then would be: "There is a
great difference between such women and the gopés." Then the word {.sy 168}rüòha-bhäväù" may be
interpreted to mean: "Not even the smallest fragment of the exalted spiritual love that is the crest
jewel of all goals of life is not seen in such women". That exalted spiritual love is present only in the
devotees, who are filled with love for the Lord. Only the devotees love the Lord. This is confirmed
by the passage beginning with the word "nanu" (Still, it is true that the Supreme Lord Himself
awards His blessings even to an ignorant worshiper, just as the best medicine works even when
taken by a person ignorant of its ingredients.) What moremay bhe said? The next verse of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.47.60) declares:


näyaà çriyo 'ìga u nitänta-rateù prasädaù
  svär-yoñitäà nalina-gandha-rucaà kuto 'nyäù

räsotasave 'sya bhuja-daëòa-gåhiöa-kaëöha-
   labdhäçiñaà ya udagäd vraja-sundaréëäm


   "When Lord Çré Kåñëa was danciong with the gopés in the räsa-lélä, the gopés were embraced by
the arms of the Lord. This transcendental favor was never bestowed upon the goddess of fortune or
other consorts in the spiritual world. Indeed, never was such a thing even imagined by the most
beautiful girls in the heavenly planets, whose bodily luster and aroma resemble the lotus flower.
Ansd what to speak of worldly women who are very beautiful according to material estimation?"*

   In this verse the word "aìge" means "on the graceful form of the master of Vaikuntha", "çriyaù"
means "of the Lord's dearmost beloved", "nitänta-rateù" means "of the love a girl feels for hewr
beloved", "prasädaù" means "happiness, and {.sy 168}näyam" means "is not". The verse then
continued: "svär-yoñitäà nalina-gandha-rucaà", which means: "If even the goddess of fortune
cannot attain that happiness, then the women of Svarghaloka, whose limbs are like golden lotus
flowers, and who do not even reside in Vaikuntha certainly cannot attain it." Then the words "kuto
'nyäù" mean "Other woemen, who are far away from them certainly cannot attain it." That is the
meaning. Then one may ask: Are there any women who care not bereft of this happiness? The
answer is given in this verse in the passage beginning with the word "räsa" (When Lord Çré Kåñëa
was danciong with the gopés in the räsa-lélä, the gopés were embraced by the arms of the Lord.)
Here the word "asya" means {.sy 168}of the form of Lord Kåñëa, the prine of Vraja". That Goddess
Laksmi yearns to attain the touch of Lord Kåñëa is also confirmed by these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.16.36):


yad-väïchayä çrér lalanäcarat tapaù. . .


   "O Lord, we do not know how the serpent Käliya has attained this great opportunity of being
touched by the dust of Your lotus feet. For this end, the goddess of fortune performed austerities for
centuries, giving up all other desires and taking austere vows."***

   Goddess Lakñmé did not only yearn to attain the love the gopés felt in separation from Lord
Kåñëa, she also yearned to attain the love they felt when they directlyenjoyed pastimes with Him.
What persons like myself say to describe that love? In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.60 the words
"räsotasave 'sya bhuja-daëòa-gåhiöa-kaëöha-labdhäçiñaà ya udagäd" mean "When, in the räsa dance,
Lord Kåñëa embraced the gopés' necks, the gopés felt all their desires were fulfilled". This means the
desire the gopés had long kept hidden in their hearts was now openly attained. That Goddess
Laksmi yearned to attain the gopés' good fortune is also confirmed by theese words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.15.8):


api yat-spåhä çréù

   "You have embraced the young cowherd women between Your two arms--a favor hankered after
by the goddess of fortune herself."***

    In Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.47.60 the word "vraja-sundaréëäm (of the beautiful girls of Vraja)
shows that the gopés are the most beautiful of all girls". That the devotees attain all exalted qualities
is confirmed by these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (5.18.12):


yasyästi bhaktir bhagavaty akiïcanä. . .


   "All the demigods and their exalted qualities, such as religion, knowledge and renunciation,
become manifest in the body of one who has developed unalloyed devotion for the Supreme
Personality of Godhead, Väsudeva."*

   Spiritual love where the devotee loves the Lord as a beloved is the crest jewel of all kinds of
spiritual love. Here two levels of that love, as manifested by Goddess Lakñmé and by the gopés, are
revealed. That this kind of spiritual love for the Lord is the most exalted is not refuted by the
following words spoken by the Lord to Uddhava in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (11.14.15):


na ca saìkarñaëo na çréù


  "My dear Uddhava, neither Lord Brahmä, Lord Çiva, Lord Saìkarñaëa, teh goddess of fortune,
nor indeed My own self are as dear to MKe as you are."***

  These words are only intended to praise devotional service and the devotees in a general way.
They do not mean that Uddhava is in a position superior to Goddess Laksmi and the other devotees
who consider the Lord their beloved. Because the gopés love Lord Kåñëa, the original form of the
Supreme Personality of Godhead, their position is most exalted.

Aquí alguien podría protestar: "¿No es cierto que los sabios que anhelan la liberación y que
¿Ya han alcanzado la liberación y son glorificados en todas las escrituras? ¿Cómo pueden los devotos ser
¿Superiores a ellos? ¿Por qué los sabios desearían algo que no fuera la liberación? Para responder a esta protesta,
Uddhava pronuncia estas palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.47.59):
kvemah striyo vana-carir vyabhicara-dustah
krsne kva caisa paramatmani rudha-bhavah nanv isvaro 'nubhajato 'viduso 'pi saksac
chreyas tanoty agada-raja ivopayuktah
"Qué asombroso es que estas mujeres sencillas que vagan por el bosque, aparentemente malcriadas por
¡El comportamiento inapropiado ha alcanzado la perfección del amor puro por Krishna, el Alma Suprema!
Sin embargo, es cierto que el Señor Supremo mismo otorga Sus bendiciones incluso a un ignorante.
adorador, así como la mejor medicina funciona incluso cuando la toma una persona ignorante de su
ingredientes."
En estos versos, de principio a fin, la gran devoción de Sriman Uddhava al Señor es
claramente visto. Aquí alguien podría protestar que la relación de las gopis con el Señor Krishna era
adúltero y por lo tanto inmoral. Esta protesta es respondida con estas palabras pronunciadas al final.
de la descripción de la danza rasa (srimad-Bhagavatam 10.33.35):
gopinam tat-patinam ca
sarvesam eva dehinam yo 'ntas carati so 'dhyaksah
kridaneneha deha-bhak
"Aquel que vive como testigo supervisor dentro de las gopis y sus maridos, y en verdad
Dentro de todos los seres vivos encarnados, se adoptan formas en este mundo para disfrutar de pasatiempos trascendentales."
La idea de los hombres malvados de que las gopis actuaron inmoralmente en su relación con el Señor
Krishna es refutado por este versículo, por la palabra "paramatmani" (la Suprema Personalidad de Dios) en
Srimad-Bhagavatam 10.47.59, y también por estas palabras de Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.47.61):
arya-patham ca hitva. . .
"Las gopis de Vrindavana han renunciado a la compañía de sus maridos, hijos y otros
miembros de la familia, que son muy difíciles de abandonar, y si han abandonado el camino de la castidad
para refugiarse en los pies de loto de Mukunda, Krishna, que uno debe buscar según los védicos.
conocimiento. Oh, déjame tener la fortuna de ser uno de los arbustos, enredaderas o hierbas en
Vrindavana, porque las gopis los pisotean y los bendicen con el polvo de sus pies."
Ahora no es el momento adecuado para refutar la idea errónea de que las gopis actuaron de forma inmoral. Más tarde
En este libro demostraremos que las gopis actuaron correctamente. En el srimad-Bhagavatam 10.47.58 y 59,
Las palabras "kvemah striyo vana-carih" significan "¿cuál es el estatus de las mujeres que disfrutaban de pasatiempos en
¿Y se refugiaron en el bosque de Vrndavana, Señor Krishna? En estos versos aparecen las palabras "kva vyabhicara-dustah
"bhava-bhiyo vayam" significa y ¿cuál es el estatus de nosotros, sabios que no hemos alcanzado la exaltación?
¿Acaso quienes no están apegados al amor espiritual y al Señor Krishna temen la existencia material?
El significado aquí es: La diferencia entre nosotros y las gopis es muy grande." Aquí la pregunta puede ser
preguntó: "¿Por qué existe una diferencia tan grande?" La respuesta se da aquí en las palabras esa
paramatmani rudha-bhavah", que significa "En las gopis se ve un gran amor extático (maha-bhava) por
la Suprema Personalidad de Dios, a quien todos adoran y quien es la morada de todos.
deseos. Ese mismo amor extático no se ve en nosotros." Si esto es así, entonces la siguiente pregunta
Se puede preguntar: Si no ves directamente las gloriosas cualidades del Señor Krishna, cualidades que hicieron...
Si las gopis se enamoran de Él, entonces ¿cómo alcanzarás ese amor extático incluso si anhelas?
¿Alcanzarlo? Esta pregunta se responde en este versículo, en el pasaje que comienza con la palabra "nanu".
(el Señor Supremo mismo otorga Sus bendiciones incluso a un adorador ignorante, al igual que el mejor
(La medicina funciona incluso cuando la toma una persona que desconoce sus ingredientes.) Aquí la palabra "avidusah"
significa que el Señor mismo hace que este amor se manifieste espontáneamente dentro de mí." Ese es el ejemplo
dado aquí. Uddhava declara en el srimad-Bhagavatam (10.47.27):
virahena maha-bhaga
mahan me 'nugrahah krtah
"Con razón has reclamado el privilegio del amor puro por el Señor trascendental, O
gopis más gloriosas. En verdad, al mostrar vuestro amor por Krishna en separación de Él, tenéis
me ha mostrado gran misericordia7"
El srimad-Bhagavatam 10.47.59 también puede interpretarse de una manera diferente, de una manera que severamente
reprende a las damas que, aunque muy fieles a sus maridos, son reacias a los rasas de
servicio devocional. En la primera interpretación de este versículo, las palabras "kvemah striah" se referían a
a las gopis, que disfrutan de pasatiempos en el bosque de Vrindavana. La segunda interpretación de este verso es
basado en la suposición de que una "a" estaba originalmente presente antes de la palabra "vana-carih" y luego
elidido por sandhi. Por lo tanto, la palabra era originalmente "avana-carih", que significaría "mujeres que no son
como las gopis". Tales mujeres materialistas son descritas en estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam.
(5.18.19):
striyo vratais tva. . .
"Mi querido Señor, ciertamente Tú eres el dueño completamente independiente de todos los sentidos. Por lo tanto, todos
mujeres que te adoran observando estrictamente los votos porque desean adquirir un marido para
Satisfacer sus sentidos seguramente está bajo una ilusión. No saben que tal marido no puede
en realidad les da protección a ellos o a sus hijos. Tampoco puede proteger su riqueza o duración.
de la vida, pues él mismo depende del tiempo, de los resultados fruitivos y de los modos de la naturaleza, que son
todos subordinados a Ti."
Estas palabras fueron dichas por srimati Laksmi-devi en medio del srimad-Bhagavatam.
descripción de Kutmala-varsa. En el srimad-Bhagavatam 10.47.59 las palabras "imah striyo vyabhicara-
"dustah krsne kva paramatmani" puede interpretarse entonces como "¿Cuál es el estatus de las mujeres que...
¿Son adversos a Krishna, la Suprema Personalidad de Dios? El significado entonces sería: "Hay una
gran diferencia entre tales mujeres y las gopis." Entonces la palabra rudha-bhavah" puede ser

presente únicamente en los devotos, que están llenos de amor por el Señor. Solo los devotos aman al Señor.
Señor. Esto se confirma por el pasaje que comienza con la palabra "nanu" (Aun así, es cierto que el
El Señor Supremo mismo otorga Sus bendiciones incluso a un adorador ignorante, al igual que el mejor
La medicina funciona incluso cuando la toma una persona que desconoce sus ingredientes. ¿Qué más se puede decir?
El siguiente verso del srimad-Bhagavatam (10.47.60) declara:
nayam sriyo 'nga u nitanta-rateh prasadah
svar-yositam nalina-gandha-rucam kuto 'nyah rasotasave 'sya bhuja-danda-grhita-kantha-
labdhasisam ya udagad vraja-sundarinam
"Cuando el Señor Sri Krishna estaba bailando con las gopis en el rasa-lila, las gopis fueron abrazadas por
los brazos del Señor. Este favor trascendental nunca fue otorgado a la diosa de la fortuna o
otros consortes en el mundo espiritual. De hecho, jamás se imaginó algo así por parte de los más
Hermosas muchachas en los planetas celestiales, cuyo brillo corporal y aroma se asemejan a la flor de loto.
¿Y qué decir de las mujeres mundanas que son muy bellas según los estándares materiales?
En este verso la palabra "ange" significa "sobre la forma grácil del maestro de Vaikuntha",
"sriyah" significa "de la más amada del Señor", "nitanta-rateh" significa "del amor que siente una niña".
para su amado", "prasadah" significa "felicidad, y nayam" significa "no es". El versículo entonces
continuó: "svar-yositam nalina-gandha-rucam", que significa: "Si incluso la diosa de la fortuna
Si no pueden alcanzar esa felicidad, entonces las mujeres de Svarghaloka, cuyos miembros son como lotos dorados
flores, y quienes ni siquiera residen en Vaikuntha ciertamente no pueden alcanzarlo." Luego las palabras "kuto
'nyah" significa "Otras mujeres, que están lejos de ellas, ciertamente no pueden alcanzarlo". Esa es la
significado. Entonces uno podría preguntarse: ¿Hay alguna mujer que no se sienta privada de esta felicidad? La respuesta
se da en este versículo en el pasaje que comienza con la palabra "rasa" (Cuando el Señor sri Krsna estaba
(bailando con las gopis en el rasa-lila, las gopis fueron abrazadas por los brazos del Señor.) Aquí
La palabra "asya" significa "de la forma del Señor Krishna, el príncipe de Vraja". Que la Diosa Lakshmi anhela.
Alcanzar el toque del Señor Krishna también queda confirmado por estas palabras del Srimad-Bhagavatam.
(10.16.36):
yad-vachaya srir lalanacarat tapah. . .
"Oh Señor, no sabemos cómo la serpiente Kaliya ha alcanzado esta gran oportunidad de ser
tocadas por el polvo de Tus pies de loto. Para este fin, la diosa de la fortuna realizó
austeridades durante siglos, renunciando a todos los demás deseos y haciendo votos austeros."
La diosa Lakshmi no solo anhelaba alcanzar el amor que las gopis sentían en la separación del Señor
Krishna también anhelaba alcanzar el amor que sentían cuando disfrutaban directamente de los pasatiempos con Él.
¿Qué dicen las personas como yo para describir ese amor? En el srimad-Bhagavatam 10.47.60 las palabras
"rasotasave 'sya bhuja-danda-grhita-kantha-labdhasisam ya udagad" significa "Cuando, en la danza rasa,
El Señor Krishna abrazó el cuello de las gopis, y las gopis sintieron que todos sus deseos se habían cumplido.
significa que el deseo que las gopis habían mantenido oculto en sus corazones durante mucho tiempo ahora se había cumplido abiertamente.
El anhelo de la diosa Lakshmi por alcanzar la buena fortuna de las gopis también se confirma con estas palabras de
Srimad-Bhagavatam (10.15.8):
api yat-sprha srih
"Has abrazado a las jóvenes pastoras entre Tus dos brazos, un favor anhelado por
la mismísima diosa de la fortuna."
En el srimad-Bhagavatam 10.47.60 la palabra "vraja-sundarinam (de las hermosas muchachas de Vraja)
muestra que las gopis son las más bellas de todas las niñas". Que los devotos alcancen todos los exaltados
Estas cualidades se confirman con estas palabras del srimad-Bhagavatam (5.18.12):
yasyasti bhaktir bhagavaty akicana. . .
"Todos los semidioses y sus cualidades exaltadas, como la religión, el conocimiento y la renuncia,
se manifiesta en el cuerpo de aquel que ha desarrollado una devoción pura por el Supremo
Personalidad de Dios, Vasudeva."
El amor espiritual, donde el devoto ama al Señor como a un amado, es la joya suprema de todas las clases.
del amor espiritual. Aquí dos niveles de ese amor, tal como lo manifiestan la Diosa Laksmi y la
gopis, se revelan. Que este tipo de amor espiritual por el Señor es el más excelso no es
refutado por las siguientes palabras pronunciadas por el Señor a Uddhava en el srimad-Bhagavatam (11.14.15):
na ca sankarsano na srih
"Mi querido Uddhava, ni el Señor Brahma, ni el Señor Siva, ni el Señor Sankarsana, ni la diosa de la fortuna,
Ni siquiera yo mismo soy tan querido para MKe como tú lo eres."
Estas palabras tienen como único propósito alabar el servicio devocional y a los devotos en general.
No quieren decir que Uddhava esté en una posición superior a la de la diosa Lakshmi y los demás devotos.
quienes consideran al Señor su amado. Porque las gopis aman al Señor Krishna, la forma original del
Suprema Personalidad de Dios, su posición es la más excelsa.
